## At a glance

---

## Job \{#job\}

A **job** is an entry of `jobs.toml`: an **id** (letters, digits, `-`, `_`; fixed once created), a description, tags, a schedule and timezone, an enabled switch, shared parameters, presets, a retry policy, alerts, a log level, a timeout — and an ordered list of steps. It is edited on the Jobs pages ([Create a job](./jobs/create.md)).

## Step \{#step\}

A **step** is one unit of work, of one of seven types: `sql_query`, `sql_copy`, `file_load`, `python`, `http`, `ldap_sync`, `call_job` ([Steps](./steps.md)). Steps run in order; a failed step stops the job, and the following ones are recorded as skipped.

## Schedule \{#schedule\}

A five-field **cron** evaluated in the job's **timezone**. The days of the week count from 0 = Monday: write them as names (`mon-fri`). No schedule means the job runs only on demand ([Schedules](./jobs/schedules.md)).

## Preset \{#preset\}

A saved set of run values — shared parameters, step arguments, steps switched off, log level — created from **Run with parameters**. A preset can carry its own schedule: one job, several schedules with different inputs.

## Trigger \{#trigger\}

What started a run: `scheduled` (the job's or a preset's schedule) or `manual` (a user, recorded by name). A job started by a `call_job` step records `call_job:<job>@<run>` as its starter.

## Run \{#run\}

One execution of a job, with an id, its trigger, its start and end, the rows affected, its steps and its log. States: `QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED`, and `MISSED` for a scheduled time that did not run ([Run history](./runs/history.md)).

## Parameters \{#parameters\}

| Level | Where | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| Shared params | The job | Every `python` step's arguments. |
| Step arguments (`op_kwargs`) | The step | That step — they win over shared params. |
| Run with parameters | One run | That run only; `jobs.toml` is not changed. |

`file_load` reads the run parameters as `${params.x}` in its path and constants; `sql_query` takes its own `params`.

## Retry policy \{#retry\}

`attempts` (tries in all, 1 = no retry), `backoff` (`fixed` or `exponential`), `base_seconds`. Applies to each step.

## Log level \{#log-level\}

`WARNING`, `INFO` (default) or `DEBUG` (adds the SQL of every query). The job's level applies to scheduled runs; a manual run picks its own.

## Alerts \{#alerts\}

A job can notify its **recipients** when a run fails, without any rule. Anything else — success, cancel, missed schedule, long run, a set of jobs — goes through notification rules ([Notifications](./notifications.md)).

---

## An example \{#example\}

The job `sales-load` has three steps: `file_load` (load the month's file), `sql_query` (refresh the aggregates), `http` (call a downstream service). Its schedule is `0 2 * * *` in `Europe/Paris`; a preset *month-end* runs it on `0 6 1 * *` with `period` set to the previous month. Each night a run is recorded; when the server was down at 02:00, a `MISSED` run is recorded and the `ops` role receives an e-mail from the rule on `missed`.

---

## Nomaflow — Catalogue — the Jobs page
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/jobs/catalog/

The Nomaflow Jobs page: the toolbar, the retention and missed-schedule panels, what a job card shows, switching a job on or off, Run now and Run with parameters (presets, steps, file uploads, log level), Cancel, Clone, Delete and Export.

The **Jobs** page lists every job of `jobs.toml` as a card, with its state, its schedule and its last run. It is reserved to superusers.

---

## At a glance

---

## The toolbar \{#toolbar\}

| Element | Use |
|---|---|
| **+ New job** | Opens the job editor — see [Create a job](./create.md). |
| **Schedule** | Every schedule by next run — see [Schedules](./schedules.md#schedule-view). |
| **↻** | Reloads the list. |
| **Filter:** | One chip per tag in use; pick some to show only those jobs, **Clear** to show all. |

Below it, two folded panels hold the policies shared by every job: **Run history retention** ([Administration](../administration.md#retention)) and **Missed schedules** ([Schedules](./schedules.md#missed)).

---

## A job card \{#card\}

| Element | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Id, description, tags | From the job's settings. |
| **enabled** / **disabled** | Click to switch the job's own schedule on or off. **Run now** works either way, and preset schedules are not affected. |
| Schedule chip | The cron, or **Manual only**. |
| *N preset schedule(s)* | Presets that carry their own schedule. |
| next · last | The next scheduled run, and the state and duration of the last one — click it to open its detail. |
| *N steps* | The number of steps. |

The card's buttons:

| Button | Effect |
|---|---|
| **▶ Run now** | Runs the job. When there is something to choose — shared parameters, step arguments, several steps, a `file_load` step — it opens **Run with parameters** first. |
| **Cancel** | Shown while the job runs: cancels the run in progress. |
| **Edit** | Opens the job editor. |
| **Clone** | Asks for a new id (`<id>_copy` proposed) and creates a disabled copy without any schedule: neither the job's own nor its presets'. |
| **Delete** | Removes the job from `jobs.toml` after confirmation. Its run history is kept. |
| **Export** | Downloads a ZIP with the job's `jobs.toml` entry and a `MANIFEST.md`. The connectors and queries it uses are not included. |

---

## Run with parameters \{#run-with-parameters\}

The window applies to this run only — `jobs.toml` is not changed. Its labels are in English.

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| **Preset** | Pick a saved preset and **Apply** it; **Save as preset…** saves the window's current state under a name, in `jobs.toml`. |
| **Shared params (apply to every step)** | The job's shared parameters, editable for this run. |
| **Steps** | One line per step with a checkbox to skip it (**All** / **None**); **Edit parameters** opens a step's arguments. A `file_load` step gets a file picker — see [Steps](../steps.md#file-load). |
| **Log level** | *WARNING — warnings + errors only*, *INFO — row counts + progress markers*, *DEBUG — full SQL of every query*. |
| **Run** | Uploads the chosen files, then starts the run. |

Typical uses: rerun only the step that failed, load one month again, run with `DEBUG` to see the SQL, run a preset by hand.

---

## Cancel \{#cancel\}

**Cancel** asks the run to stop. SQL, HTTP, file-load and `async` Python steps stop at once; the run ends **CANCELED**. A synchronous Python function cannot be interrupted: the run is marked cancelled and the function finishes on its own — see [Troubleshoot](../runs/troubleshoot.md#cancellation-doesnt-stop-my-step).

---

## Nomaflow — Create a job
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/jobs/create/

The Nomaflow job editor: the Job section (id, schedule, timezone, tags, enabled), presets and their schedules, the retry policy, alerts, shared parameters and the step pipeline — and what is set only in jobs.toml.

**+ New job** on the Jobs page, or **Edit** on a card, opens the job editor. One **Save** at the top writes the whole job to `jobs.toml`, reloads the scheduler and goes back to the Jobs page; **Cancel** leaves without saving. An invalid job is refused with a message at the top of the editor.

---

## At a glance

---

## The sections \{#sections\}

### Job

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Id** | Letters, digits, `-` and `_`. Fixed once the job exists — it keys the run history. To rename, **Clone** under the new id, then delete the old job. |
| **Description** | Shown on the card. |
| **Schedule (cron)** | Ready-made choices (Manual, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly) or a five-field cron; **Next runs** previews the next five. Blank: manual only. See [Schedules](./schedules.md). |
| **Timezone** | The IANA name the schedule is evaluated in. |
| **Tags** | Free labels, used by the filter of the Jobs page. |
| **Enabled** | Switches the job's own schedule on or off. |

### Presets & schedules

Presets are saved from **Run with parameters → Save as preset…**. Here each one can get its own **Schedule (cron)**, **Timezone** and **Schedule enabled** — see [Schedulable presets](./schedules.md#schedulable-presets).

### Retry policy

**Retry failed steps**, then **Attempts** (tries in all), **Backoff** (`fixed` or `exponential`) and **Base seconds** between tries. The policy applies to each step.

### Alerts

**Send alerts** with **On failure** sends a notification to the **Recipients** when a run fails, in the bell and by e-mail. Write recipients as `user:alice`, `role:ops` or `email:ops@example.com` — an entry without a prefix is taken as an e-mail address. **Warn if a run exceeds (minutes)** sends them a second notification when a run lasts at least that long, whatever its outcome. For several jobs at once or other events, use a notification rule: see [Notifications](../notifications.md#job-alerts).

### Shared params

Name / value pairs merged into the arguments of every `python` step (a step's own value wins). They also appear, editable, in **Run with parameters**.

### Steps

The **Add step:** bar has one button per type — `sql_query`, `sql_copy`, `file_load`, `python`, `http`, `ldap_sync`, `call_job`. Each step is a card: click it to open or fold its form; the arrows move it up or down; the copy icon clones it; the bin removes it. The fields of each type are on [Steps](../steps.md).

---

## Only in jobs.toml \{#toml-only\}

A few settings have no field in the editor; set them in `jobs.toml`:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `log_level` (job) | `INFO` | The level of scheduled runs: `WARNING`, `INFO` or `DEBUG`. A manual run picks its own in **Run with parameters**. |
| `timeout_seconds` (job) | `14400` | The whole run stops after this time. |
| `enabled` (step) | `true` | `false` always skips the step. |
| `timeout_seconds` (step) | `3600` | The step stops after this time. |
| `pool` (`sql_query`, `sql_copy` endpoints) | — | Another pool of the connector — see [Steps](../steps.md#sql-query). |

```toml title="jobs.toml"
[[jobs]]
id = "sales-load"
description = "Monthly sales files into the facts table"
schedule = "0 2 * * *"
timezone = "Europe/Paris"
tags = ["etl"]
log_level = "INFO"

[jobs.params]
period = "2026-10"

[jobs.retry]
attempts = 3
backoff = "exponential"
base_seconds = 60

[[jobs.steps]]
type = "file_load"
name = "load-sales"
# … see Steps → File load
```

---

## Tips \{#tips\}

- Give each step a short verb-noun name (`load-sales`, `refresh-totals`): it is what the run detail shows.
- Keep one job per business flow; chain jobs with a `call_job` step rather than copying steps.
- Save, then run once by hand with **Run with parameters** in `DEBUG` before enabling the schedule.

---

## Nomaflow — Schedules
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/jobs/schedules/

When Nomaflow jobs run: the five-field cron syntax and its day-of-week numbering, timezones, the preview of the next runs, the Schedule view, schedulable presets, and missed schedules recorded as MISSED runs.

A job runs on its own **schedule** — a cron expression and a timezone — and on the schedules of its **presets**. A job without any schedule runs only when someone clicks **Run**.

---

## Cron in Nomaflow \{#cron\}

A schedule has **five fields**:

```
┌──── minute (0-59)
│ ┌── hour (0-23)
│ │ ┌── day of month (1-31)
│ │ │ ┌── month (1-12)
│ │ │ │ ┌── day of week (mon-sun)
0 2 * * *
```

| Operator | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `*` | every value | `* * * * *` — every minute |
| `,` | a list | `0 6,12,18 * * *` — at 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00 |
| `-` | a range | `0 9 * * mon-fri` — weekdays at 09:00 |
| `/` | a step | `*/10 * * * *` — every 10 minutes |

:::warning[Write the days of the week as names]
The scheduler numbers the days of the week from **0 = Monday** to **6 = Sunday** — not like Unix cron, where 0 is Sunday. `0 9 * * 1` runs on **Tuesday**. Write `mon`, `tue`… `sun` (`mon-fri`, `sat,sun`): the names leave no doubt, and the preview under the field confirms the days.
:::

When both the day of the month and the day of the week are set, **both** must match: `0 9 15 * mon` runs on a 15th that falls on a Monday.

| Need | Cron |
|---|---|
| Every 5 minutes | `*/5 * * * *` |
| Every hour at :15 | `15 * * * *` |
| Every day at 02:00 | `0 2 * * *` |
| Weekdays at 09:00 | `0 9 * * mon-fri` |
| Every Monday at 06:00 | `0 6 * * mon` |
| The 1st of every month at 07:00 | `0 7 1 * *` |
| Every quarter (1st of Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct) at 03:00 | `0 3 1 1,4,7,10 *` |

---

## In the job editor \{#editor\}

The **Schedule (cron)** field of the job editor offers ready-made choices — **Manual**, **Hourly**, **Daily**, **Weekly**, **Monthly** — and a free cron. Under the field, **Next runs** lists the next five runs in the job's timezone; it is recomputed shortly after each change, and an invalid expression is reported there.

**Timezone** is an IANA name (`Europe/Paris`, `America/New_York`). The schedule is evaluated in that timezone, daylight saving time included: `0 2 * * *` in `Europe/Paris` runs at 02:00 Paris time all year round.

---

## The Schedule view \{#schedule-view\}

**Schedule** in the Jobs toolbar lists every schedule, by next run:

| Group | Content |
|---|---|
| **Upcoming** | One row per active schedule — the job's own, and one per preset with a schedule (the preset's name is shown next to the job). Columns: Job, Schedule, Next run, Last run. |
| **Manual / disabled** | Jobs without a schedule, and schedules that are set but switched off — marked *(disabled)*. |

---

## Schedulable presets \{#schedulable-presets\}

A **preset** is a saved set of run parameters (parameters, step arguments, steps switched on or off, log level), created from the **Run with parameters** window with **Save as preset**. In the job editor, the **Presets & schedules** section gives each preset its own **Schedule (cron)** and **Timezone**, and a **Schedule enabled** checkbox.

The scheduler then runs the job on that schedule with the preset's parameters: one job, several schedules, different inputs — a nightly full load and an hourly incremental of the same ETL, for instance.

A preset's schedule is independent of the job's **Enabled** switch: an enabled preset runs even when the job's own schedule is off.

:::info[Cloning a job]
**Clone** creates a disabled copy without any schedule: the job's own cron and the presets' schedules are dropped, so the copy never fires alongside the original. Give it its schedules once it is ready.
:::

---

## Missed schedules \{#missed\}

A run can fail to happen: the server was stopped at that time, or the previous run of the same job was still in progress. Nomaflow checks for such gaps and records each one as a run in state **MISSED**, with the expected time, in the run history and as the job's last run. A rule on the `missed` event can warn someone — see [Notifications](../notifications.md).

The **Missed schedules** panel of the Jobs page (next to the retention panel) shows the policy and the last check, and **Check now** runs a check at once.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Check** | on | Switches the check on or off. |
| **Grace (min)** | 10 | A run started within this delay after the expected time — a scheduled one, or a manual one — counts for it. |
| **Check interval (min)** | 5 | How often the check runs. |
| **Look back (hours)** | 24 | How far back a check looks, at most. A job that never ran is checked from the scheduler's start only. |

The policy is saved in `jobs.toml` under `[meta.missed]`. A missed time is recorded once: a restart does not report it again.

---

## Pausing a schedule \{#pause\}

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| The job's **Enabled** switch on the Jobs page | The job's own schedule stops. **Run** still works; preset schedules keep running unless switched off. |
| **Manual** in the Schedule field | The job's own schedule is removed. |
| **Schedule enabled** off on a preset | That preset's schedule stops. |

---

## Tips \{#tips\}

- Spread heavy jobs over the night (02:00, 02:30, 03:00) rather than starting them all at midnight.
- Prefer `15 * * * *` to `0 * * * *` for hourly jobs: many other systems run on the hour.
- Use a timezone name, never a fixed offset, so that daylight saving time is followed.
- Check the **Next runs** preview after every change: it is the quickest way to catch a wrong day.

---

## Nomaflow — Steps
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/steps/

The seven Nomaflow step types — sql_query, sql_copy, file_load, python, http, ldap_sync, call_job — what each one does, its fields and defaults, and what it records in the run.

A **step** is one unit of work in a job. Steps run in order; when one fails, the following ones are recorded as *skipped: earlier step failed*.

| The step… | Type |
|---|---|
| runs one named query of a SQL connector | **`sql_query`** |
| copies a whole table from one connector to another | **`sql_copy`** |
| loads a spreadsheet or a CSV file into a table | **`file_load`** |
| calls a Python function of a plugin | **`python`** |
| calls a URL | **`http`** |
| reads an LDAP / Active Directory directory into a table | **`ldap_sync`** |
| runs another job and waits for it | **`call_job`** |

In the job editor, the **Add step:** bar has one button per type, and each step opens a form with its own fields. A few keys exist only in `jobs.toml` (noted below).

---

## At a glance

---

## Common fields \{#common\}

| Field | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | — | Shown in the run detail; unique within the job. |
| `type` | — | One of the seven types. |
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` skips the step (recorded as *skipped: disabled*). Set in `jobs.toml`, or for one run in the **Run with parameters** window. |
| `timeout_seconds` | `3600` | The step is cancelled after this time. Set in `jobs.toml`. |

---

## SQL query — `sql_query` \{#sql-query\}

Runs one **named query** of a SQL connector — a query defined on the connector's page, read or write.

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `connector` | yes | The SQL connector. |
| `query` | yes | The name of the query, not SQL text. |
| `params` | no | Values bound to the query's parameters. |
| `pool` | no | Another pool of the connector's set — see [Multi-pool connectors](../framework/connectors.md#multi-pool). `jobs.toml` only. |

Records the number of rows returned or affected. To refresh a materialised view, call a procedure or purge a table, write the statement as a query of the connector, then call it here.

---

## SQL copy — `sql_copy` \{#sql-copy\}

Streams the rows of a source table to a target table, possibly on another database.

| Field | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `source` = `{connector, schema, table}` | — | Required. `pool` may be added (`jobs.toml` only). |
| `target` = `{connector, schema, table}` | — | Required. Same. |
| `mode` | `overwrite` | `overwrite`: the rows are written to a work table `<table>__new`, which then replaces the target in one transaction — the target is never empty during the copy. `append`: rows are inserted into the target as it is. |
| `type_coercion` | `jde` | `jde` applies the JD Edwards rules (scaled decimals, Julian dates, padded codes); `none` copies the values as they are. |
| `decimal_mode` | `truncate` | With `jde`: `truncate` or `preserve` the decimal part. |
| `batch_size` | `10000` | Rows per batch. |
| `strip_both_columns` | `[]` | Columns whose values are trimmed on both sides. |

`upsert` is accepted by the schema but refused at run time: for an insert-or-update, write a `MERGE` / `ON CONFLICT` query and call it with `sql_query`. Records the number of rows written.

---

## File load — `file_load` \{#file-load\}

Loads an Excel workbook (`.xlsx`, `.xlsm`) or a text file (`.csv`, `.txt`, `.tsv`) into a table — on a schedule, without anyone at the keyboard, at the volume a facts table needs, and replayable for one period without touching the others.

### The file

The file comes from, in this order of priority:

1. **a file chosen when the job is run** — the **Run with parameters** window shows a file picker for each `file_load` step (the window opens for any job that has one);
2. **`path`** — a path on the server, which may contain `${params.x}` (a run parameter), `${run.id}` and `${job.id}`: `/data/in/sales-${params.period}.xlsx`;
3. **a watched folder** — `watch_dir` and `watch_pattern` (`*.xlsx`): every matching file is loaded in name order, each in its own transaction, then moved to `done/` or `failed/` under a time-stamped name. A file that fails stops the run; the files after it stay in the folder. An empty folder is not an error.

| Field | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `sheet` | first sheet | A name or a number (1 = first). |
| `header_row` | `1` | The row of the column headers; data starts below. Empty rows are skipped. |
| `delimiter` | detected | CSV separator; detected among `;` `,` tab `|` when empty. |
| `encoding` | `utf-8-sig` | CSV only. |

### The target

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `target` = `{connector, schema, table}` | A SQL connector; the table must exist. |
| `columns` | Target column ← file header or position (`#3`). Headers match ignoring case, spaces, `_` and `-`; unmapped columns match by name. |
| `constants` | Target column ← value, for what the file does not carry: `period = "${params.period}"`, `batch_id = "${run.id}"`. |

Each cell is converted to the type of its target column: integers, decimals (`12,5` and `12.5` both read as 12.5; a lone comma is the decimal separator), dates (`2026-10-27`, `27/10/2026`, `27.10.2026`, `20261027`, and Excel dates), booleans (`1`, `true`, `yes`, `oui`…), text. A number typed as text keeps no leading zeros that the spreadsheet already removed.

### Load mode

| Field | Choice |
|---|---|
| `load_mode` | `append` (default) inserts the rows. `replace_partition` first deletes the rows of the partitions the file carries, then inserts — **in one transaction**: a failed load leaves the previous data in place, and a corrected month replaces that month only. |
| `partition_by` | The partition columns (`period, company`) — required with `replace_partition`. The partitions come from the constants when they cover every column, otherwise from the distinct values found in the file. |
| `on_error` | `fail` (default): the first bad cell fails the step and names the row. `skip`: bad rows are counted as rejected and written to a CSV (file, row, reason) offered in the run detail. |
| `batch_size` | `10000` rows per insert. |

### Guards

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `refuse_query` | A named query run before anything is touched, with the run parameters and the constants as binds. If it returns a row, the load is refused and the first column is the reason: *period 2026-02 is closed*. `refuse_connector`: its connector, the target's by default. |
| `control_column` + `control_total` | The column is summed over the loaded rows and compared with a value, `${params.total}`, or a cell of the file (`@B2`, `@Totals!B2`), within `control_tolerance`. A difference rolls the file's load back and names both figures. |

### In the run

The run detail shows *N read · N inserted · N rejected* and, when rows were rejected, **Rejected rows (csv)** to download them. The log adds the partitions replaced and the rows deleted.

Uploaded files and reject files go to the jobs' work area, `.nomaflow/files` next to the configuration; an upload is limited to 200 MB.

```toml title="jobs.toml"
[[jobs.steps]]
type = "file_load"
name = "load-sales"
path = "/data/in/sales-${params.period}.xlsx"
sheet = "Sales"
target = { connector = "sales", schema = "public", table = "fact_sales" }
columns = { company = "Company", article = "Item", qty = "Quantity", revenue = "Revenue" }
constants = { period = "${params.period}", batch_id = "${run.id}" }
load_mode = "replace_partition"
partition_by = ["period", "company"]
refuse_query = "period_closed_get"
control_column = "revenue"
control_total = "@Totals!B2"
```

---

## Python — `python` \{#python\}

Calls a function of a plugin: `callable = "package.module:function"`.

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `callable` | `module.path:function` — checked for shape when saved, imported when the step runs. |
| `op_kwargs` | Arguments passed to the function, merged over the job's shared parameters. |

The function receives its arguments as keyword arguments and, when it declares them by name, `connectors` (the connector registry), `ctx` (the run: `ctx.run_id`, `ctx.job_id`, `ctx.trigger`) and `settings`. It may be `async` or not. Its return value: an `int` is the number of rows affected, a `dict` is kept as the step's details, `None` is fine; an exception fails the step. To reach the run log, write with a logger of a registered namespace. The full contract is in [Write a callable](../framework/build/plugins/write-a-callable.md).

---

## HTTP — `http` \{#http\}

| Field | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | — | Required. Used as written. |
| `method` | `GET` | `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`. |
| `headers` | `{}` | Sent as they are. |
| `body` | none | Text, or a table sent as JSON (with `Content-Type: application/json` when none is set). |

A 2xx answer succeeds; anything else fails the step with the status. The step keeps the status, the first 4 KB of the answer and the duration. Values from the environment are written `${NAME}` in `jobs.toml` and replaced when the file is loaded.

---

## LDAP sync — `ldap_sync` \{#ldap-sync\}

Reads entries from an LDAP directory and runs a write query of a SQL connector for each entry.

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `server` | `ldaps://ad.example.com:636`. |
| `bind_dn`, `bind_password` | The account used to read; write the password as `${LDAP_PASSWORD}`. |
| `search_base`, `search_filter` | Where and what to search: `DC=example,DC=com`, `(objectClass=user)`. |
| `attributes` | The attributes to read. |
| `target_connector`, `target_query` | The write query run for each entry. |
| `mapping` | LDAP attribute → query parameter. A missing attribute gives `NULL`. |

Records the number of entries read and rows written.

---

## Call a job — `call_job` \{#call-job\}

`target_job_id` names another job. The step starts it, waits for it to end and takes its result: success, failure or cancellation. The called job has its own run in the history, and inherits the caller's log level and run parameters. A job that would end up calling itself is refused.

---

## Retries and timeouts \{#retry\}

The job's **Retry policy** block (`attempts`, `backoff` fixed or exponential, `base_seconds`) applies to each step: a step is tried up to `attempts` times in all (`1`, the default, means no retry), with a wait of `base_seconds` between tries — constant, or doubling with `exponential`. The job as a whole stops after `timeout_seconds` (4 hours by default).

---

## Nomaflow — Run history
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/runs/history/

Where Nomaflow runs are recorded and how to read one: the run states, the Run detail page (summary, per-fire overrides, steps, log with Follow and Download), the Job Runs list, and how long the history is kept.

Every run of a job — scheduled, manual, called by another job, or missed — is recorded with its steps and its log.

---

## At a glance

---

## Where to find runs \{#where\}

| From | Opens |
|---|---|
| *last* on a job card | The detail of the job's last run. |
| The **Job Runs** list (the Nomaflow menu; **Job Runs** at the top of a run detail) | The latest runs of every job. |
| A notification about a run | Its detail, through the notification's link. |

---

## Run states \{#states\}

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `QUEUED` | Accepted, waiting to start. |
| `RUNNING` | In progress. |
| `SUCCEEDED` | Every step succeeded or was skipped on purpose. |
| `FAILED` | A step failed after its retries. The following steps are recorded `CANCELED` with *skipped: earlier step failed*. |
| `CANCELED` | Cancelled by an operator or by a timeout. |
| `MISSED` | A scheduled time at which the job did not run — see [Missed schedules](../jobs/schedules.md#missed). |

A run interrupted by a server restart is closed as failed with *abandoned: process restart during run* when the server starts again.

---

## The Run detail page \{#detail\}

The page refreshes itself every two seconds while the run is in progress (*live*).

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| **Summary** | Job, Trigger (`scheduled` or `manual`, and who started it — a user name, or `call_job:<job>@<run>` for a job called by another), Started, Finished, Rows affected. |
| **Run with parameters** | Shown when the run was started with overrides: the values chosen for this run (shared parameters, step arguments, skipped steps, log level). |
| **Steps** | One row per step: #, name, Type, Attempt, State, Error. A `file_load` step also shows *N read · N inserted · N rejected* and, if needed, **Rejected rows (csv)**. |
| **Log** | The lines written during the run, at the run's log level. **Follow** keeps the newest lines in view (**Pause** stops it); **Download** saves the whole log. |

The log keeps the last 5,000 lines of a run.

---

## How long runs are kept \{#retention\}

The **Run history retention** panel of the Jobs page deletes old runs with their steps and logs: by default runs older than 30 days, keeping at most 100 runs per job, checked every 60 minutes. See [Administration](../administration.md#retention).

---

## Nomaflow — Troubleshoot
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/runs/troubleshoot/

Fixing Nomaflow runs: a run that failed, a step that does the wrong thing, a run that hangs, a cancel that does not stop a Python step, a schedule that does not fire, a job missing from the list, an empty log.

Start from the run detail: the **Error** column of the failed step, then the **Log**. Run again with **Run with parameters** at `DEBUG` to see the SQL of every query.

---

## A run shows FAILED \{#failed\}

| Error in the step row | Usual cause |
|---|---|
| *step timed out after N s* | The step exceeded its `timeout_seconds` (3 600 by default). Raise it in `jobs.toml`, or split the work. |
| *→ 404*, *→ 500* (http step) | The called URL answered with that status. |
| A database error | Wrong credentials, a missing table, a constraint. Test the pool in **Settings → Pools** and the query on the connector page. |
| *cannot import module …* / *has no attribute …* (python step) | The plugin is not where `callable` says, or the server was not restarted after a change — see [Deploy and debug](../../framework/build/plugins/deploy-and-debug.md). |
| *period … is closed* (file_load) | The step's refuse query rejected the load on purpose. |
| *control total mismatch …* (file_load) | The loaded total differs from the expected one; nothing was written. |

After fixing, rerun only the failed step: **Run with parameters**, untick the steps that already succeeded, **Run**.

---

## A step succeeded but did the wrong thing \{#wrong-result\}

Look at **Rows affected** and at the step's details, then rerun at `DEBUG`: the log shows each query with its values. For a `file_load`, compare *read / inserted / rejected* and download the rejected rows.

---

## A run stays RUNNING \{#hangs\}

A step waits on something slow — a locked table, a remote API, a long sync. Each step stops at its `timeout_seconds`, the job at its own (4 hours by default). **Cancel** on the job's card stops it sooner.

---

## Cancel doesn't stop my step \{#cancellation-doesnt-stop-my-step\}

SQL, HTTP, file-load and `async` Python steps stop at once. A Python function written with `def` runs in a worker thread that cannot be interrupted: the run shows **CANCELED**, but the function goes on until it returns. Write long functions as `async` — see [Write a callable](../../framework/build/plugins/write-a-callable.md).

---

## The schedule doesn't fire \{#schedule\}

| Check | Fix |
|---|---|
| The card shows **disabled** or **Manual only** | Switch the job on, or give it a schedule. |
| The day is wrong | The scheduler counts the days of the week from 0 = Monday. Write `mon-fri`, not `1-5` — see [Schedules](../jobs/schedules.md#cron). |
| The **Next runs** preview is not what was expected | Fix the cron or the timezone. |
| The server was down at that time | The run is recorded **MISSED**; run it by hand. |

---

## The job is missing from the list \{#missing\}

`jobs.toml` was edited by hand and no longer validates: the server log names the error. A key not in the schema is refused — check the spelling against [Steps](../steps.md) and [Create a job](../jobs/create.md#toml-only). After fixing the file, **Settings → Reload config**.

---

## The log is empty \{#empty-log\}

The run's log level is `WARNING`, or a Python plugin logs under a namespace that is not registered — see [Custom Python steps](../custom-python.md#logging).

---

## 403 on the Jobs page \{#forbidden\}

The Nomaflow pages and their API are reserved to superusers.

---

## Nomaflow — Scheduled sync
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/workflows/scheduled-sync/

Recipe — copy tables every night from an operational database to a reporting database with sql_copy, refresh the aggregates with sql_query, and be warned when it fails or does not run.

Every night, copy the `orders` and `customers` tables of the operational database into the reporting database, then refresh the aggregates the dashboards read.

---

## What you need \{#needs\}

- Two SQL connectors: `ops-db` (source, read-only account) and `reporting` (target).
- On `reporting`, a write query `daily_totals_refresh` that rebuilds the aggregates (`REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW …`, or `DELETE` + `INSERT … SELECT …`).

---

## The job \{#job\}

**+ New job**: id `nightly-reporting-sync`, tag `etl`, **Schedule (cron)** `0 2 * * *`, **Timezone** `Europe/Paris`. Then three steps:

| # | Type | Settings |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `sql_copy` | Source `ops-db` · `public` · `orders`; target `reporting` · `staging` · `orders`; mode `overwrite`. |
| 2 | `sql_copy` | Same for `customers`. |
| 3 | `sql_query` | Connector `reporting`, query `daily_totals_refresh`. |

`overwrite` writes into `<table>__new` and swaps it with the target in one transaction: the dashboards never see a half-filled table, and a failed copy leaves yesterday's data in place.

:::warning[Type coercion]
`sql_copy` applies the JD Edwards conversion rules by default (`type_coercion = "jde"`, `decimal_mode = "truncate"`). Between two ordinary databases, set `type_coercion = "none"` in `jobs.toml` so that values are copied as they are.
:::

```toml title="jobs.toml"
[[jobs]]
id = "nightly-reporting-sync"
schedule = "0 2 * * *"
timezone = "Europe/Paris"
tags = ["etl"]

[jobs.retry]
attempts = 3
backoff = "exponential"
base_seconds = 60

[[jobs.steps]]
type = "sql_copy"
name = "copy-orders"
source = { connector = "ops-db", schema = "public", table = "orders" }
target = { connector = "reporting", schema = "staging", table = "orders" }
mode = "overwrite"
type_coercion = "none"

[[jobs.steps]]
type = "sql_copy"
name = "copy-customers"
source = { connector = "ops-db", schema = "public", table = "customers" }
target = { connector = "reporting", schema = "staging", table = "customers" }
mode = "overwrite"
type_coercion = "none"

[[jobs.steps]]
type = "sql_query"
name = "refresh-totals"
connector = "reporting"
query = "daily_totals_refresh"
```

---

## Be warned \{#notify\}

In **Settings → Notifications**, a rule on *A job event*: job `nightly-reporting-sync`, events `failure` and `missed`, channel `email`, recipient `role:ops`, subject `{JOB}: {STATE}`, body `{ERROR}`. See [Notifications](../notifications.md).

---

## Check it \{#check\}

**▶ Run now**, then open the run: each step shows its rows; `DEBUG` in **Run with parameters** shows the queries. Once it is right, leave the schedule on.

---

## Nomaflow — API pull
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/workflows/api-pull/

Recipe — fetch records from a REST API every hour with a Python step and write them through a connector's query, with the token kept out of the job.

Every hour, fetch the latest releases of a project from a REST API and upsert them into a table.

The `http` step calls a URL and checks the answer, but does not hand the body to the next step: to read an API's data and store it, use a `python` step that calls the API and writes through a named query of a connector.

---

## What you need \{#needs\}

- A SQL connector `reporting` with a write query `release_upsert` — for PostgreSQL:

```sql title="release_upsert"
INSERT INTO releases (tag, name, published_at)
VALUES (:TAG, :NAME, :PUBLISHED_AT)
ON CONFLICT (tag) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name, published_at = EXCLUDED.published_at
```

- The API token in the server's environment: `GITHUB_TOKEN` (in `release/.env` on Docker, in the service's environment file on a Python install).

---

## The function \{#function\}

```python title="plugins/integrations/releases.py"
import logging
import os

import httpx
from liberty.connectors import ConnectorRegistry
from liberty.jobs.steps.base import StepResult

_log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

async def pull_releases(*, repo: str, target_connector: str, connectors: ConnectorRegistry) -> StepResult:
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['GITHUB_TOKEN']}"}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30) as client:
        resp = await client.get(f"https://api.github.com/repos/{repo}/releases", headers=headers)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        releases = resp.json()

    target = connectors.sql(target_connector)
    for r in releases:
        await target.execute("release_upsert", {
            "TAG": r["tag_name"], "NAME": r["name"], "PUBLISHED_AT": r["published_at"],
        })
    _log.info("%d release(s) upserted", len(releases))
    return StepResult(rows_affected=len(releases))
```

Register the package once so that its lines reach the run log: `register_namespace("integrations")` in `plugins/integrations/__init__.py` — see [Custom Python steps](../custom-python.md#logging).

---

## The job \{#job\}

```toml title="jobs.toml"
[[jobs]]
id = "pull-releases"
schedule = "15 * * * *"
timezone = "Europe/Paris"
tags = ["integration"]

[jobs.retry]
attempts = 3
backoff = "exponential"
base_seconds = 30

[[jobs.steps]]
type = "python"
name = "pull-releases"
callable = "integrations.releases:pull_releases"
op_kwargs = { repo = "acme/platform", target_connector = "reporting" }
```

An error raised by `raise_for_status()` fails the step; the retry policy tries again after 30 s, then 60 s.

---

## Variants \{#variants\}

| Need | Change |
|---|---|
| Pages of results | Loop on the API's next-page link inside the function. |
| Another repository on another schedule | A preset with its own `repo` and schedule — see [Schedulable presets](../jobs/schedules.md#schedulable-presets). |
| Just check that a service answers | An `http` step on its health URL is enough. |

---

## Nomaflow — Conditional cleanup
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/workflows/conditional-cleanup/

Recipe — purge old rows every night, but only when there are enough of them, in batches, with the decision and the counts in the run log.

Every night, delete the audit rows older than 90 days — but only when more than 10 000 have piled up, in batches so the table is not locked for long.

---

## What you need \{#needs\}

Two named queries on the connector `ops-db` — for PostgreSQL:

```sql title="audit_old_count_get"
SELECT COUNT(*) AS N FROM audit_log WHERE created_at < CURRENT_DATE - CAST(:DAYS AS INTEGER)
```

```sql title="audit_old_batch_delete"
DELETE FROM audit_log
WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM audit_log WHERE created_at < CURRENT_DATE - CAST(:DAYS AS INTEGER) LIMIT 5000)
```

---

## The simple way \{#simple\}

When no threshold is needed, a `sql_query` step calling `audit_old_batch_delete` is enough — schedule it often enough that each run deletes one batch.

---

## With a threshold \{#threshold\}

```python title="plugins/housekeeping/audit.py"
import asyncio
import logging

from liberty.connectors import ConnectorRegistry
from liberty.jobs.steps.base import StepResult

_log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

async def purge_audit(*, connector: str, days: int, threshold: int, connectors: ConnectorRegistry) -> StepResult:
    db = connectors.sql(connector)
    count = (await db.execute("audit_old_count_get", {"DAYS": days})).rows[0]["N"]
    if count < threshold:
        _log.info("%d old row(s), below %d — nothing to do", count, threshold)
        return StepResult(rows_affected=0, extras={"old_rows": count, "purged": False})

    deleted = 0
    while True:
        n = (await db.execute("audit_old_batch_delete", {"DAYS": days})).rowcount
        deleted += max(n, 0)
        if n <= 0:
            break
        await asyncio.sleep(0)          # lets Cancel stop the loop between batches
    _log.info("%d row(s) deleted", deleted)
    return StepResult(rows_affected=deleted, extras={"old_rows": count, "purged": True})
```

```toml title="jobs.toml"
[[jobs]]
id = "purge-audit"
schedule = "30 3 * * *"
timezone = "Europe/Paris"
tags = ["housekeeping"]

[[jobs.steps]]
type = "python"
name = "purge-audit"
callable = "housekeeping.audit:purge_audit"
op_kwargs = { connector = "ops-db", days = 90, threshold = 10000 }
```

The run detail shows the rows deleted; the log tells whether the threshold was reached. `days` and `threshold` can be changed for one run in **Run with parameters**.

---

## Variants \{#variants\}

| Need | Change |
|---|---|
| A dry run first | Add a `dry_run: bool = False` argument that only counts, and run once with `dry_run = true`. |
| Several tables | One job per table, or one function that takes the table's queries as arguments. |
| Be told when the purge ran | A notification rule on `succeeded` for this job. |

---

## Nomaflow — Bundled jobs
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/bundled-jobs/

The Nomaflow job catalogue shipped with the liberty-apps wheel — install / preload / refresh / sync / SOD / audit jobs that drive Nomasx-1 and Nomajde without the operator writing a single line of TOML. Run from Nomaflow → Catalogue → ▶ Run now, schedule via the standard scheduler, or trigger from CI.

The **`liberty-apps`** wheel ships a curated catalogue of Nomaflow jobs in `plugins/nomaflow/jobs.toml`. They land in Nomaflow's catalogue automatically after the wheel install + a framework reload — no `[[jobs]]` block to author, no scheduling to wire by hand.

Each job is a thin wrapper over a Python callable shipped in the **`nomasx1`** plugin package (`plugins/nomasx1/`). The bundle keeps the orchestration **declarative** (the `[[jobs]]` block in `jobs.toml`) and the work **imperative** (the callable in Python) — same pattern Liberty uses everywhere.

| Family | Purpose | Read |
|---|---|---|
| **Install** | One-time provisioning of databases + schema. | [Install jobs](#install) |
| **Preload** | Curated reference data export / import — for fresh customer installs or cross-env promotion. | [Preload jobs](#preload) |
| **Sync** | Copy upstream control + dictionary tables to the local Nomajde mirror. | [Sync jobs](#sync) |
| **Security collection** | Read JD Edwards security + LDAP into the Nomasx-1 schema. | [Security collection jobs](#security) |
| **License collection** | Read JDE license / employee / OUT data into the Nomasx-1 schema. | [License collection jobs](#license) |
| **SoD detection** | Run the segregation-of-duties matrix against the collected security data. | [SoD jobs](#sod) |
| **Database properties** | Read Oracle database metadata (options, features, partitioning, licenses). | [Database jobs](#database) |
| **Audit trail** | LogMiner-driven change capture from the audit-source DB. | [Audit-trail jobs](#audit-trail) |
| **Maintenance** | Materialised-view refresh, cross-reference rebuild, SCN reset, schema upgrade. | [Maintenance jobs](#maintenance) |

All bundled jobs ship with **`enabled = false`** — they appear in the catalogue but don't fire automatically. The operator enables a schedule (or runs them on demand) once the install is wired.

---

## At a glance

---

## How the bundle is delivered

The path of a bundled job from the wheel to the catalogue:

| Step | What |
|---|---|
| **1. Wheel install** | `pip install liberty_apps-*.whl` puts the carried payload inside the framework's site-packages. |
| **2. `liberty-apps install`** | Copies `plugins/nomaflow/jobs.toml` to `${LIBERTY_APPS_DIR}/../plugins/nomaflow/jobs.toml` and `plugins/nomasx1/` to `${LIBERTY_APPS_DIR}/../plugins/nomasx1/`. |
| **3. Reload** | Nomaflow re-reads `jobs.toml`; the framework re-imports the `nomasx1` package; the new jobs appear in the catalogue. |

Full procedure: [Installation → Deploy prebuilt apps](../installation/deploy-prebuilt-apps.md).

### Editing or extending the bundle

The bundled `jobs.toml` is **operator-editable** — it lives in your install's plugins directory after `liberty-apps install`. Add custom jobs by appending `[[jobs]]` blocks; the bundle's vendor jobs stay alongside yours. On the next wheel upgrade, the installer **replaces the file by default**, so commit your local additions to source control or move them to a separate `jobs.toml` next to the bundle's.

The Python callables (`plugins/nomasx1/`) are vendor-owned and refreshed on every wheel upgrade — don't edit them in place.

---

## Common parameters

Most jobs in the bundle share the same parameter shape under `[jobs.params]`:

| Parameter | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `apps_id` | `10` | The Nomasx-1 application id the job operates against. Override when running multi-tenant against several `nomasx1` apps. |
| `source_connector` | varies | The connector to **read from** — `jdedwards`, `unused` (for jobs that don't read upstream), `oracle-target` (for DB-introspection jobs). |
| `target_connector` | `nomasx1` | The connector to **write to**. Override for a parallel install (`nomasx1b`). |
| `target_schema` | `nomasx1` | The schema name inside the target connector. |

Overrides at run time: open *Run with parameters* on the job card before ▶ Run now. Per-schedule overrides: set them on the `[[jobs.schedules]]` block in your override `jobs.toml`.

---

## Install jobs \{#install\}

One-time provisioning. Run **once** at customer-stand-up; safe to re-run (idempotent) but pointless.

### `deploy-databases` \{#deploy-databases\}

**First-deploy DB provisioning.** Creates the application login roles and the per-target Postgres databases on the framework's `default` pool, then runs the Nomasx-1 schema bootstrap on the freshly-created database. The companion-step for the Nomajde mirror is created (empty schema — the sync jobs populate it).

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `create-roles-and-databases` | `nomasx1.db:create_databases` — creates the `nomasx1` + `nomajde` roles and databases. `create_roles = true` provisions the login roles too. |
| `init-schema-nomasx1` | `nomasx1.db:init_schema` — runs the Nomasx-1 schema bootstrap on the `nomasx1` DB. |

**Parameters**

| Key | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `admin_connector` | `default` | The pool to issue the `CREATE DATABASE` / `CREATE ROLE` statements through. Must have those rights on the Postgres server. |
| `targets` | `["nomasx1", "nomajde"]` | Per-target databases / roles to provision. |
| `create_roles` | `true` | Set `false` if your DBA created the login roles by hand. |
| `target_connector` *(init-schema step)* | `nomasx1` | The freshly-created DB to bootstrap. |

**When to run** — once on a fresh install, right after `liberty-apps install` + reload. The deploy-databases run typically takes 5-30 seconds.

---

### `nomasx1-init-db` \{#nomasx1-init-db\}

**One-time setup of a parallel Nomasx-1 deployment.** Clones the existing `nomasx1` app configuration under a new name (e.g. `nomasx1b`) — refuses if the target already exists — and provisions a parallel database. Used for multi-tenant hosting (one Liberty install serving two independent customer-data sets).

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `clone-app` | `liberty.web.clone:clone_app_step` — duplicates the source app's screens / menus / connector binding under the new name + pool. |
| `init-schema` | `nomasx1.db:init_schema` — schema bootstrap on the new DB. |

**Parameters**

| Key | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `source_app` | `nomasx1` | The app to clone from. |
| `new_app` | `nomasx1b` | The new app's name. Will become the menu / screens / connector name. |
| `new_pool` | `nomasx1b` | The new pool name to wire under the cloned connector. |
| `target_connector` *(init-schema step)* | `nomasx1b` | Same as `new_app` by convention. |

**When to run** — once per additional Nomasx-1 instance. For **recurring schema upgrades** after Python model changes, use `nomasx1-init-schema-1` (below) instead — it skips the clone step.

---

### `nomasx1-init-schema-1` \{#nomasx1-init-schema-1\}

**Create any missing Nomasx-1 tables + materialised views on `target_connector`.** Idempotent — safe to re-run after `models.py` changes that add new tables. Does NOT drop columns that disappeared from the model (use `nomasx1-upgrade-schema-1` for that).

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `init-schema` | `nomasx1.db:init_schema` |

**Parameters**

| Key | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `target_connector` | `nomasx1` | The DB to add the missing objects to. |

**When to run** — after every wheel upgrade that adds new tables (release notes will flag it).

---

### `nomasx1-upgrade-schema-1` \{#nomasx1-upgrade-schema-1\}

**Apply pending alembic migrations on `target_connector`.** Runs `alembic upgrade head` against the Nomasx-1 schema. Idempotent — no-op when already at head.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `upgrade-schema` | `nomasx1.db:upgrade_schema` |

**Parameters**

| Key | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `target_connector` | `nomasx1` | The DB to upgrade. |

**When to run** — after every wheel upgrade that ships schema deltas (release notes will say so). Pair with a database backup; alembic migrations are forward-only.

---

### `nomasx1-audit-trail-precheck-1` \{#nomasx1-audit-trail-precheck-1\}

**Read-only verification that the audit-source DB has every AUDIT_TRAIL prerequisite.** Checks LogMiner availability, archive-log mode, supplemental-logging settings, and the schema rights the audit-trail collector needs. Reports remediation SQL for any failing check.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `AUDIT_TRAIL_PRECHECK` | `nomasx1.audit_trail:j_audit_trail_precheck` |

**Parameters**

| Key | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `apps_id` | `10` | Nomasx-1 app id. |
| `source_connector` | `unused` | Not used by the precheck — it reads via the audit-source connector configured in the application's settings. |
| `target_connector` | `nomasx1` | Where the precheck report is written. |

**When to run** — once before enabling `nomasx1-audit-trail-1`; the report's remediation SQL goes to your DBA.

---

## Preload jobs \{#preload\}

The curated **reference bundle** ships in `${LIBERTY_APPS_DIR}/nomasx1-reference.tar.gz`. The export job builds the bundle from a source install; the import job loads it into a target install.

### `nomasx1-export-reference` \{#nomasx1-export-reference\}

**Dump the curated Nomasx-1 reference tables to a `.tar.gz` bundle.** The bundle contains `settings_*` + `sod_*` baseline rows (~2k rows, ~35 KB) — the curated reference data Nomasx-1 ships with, suitable for seeding fresh customer installs. Override `output_path` / `source_connector` via *Run with parameters*.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `export` | `nomasx1.preload:j_export_reference` |

**Parameters**

| Key | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `source_connector` | `nomasx1` | The DB to read the reference rows from. |
| `schema` | `nomasx1` | The schema name inside the source connector. |
| `output_path` | `/tmp/nomasx1-reference.tar.gz` | Where to write the bundle. The framework's service user needs write access. |

**When to run** — when curating a vendor release (NOMANA-IT-internal); not part of typical customer ops.

---

### `nomasx1-import-reference` \{#nomasx1-import-reference\}

**Load a curated Nomasx-1 reference bundle into `target_connector`.** Operator must create the target application in *Settings → Applications* first — the import precheck refuses to start otherwise. Set `replace = true` for a destructive TRUNCATE-then-INSERT cycle.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `import` | `nomasx1.preload:j_import_reference` |

**Parameters**

| Key | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `target_connector` | `nomasx1` | The DB to import into. |
| `schema` | `nomasx1` | The schema name inside the target connector. |
| `bundle_path` | `/tmp/nomasx1-reference.tar.gz` | The bundle to load. After `liberty-apps install`, the default bundle lives at `${LIBERTY_APPS_DIR}/nomasx1-reference.tar.gz` — set this parameter accordingly. |
| `replace` | `false` | When `true`, TRUNCATE each target table before INSERT. Use only for a clean re-seed. |
| `target_apps_ids` | `""` | Comma-separated app ids to restrict the import to (e.g. `"10,20"`). Empty = all apps in the bundle. |

**When to run** — once after `deploy-databases`, to seed the SoD baseline + reference settings. The job is safe to re-run with `replace = false` (only adds missing rows).

---

## Sync jobs \{#sync\}

Mirror upstream control / dictionary tables from JD Edwards into the local Nomajde database. Schedule daily — the data they read changes infrequently.

### `nomajde-daily-sync` \{#nomajde-daily-sync\}

**Daily sync of JDE control + data-dictionary tables to Nomajde.** Reads from the configured `jdedwards` connector and overwrites the matching tables in the `nomajde` connector. Each step is a single-table `sql_copy` with `mode = "overwrite"` — full-table refresh per run.

**Tables synced**

| Source (JDE) | Target (Nomajde) | What it carries |
|---|---|---|
| `PS920CTL.F0004` | `nomajde.f0004` | UDC types. |
| `PS920CTL.F0005` | `nomajde.f0005` | UDC values. Trailing whitespace on `DRKY` is trimmed via `strip_both_columns`. |
| `DD920.F9200` | `nomajde.f9200` | Data dictionary master. |
| `DD920.F9202` | `nomajde.f9202` | Data dictionary text. |
| `DD920.F9210` | `nomajde.f9210` | Data dictionary glossary. |
| `OL920.F9860` | `nomajde.f9860` | Object librarian master. |
| `OL920.F9865` | `nomajde.f9865` | Object librarian dependencies. |

**Type coercion**

Each step uses `type_coercion = "jde"` + `decimal_mode = "truncate"` — JDE column types are mapped to standard SQL on the way in (e.g. `JULIANDATE` → `DATE`, `STRING(N)` trimmed to `VARCHAR`), with truncation rather than rounding on decimals.

**Schedule** — `30 2 * * *` (02:30 daily, Europe/Paris timezone in the bundle). `enabled = false` by default — enable from the catalogue card once `jdedwards` is wired and the first run succeeded as a manual ▶ Run now.

**Retry / alerts** — 2 retry attempts, alert when the run exceeds 120 minutes.

---

### `nomajde-remerge-security` \{#nomajde-remerge-security\}

**Re-merge the JDE security (F00950 / F00950W / F9006) of every parent role affected by a change captured in the active draft package.** Driven by the `nomajde.security:j_remerge_security` plugin with `scope = "package"`.

This job — and its `-all` sibling — solves the JDE-specific problem that role security is **derived** from a tree of parent → child role assignments. Changing a child role's permissions only affects production once every parent that includes it has been re-merged. Doing that by hand on a wide change is tedious and error-prone; the job walks the change package, derives the impacted parents from the captured writes, and re-runs the merge for each.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `REMERGE_SECURITY` | `nomajde.security:j_remerge_security` — reads the active draft package, derives the impacted parent set via the anchored `F00926` role queries, re-merges F00950 / F00950W / F9006 per parent. |

**Parameters**

| Key | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `apps_id` | `10` | Nomajde application id. |
| `source_connector` | `nomajde` | Where the merged security tables live (the Nomajde mirror that holds the F564* tables). |
| `target_connector` | `jdedwards` | The live JDE database the re-merged rows write back to. |
| `scope` | `package` | `package` → only the parents impacted by the active draft. `all` → every parent (use `nomajde-remerge-security-all` instead). |

**When to run** — as a **post-apply step** on a change package that touches roles or role-to-role assignments. Register the job's id (`nomajde-remerge-security`) on the contributing screen's `Screen.post_apply`; the framework then runs it once on the target after the bundle's rows land. Manual ▶ Run now works too, in which case the active draft on the configured application is used.

The job's diagnostics land in the run log under the `nomajde.*` logger namespace (registered by the plugin) — useful when the merge skipped a parent because its `F00926` row was missing.

**Idempotent** — re-running on the same draft package re-merges the same parents and produces the same rows. Safe to retry after a partial failure.

---

### `nomajde-remerge-security-all` \{#nomajde-remerge-security-all\}

**Re-merge the JDE security of every parent role in the system, regardless of recent changes.** Same plugin as above (`nomajde.security:j_remerge_security`) but with `scope = "all"`.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `REMERGE_SECURITY_ALL` | `nomajde.security:j_remerge_security` with `scope = "all"`. |

**When to run** — once after a clean import of the JDE security tables (`F00950` / `F00926` from a fresh extract), or as a recovery step after a known-bad merge. Not scheduled by default; not idempotent in the trivial sense (re-running on a stable system is a no-op data-wise but writes the same rows again, which can take minutes on a large JDE install).

For a partial re-merge — only the parents affected by *this* change — use `nomajde-remerge-security` (`scope = "package"`).

---

## Security collection jobs \{#security\}

Read JD Edwards security data into the Nomasx-1 schema. The shape is a long chain of single-callable steps — one Python function per JDE entity / Nomasx-1 derived table.

### `nomasx1-security-1` \{#nomasx1-security-1\}

**Collect all security data for an application** — Users / Roles / Assignments / Menus / Access. Each step extracts one JDE entity (objects, sec objects, sec menus, etc.) or builds one Nomasx-1 derived table (security_users, security_rights_actions, etc.).

| Family | Steps | What |
|---|---|---|
| JDE entities | `JDE_OBJECTS`, `JDE_OBJECTS_VERSIONS`, `JDE_SEC_OBJECTS`, `JDE_SEC_MENUS`, `JDE_TASKS`, `JDE_MENUS` | Raw extraction from F00950, F0094, F0092, F9012, F9001, F9000. |
| Nomasx-1 catalogs | `SECURITY_USERS`, `SECURITY_USERS_DATA`, `SECURITY_ROLES`, `SECURITY_ASSIGNMENTS`, `SECURITY_MENUS` | Per-app users + roles + role assignments + menu trees. |
| Derived rights | `SECURITY_RIGHTS_MENUS`, `SECURITY_RIGHTS_APPS`, `SECURITY_RIGHTS_ACTIONS`, `SECURITY_RIGHTS_APPS_USERS`, `SECURITY_RIGHTS_ACTIONS_USERS` | Effective rights — by role, by user, on menus / apps / actions. |
| Audit | `SECURITY_RIGHTS_AUDIT` | Audit trail of right grants/revocations. |
| Refresh | `REFRESH_VIEWS` | Materialised-view refresh at the end. |

All steps run sequentially (no parallelism — order matters for the derived tables).

**Standard params** (`apps_id`, `source_connector = jdedwards`, `target_connector = nomasx1`, `target_schema = nomasx1`).

**Retry / alerts** — 2 attempts, long-run alert at 30 minutes.

**When to run** — daily for active installs (read-only against JDE). The first run after a new role / user / right grant in JDE refreshes the Nomasx-1 catalog; until then the UI shows the previous snapshot.

---

### `nomasx1-ldap-1` \{#nomasx1-ldap-1\}

**Collect Active Directory users** through the LDAP / AD connection configured in *Settings → LDAP*. Populates the Nomasx-1 `security_ldap` table that backs the LDAP reconciliation pages.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `SECURITY_LDAP` | `nomasx1.ldap:j_security_ldap` |

**Params** — standard shape (`source_connector = unused` — the LDAP server is configured separately).

**When to run** — daily, after the LDAP source has been refreshed; or on-demand before a quarterly access review.

---

## License collection jobs \{#license\}

Read JDE license-relevant data — employees, transactional users, Object Usage Tracking — into the Nomasx-1 schema. Drive the *Licenses → JD Edwards* dashboards.

### `nomasx1-employees-1` \{#nomasx1-employees-1\}

**Collect employees from JD Edwards HR modules** — internal + external. Populates the `license_jde_employees` table; refresh the materialised views at the end.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `LICENSE_JDE_EMPLOYEES` | `nomasx1.license:j_license_jde_employees` |
| `REFRESH_VIEWS` | `nomasx1.security:j_refresh_views` |

**Long-run alert** — 5 minutes.

**When to run** — weekly. The HR data doesn't change daily.

---

### `nomasx1-license-1` \{#nomasx1-license-1\}

**Collect users from JD Edwards tables — transactions only.** Reads who's actually transacted in JDE over the recent window (used as the input for licensable-user counting). Populates `license_jde_users`.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `LICENSE_JDE_USERS` | `nomasx1.license:j_license_jde_users` |
| `REFRESH_VIEWS` | `nomasx1.security:j_refresh_views` |

**Long-run alert** — 30 minutes.

**When to run** — daily (active installs) or weekly (slower installs). Pair with `nomasx1-employees-1` so transactional users join back to employee records.

---

### `nomasx1-out-1` \{#nomasx1-out-1\}

**Collect Object Usage Tracking from JD Edwards.** Aggregates the OUT data and purges retained rows per the retention defined in *Nomasx-1 → Settings → JDE → OUT retention*. Drives the OUT dashboards (components, users, objects).

| Step | What |
|---|---|
| `LICENSE_JDE_OUT` | Raw OUT extraction from JDE. |
| `LICENSE_JDE_OUT_OBJECTS` | Per-object aggregation. |
| `LICENSE_JDE_OUT_USERS` | Per-user aggregation. |
| `LICENSE_JDE_OUT_PURGE` | Purge rows older than the retention setting. |
| `REFRESH_VIEWS` | Materialised-view refresh. |

**Long-run alert** — 15 minutes.

**When to run** — daily. OUT data accumulates fast; running daily keeps the dashboard relevant and the purge step keeps the DB bounded.

## SoD jobs \{#sod\}

### `nomasx1-sod-1` \{#nomasx1-sod-1\}

**Collect Segregation of Duties (SoD) based on the security data and the matrix defined in *Nomasx-1 → Settings → SoD*.** Security data is a prerequisite — run after `nomasx1-security-1`.

| Step | What |
|---|---|
| `SOD_CONFLICT_DETAILS` | Per-user-per-conflict detail rows. |
| `SOD_CONFLICT_SUMMARY` | Aggregated counts driving the SoD dashboard. |
| `REFRESH_VIEWS` | Materialised-view refresh. |

**Long-run alert** — 10 minutes.

**When to run** — daily, scheduled after `nomasx1-security-1` (so the SoD scan sees the freshest assignments). Or on-demand after a major access-review action.

---

## Database jobs \{#database\}

Read Oracle metadata from the JDE-hosting database (or any Oracle target wired as `oracle-target`). Drives the *Database → Oracle* page.

### `nomasx1-database-1` \{#nomasx1-database-1\}

**Collect Oracle database properties.**

| Step | What |
|---|---|
| `DB_ORA_PROPERTIES` | Version, edition, parameters. |
| `DB_ORA_OPTIONS` | Installed options (Spatial, OLAP, RAC, etc.). |
| `DB_ORA_FEATURES` | Feature usage from `DBA_FEATURE_USAGE_STATISTICS`. |
| `DB_ORA_PARTITIONS` | Partitioning usage per schema. |
| `DB_ORA_LICENSES` | Aggregated license-relevant signals (option + feature + partitioning use). |

**Source connector** — `oracle-target` (a connector you configure pointing at the Oracle DB you want introspected). The job won't read from `jdedwards` — by design, so a separate Oracle target can be audited without giving Nomasx-1's JDE connector extra read rights.

**Long-run alert** — 10 minutes.

**When to run** — monthly is typically enough. The data feeding the Oracle dashboards changes slowly.

## Audit-trail jobs \{#audit-trail\}

LogMiner-driven change-data capture from the audit-source database — Oracle archive logs. Operate independently of the security / license / SoD jobs.

### `nomasx1-audit-trail-1` \{#nomasx1-audit-trail-1\}

**Capture LogMiner-driven change-data — Audit Trail using Oracle archive logs.**

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `AUDIT_TRAIL` | `nomasx1.audit_trail:j_audit_trail` |

**Source connector** — `unused` here (the audit-source connector is read from the application's settings, not the job's params).

**Long-run alert** — 30 minutes.

**When to run** — typically scheduled hourly or every 15 minutes. Before enabling, run [`nomasx1-audit-trail-precheck-1`](#nomasx1-audit-trail-precheck-1) and fix any reported gaps.

---

### `nomasx1-audit-trail-reset-scn-1` \{#nomasx1-audit-trail-reset-scn-1\}

**Reset the last SCN used by Audit Trail for an application.** Use after a long pause (audit-trail catching up on too much history would be slow) or after switching audit sources. Default `scn = 0` makes the next run pick up the current SCN — i.e. start fresh from "now". Override `scn` via *Run with parameters* to set a specific SCN.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `AUDIT_TRAIL_RESET_SCN` | `nomasx1.audit_trail:j_audit_trail_reset_scn` |

**Params** — standard shape + `scn = 0` (the default).

**When to run** — on demand. Not scheduled.

---

### `nomasx1-audit-trail-purge-values-1` \{#nomasx1-audit-trail-purge-values-1\}

**Purge the audit-trail values to reclaim space.** Deletes rows of `AUDIT_TRAIL_VALUES` — the field-level before / after values the Audit Lookup screen filters on. The captured statements (`AUDIT_TRAIL_QUERY`) are kept, so any period can be rebuilt later with [`nomasx1-audit-trail-rebuild-values-1`](#nomasx1-audit-trail-rebuild-values-1).

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `AUDIT_TRAIL_PURGE_VALUES` | `nomasx1.audit_trail:j_audit_trail_purge_values` |

**Params** — standard shape, plus:

| Param | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `older_than_days` | `0` | `0` or less: delete every value of the application. More than `0`: delete only the values whose statement is older than that number of days. |
| `table` | `""` | Limit the purge to one table. Empty: every table. |

Records the number of value rows deleted.

**When to run** — on demand, when the values table grows too large. Not scheduled.

---

### `nomasx1-audit-trail-rebuild-values-1` \{#nomasx1-audit-trail-rebuild-values-1\}

**Rebuild the audit-trail values of a table and a period** by parsing again the statements kept in `AUDIT_TRAIL_QUERY` — after a purge, when value-level analysis is needed again. The audited columns set per table are applied, so the rebuilt values match what live capture would have written.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `AUDIT_TRAIL_REBUILD_VALUES` | `nomasx1.audit_trail:j_audit_trail_rebuild_values` |

**Params** — standard shape, plus:

| Param | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `table` | `""` | The table to rebuild. Empty: every table. |
| `date_from`, `date_to` | `""` | The period, `YYYY-MM-DD`, end date included. Empty: no bound. |
| `replace` | `true` | Clear the values of the window first, so that running the job twice gives the same result. |

Records the number of value rows written.

**When to run** — on demand, after a purge. Not scheduled.

## Maintenance jobs \{#maintenance\}

### `nomasx1-refresh-views` \{#nomasx1-refresh-views\}

**Refresh materialised views** — speeds up Nomasx-1 queries. All major collection jobs run this at their end, so a dedicated invocation is rarely needed. Useful after a manual SQL data fix or a bulk import.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `refresh-views` | `nomasx1.db:refresh_views` |

**Params** — `target_connector = nomasx1`.

**When to run** — after a manual data fix; not scheduled.

---

### `nomasx1-xref-1` \{#nomasx1-xref-1\}

**Generate cross-reference for JD Edwards objects.** Builds the JDE_XREF_APPS table that backs the cross-reference views (which app references which object).

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `JDE_XREF_APPS` | `nomasx1.xref:j_jde_xref_apps` |

**Params** — `object_id = "all"` (default — process every object). Override to a specific object id for a targeted rebuild.

**Long-run alert** — 30 minutes.

**When to run** — weekly. XRef data changes slowly; only objects added/modified in JDE matter.

---

### `nomasx1-xref-dump-object-1` \{#nomasx1-xref-dump-object-1\}

**Diagnostic: dump the raw definition of one JD Edwards object.** Writes to files the decompressed OMW XML of the object's forms (F98751) and the text it references (F98750), to inspect the raw structure — for example a missing tab or control id. Read-only: nothing is written to the target database.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `JDE_XREF_DUMP_OBJECT` | `nomasx1.xref:j_jde_xref_dump_object` |

**Params** — standard shape, plus:

| Param | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `object_id` | `P01012` | The object to dump — set it in *Run with parameters*. |
| `output_dir` | `""` | The folder of the files. Empty: a temporary folder on the server. |

**When to run** — on demand, to analyse a cross-reference gap. Not scheduled.

---

### `nomasx1-activity-log-1` \{#nomasx1-activity-log-1\}

**Refresh Activity Log.** Queries every JDE table that has been modified recently and aggregates records for user + date. **Only the modified tables are scanned** — the job tracks per-table watermarks so it doesn't re-read the whole history each run.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `SECURITY_ACTIVITY_LOG` | `nomasx1.activity_log:j_security_activity_log` |

**Long-run alert** — 15 minutes.

**When to run** — daily.

---

### `config-versions-purge` \{#config-versions-purge\}

**Purge the old configuration versions** kept by the [configuration history](../framework/configuration/config-history.md) — file snapshots and screen bundles. For each file, a version is removed when it is beyond the 20 most recent or older than 90 days; the newest version of each file is always kept, so the history never empties.

| Step | Callable |
|---|---|
| `purge` | `liberty.jobs.maintenance:purge_config_versions` |

**Step arguments** — `max_versions = 20`, `max_age_days = 90`; `0` or less turns that rule off.

Records the number of versions removed. Two attempts in all on failure.

**Schedule** — **enabled**, every day at 03:00 (Europe/Paris).

## Scheduling tips

A typical daily cadence on an active install:

| Time | Job |
|---|---|
| 02:30 | `nomajde-daily-sync` (the shipped schedule). |
| 03:00 | `nomasx1-security-1`. |
| 03:30 | `nomasx1-license-1`. |
| 04:00 | `nomasx1-out-1`. |
| 04:30 | `nomasx1-ldap-1`. |
| 05:00 | `nomasx1-sod-1` (after security so it has the freshest assignments). |
| 05:30 | `nomasx1-activity-log-1`. |

Audit-trail (`nomasx1-audit-trail-1`) typically runs every 15-60 minutes — it's a separate cadence from the security / license refresh.

The bundled jobs are **enabled = false** out of the box. Set the schedule per job from *Nomaflow → Catalogue → \<job\> → Schedules tab*, then toggle `Enabled` on the catalogue card.

---

## Common pitfalls

| Mistake | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Bundle's `jobs.toml` overwritten on wheel upgrade — local edits lost. | Custom `[[jobs]]` blocks disappear after `liberty-apps install`. | Keep custom jobs in a separate `jobs.toml` outside the bundle's plugin dir; or back up the file before upgrading. |
| Collection job fails with `No module named 'nomasx1'`. | Plugin code isn't in the framework's plugins path. | Run `liberty-apps install --target $LIBERTY_APPS_DIR` to materialise the payload; reload the framework. |
| `nomasx1-import-reference` fails with *"target application not found"*. | Application not created in *Settings → Applications*. | Create the app in the UI first; the precheck refuses to start otherwise. |
| `deploy-databases` errors with permission denied. | `default` pool can't create DBs / roles. | Temporarily point `default` at a Postgres superuser; revert after the run. |
| Schedule set but job doesn't fire. | Toggle on the catalogue card is OFF (the bundle ships `enabled = false`). | Toggle `Enabled` on the card AFTER setting the schedule. |
| Daily sync runs but Nomajde tables remain empty. | The `jdedwards` connector isn't configured (the sync job silently runs zero rows). | *Settings → Connectors → jdedwards* — test the connection from the UI before the next run. |
| Audit trail starts producing thousands of rows per minute. | The job started from SCN 0 — replaying the whole archive log. | Run `nomasx1-audit-trail-reset-scn-1` (default `scn = 0` → next run picks current SCN) to start fresh. |
| Materialised views show stale data after a custom SQL fix. | The collection job's end-of-run REFRESH_VIEWS step didn't run (you bypassed it). | Run `nomasx1-refresh-views` manually. |
