## Nomaflow — Change packages
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/change-packages/

Capture every tracked data write into a reviewable package — old → new diffs grouped by entity, exclude entries cherry-pick style, submit / approve / reject the package, export a JSON bundle and apply it on another environment with full pre-image drift detection. The canonical use case is promoting JD Edwards security from dev to prod.

The **Change packages** page captures every tracked data write into a grouped, reviewable, promotable set. The use case the feature was built around is **promoting JD Edwards security from a development environment to production** — copy a role, attach a few menus, save → the writes land in production tables on dev, AND in a *change package* the operator can review, approve and ship to prod as a JSON bundle.

The same pattern fits every other "make changes here, replay them there" workflow: a curated UDC catalogue refresh, a batch of new permissions on a custom screen, a routing-rule update on a configuration table. As soon as a screen is **`change_tracked`**, its inserts / updates / deletes land in the active draft package alongside the production write.

This is the operator-facing pairing of a deeper engine: the framework persists every tracked write into the **`ly_change_packages`** + **`ly_change_entries`** tables (the **change-set DB** — same pool as the framework, separate from the audit mirror), and the apply path replays them on the target with pre-image drift detection.

:::info[Added in framework 2026.06]
The page lives under Nomaflow because the workflow — *capture → review → submit → approve → export → apply* — is a flow, not a setting. The Settings → Package screen still exists for config slices (screens / menu items / dashboards); Change packages is the **data** equivalent. The two coexist.
:::

---

## Opening the page

- Sidebar → **Nomaflow → Changes**.
- From the Settings → Connectors page, *Track changes* in the screen card opens the page filtered on the matching application.

---

## At a glance

---

## How a package fills up

Three things have to be in place for a write to land in a package.

| Required | What |
|---|---|
| **Screen is `change_tracked = true`** | A flag in the screen's *General* tab (or its TOML). Without it, writes go to the underlying table only — no capture. |
| **An active draft exists for the application** | The screen's connector → its `application`. The framework keeps **at most one DRAFT per application** (enforced by a partial unique index). The first tracked write on that application creates one if none exists. |
| **The user is signed in** | The package records `captured_by` from the session. Anonymous writes are not tracked. |

Once those are in place, every tracked write produces one **change entry**:

| Operation | What's captured |
|---|---|
| `INSERT` | `new_values` — the bound write columns. |
| `UPDATE` | `old_values` (the pre-image fetched through the screen's `read_query` before the write) + `new_values`. The pre-image is what drives drift detection on apply. |
| `DELETE` | `old_values` only. |
| `CALL_API` | The resolved call parameters + the configured `change_replay` flag — re-issued verbatim on apply when `replay = true`. |
| `CALL_PLUGIN` | Same — the plugin id + resolved kwargs, gated by `change_replay`. |

Each entry also records:

- `connector` + `query` — the framework can route the replay to the matching connector on the target.
- `entity` — the optional `change_entity` from the screen (`role`, `user`, `relationship`, `security`, …). The UI groups entries by this label on the detail page; a screen with no `change_entity` still captures, just grouped by `query`.
- `entity_key` — the natural key of the row (resolved from the screen's `key_columns`). Drives **compaction** on export — `INSERT then UPDATE then UPDATE` on the same key collapses to one effective net entry; `INSERT then DELETE` cancels out entirely.
- `source_action` — the label of the action that triggered the write, threaded from the firing context. Lets the detail view group a batch as "imported by *import security*" instead of an unattributed wall of inserts.
- `read_query` — the screen's read query, used by the apply path to fetch the current target row and compare to `old_values` for drift detection.
- `seq` — monotonic per package, so replay preserves the capture order. A role has to exist before it can be referenced; the seq guarantees that.

### What `change_tracked` does NOT track

| Not tracked | Why |
|---|---|
| Writes from a screen with `change_tracked = false`. | Default. Audit-only tables (notification log, retry stats) shouldn't pollute promotion bundles. |
| Writes from a Nomaflow job, a bulk import, the CLI. | Tracking is per-screen and runs through the screen's write path. Jobs use `j_*` callables directly against the connector. |
| Reads — no SELECT is ever captured. | The package is a *change* log. |
| The framework's own metadata writes (`ly_jobs`, `ly_users`, the change-set tables themselves). | The capture loop checks `change_tracked` on the connector's screen, not on the table. |

---

## The lifecycle

A package walks through these states:

```text
    DRAFT ─── submit ───▶ PENDING ─── approve ──▶ APPROVED ─── export ──▶ EXPORTED
                              │
                              └── reject ──▶ REJECTED
```

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **`DRAFT`** | The active package on its application. New tracked writes attach here. Entries can be excluded / re-included. |
| **`PENDING`** | Submitted for approval. No new writes attach (a fresh DRAFT opens for the application on the next capture). Reviewer can approve or reject. |
| **`APPROVED`** | Frozen, ready to export. Entries can no longer be excluded. |
| **`EXPORTED`** | A JSON bundle has been downloaded. The package is now the source-side record of what was shipped; the bundle is what reaches the target. |
| **`REJECTED`** | The reviewer turned it down. It stays rejected; the next tracked write on the application opens a new draft. |

The four lifecycle buttons on the detail header — *Submit*, *Approve*, *Reject*, *Export* — fire `POST /admin/changesets/<id>/submit` (or `…/approve`, `…/reject`, `…/export`). Change packages are reserved to superusers.

### Per-entry: exclude / re-include

While the package is `DRAFT`, every captured entry has an **Exclude** button. Excluded entries are not removed (no audit loss); they're flagged `status = excluded` and skipped on compaction + export. Re-including is one click. Useful for cherry-picking: capture a wide set of changes during the day, exclude the experiment that didn't pan out, ship the rest.

Compaction is computed at **export time**, not on capture — exclusions take effect immediately the moment the bundle is built.

---

## The Changes tab — review and act

The page has two tabs: **Changes** (the package catalogue) and **Apply** (covered below).

### Left column — the package list

| Element | What |
|---|---|
| Filter box | Matches the package name or status. |
| Active package | Pre-selected on open (the draft of the application the operator last touched). Highlighted blue. |
| Package row | Name + meta line (`status · captured_by · timestamp · entry_count`) + a coloured status badge. |
| Status colours | `DRAFT` blue, `PENDING` orange, `APPROVED` green, `EXPORTED` grey, `REJECTED` red. |
| Trash icon | Deletes the package log — the rows already written to the underlying tables are NOT affected; only the change-package record is removed. Confirmed via the themed dialog. |

### Right column — package detail

| Element | What |
|---|---|
| Header | Package name + application + entry count + lifecycle buttons (*Submit* / *Approve* / *Reject* / *Export*) + the resolved post-apply step ids (when set on contributing screens). |
| Entries grouped by entity | Default groups: `ROLES`, `USERS`, `RELATIONSHIPS`, `SECURITY`, `MENUS`, `ACTION REPLAYS` (the CALL_API / CALL_PLUGIN entries) — the group label comes from each entry's `change_entity`. Click the group head to fold / unfold. |
| Group head | The label + the entry count + a short sample of the natural keys (e.g. `PRJM_NEW · UDC_ADM · BUYER_R2`). |
| Entry row | Operation badge + the natural key + the firing action label. Click the chevron to expand the `old → new` diff. |
| Diff view | Two-column `field` / `value` table with three tones: red strikethrough = old, green = new, secondary = unchanged. A small *Show unchanged* toggle reveals the noise of untouched columns when reviewing a renamed-but-not-changed entry. |
| Per-entry buttons | *Exclude* (only on `DRAFT` packages) flips the entry to `EXCLUDED` and dims it. Click again to re-include. |

### Post-apply steps on the header

A screen can name **post-apply steps** (`Screen.post_apply`): actions to run once on the target after the package's rows have landed — re-merge a security model, refresh a materialised view. They come from a library of post-apply steps shared by the application, each step being a plugin call (`call_plugin`), an API endpoint (`call_api`) or a query (`run_query`). Their ids accumulate on the package header, and on export they are appended to the bundle as final operations.

---

## The Apply tab — bring a bundle in

Run this on the **target** install (typically prod) to bring a bundle exported from the source (typically dev).

The apply flow is two-pass: **dry-run first** to see the per-op drift report, then real apply, optionally with *force* ticked on rows you want to override.

| Step | What |
|---|---|
| 1. **Pick the JSON** | The exported bundle. The header shows its name, application and op count once parsed. |
| 2. **Dry-run** | `POST /admin/changesets/apply { bundle, dry_run: true }`. The server walks every op, fetches the current target row via the captured `read_query`, compares to the captured `old_values`, and tags the op with a status. **No write happens.** |
| 3. **Read the report** | Each op shows its status badge: `would_apply` (clean), `conflict` (the target differs from the captured state — see below), `would_force` (a conflict the operator chose to apply), `unverified` (no drift check possible), `skipped` (an action captured for review only), `error`. The summary line totals each status. |
| 4. **Tick the conflicts to apply anyway** | Each `conflict` op has a checkbox. Ticking it **applies** the op despite the difference (it then reads `would_force`); an unticked conflict is not applied. |
| 5. **Apply** | `POST /admin/changesets/apply { bundle, dry_run: false, force: [<indexes>] }`. Each op runs in its own transaction; per-op rowcounts + status come back in the report. |
| 6. **Confirmation** | A row lands in the target's import log (top of the *Apply* tab), with the bundle's checksum. The source package stays `EXPORTED`. |

### Drift detection — what it compares

For every row op, the apply path reads the target's current row with the captured `read_query` and key, then:

| Op | Target row | Status |
|---|---|---|
| INSERT | absent | `would_apply` |
| INSERT | already exists | `conflict` |
| UPDATE / DELETE | equal to the captured pre-image | `would_apply` |
| UPDATE / DELETE | different, or missing | `conflict` |
| any | no read query or key captured, or unreadable | `unverified` — applied without check |
| `CALL_API` / `CALL_PLUGIN` | — | `unverified` — re-run on apply; `skipped` when the action was captured without `change_replay` |
| post-apply step | — | `unverified` — always runs, after the change ops |

A conflict is applied only when its checkbox is ticked. An op whose write raises is reported `error` with the database message.

### Re-applying the same bundle

The import log uses the bundle's **checksum** (a SHA-256 of its ops) as the identity. Re-applying the same file is detected before any write runs — the dry-run report carries an `already_applied` block with the previous `applied_at` / `applied_by`. The operator can either confirm and re-apply (rows land again where the target matches the pre-image; the others come back as conflicts) or close the file.

### Action replay (`CALL_API` / `CALL_PLUGIN`)

A change-tracked screen captures **every** API / plugin call it fires (so the package shows it for review). Whether the call is **replayed** on the target is gated by the action's `change_replay` flag:

| `change_replay` | What gets replayed on the target |
|---|---|
| `true` *(opt-in)* | The action is re-issued verbatim with the captured resolved params. Used for server-side merge plugins like `nomajde.security:j_remerge_security` — re-merging the security on the target is correct after the row writes land. |
| `false` *(default)* | The capture is shown in the package for review but **not** re-fired. Used for one-off side effects that shouldn't run twice (email sends, external webhook). |

A replayed action runs in the same transaction as the surrounding row writes when the dialect allows it; in practice this means a successful security-merge plugin run lands atomically with the role / assignment writes that triggered it.

---

## Promoting JD Edwards security — the canonical use case

The motivating workflow for this feature. On the **dev** instance:

1. Operator creates a role `PRJM_NEW`, attaches three menus, edits two existing roles' permissions. Every write lands in the **`JDE-PROD`** application's draft package as it happens.
2. Operator opens *Nomaflow → Changes*, reviews the draft. The detail view shows the three roles grouped as `ROLES`, the menu attachments as `MENUS`, the touched security as `SECURITY`. A `CALL_PLUGIN` entry to `nomajde.security:j_remerge_security` is also captured.
3. Operator excludes one entry — a typo correction they want to roll back manually instead. Submits, then *Approves*, then *Exports*.
4. The browser downloads `jde-prod-security-2026-06-09.changeset.json`.

On the **prod** instance:

5. Operator opens *Nomaflow → Changes → Apply*, drops the JSON in.
6. Dry-run runs. The report shows 11 `would_apply` and 1 `conflict` on the role `BUYER_R2` (someone touched it on prod since the package was captured). Operator ticks that row to apply it anyway.
7. Operator clicks *Apply*. Every row lands; the post-apply step fires last, re-merging the security for the affected parent roles on prod.
8. The prod-side import log records the bundle with its checksum.

For the deep reference of the merge SQL the post-apply step runs, see [Nomaflow → Bundled jobs → nomajde-remerge-security](./bundled-jobs.md#nomajde-remerge-security-all).

---

## Configuring a screen for change tracking

The screen's *General* tab carries three toggles:

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| **`change_tracked`** | Master toggle. When on, the screen's writes attach to the active package on its application. |
| **`change_entity`** | Optional label that groups entries on the detail page. Free text — `role`, `user`, `relationship`, `security` are conventions. Empty falls back to the query name. |
| **`Screen.post_apply`** | Ids of post-apply steps (from the post-apply library) to run **once on the target** after the package's rows have landed. Use sparingly — these are the cross-cutting "now re-merge security" / "now refresh materialised views" steps. |

For an action embedded in the screen, an additional toggle on the action's *General* tab:

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| **`change_replay`** | When on, a `CALL_API` / `CALL_PLUGIN` invocation of this action is replayed on the target. Default off — capture-only. |

---

## API contract

| Endpoint | Method | What |
|---|---|---|
| `/admin/changesets` | `GET` | List packages. Filters: `application=<id>`, `status=<one-of>`. Superuser-only. |
| `/admin/changesets/<id>` | `GET` | Package detail — header + every entry with old / new values. |
| `/admin/changesets/<id>` | `DELETE` | Delete the package log only (not the underlying writes). |
| `/admin/changesets/<id>/submit` | `POST` | Move `DRAFT` → `PENDING`. |
| `/admin/changesets/<id>/approve` | `POST` | Move `PENDING` → `APPROVED`. |
| `/admin/changesets/<id>/reject` | `POST` | Move `PENDING` → `REJECTED`. |
| `/admin/changesets/<id>/entries/<entry_id>/exclude` | `POST` | Flip an entry's status to `EXCLUDED`. |
| `/admin/changesets/<id>/entries/<entry_id>/include` | `POST` | Flip an entry's status to `CAPTURED`. |
| `/admin/changesets/<id>/export` | `GET` | Returns the compacted JSON bundle; flips the package to `EXPORTED`. |
| `/admin/changesets/apply` | `POST` | Body: `{ bundle, dry_run, force: [<indexes>] }`. Returns the per-op report. |
| `/admin/changesets/applied` | `GET` | The target's import log (every applied bundle). |

The bundle shape:

```json
{
  "format": "liberty-changeset/1",
  "package": { "id": "...", "name": "...", "application": "JDE-PROD", "approved_by": "...", "approved_at": "..." },
  "op_count": 12,
  "ops": [
    { "seq": 1, "connector": "jdedwards", "query": "roles", "read_query": "roles_by_key",
      "operation": "INSERT", "entity": "role", "entity_key": {"RLDF": "PRJM_NEW"},
      "new_values": {"RLDF": "PRJM_NEW", "RLDC": "1", ...},
      "source_action": "import security" }
  ],
  "checksum": "9f2c…"
}
```

The format is stable across framework upgrades — a bundle built on `2026.06` applies cleanly on `2026.07`. The `format` field names the bundle version (`liberty-changeset/1`); post-apply steps travel as the last entries of `ops`.

---

## What's NOT in this page

The framework does ship the engine for these but the UI today is intentionally bare:

| Surface | Status |
|---|---|
| **Schedule an automatic submit / approve** | No. Manual lifecycle by design (an approved package goes to prod — a sign-off is the point). |
| **Diff between two packages** | No. Compare on the target via the Applied bundles log + the source's detail view. |
| **Roll back a promoted package** | No. The framework records the apply but doesn't synthesise a reverse bundle. To undo, capture a new package on the source that reverts the rows + promote it. |
| **Live multi-tab updates** | No. A capture on another tab doesn't refresh this page; click *Refresh* (top-right) to reload. |

---

## Common pitfalls

| Mistake | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Screen wasn't marked `change_tracked`. | Writes go through; no entries appear in the package. | Open the screen's *General* tab, toggle on, save. The change applies to subsequent writes only — earlier writes don't backfill. |
| Two operators have a DRAFT package open on the same application. | At most one DRAFT exists at a time; the second operator's writes attach to the same package. | Coordinate. The package's `created_by` records the original author; subsequent captures stamp `captured_by` on each entry, so attribution survives. |
| Bundle applied on the wrong target (staging instead of prod). | Apply lands; rows exist on staging. | Capture a reverse package on staging, promote to prod — the framework doesn't synthesise this automatically. Workflow discipline matters more than tooling here. |
| `conflict` on every UPDATE in the dry-run. | The target's pre-image diverged broadly — typically because the source and target weren't in sync to begin with. | Audit the divergence first. Forcing everything propagates the source's state wholesale; sometimes that's right, sometimes the source is the one that's stale. |
| `CALL_PLUGIN` captured but didn't fire on apply. | `change_replay` is off on the action. | Open the action's *General* tab, toggle `change_replay` on, save. Future captures will replay; past ones in already-exported packages stay as-is. |
| Post-apply step never ran. | The contributing screen's `Screen.post_apply` field is empty. | Add the step's id to the screen's `post_apply`. New captures accumulate it on the package header; existing packages are not back-filled. |
| Bundle re-applied accidentally. | Dry-run shows `already_applied` with the previous timestamp. | Read the existing apply's report. Re-applying is allowed and idempotent on clean rows; only do it intentionally. |

---

- [Nomaflow → Bundled jobs → nomajde-remerge-security](./bundled-jobs.md#nomajde-remerge-security-all) — the security re-merge plugin most often wired as a post-apply step on JDE promotions.

## Nomaflow — Custom Python steps
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/custom-python/

Write a Python function for a Nomaflow python step: where it lives, what it receives (its arguments, connectors, the run context), what it returns, how it logs to the run, how it fails and how it is cancelled.

When no other step type fits, a `python` step calls a function you write. The function lives in a plugin of the apps folder, receives its arguments from the job, and its result lands in the run like any other step.

This page is the short version for job authors. The full reference — injected arguments, return values, cancellation, worked example — is in [Write a callable](../framework/build/plugins/write-a-callable.md), and deployment in [Deploy and debug](../framework/build/plugins/deploy-and-debug.md).

---

## Where the function lives \{#where\}

A plugin is a Python package in the `plugins/` folder next to the configuration folder (`LIBERTY_APPS_DIR/../plugins`). The step names the function as `package.module:function`:

```toml title="jobs.toml"
[[jobs.steps]]
type = "python"
name = "refresh-summary"
callable = "reports.summary:refresh"
op_kwargs = { period = "2026-10", target_connector = "reporting" }
```

Modules are imported once: after changing the code, restart the server (`./liberty restart` or `liberty-ops restart`).

---

## What the function receives \{#arguments\}

```python title="plugins/reports/summary.py"
import logging
from liberty.connectors import ConnectorRegistry
from liberty.jobs.steps.base import RunContext, StepResult

_log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

async def refresh(*, period: str, target_connector: str,
                  connectors: ConnectorRegistry, ctx: RunContext) -> StepResult:
    _log.info("refresh %s · run %s", period, ctx.run_id)
    conn = connectors.sql(target_connector)          # connectors.api(...) for an API connector
    await conn.execute("summary_refresh_put", {"PERIOD": period})   # a named query of the connector
    ...
    return StepResult(rows_affected=count, extras={"period": period})
```

| Argument | Comes from |
|---|---|
| Its own arguments (`period`, `target_connector`) | The job's shared parameters, then the step's `op_kwargs` (the step wins), then the values typed in **Run with parameters**. Values are converted to the annotated type (`apps_id: int`). |
| `connectors` | The connector registry — run a connector's named queries or endpoints. Given only if the function declares it. |
| `ctx` | The run: `ctx.run_id`, `ctx.job_id`, `ctx.trigger`, `ctx.prev_rows_affected` (rows of the previous step). Given only if declared. |
| `settings` | The server settings. Given only if declared. |

The function may be `async` (recommended) or a plain `def`, which runs in a worker thread.

---

## What it returns \{#return\}

| Return | In the run |
|---|---|
| `None` | Nothing more. |
| an `int` | The number of rows affected. |
| a `dict` | Kept as the step's details (not counted as rows). |
| a `StepResult(rows_affected=…, extras={…})` | Both. |

Any other type — a `bool` for instance — fails the step, so that a mistake does not pass for a success.

---

## Logging to the run \{#logging\}

The run log keeps the lines of the `liberty.*` loggers and of the namespaces a plugin registers. Register the package once, in `plugins/reports/__init__.py`:

```python
from liberty.jobs.runlog import register_namespace
register_namespace("reports")
```

Then `logging.getLogger(__name__)` in any module of the package writes to the run log, and `print()` does not. The run's log level (**Run with parameters** → log level) applies.

---

## Failing and cancelling \{#errors\}

- Let exceptions out: the step fails with the message, the job's **Retry policy** applies, the following steps are skipped. Raise `StepFailed("…")` (from `liberty.jobs.steps.base`) for a clearer message.
- **Cancel** on the job's card cancels an `async` function at its next `await`. A plain `def` cannot be interrupted: the run is marked cancelled, the function finishes on its own.

---

## Tips \{#tips\}

- Put SQL in the connector's named queries and call them from the function: the query stays visible and testable in the connector page.
- Keep functions short; split long work into several steps so the run detail shows where it stopped.
- Test the function like any Python code, passing a registry pointed at a test database.

---

## Nomaflow — Notifications
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/notifications/

Liberty Next notifications: rules that react to a screen write, a Nomaflow job event (failure, success, cancel, missed schedule, long run) or a screen action, and deliver to the in-app bell, by e-mail or through a connector query or endpoint. SMTP account, recipients, placeholders, job alerts.

A notification tells someone that something happened: a period was closed, a nightly job failed, a schedule was missed. **Rules** decide when; **channels** decide how — the bell in the application, an e-mail, or a call to a connector.

---

## At a glance

---

## What users see \{#inbox\}

- **The bell** in the header shows the number of unread notifications, updated live. Its menu lists the latest six; **Mark all read** and **View all** are at the bottom. Clicking a notification marks it read and opens its link.
- **The Notifications page** (from **View all**) lists them with **All** / **Unread** tabs and **Mark all read**.

Each user sees only their own notifications.

---

## The e-mail account \{#smtp\}

E-mail goes through the SMTP server set in **Settings → App → Notifications (email)**:

| Field | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Notifications enabled | on | Off: no rule fires. |
| SMTP host, Port | —, `587` | Without a host, only the bell works. |
| Encryption | STARTTLS | *STARTTLS (usually port 587)*, *SSL / implicit TLS (usually port 465)* or *None*. Changing it sets the usual port. |
| Timeout (s) | `20` | |
| User, Password | — | The password is encrypted with the install's master key. |
| From address | the user | Falls back to the user name when empty. |

| Keep read notifications (days, 0 = forever) | `90` | Read notifications older than that are purged, at startup and every six hours. Unread ones are kept. |

E-mails are plain text: the subject, then the body, then the rule's link.

---

## Rules \{#rules\}

Rules are edited in **Settings → Notifications** and saved in `notifications.toml` — a change applies without a restart. **Send a test** sends the rule being edited, even unsaved, with sample values to its recipients.

### Triggers

| Trigger | Fires when | Settings |
|---|---|---|
| **A screen event** | A row is inserted, updated or deleted through a screen. | App, Screen, Events (`insert` / `update` / `delete`), and optionally **Only when the written row has**: field = value conditions, all required (`STATUS = closed`). |
| **A job event** | A Nomaflow run ends. | Jobs (empty = every job) and Events: `failure`, `succeeded`, `canceled`, `missed` (a schedule that did not run — see [Schedules](./jobs/schedules.md#missed)), `long_run` with a threshold in minutes. |
| **A screen action** | A screen action of type `send_notification` runs (a button or a step of an action chain). | Nothing more: the screen action names the rule and passes the row's values. |

`long_run` is checked when the run ends: it reports a run that lasted at least the threshold, not a run still in progress.

### Channels

| Channel | Delivers |
|---|---|
| `portal` | A notification in the bell of each recipient user. |
| `email` | An e-mail to each recipient that has an address. |
| `action` | Runs a query (SQL connector) or calls an endpoint (API connector) with the message's values — to post to Teams or a webhook, or to write a log table. Its parameters are the event's values plus `SUBJECT`, `BODY` and `RULE`. |

A channel that fails is logged and does not stop the others. Sending runs in the background: a save or a job never waits for the mail server.

### Recipients

| Form | Means |
|---|---|
| `user:alice` | That user. |
| `role:controllers` | Every active user holding the role. |
| `email:finance@example.com` | An address — e-mail only. |

In the editor, pick users and roles from the list or type an address. An entry without a prefix is sent to as an address when it contains `@`; any other is ignored and logged.

### Placeholders

Subject, body and link take `{NAME}` placeholders, written in any case:

| Trigger | Placeholders |
|---|---|
| Screen event | Every column of the written row, plus `USER`, `APP`, `SCREEN`, `EVENT`. |
| Job event | `JOB`, `RUN_ID`, `STATE`, `ERROR`, `DURATION_MINUTES`, `ROWS`, and `EXPECTED_AT` for a missed schedule. |
| Screen action | The values passed by the action, plus `USER`. |

An unknown placeholder is left as written.

### In TOML

```toml title="notifications.toml"
[notifications.period_closed]
label = "Period closed"
trigger = { kind = "screen", app = "sales", screen = "period_status", events = ["update"], when = [{ field = "STATUS", value = "closed" }] }
channels = ["portal", "email"]
recipients = ["role:controllers", "email:finance@example.com"]
subject = "Period {PERIOD} closed by {USER}"
body = "Company {COMPANY}: the period is now read-only."
link = "/screen/sales/period_status"

[notifications.job_failed]
trigger = { kind = "job", events = ["failure", "missed"] }
channels = ["email"]
recipients = ["role:ops"]
subject = "{JOB}: {STATE}"
body = "{ERROR}"
```

---

## A job's own alerts \{#job-alerts\}

A job can also warn on failure without a rule, from the **Alerts** block of the job editor:

```toml title="jobs.toml"
[jobs.alerts]
on_failure = true
recipients = ["role:ops", "user:alice"]
```

On failure, each recipient gets a notification *Job &lt;id&gt; failed* with the error, in the bell and by e-mail. With **Warn if a run exceeds (minutes)** (`on_long_run_minutes`), a run that lasts at least that long also sends *Job &lt;id&gt; ran N min (threshold T)*, whether it failed or not. Write recipients as `user:`, `role:` or `email:` — an entry without a prefix is taken as an e-mail address.

---

## Tips \{#tips\}

- Start with one rule: `failure` and `missed` on every job, to the operations role.
- Prefer roles to named users: the rule follows team changes.
- Use **Send a test** after changing the SMTP account.
- Keep the bell for what needs action; send the rest by e-mail to a shared box.

---

## Nomaflow — Administration
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/administration/

Running Nomaflow on a server: where runs and files are kept, one instance, what happens on restart, run history retention, the run log buffer, who can use the Jobs pages, backup and health.

Nomaflow runs inside the Liberty Next server: its scheduler, its runner and its run history need no separate service.

---

## At a glance

---

## Storage and limits \{#settings\}

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Run history | In the framework's database, five tables: `nomaflow_job_runs`, `nomaflow_step_runs`, `nomaflow_run_logs`, `nomaflow_run_overrides`, `nomaflow_step_run_extras`. The server creates and completes them at start-up. |
| Jobs | The jobs file `plugins/nomaflow/jobs.toml`, next to the configuration folder — edited from the Jobs pages. |
| Run log | The last 5,000 lines of each run are kept. |
| Files | Files uploaded with **Run with parameters** and the reject files of `file_load` steps go to `.nomaflow/files`, next to the configuration. |
| Upload size | 200 MB at most per file. |

---

## One instance \{#one-instance\}

Run **one** Liberty Next instance: the scheduler fires from the server process, with no lock shared between instances, so two instances would run every job twice. See [Production checklist](../installation/production.md#replicas).

---

## Restart \{#restart\}

- Runs in progress when the server stops are closed as **FAILED** with *abandoned: process restart during run* at the next start.
- Scheduled times that fell while the server was down are recorded as **MISSED** — see [Missed schedules](./jobs/schedules.md#missed). They are not run again on their own: run them by hand if needed.
- Jobs, presets and policies are in `jobs.toml`; the history is in the database — both survive the restart.

---

## Run history retention \{#retention\}

The **Run history retention** panel of the Jobs page (labels in English):

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Auto-sweep** | on | The recurring clean-up. |
| **Days kept** | 30 | Finished runs older than this are deleted, with their steps and logs. |
| **Cap per job** | 100 | Each job keeps at most this many recent runs. |
| **Sweep interval (min)** | 60 | How often the clean-up runs. |

**Clean now** runs it at once. The policy is saved in `jobs.toml` under `[meta.retention]`.

---

## Run log \{#run-log\}

Each run collects its log lines in memory — the `liberty.*` loggers, the `nomaflow` lines and the namespaces registered by plugins — and writes them to the database when it ends. The level is the run's: `WARNING`, `INFO` or `DEBUG` (`DEBUG` adds the SQL of every query). The server log receives the same lines.

---

## Who can use Nomaflow \{#permissions\}

The Jobs pages and their API (`/admin/jobs/…`) are reserved to **superusers**. Notifications about jobs reach other users through notification rules — see [Notifications](./notifications.md).

---

## Backup \{#backup\}

`./liberty backup` (Docker) or `liberty-ops backup` (Python) saves the configuration — `jobs.toml` included — and the database that holds the history. See [Operations](../installation/operations.md#backup).

---

## Health \{#health\}

The server's `/ready` answers when the framework database — which holds the history — is reachable. The Jobs page shows the last state of each job; a notification rule on `failure` and `missed` is the simplest monitoring.

---

## Common tasks \{#tasks\}

| Task | How |
|---|---|
| Pause one job | Its **enabled** switch on the Jobs page. |
| Move a job to another server | Carry it in a package — see [Packages](../framework/build/packages.md). The connectors and queries it uses must exist there. |
| Investigate a job without stopping the others | Switch it off, run it by hand at `DEBUG`. |

---
