## NomaUBL — Service and logs
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/monitoring/service-and-logs/

Operate NomaUBL from the host — wrapper status (nomaubl.sh on Linux/macOS, nomaubl.cmd on Windows), the log file for live diagnostics, /api/build-info and /api/license for machine-readable checks. Patterns for external alerting and log forwarding.

The host-side monitoring surface — what an ops engineer / SRE looks at when the web UI isn't enough or when wiring external monitoring. Covers the wrapper's `status` (works the same on Linux / macOS via `nomaubl.sh` and on Windows via `nomaubl.cmd`), the log file's structure, the two HTTP endpoints meant for probes and the patterns to push alerts when something goes wrong.

---

## `status` — the quick health check

```bash title="Linux / macOS"
./nomaubl.sh status
# NomaUBL [demo] is running (PID 12345)
# NomaUBL [uat]  is running (PID 12346)
# NomaUBL [prod] is running (PID 12347)
```

```cmd title="Windows"
nomaubl.cmd status
REM   [demo]  running  (PID 12345)
REM   [uat]   running  (PID 12346)
REM   [prod]  running  (PID 12347)
```

Without arguments, the wrapper lists every `nomaubl-*.pid` file next to the JAR and prints the live state of each. With an environment name, it reports just that one:

```bash title="Linux / macOS"
./nomaubl.sh status prod
# NomaUBL [prod] is running (PID 12347)
```

```cmd title="Windows"
nomaubl.cmd status prod
REM NomaUBL [prod] is running (PID 12347)
```

The wrapper also **prunes stale PID files** — entries for processes that are no longer alive are removed. So a single `status` call cleans up after itself.

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Every named env is running. |
| `1` | At least one env is down. |
| `2` | The named env's PID file doesn't exist *(Linux / macOS)*. |

Useful in scripts and systemd `ExecStartPre`:

```bash title="Linux / macOS"
./nomaubl.sh status prod >/dev/null || { echo "prod is down"; exit 1; }
```

```cmd title="Windows"
nomaubl.cmd status prod >NUL || ( echo prod is down & exit /b 1 )
```

---

## The log file — `nomaubl-<env>.log`

Each environment writes its stderr + stdout to a single log file next to the JAR:

```text title="Linux / macOS"
/opt/nomaubl/
├── nomaubl.jar
├── nomaubl.sh
├── nomaubl-demo.log
├── nomaubl-uat.log
└── nomaubl-prod.log
```

```text title="Windows"
C:\nomaubl\
├── nomaubl-fat.jar
├── nomaubl.cmd
├── nomaubl-demo.log
├── nomaubl-uat.log
└── nomaubl-prod.log
```

Tail it:

```bash title="Linux / macOS"
./nomaubl.sh log demo
# or directly
tail -f /opt/nomaubl/nomaubl-demo.log
```

```cmd title="Windows"
nomaubl.cmd log demo
REM uses PowerShell Get-Content -Wait under the hood
```

### Lines you'll see often

| Line shape | What it means |
|---|---|
| `[INFO] Loaded config: /opt/nomaubl/demo/config/config.json` | Service started, config parsed. |
| `[INFO] Master key file: /opt/nomaubl/demo/.nomaubl-master.key` | The master-key file was found and loaded. |
| `[INFO] Connected to db-nomaubl as nomaubl` | JDBC works. |
| `[INFO] Schema bootstrap: 23 tables created` | First start on an empty schema — F564* tables landed. |
| `[INFO] HTTP server listening on :8090` | Web UI is up. |
| `[INFO] Scheduler started — fetchImportInterval=15min fetchStatusInterval=15min fetchAllInterval=0` | Background scheduler intervals at startup. |
| `[INFO] scheduler tick · fetch-import · 0 invoices to import` | Routine scheduler tick. |
| `[INFO] pa-default API call · import · status 200 · 1.2 s` | One successful PA submission. |
| `[WARN] pa-default API call · import · status 429 · retrying in 30s` | PA rate-limit; will retry. |
| `[ERROR] Connection refused — jdbc:oracle:thin:...` (or `jdbc:postgresql://...`) | Database unreachable — diagnose at the network / DB side. |

The format is line-based, level-prefixed. Easy to grep, easy to ship.

### Common diagnostic flows

| Question | Linux / macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| Did the last scheduler tick run? | `grep "scheduler tick" nomaubl-prod.log \| tail -10` | `Select-String -Path nomaubl-prod.log -Pattern "scheduler tick" \| Select-Object -Last 10` |
| Have there been PA failures recently? | `grep "pa-default" nomaubl-prod.log \| grep -v "status 200"` | `Select-String -Path nomaubl-prod.log -Pattern "pa-default" \| Where-Object { $_ -notmatch "status 200" }` |
| What was the last error? | `grep "\[ERROR\]" nomaubl-prod.log \| tail -1` | `Select-String -Path nomaubl-prod.log -Pattern "\[ERROR\]" \| Select-Object -Last 1` |
| Did the service start cleanly today? | `grep -A 5 "HTTP server listening" nomaubl-prod.log \| tail -10` | `Select-String -Path nomaubl-prod.log -Pattern "HTTP server listening" -Context 0,5 \| Select-Object -Last 10` |

### Verbose mode

Some CLI modes accept `--verbose` to emit per-document lines (one log line per invoice). On heavy nightly batches this is **off by default** to keep the log readable; turn on per-run for investigation.

---

## HTTP endpoints — `/api/build-info` and `/api/license`

The two unauthenticated endpoints meant for machine probes:

### `/api/build-info`

```bash
curl http://localhost:8090/api/build-info
```

```json
{
  "version": "2026.05.26",
  "buildDate": "2026-05-26T14:33:00Z",
  "buildHash": "a8c4d1f2…"
}
```

| Field | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| `version` | Release tag (matches the JAR filename / release notes). |
| `buildDate` | When the JAR was built. |
| `buildHash` | Git short SHA — useful when correlating with a specific deployment. |

Useful for:

- **Post-deploy smoke test** — assert the version matches what you deployed.
- **Liveness probe** — non-200 = service down.
- **Multi-instance audit** — confirm every environment runs the expected version.

### `/api/license`

```bash
curl http://localhost:8090/api/license
```

Sample responses:

```json
{ "mode": "full", "customer": "ACME Corp", "expiresAt": "2026-12-31" }
```

```json
{ "mode": "restricted", "reason": "License expired on 2026-04-30" }
```

```json
{ "mode": "restricted", "reason": "No license configured" }
```

| Field | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| `mode` | `full` (everything works) or `restricted` (limited functionality without a license). |
| `customer` | Subject of the license (only when `mode = full`). |
| `expiresAt` | License expiry date. |
| `reason` | Why the license isn't loaded (only when `mode = restricted`). |

Useful for:

- **Daily license check** — alert when `mode` flips to `restricted` (somebody's license expired or wasn't installed).
- **Pre-deploy validation** — confirm the new env has its license before going live.

### What these endpoints are NOT

| Misconception | Reality |
|---|---|
| `/api/build-info` is a health check. | It returns build metadata, not health state. The HTTP status code (200) is your liveness signal. |
| `/api/license` is rate-limited. | No — poll as often as your probe cadence requires. Each call hits an in-memory cache, not the database. |
| They expose secrets. | No — the build hash + customer name + expiry date are not secrets. No passwords, no tokens. |
| They respect permissions. | No — unauthenticated. Restrict at the reverse proxy if your install is public-facing. |

---

## Scheduler — confirm it's ticking

The background scheduler runs **inside** the `-serve` process; there is no separate scheduler daemon. The [Scheduled jobs](../sync/scheduled-jobs/overview.md) page shows each job with its state, last run, result and next run; from the host, the log file confirms the ticks.

```bash
grep "scheduler tick" /opt/nomaubl/nomaubl-prod.log | tail -10
```

If the last tick was more than `fetchImportInterval + fetchStatusInterval + fetchAllInterval` minutes ago, the scheduler is **probably stuck**. The fixes:

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| No `scheduler tick` lines at all. | Every poll is inactive or its interval is `0`. | Enable the polls on [Scheduled jobs](../sync/scheduled-jobs/overview.md) and set their interval in the job editor. |
| Ticks fire but never advance invoices. | The PA template (`pa-default`) is unreachable — each call times out. | Test from the host: `curl https://<pa-base-url>/api/login_check`. |
| Ticks fire occasionally then stop for hours. | The JVM hit an OOM and the scheduler thread died without restarting the JVM. | Check the log for `OutOfMemoryError`; bump `-Xmx`; consider `Restart=on-failure` in systemd (covered in [Service and systemd](../installation/service-and-systemd.md)). |

### Force a tick from the CLI

When investigating, run the sweep manually:

```bash
./nomaubl.sh fetch-status prod
# → runs one synchronous -fetch-status pass; output goes to stdout
```

Both `fetch-import` and `fetch-status` are safe to run on demand — they're idempotent against the PA.

---

## External monitoring patterns

NomaUBL doesn't export Prometheus metrics or OpenTelemetry traces. The three patterns that cover most real installs:

### Pattern A — Log-based alerting

The single highest-leverage monitoring. Pipe the log file to your central log store (Loki / ELK / Splunk / Datadog Logs / Cloudwatch), then build alerts on log patterns:

| Log pattern | Alert |
|---|---|
| `\[ERROR\]` | Page on-call for any ERROR; throttle to N per hour. |
| `\[WARN\] pa-default .* status 5..` | PA-side failures; page if persistent over 5 minutes. |
| `OutOfMemoryError` | Page immediately. |
| No `scheduler tick` lines for > 30 min | Scheduler is dead. |
| `Connection refused.*jdbc:(oracle\|postgresql)` | Database unreachable. |

```yaml
# Example logrotate + filebeat config snippet
- type: log
  paths:
    - /opt/nomaubl/nomaubl-*.log
  fields:
    service: nomaubl
    env: prod
```

### Pattern B — Endpoint polling

A small cron script that hits both endpoints and pages on failure:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# /usr/local/bin/nomaubl-probe.sh
set -e
for env in demo uat prod; do
  port=$(case "$env" in demo) echo 8090;; uat) echo 8091;; prod) echo 8092;; esac)
  # Liveness
  curl -fsS http://localhost:$port/api/build-info > /dev/null \
    || { echo "[$env] DOWN" | mail -s "NomaUBL $env down" ops@example.com; exit 1; }
  # License
  mode=$(curl -fsS http://localhost:$port/api/license | jq -r '.mode')
  if [ "$mode" != "full" ]; then
    echo "[$env] License mode=$mode" | mail -s "NomaUBL $env license alert" ops@example.com
  fi
done
```

Schedule via systemd timer / cron (Linux / macOS) or Windows Task Scheduler — `*/5 * * * *` (or a `/SC MINUTE /MO 5` task) is a reasonable cadence.

### Pattern C — Host + JVM metrics

For deeper observability:

| Tool | What it captures |
|---|---|
| **`node_exporter`** | Host CPU, memory, disk, network — every running NomaUBL process counts as one Java process. |
| **`process_exporter`** | Per-process CPU / RSS — track each `nomaubl-<env>` separately. |
| **JMX exporter** (Prometheus JVM exporter as a Java agent) | JVM-internal metrics — heap, GC, thread count. Add `-javaagent:/opt/jmx_prometheus_javaagent.jar=9404:config.yml` to the JAR command. |
| **DB exporter** (Oracle exporter, `postgres_exporter`, …) | DB-side metrics — active sessions, top SQL, tablespace usage. |

These four together give 95% of the observability a production install needs. Wire them into the same Prometheus / Grafana stack you already operate.

---

## Log forwarding — keep history off-host

The wrapper writes everything to `nomaubl-<env>.log` next to the JAR. For long-term retention + searchability:

| Setup | What |
|---|---|
| **Filebeat → Logstash / Loki / Cloudwatch** | The standard pattern. One line per JSON record — Filebeat reads, ships, you query in Kibana / Grafana / Cloudwatch Logs Insights. |
| **Vector** | Lighter-weight alternative. |
| **Custom — `journalctl` if running under systemd** | systemd captures stderr / stdout into the journal; `journalctl -u nomaubl@prod` searches it. |
| **`logger` for one-off pipes** | `tail -f nomaubl-prod.log | logger -t nomaubl-prod` sends everything to syslog. |

The server rotates its own log: above the *Log size cap* (100 MB by default) the file is copied to `.1` and truncated in place, and five copies are kept — see [`global → Logs`](../configuration/system/global.md). Identical warnings repeated within the *Log repeat window* are counted rather than written, and the *Log levels* field lowers the volume per module. Logrotate (`copytruncate`, see [Service and systemd](../installation/service-and-systemd.md)) is only needed when the server runs under another launcher. Keep the long-term history in the central log store.

---

## Common ops pitfalls

| Mistake | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Watching the IT dashboard but ignoring the log file. | A scheduler hang shows up in logs hours before the dashboard reflects "no new invoices today". | Wire log-based alerting (Pattern A above). |
| Polling `/api/build-info` every second. | Pointless load + noise in access logs. | 30 s is more than enough. |
| Treating `/api/license` `restricted` mode as a hard failure. | Service still serves licensed features in restricted mode for grace period configurations; alarms wake people up unnecessarily. | Read the `reason` field; alert on `expired` / `revoked`; tolerate `restricted` only when expected. |
| Ignoring `OutOfMemoryError` in the log. | The JVM continues serving but the scheduler thread died — no batch is fired. | Set `Restart=on-failure` in systemd; bump `-Xmx`. |
| Logrotate without `copytruncate`. | The JVM keeps writing to the deleted inode — the new log file stays empty. | `copytruncate` in the logrotate config. |
| No PID file → systemd reports the service as dead while the JVM is actually running. | systemd kills the JVM on the next restart. | Always go through `nomaubl.sh start` (writes the PID file) or set `PIDFile=...` in the systemd unit. |

## NomaUBL — Billing overview
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/billing-overview/

The NomaUBL Billing overview, the landing page: the invoices of the period in amounts (revenue and VAT net of credit notes, invoice count, transmission or acceptance rate) compared with the previous period, twelve months of invoiced amounts, what needs a decision in amounts, and the split per company, per transaction type and the e-reporting position, for sales or purchases.

The **Billing overview** is the page NomaUBL opens on after sign-in. It is written for finance and customer service: the invoices of the period **in amounts**, what became of them, what still **needs a decision**, and where each company stands in e-reporting. Every figure is compared with the previous period. The page reads the NomaUBL database, so it works the same whatever the source system (JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP).

Open it from **Billing overview**, first entry of the Navigation group. The day-to-day work queues are on the [Operations](./dashboard.md) dashboard, the stage-by-stage analysis on [Statistics](./statistics.md).

---

## At a glance

---

## Header \{#header\}

| Control | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Sales / Purchases** | Sales | Switches every figure of the page between the invoices issued and the invoices received. |
| **Period** | This month, or the [default period](../configuration/default-periods.md) set for this view | The [period picker](../configuration/default-periods.md#period-picker): presets, two-month calendar and the date basis. |
| **Date basis** | Document date | *Document date*, *Activity date* or *Archive date*, chosen in the footer of the period picker. |
| **Exclude reviewed errors** | On | Hides the invoices already reviewed by customer service that still sit in an error status. Reviewed invoices in other statuses stay counted. |
| **Compared to …** | — | Shows the previous period used for the changes (see below). Hidden when the period is *All*. |
| **↻** | — | Reloads the page with the same filters. Figures are reused for the [dashboard cache](../configuration/default-periods.md#dashboard-cache) delay (60 minutes unless set); the time they were loaded shows next to it (*Updated 14:05*). |
| **PDF** | — | Key figures, chart and tables in the layout of the [audit report](reports/audit-report.md) (`billing-overview.pdf`). |

The period, the date basis, the switch and the direction are remembered in the browser, so the page opens again as it was left.

### Previous period \{#previous-period\}

The change shown next to each figure compares the period with the one before it, chosen as follows:

| Period | Compared with |
|---|---|
| Starts on 1 January (e.g. *This year*) | The same dates one year earlier. |
| Starts on the 1st of a month (*This month*, *Last month*, *This quarter*…) | The same dates moved back by the length of the period in months: *This month* to date compares with the same days of last month, a whole month with the previous month, a quarter with the previous quarter. |
| Any other period (*Last 7 days*, a custom range…) | The period of the same length just before. |

The [Statistics](./statistics.md) dashboard uses the same rule.

---

## Key figures

| Figure | Value | Sub-line | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Revenue excl. VAT** *(Purchases: Purchases excl. VAT)* | Invoices minus credit notes. | `Invoices … · Credit notes −…` | in % |
| **VAT** | VAT of the invoices minus that of the credit notes. | — | in % |
| **Invoices and credit notes** | Number of documents. | `… invoices · … credit notes` | in % |
| **Transmission rate** *(Purchases: Acceptance rate)* | Share of the invoices transmitted to the customer (accepted, for purchases), counted over the invoices meant for the platform — sent, or held for review; document types not sent to the platform do not lower it. | `… issued · … not issued` (`… accepted`) | in points |

A change is green when it goes up and red when it goes down, followed by the previous value (`vs …`).

---

## Amount invoiced per month

A stacked bar chart of the **last twelve months**, ending with the month of the period end, by what became of the invoice: *Transmitted to the customer* (purchases: *Accepted*), *In progress*, *To correct*, *Refused or disputed*. Credit notes are left out of the chart. The title reads *Amount received excl. VAT per month* for purchases.

---

## What needs a decision

The invoices waiting for someone, **all dates together**, in amounts including VAT. The subtitle gives the total.

| Row | Content | Next step shown |
|---|---|---|
| One row per business-error status (*Disputed*, *Refused*…) | Biggest amount first. | *Decision to take with the customer* |
| **Rejected by the platform** | Status 213. | *Correct, then send again* |
| **To correct before sending** | The other technical-error statuses together. | *A check or the platform import failed* |

Each row gives the amount and the number of invoices; a click opens [E-Invoicing](./invoices.md) filtered on those statuses, over all dates. When nothing waits, the block reads *Nothing awaits a decision.*

---

## Per company, per transaction type, e-reporting

| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| **Per company** | Invoice count, amount excl. VAT and share transmitted (over the invoices meant for the platform), per company. |
| **Per transaction type** | One bar per type with its flow: *B2B national* (e-invoicing), *B2B international* (e-reporting 10.1), *B2C* (e-reporting 10.3), *Other*. National B2B goes through the platform; international B2B and B2C are declared in [e-reporting](./ereporting.md). |
| **E-reporting** *(sales only)* | Per company: the end of the last declared period (or *No declaration yet*), the next period to declare and its status. |

---

## Access \{#access\}

Grant the **Billing overview** page in the Navigation group on the [Roles](../configuration/security/roles.md) page; the server and the AI assistant's `billing_overview` tool check the same grant. Figures follow the companies and the [row filters](../configuration/security/roles.md#row-filters) of the signed-in user's role. It is the default [start page](../configuration/default-periods.md#start-page) after sign-in; under a restricted licence, the application opens on the [Operations](./dashboard.md) dashboard.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Leave *Exclude reviewed errors* on for the monthly review.** The amounts then show only the errors nobody has handled yet.
- **Use *Document date* to reconcile with accounting.** It is the date printed on the invoice, the one the VAT declaration also relies on; *Archive date* matches the processing reports.
- **Start from *What needs a decision*.** A click lands on the invoices concerned, all dates, ready to be handled.
- **Set the opening period once for everyone** under [Default periods](../configuration/default-periods.md) — for example *Last month* for a team that reviews the closed month.
- **Send it by email.** A [daily digest](../sync/scheduled-jobs/daily-digest.md#business-dashboards) can send the page as PDF or Excel — for example on the 1st, last month's overview, as a given role sees it.

## NomaUBL — Operations
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/dashboard/

The NomaUBL Operations dashboard: what the team has to handle on the period, as three work queues (in progress, to correct and send again for IT, a new invoice to issue for customer service), the activity chart, the invoices blocked the longest, the latest events, the top failing rules, the PA round-trip time and the e-reporting coverage, for sales or purchases.

The **Operations** dashboard shows **what the team has to handle** on the period. Its core is three work queues, each with the team it belongs to: what is in progress and needs nothing, what IT must correct and send again, and what customer service must settle by issuing a new invoice. Below them come the activity of the period, the invoices blocked the longest, the latest events and the rules that fail most. Every number is read from the NomaUBL database, whatever the source system (JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP).

Open it from **Operations** in the Navigation group, after the [Billing overview](./billing-overview.md). Under a restricted licence, or for a role without the Billing overview, it is the page the application opens on. The technical health of the server is on the [IT dashboard](./tech-dashboard.md).

---

## At a glance

The page description sums up the period: `… invoices on the period · … approved · … in progress · … to handle`.

---

## Filter bar

| Control | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Sales / Purchases** | Sales | Switches the whole dashboard between issued and received invoices. |
| **Period** | This month, or the [default period](../configuration/default-periods.md) set for *Operations dashboard* | The shared [period picker](../configuration/default-periods.md#period-picker). |
| **Date basis** | Activity date | *Activity date* (last update), *Document date* (BT-2) or *Archive date*, in the footer of the picker. Every block follows it. |
| **Exclude reviewed errors** | On | See below. |
| **↻** | — | Reloads every block. Figures are reused for the [dashboard cache](../configuration/default-periods.md#dashboard-cache) delay (60 minutes unless set); the time they were loaded shows next to it (*Updated 14:05*). |

The filters are kept while the application stays open: leaving the dashboard and coming back finds them as they were.

### Exclude reviewed errors \{#exclude-reviewed\}

The **Exclude reviewed errors** switch hides the invoices that customer service has already reviewed (*Reviewed* in the **Review** column of [E-Invoicing](./invoices.md)) but that still sit in an error status — the `errorTech` / `errorBusiness` groups of the [statuses template](../configuration/system/statuses.md). The queues then show only what is left to handle.

- Reviewed invoices in any other status stay counted, so the totals remain the real number of invoices.
- A click on a queue carries the switch to the [E-Invoicing](./invoices.md#exclude-reviewed) list, so the count on both pages agrees.

---

## Work queues

| Queue | For whom | Rows | Click |
|---|---|---|---|
| **In progress** | *Followed automatically, nothing to do* | *Created, waiting to be sent* · *Sent to the platform* · *Waiting for the platform* · *Being transmitted to the customer* (status groups `created`, `sent`, `pending`, `transmission`) | The invoices of the group. |
| **To correct and send again** | *To be handled by IT* | `213` Rejected, `9905` Validation failed, `9907` PA import failed, then any other technical-error status that has invoices. | The invoices in that status. |
| **A new invoice must be issued** | *To be handled by customer service* | `207` Disputed, `208` Suspended, `210` Refused, then any other business-error status that has invoices. | The invoices in that status. |

Each queue gives its total; the rows split it. A click on the total opens all the invoices of the queue in [E-Invoicing](./invoices.md), a click on a row only that row's (full licence).

---

## Activity chart

**Activity per day** — or **per week** above 62 days, **per month** above 400 days — stacks the invoices of the period as *Approved*, *In progress*, *To correct*, *New invoice to issue* and *Other*. A single slack day or a spike of errors shows at once.

---

## Blocked invoices and latest events

| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| **Blocked the longest** *(oldest first)* | Invoices whose status has not moved for the longest time, with the document triplet (`doc · dct · kco`), the status and the age (*12 days ago*). Empty when every invoice is in a final or transmission status. |
| **Latest events** *(last 10)* | The latest lifecycle events, with the triplet, the status and the time. |

A row opens [E-Invoicing](./invoices.md) on its status.

---

## Rules, round-trip and e-reporting

| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| **Top failing rules** | The validation rules with the most failures on the period, ranked, with their description. Tabs **ALL** / **UBL** (Schematron and XSD) / **INTEG** (lifecycle and runtime errors). *View all errors →* opens [Integration errors](diagnostics/integration-errors.md) grouped by rule; a rule opens its events. |
| **PA round-trip time** *(avg days, sent → status)* | For the invoices sent to the platform, the average number of days until the platform set one of its own statuses. A rise reveals a slowdown on the platform side. |
| **E-Reporting coverage** | The latest report per company and flow, with the number of reports and invoices. *Open page →* opens [E-Reporting](./ereporting.md). |

---

## About this build

The folded **About this build** block at the bottom gives the release, the AFNOR profile and the versions of the shipped Schematrons (see [Schematrons](../references/schematrons.md)).

---

## Access

Grant the **Operations** page in the Navigation group on the [Roles](../configuration/security/roles.md) page. The role sees the whole dashboard or nothing; the [Billing overview](./billing-overview.md) and [Statistics](./statistics.md) are granted apart. Figures follow the companies and the [row filters](../configuration/security/roles.md#row-filters) of the role. Clicks to the invoice list need a full licence.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Read the queues by team.** *In progress* needs nobody; the red queue goes to IT, the orange one to customer service — each team starts from its own.
- **Use *Yesterday* for the morning check.** It covers yesterday and today, so the night batches are counted in full; set it as the [default period](../configuration/default-periods.md) of the view if the team always starts that way.
- **Keep *Exclude reviewed errors* on during the day.** The queues then shrink as customer service marks invoices as reviewed.
- **Top failing rules drives the corrections.** A single rule with hundreds of hits usually points to one upstream change (a renamed field, an outdated tax code); its [Schematron rule](../references/schematrons.md) says exactly what is expected.
- **Investigate elsewhere.** The dashboard spots the problem; the [E-Invoicing](./invoices.md) detail window and the [Integration errors](diagnostics/integration-errors.md) page explain it.

## NomaUBL — IT dashboard
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/tech-dashboard/

The NomaUBL IT dashboard: a health strip (application, database, disk, memory, scheduler, configuration), the four action cards (send failed, waiting for review, to reprocess, to reprocess in full), processing over the last 14 days (volume, errors, retries, time per document), what is running right now, recent errors, and folded technical details (system, filesystem, JVM, configuration check, database tables, links).

The **IT dashboard** is the IT team's view of NomaUBL. It reads top-down like a checklist: **is everything up?** (a health strip), **what is there to do?** (four action cards with their bulk action), **how did processing go over the last 14 days?**, **what is running right now?**, and the **recent errors**. The detailed technical cards — system, filesystem, JVM, configuration check, database tables — are folded at the bottom and open from the health strip. It complements the [Operations](./dashboard.md) dashboard, which follows the invoices rather than the server.

The page applies regardless of source system — JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP. The cards read host-level metrics and the NomaUBL processing log.

---

## Opening the page

- Menu → **Navigation → IT dashboard**, after Operations.

---

## At a glance

A **Refresh** button in the page header reloads every card.

---

## Health strip

The **Is everything up?** strip gives six tiles, each with a green, orange or red dot. A click on a tile scrolls to its detail and, except for *Scheduler*, opens the folded [technical details](#technical-details):

| Tile | Shows | Opens |
|---|---|---|
| **Application** | The release and `up for …`. | System Health |
| **Database** | The ping in ms, or *Unreachable*. | System Health |
| **Disk** | `… % free` on the fullest disk. | Filesystem |
| **Memory** | Heap use in %. | JVM · threads + GC |
| **Scheduler** | *Running*, `… paused` or `… job(s) failed`, and the next run. | The Scheduler card in *Right now* |
| **Configuration** | *No issue* or `… issue(s)`. | Configuration check |

---

## To do

Four cards count the invoices waiting for an IT action, each with a button that handles them all at once through the [shared progress window](#shared-progress-window). The manual one-click retry of *Send failed* and the scheduled overnight sweep of the [Auto-Retry](../sync/scheduled-jobs/auto-retry.md) page call the same replay path.

### Send failed (9904) \{#send-failed\}

A single big-number card showing how many invoices are currently in *Send failed* (status `9904`). When the count is non-zero, a **Resend all N** button below the number replays every matching invoice to the [Plateforme Agréée](../configuration/system/einvoicing.md). Clicking it opens the [shared progress window](#shared-progress-window) — live counters, a *Cancel* button and a *Run in background* button that hides the window while the work keeps going server-side. The resend is throttled at **100 ms per call** so the PA stays inside its rate budget.

| Element | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Count | Live total — refreshed by the page's *Refresh* button and at every dashboard mount. Coloured red when non-zero. |
| **Resend all N** button | Disabled when the count is zero. Click to replay every status-`9904` invoice; opens the progress window. |
| Progress window | Live counters (*processed* / *succeeded* / *failed*), a *Cancel* button and a *Run in background* button — same component as every long-running operation on the platform. |
| Throttle | 100 ms between calls — fixed in code; not operator-tunable here. The [Auto-Retry](../sync/scheduled-jobs/auto-retry.md) schedule exposes its own throttle for the scheduled equivalent. |

Use the manual button for a one-shot replay during business hours (a brief PA outage that cleared, a small batch you want resent now). For unattended overnight retries, schedule a row on the [Auto-Retry](../sync/scheduled-jobs/auto-retry.md) page — same code path, no operator action required.

### Waiting for review \{#waiting-for-review\}

A big-number card that counts the invoices **held before sending** — the ones whose document type carries the `W` (*Waiting*) send flag on the [Document Types](../configuration/system/document-types.md) page. These invoices were generated and validated but deliberately not transmitted, so a user can check them first. When the count is non-zero, a **Send all N** button releases every held invoice to the [Plateforme Agréée](../configuration/system/einvoicing.md) in one action, through the same [progress window](#shared-progress-window) as *Send Failed*. It mirrors the *Send Failed* card — same big number, same one-click bulk action — but for the review queue rather than the failure queue.

### To reprocess \{#to-reprocess\}

A big-number card that counts the invoices **eligible for reprocessing** — those the platform **deposited but did not transmit** (status 200, reason `NON_TRANSMISE`), on a template with **Allow reprocess** enabled. When the count is non-zero, a **Reprocess all N** button **reprints** every eligible invoice from its archived source — readable PDF / XML and UBL file regenerated, no database change, no new validation — through the same [progress window](#shared-progress-window). Reprocessing keeps each invoice's status, records a *Retraitement* history entry and never re-sends to the platform — see [Documents → Allow reprocess](../management/documents.md) for the per-template switch and [Invoices](invoices.md#reprocess) for the same action on selected rows.

### To reprocess in full \{#to-reprocess-full\}

The counterpart of the previous card for **validation-failed** invoices (`9905`) on a template with **Allow full reprocess** enabled. Once the data was corrected at the source, a **Reprocess all N** button reprocesses every eligible invoice **in full** from its archived source: the enrichment is queried again, the UBL regenerated, validated and sent to the PA when the template and document type say so. The status history is kept and a reprocess marker opens a new cycle, so the statuses that follow are recorded as new.

Both cards run **one batch per template**, in the background with its live log: the sources are staged in a working folder, the **Max threads** setting of the global settings bounds the parallelism, and an invoice is never processed twice.

---

## Processing · last 14 days

One card with four tabs: **Volume**, **Errors**, **Retries**, **Time per document**.

### Volume

**Documents processed per day** over the last 14 days, as stacked bars: *Processed* and *In technical error*; the subtitle gives the totals and the time they were loaded. This card is kept on the server for every user for the [dashboard cache](../configuration/default-periods.md#dashboard-cache) delay; **Refresh** reads it again. **Click a bar** to open [E-Invoicing](./invoices.md) on that day, by archive date — a quick path from "today's column is short" to "show me what was processed".

### Errors

The **Error rate · 14d** card: a 14-day sparkline of error events recorded in `F564237` (level `ERROR` or `FATAL`). Hovering a point reveals the day and count; the subtitle shows the daily average plus today's running count.

### Retries

The **Retry rate · 14d** card: a single big number, ratio of *runs that succeeded only after one or more retries* over total runs in the trailing 14 days. The subtitle gives the absolute counts and the delta against the previous 14-day window (green when down, orange when up).

### Time per document

The **Template processing time · 14d** card: average end-to-end processing time per template, in seconds, over the last 14 days. The card pulls flat `START` / `END` events from `F564237` and pairs them in Java keyed on `(FEWDS1|FEUPMJ)` — the prior implementation used a self-join SQL with ambiguous `FETMPL` and incorrect `e.FEUPMT - s.FEUPMT` math, which is now fixed.

#### Per-step breakdown when `debugProfile` is on

When the [`debugProfile`](../configuration/system/global.md) toggle on the `global` template is set to `Y`, every processing run writes one row per pipeline stage to `F564237` — **header parsing**, **lines parsing**, **validation**, **UBL emit**, **PA send**. The Template processing time card surfaces them as a stacked breakdown under the per-template totals, so a slow stage is visible at a glance without digging into the runtime log.

The Live process events tail below also tags the rows with the step name so a slow batch can be triaged in real time. Leave `debugProfile` at `N` in production; flip it to `Y` for the duration of a batch run when triaging a slow pipeline — the extra rows inflate `F564237` quickly under load.

---

## Right now

What is running on the server at this moment: the running processes, the live process events, the scheduler and the active sessions.

### Running processes \{#running-processes\}

The processing JVMs alive on the host, polled every 5 s: those started by this server, with the last line each printed, and the **detached** ones left by a previous instance, a cron or a manual run (*output not captured*). Each row shows the mode (`-process`, `-watch-folders`, `-import`), the arguments, the elapsed time and a **Stop** button, which terminates that JVM and its own child processes only — invoices in progress stay in their current state and input files are left in place. Stopping requires the *integration-run* grant. Nothing is stopped when the server restarts, so a batch can run through an upgrade.

### Live process events

A live feed of jobs starting and finishing in real time — most of them launched by the background scheduler. Polls `F564237` every **5 seconds** with an incremental `since=` cursor; each row carries a coloured **method badge**:

| Badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **START** *(green)* | A job has just started — `fetch-all`, `retrieve-statuses`, an inbound process, etc. |
| **END** *(blue)* | The matching `END` event for a previously-started job, with the elapsed time when available. |
| **ERROR** *(red)* | An inline error emitted while the job ran — `ERROR`, `FATAL`, `FAILED` keywords promote any row to this kind, even when its method was `START` or `END`. |
| **INFO** *(muted)* | Anything else the runtime logger wrote during the job. |

Each row shows the badge, the **template** + **mode** + **source file** when present, the message, and the timestamp. A **pulsing green dot** appears next to the title when an event has been observed in the last 30 seconds (a job is running right now); it switches to grey when the feed has been idle longer.

The feed is **deduplicated on `FEUKID`** so the same row never appears twice across polls, even when the clock jitters. A **Pause / Resume** button on the right of the title freezes polling — useful when reading a long line without it scrolling away.

The scrollable list is capped at the latest 100 events; older rows fall off the bottom as new ones come in. For deeper investigation use the [Processing Log](diagnostics/processing-log.md) page, which keeps the full history with grouped-job views.

### Scheduler

Lists every active scheduler job:

- **Built-ins** — `retrieve-statuses`, `notif-purge`, `clean-archive`, etc. — driven by `BackgroundScheduler` polling intervals.
- **Per-template `fetch-all`** — one row per template that has a scheduled extract / sync.
- **Per-row Auto-Retry sweeps** — one row per saved entry on the [Auto-Retry](../sync/scheduled-jobs/auto-retry.md) page, with the scheduled hour and the matched status list as the cadence.
- **Daily lifecycle checks** — one row per scheduled entry on the [Lifecycle checks](../sync/scheduled-jobs/lifecycle-checks.md) page, next to the digests and auto-retries, with its time and last run.

Each row shows the job name, the cadence, and a status pill (green active, blue scheduled-soon, orange paused). The card subtitle reports the active count; the **Open Scheduled jobs** button opens [Scheduled jobs](../sync/scheduled-jobs/overview.md), where every job is run, paused and edited.

The **PA import poll** and **PA status retrieve** jobs carry a **pause / resume** button — effective on the next tick and deliberately runtime-only, so a server restart always resumes and a pause can't be forgotten. The [daily quiet window](../configuration/system/global.md) (`fetchQuietFrom` / `fetchQuietTo`) is shown here too, highlighted while active — during it both pollers skip their runs automatically.

### Active sessions / Active clients · 15m

Two modes:

- **Auth enabled** — title reads *Active sessions*. Lists every session present in `F564252` whose `SSETDTIM` is within the last hour.
- **Auth disabled** — title reads *Active clients · 15m*. Lists every IP touched by `WebServer.handle()` in the last 15 minutes, sourced from the new in-memory `ActivityTracker` (no `F564252` rows exist when auth is off).

Either way, each row shows IP / user, the last-seen timestamp, and the running hit count.

---

## Recent errors

The **Recent errors** card lists the last 8 events from `F564237` filtered on `level IN ('ERROR', 'FATAL')`. Each row shows the level badge, the lifecycle code and triplet, the message, and a relative timestamp (*2m ago*, *1h ago*). Clicking a row tied to an invoice opens the *Integration Errors* view of [Diagnostics](./diagnostics/overview.md) narrowed to that invoice; a processing row opens the *Processing Log* view. **Open Integration Errors →** opens the view unfiltered.

---

## Technical details \{#technical-details\}

A folded section — *system, filesystem, JVM, configuration check, database tables, links* — that opens by itself when a tile of the health strip is clicked.

### System Health

JVM, database and host metrics. The most-watched values are colour-coded:

| Stat | Source | Tone rules |
|---|---|---|
| **Java** | `Runtime.version()` | neutral. |
| **Heap** | `MemoryMXBean.getHeapMemoryUsage()` | green &lt; 60 %, orange &lt; 85 %, red ≥ 85 %. |
| **Uptime** | `RuntimeMXBean.getUptime()` | neutral, formatted as `Xd Yh` / `Xh Ym`. |
| **CPU cores** | `Runtime.availableProcessors()` | neutral. |
| **Database** | `dialect.ping()` | green &lt; 100 ms, orange &lt; 500 ms, red beyond or on error. |
| **Schema** | `db-nomaubl` config | neutral. |
| **OS** | `os.name` + `os.arch` | neutral. |
| **PA mode** | `paUseMock` flag | green when *Live*, orange when *Mock*. |

The card subtitle on the right shows the **build version + build date** baked into `nomaubl-version.properties`.

### Quick links

Static shortcut list — the IT operator's most-used pages, opened directly: **Processing Log** and **Integration Errors** (both views of [Diagnostics](./diagnostics/overview.md)), **Notifications**, **Process Document**, **File Versions** and **Settings**.

### Filesystem

For each configured path (`appHome`, `processHome`, `dirInput`, `singleOutput`, `burstOutput`, `dirArchive`, `dirError`):

- **Free / total** disk space on the underlying volume.
- **File count** of a recursive walk through the path, **capped at 5000 files** to keep the call cheap.

Path values that contain runtime placeholders (`%TEMPLATE%`, `%FILE_NAME%`) are truncated at the first placeholder, and the report runs against the deepest **existing-by-shape** directory above it. `dirOutput` is excluded because it is always covered by `processHome`.

### JVM · threads + GC

Companion card to System Health for deeper JVM diagnostics:

- **Threads** — current count + peak.
- **Daemon threads** — running daemons.
- **GC** — collector name + total time spent in GC.
- **Loaded classes** — class-loader counter, useful for spotting metaspace leaks.

### Configuration check

Validates the *connector-style* configuration the application uses today. Issues are listed by area with severity (red error, orange warning, blue info). The check runs against:

| Area | Validates |
|---|---|
| **PA connector** | `baseUrl`; `authType`; credentials per auth type — `OAUTH2` (clientId/secret/token endpoint), `BASIC` (username/password), `BEARER` (token); presence of an endpoint named `import` (warns when `import-status` is missing). |
| **e-Directory** | `baseUrl` and `directory-check` endpoint when `checkDirectory=Y`. |
| **e-Reporting** | `issuerSiren`, `frequency`, `flux` when `sendToPA=Y`. |
| **Statuses** | Every PA status code received but not mapped in the [status catalogue](../configuration/system/statuses.md): the warning gives the number of events skipped since the server started and an example invoice. Add the code to the catalogue to record these events. |

The validation assets (XSD / Schematron) are bundled in the JAR.

A clean check renders as `✔ 0 issues` in green; otherwise the card lists the issues in order of severity.

### Database tables

Per-table row count for every NomaUBL table — invoices (`F564231`), lifecycle (`F564235`), validation (`F564236`), runtime log (`F564237`), notifications (`F564253`), e-Reporting (`F564260`–`F564262`), auth (`F564250`–`F564252`, `F564254`). Useful for spotting unexpected growth (e.g. a notifications table that should be ~hundreds of rows but holds millions).

---

## Shared progress window \{#shared-progress-window\}

Every long-running operation in the platform — Resend All from this page, the [Auto-Retry](../sync/scheduled-jobs/auto-retry.md) sweep, the *Detailed view* export on [Integration Errors](diagnostics/integration-errors.md), the upcoming bulk re-imports — opens the **same modal**. One component, one set of habits.

The window stays open by default while the operation runs; closing it is a deliberate action.

| Element | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Progress bar** | Visual counter of processed-vs-total. Updates every ~250 ms as the server pushes increments. |
| **Live counters** | Three numbers: *Processed* (total touched so far), *Succeeded*, *Failed*. Each is clickable when non-zero and opens a small drawer with the per-invoice triplets, so a failure on invoice `12345 / RI / 00070` is one click away from its log entry. |
| **Cancel** | Stops the operation cleanly between two invoices. Already-processed invoices keep their new state; the rest are left untouched. The button is replaced by *Cancelled* (greyed) once the signal lands. |
| **Run in background** | Hides the modal without stopping the operation. The work continues server-side; a small persistent banner at the top of the page surfaces the count + a *Show progress* link. Click the link to reopen the modal at any time. |
| **Done** | Replaces *Cancel* / *Run in background* when the operation finishes. A summary line shows total / succeeded / failed and the elapsed time. |

Multiple operations can run side by side — each gets its own banner when sent to the background. Closing the browser tab does **not** cancel the work; the server-side run keeps going. Reopening the page surfaces the banner again until the run completes.
---

## How widgets refresh

The Refresh button (or page mount) calls four endpoints in parallel:

| Endpoint | Feeds |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/system` | System Health, JVM extras, Filesystem |
| `GET /api/dashboard/tech` | Volume, Errors, Retries, Time per document, Active sessions, Database tables, Recent errors |
| `GET /api/dashboard/log-tail` | Live process events (incremental, polled every 5 s with `since=`) |
| `GET /api/dashboard/config-check` | Configuration check |

The Scheduler card reads `GET /api/scheduler/status`. Each call fails independently — a misconfigured database returns *Not configured* on the data card without breaking System Health or the live tail.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Watch Heap, Database ping and Filesystem free space.** The three early-warning signals — heap drift before an OOM, database latency before a stall, archive volume before disk fills.
- **Live process events beats `tail -f`.** It shows scheduler jobs starting and ending in real time, errors stand out in red, and the feed survives an SSH disconnect. Keep it open during a release window or a batch import — most regressions surface here within seconds, and the green pulsing dot tells you whether anything is actually running right now.
- **Configuration check should always read green.** A non-zero issue count after a deploy is the fastest path to "what changed". Run it on every environment after every config edit.
- **Recent errors over Database tables.** When triaging an incident the recent-errors feed is denser per pixel; the table stats card is for trend-watching across days.
- **Empty Active clients does not mean nobody is using the app.** With auth enabled, sessions older than an hour drop off the list — the database lifecycle still records them. The card shows *who is on right now*, not *who was on this morning*.
- **Processing-time spikes pair with volume dips.** When you see a tall bar in the Volume tab followed by a slow template the next day, expect the queue to back up — the IT team can pre-empt by adjusting the scheduler cadence.

---

## NomaUBL — Statistics
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/statistics/

The NomaUBL Statistics dashboard: where the invoices of the period stand in five stages, how they flowed over the period, how long the open ones have waited, the statuses and most frequent reasons, splits per transaction type and activity code, and a detail table by activity, status and reason, all compared with the previous period, with Excel and PDF exports.

The **Statistics** dashboard answers three questions about the invoices of the period: **where do they stand**, **how did they flow**, and **how long have the open ones been waiting**. Each figure is compared with the previous period, and every bar or row opens the invoices behind it. It also holds the detail table by activity code, status and reason. The dashboard reads the NomaUBL database, whatever the source system (JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP).

Open it from **Statistics** in the Navigation group, after the [IT dashboard](./tech-dashboard.md).

---

## At a glance

---

## Header

The header is the same as on the [Billing overview](./billing-overview.md#header): **Sales / Purchases**, the [period picker](../configuration/default-periods.md#period-picker) (date basis *Document date* by default, also *Activity date* or *Archive date*), **Exclude reviewed errors** (on by default) the *Compared to …* tag and **↻** to reload — figures are kept for the [dashboard cache](../configuration/default-periods.md#dashboard-cache) delay, with their load time (*Updated 14:05*). The previous period follows the [same rule](./billing-overview.md#previous-period). Two buttons export the whole page:

| Button | Content |
|---|---|
| **Excel** | One sheet per block: *Stages*, *Statuses*, *Trend*, *Waiting time*, *Transaction types*, *Activities*, *Reasons*, *Pivot*, and a *Data* sheet with the invoices behind them. |
| **PDF** | Key figures, stages, trend, waiting time, statuses, types, activities, the detail table and reasons. |

---

## Key figures

| Figure | Value | Change |
|---|---|---|
| **Invoices issued** *(Purchases: Invoices received)* | Number of invoices, with the amount excl. VAT below. | in % |
| **Reached the platform** *(Purchases: Integrated)* | Share of the invoices *At the platform* or *Completed*, over the invoices meant for the platform (sent, or held for review), as on the Billing overview. | in points |
| **To handle** | *To correct* + *Decision needed*, shown in red when above zero. | in %, a decrease counts as good |
| **Open for more than 7 days** | Invoices not completed whose last status change is more than 7 days old, out of the open ones. | — |

---

## Stages \{#stages\}

Every status belongs to one of **five stages**, the same as the [status by stage](./invoices.md#status-by-stage) filter of E-Invoicing:

| Stage | Statuses |
|---|---|
| **To correct** | Technical errors: 213 Rejected, 9904 Send failed, 9905 Validation failed, 9907 PA import failed, 9909 PA export failed. |
| **Decision needed** | Business errors: 206, 207, 208, 210, 221, 501, 600. |
| **Processing** | Created, sent or pending in NomaUBL: 9900, 9901, 9902, 9903, 9906, 9912. |
| **At the platform** | Being transmitted by the platform: 201, 202, 203, 204, 214, 224, 225, 226, 227, 9911, 9913. |
| **Completed** | Final or approved statuses: 200, 205, 209, 211, 212, 220, 228, 9908, 9914. |

An **Other** stage appears only when a status outside these groups has invoices. The groups come from the [statuses template](../configuration/system/statuses.md).

The **Where the invoices stand** block shows a strip of the five stages, then one button per stage with its count, its share and the change from the previous period. A button opens [E-Invoicing](./invoices.md) on the statuses of that stage.

---

## Trend and waiting time

| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| **Invoices by stage over the period** | Stacked bars by stage, **per day** up to 35 days, **per week** up to 120 days, **per month** beyond. With *All*, the last twelve months. A bar opens the invoices of that bucket and stage. |
| **Open invoices by waiting time** | The invoices not completed, by days since their last status change: `≤ 1 day`, `2–3 days`, `4–7 days`, `8–30 days`, `> 30 days`, stacked by the four open stages. |

---

## Statuses, reasons and splits

| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| **Statuses** | One row per status: label, code, bar, count, share of the period and change. A row opens the invoices in that status. |
| **Most frequent reasons** | The eight reasons recorded most often on the invoices of the period, each with its main status. |
| **Per transaction type** / **Per activity code** | A stacked bar by stage for each transaction type and for the eight main activity codes. |

---

## Detail by activity, status and reason \{#detail-table\}

A ready-made pivot of the invoices: rows by **activity code → status → reason code**, one column per **transaction type** (`B2B`, `B2BINT`, `B2C`, `B2G`). Every value carries its share of the level above — a reason as a share of its status, a status as a share of its activity, an activity as a share of the whole.

| Control | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Group by** | *Activity code*, *Status*, *Reason code*, in any combination; at least one stays on. Expansion, shares and export follow the grouping. |
| **Measure** | *Invoice count* (default) or *Net amount* (BT-109). A handful of invoices can carry most of the money. |
| **Excel** | This table as shown, with the rows behind it (`statistics-count.xlsx` or `statistics-amount.xlsx`). |

Rows expand and collapse with subtotals at every level; a status with a single reason shows as one compact line.

---

## Access

Grant the **Statistics** page in the Navigation group on the [Roles](../configuration/security/roles.md) page; the server and the AI assistant's `status_statistics` tool check the same grant. Figures follow the companies and the [row filters](../configuration/security/roles.md#row-filters) of the signed-in user's role.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Watch *Open for more than 7 days*.** It is the backlog nobody moves; the waiting-time block shows at which stage it is stuck.
- **Compare like with like.** *This month* is compared with the whole previous month, *This year* with the same dates a year earlier — pick the period accordingly before reading the changes.
- **Switch the detail table to *Net amount*** before a meeting with finance: the ranking of activities often changes.
- **Build a recurring report in the [Explorer](./explorer.md)** when a breakdown is needed that the page does not offer; the ready-made *Status statistics* analysis is a good starting point.
- **Send it by email.** A [daily digest](../sync/scheduled-jobs/daily-digest.md#business-dashboards) can send the page as PDF or Excel, over last month or the month to date, as a given role sees it.

## NomaUBL — E-Invoicing
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/invoices/

The day-to-day NomaUBL invoice list — search, filter and inspect every invoice; open a detail view to consult parties, lines, VAT, lifecycle and PDF; edit, copy, resend or e-mail invoices; manually set a status.

The **E-Invoicing** screen is the central operational page of NomaUBL — the official entry point for the *Réforme de la Facturation Électronique* (RFE) workflow. It lists every invoice the platform has processed, with rich filters, a status-driven detail view, and the actions a user needs day to day: edit, copy, delete, manually set a status, e-mail the PDF to the customer, resend to the Plateforme Agréée.

The page applies regardless of source system — JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP. Every record visible here was persisted in the local NomaUBL database after going through the processing pipeline.

---

## At a glance

---

## Toolbar

Above the grid, two rows: the **period**, the **direction**, **Exclude reviewed errors** and, at the right, **+ New Invoice**; then the **status by stage**. **+ New Invoice** is shown to the roles allowed to create invoices (`invoice.create`), which opens the [Create / Edit invoice modal](#create-invoice). The [Advanced Filters](#advanced-filters) panel and the grid toolbar (search, **Run**, bulk actions) follow.

### Period

The shared [period picker](../configuration/default-periods.md#period-picker): presets, two-month calendar, and the date basis in its footer. The list opens on *This month*, or on the [default period](../configuration/default-periods.md#default-periods) set for the *Invoices* view. A list opened from a dashboard or a VAT drill-down takes the dates of that page.

### Date basis \{#date-basis\}

The footer of the period picker chooses **which date column the period is read against**.

| Value | Date column | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| **Update date** *(default)* | The last time the invoice was modified in NomaUBL. | Day-to-day operations. |
| **Issue date** | The date printed on the invoice itself (BT-2 from the UBL). | Reconciling against the [VAT Declaration](./vat-declaration.md) page or any external system that keys off the issue date. |
| **Archive date** | The date the document was processed into the archive. | Reconciling against the [IT dashboard](./tech-dashboard.md) and the processing reports. |

The choice is **remembered for the current session**. It is also **set automatically** when the list is opened from a dashboard or a VAT drill-down, so the count on E-Invoicing matches the count you came from.

### Direction \{#direction-chip\}

A selector next to the period: **Issued (sales)** *(default)*, **Received (purchases)**, or **All directions**.

| Value | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Issued (sales)** | Only the invoices sent to customers (`UHDRIN = '2'`). |
| **Received (purchases)** | Only the supplier invoices pulled from the PA (see [Sync → Fetch Input → PA inbound](../sync/fetch-input.md) and the bundled `received-ubl` document). |
| **All directions** | No direction filter — both are listed. |

The selector resolves against the `UHDRIN` flag stored on each row — a template's *Direction* change does not re-classify historical rows, so the result is stable over time.

On a *Received* row the **Counterparty** column reads from `AccountingSupplierParty` (the supplier), not from `AccountingCustomerParty` — so the column shows the supplier name on inbound invoices and the customer name on outbound ones. The status workflow, the detail modal and the column catalog are otherwise identical; only the emit-only seller actions (Resend to PA, Send completed, Credit note…) are hidden on received-direction rows.

### Exclude reviewed errors \{#exclude-reviewed\}

The **Exclude reviewed errors** switch, next to the direction selector, hides the rows already marked *Reviewed* that still sit in an error status (`errorTech` / `errorBusiness` groups of the [statuses template](../configuration/system/statuses.md)), so the list keeps only the errors nobody has looked at yet. Reviewed rows in any other status stay listed. The switch is on by default; a list opened from a dashboard ([Billing overview](./billing-overview.md), [Statistics](./statistics.md), [Operations](./dashboard.md#exclude-reviewed)) takes the dashboard's choice. The `GET /api/invoices` endpoint takes the same filter as `excludeReviewedErrors=true`.

### Status by stage \{#status-by-stage\}

The **Status** row groups the statuses of the period into the five stages of the [Statistics](./statistics.md#stages) dashboard — **To correct**, **Decision needed**, **Processing**, **At the platform**, **Completed** — plus **Other** when a status outside these groups has invoices or is selected. Each stage is a pill with its colour and count.

| Gesture | Effect |
|---|---|
| Click on the stage name | Selects every status of the stage (*Show only this stage*); a second click shows every status again. |
| Click on the caret **▾** | Opens *Choose statuses*: a checkbox for the whole stage (all, none or partial) and one per status, with its colour, label and count, biggest first. |
| Partial selection | The count reads `picked / total` and the pill gets a dashed border. |
| **✕ Clear filters** | Appears when a status is selected; clears the selection. |

A stage with no invoice on the period is greyed out. A dashboard click (a queue, a stage, a status) lands on the list with the matching statuses already picked.

### Advanced Filters \{#advanced-filters\}

A collapsible **Advanced Filters** panel sits below the status row. It offers one row per filterable column of the active [List Views](../configuration/list-views.md) spec — by default *DOC*, *DCT*, *Company*, *Party Number*, *Party Name*, *Bar code*, *Review*, *Status*, *Invoice type*, *Activity code*, *Reason code* — with a per-column operator picker (`contains`, `equals`, `≠`, `<`, `≤`, `>`, `≥`, `between`, `empty`, `not empty`). Edits stay as a draft until **Run** commits them, so typing in the panel does not spam the back-end.

:::info[How the text filters match]
A text filter matches from the **start** of the value and uses the column's index, so the list stays fast on a large table. To search for text anywhere in the value, wrap it in percent signs — `%acme%` matches *acme* wherever it appears, at the cost of a full scan. The **DOC** filter takes a shortcut: an all-digits value seeks the document number directly rather than scanning. Filters on columns backed by a reference list (status, routing…) accept **several values at once** — pick more than one and the list shows rows matching any of them.
:::

The set of columns that can be filtered is defined in the spec's `filter: true` allow-list — operators decide which columns they actually query and trim the rest from the panel without losing them from the grid. See [List Views](../configuration/list-views.md) for the editor.

The page runs in **hybrid client-side mode**: each *Run* loads one capped slice from the server (`spec.maxRows`, the *Rows loaded* of [Settings › Navigation & lists](../configuration/default-periods.md#lists) unless the view sets its own — 100 000 by default) and the grid handles filter / sort / paginate / group within that slice — no roundtrip while typing in the per-column filter row, filters survive pagination naturally. When the slice cap is hit, an `X / Y rows` notice next to *Run* tells the operator to narrow the period or the *Advanced Filters*.

RefList columns (Status, eReporting Status, custom lists) get a **multi-select picker** in both the Advanced Filters panel and the per-column filter row — pick any number of codes, the trigger shows `N selected` past the inline cap, and a `✕` on the right resets the selection in one click. The server applies an `IN (?,?,?)` clause so picking three statuses returns the union. A code can also be typed in the search box of the picker (Enter, comma-separated for several), so a list that is incomplete or still empty still filters.

### Grid toolbar

Next to the search box of the grid: **Run** (reloads the list with the current filters), then **Resend selected (N)**, **Reprocess selected (N)** and **Mark reviewed (N)** when rows are ticked (see [Bulk resend](#bulk-resend), [Reprocess](#reprocess) and [Mark reviewed](#mark-reviewed)).

---

## Invoice list

The table shows one row per invoice. Default sort: most recent document number first. Click any column header to sort by that column.

The grid renders through **DataTableV2** in spec-driven mode: column shape, labels, format, alignment, width and the filter-row allow-list come from the `view.invoices` spec stored on `db-nomaubl` (with a bundled default in the JAR). Adding or removing columns is done from the [List Views](../configuration/list-views.md) editor — no code change required when the column already lives in the catalog.

The **Updated** value carries the time of day, so an *Updated* column formatted as `datetime` in the spec shows `2026-09-15 15:23:45` rather than the bare date. (The issue date stays date-only — JDE stores no time for it.)

### Default columns

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| **Doc** | Internal document number. |
| **Dct** | Document type. |
| **Kco** | Company code. |
| **UBL number** | The invoice number as it appears in the generated UBL document. Filterable from the **Advanced Filters** panel and via the `?ublNumber=` query parameter, on top of the free-text search box. |
| **Issue date** | BT-2 from the UBL. |
| **Customer** | Buyer party name. |
| **Country** | ISO 3166 two-letter code of the counterparty (`FR`, `DE`, `BE`, `US`…). Captured at insert from the UBL — buyer country on sales, supplier country on purchases. Drives the country-group classification used by the [VAT Declaration](./vat-declaration.md) page. |
| **Total HT** | Total amount excluding VAT. |
| **Total TTC** | Total amount including VAT. |
| **Currency** | ISO 4217 code. |
| **Status** | Status badge — code + label, coloured by family. |
| **Send to PA** | Destination of the invoice: *For the platform*, *Not for the platform* or *Held for review before sending* (`list-send-pa`), filterable. |
| **Review** | Coloured **review badge** — *Pending* (awaiting customer service) or *Reviewed*. Lit up when the row needs operator attention — a status the dispatcher could not auto-resolve, a manual edit flagged on save, or a downstream system marking the row for re-check. It also lights up for an invoice **Deposited (200) with reason `NON_TRANSMISE`**: not an error, but the recipient has no active reception address, so the operator must forward it manually — other 200s keep a quiet dash. An invoice **corrected by hand** — saved from the invoice window or repaired with *Fix buyer* — is flagged *Reviewed* as soon as the validation that follows raises no error, whatever its status. Empty when nothing is pending: a few badges in an otherwise clear page tell you exactly where to start. |

A page-size selector at the bottom defaults to 50 rows per page; values up to 500 are accepted. The total count of matching invoices is shown next to the pagination controls.

### Catalog columns

The Invoices view's SQL now joins `F564231` (UH) and `F564230` (FE) on doc / dct / kco via a `LEFT JOIN`, so the column catalog exposes 16 additional archive / log columns. Any of them can be added to the spec via the [List Views](../configuration/list-views.md) editor's `+ Add column` picker — the `LEFT JOIN` keeps invoice rows when no log entry exists.

| Catalog column | What it carries |
|---|---|
| `logSourceFile` | Name of the source file that produced the invoice. |
| `logActivityCode` / `logSubType` | Activity code and sub-type recorded at ingestion. |
| `logAlphaKey` | Alpha-key alias used by some upstream systems. |
| `logAmount` | Amount carried by the log row (raw, no currency rebase). |
| `logInvoiceDate` / `logDueDate` | Invoice date and due date recorded at ingestion. |
| `logCreated` | Creation timestamp (`UPMJ + UPMT` composite). |
| `logUser` / `logJobn` / `logPid` / `logVersion` | JDE user, job, PID and version stamps. |
| `logBusinessUnit` | Business unit recorded at ingestion. |
| `logRouting` | BAR routing recorded at ingestion. |
| `logSendToPaFlag` | Flag captured at ingestion telling whether the row was eligible for PA submission. |
| `logPaUuid` | PA-side UUID assigned to the invoice at submission time. |

### Click-through

Clicking any row opens the **Detail modal** for that invoice. Most actions are per-invoice, but the list also supports a **bulk resend** — see below.

### Mark reviewed \{#mark-reviewed\}

Customer service marks the invoices in error it has handled as **reviewed**, so they leave the error counts and lists while *Exclude reviewed errors* is on. The invoice keeps its status.

- **From the list** — tick the invoices, then **Mark reviewed (N)**. The button shows when at least one ticked invoice is in error and not yet reviewed. A confirmation says that *the selected invoice(s) will be considered handled and will no longer appear among the errors to handle*; only invoices still in error are marked.
- **From the invoice window** — the **Reviewed** chip at the right of the tabs sets the mark (dashed when not set) or clears it (green when set), each time after a confirmation. Clearing brings the invoice back among the errors to handle.

Both require the *Mark reviewed* action (`invoice.review`) on the [Roles](../configuration/security/roles.md) page. The mark is the **Review** column (`UHALRTPSD`).

### Bulk resend \{#bulk-resend\}

Each row carries a **checkbox**, and a **Resend selected (N)** button appears in the toolbar once at least one row is ticked. It resends the whole batch to the [Plateforme Agréée](../configuration/system/einvoicing.md) in one action, through the same progress window used elsewhere (live counters, *Cancel*, *Run in background*). Only invoices that may actually be sent are selectable — rows whose document type is set to *Do not send* are disabled, so a non-transmissible invoice can't be swept into a batch by mistake. For the same reason, the per-invoice **Resend** action is hidden on *Do not send* rows.

### Reprocess \{#reprocess\}

A **Reprocess selected (N)** button appears next to *Resend selected* when the ticked rows include invoices eligible for reprocessing. Reprocessing is a **reprint**: for an invoice the platform **deposited but did not transmit** (status 200, reason `NON_TRANSMISE`), it regenerates the readable PDF / XML and the UBL file from the JDE XML source archived at first submission, into the output and burst folders. Nothing changes in the database and the UBL is not validated again — the stored e-invoice, including a later *Fix buyer* correction, stays the reference, and its validation results are kept. The invoice keeps its current status, a *Retraitement* entry is added to its history, nothing is re-sent to the platform, and each invoice is reprocessed only once. Only invoices on a template with **Allow reprocess** enabled (an XML-source template — see [Documents](../management/documents.md)) are eligible; the others are ignored in the selection. The same run is available from the [IT dashboard](tech-dashboard.md#to-reprocess) and the command line.

The selection also covers **validation failures**: an invoice in *Validation failed* (`9905`) on a template with **Allow full reprocess** enabled is **reprocessed in full** — enrichment queried again, UBL regenerated, validated and sent to the PA when the template and document type say so; the history is kept and a new cycle starts. The confirmation states which invoices are reprinted and which are reprocessed in full. The invoice window offers the same full reprocess through a **Reprocess** button on a `9905`.

Several invoices are reprocessed as **one batch per template**, in the background with its live log: their sources are staged in a working folder, the *Max threads* global setting bounds the parallelism and an invoice is never processed twice. A single invoice still runs on its own.

### Export

A small **Export** button in the toolbar exports the current view (filters applied) as a CSV file named `invoices.csv`.

---

## Detail modal

Clicking a row opens a modal with seven tabs along the top: **Summary**, **Parties**, **Lines**, **VAT**, **Notes**, **History**, **PDF**. The modal title shows the invoice's `DOC / DCT / KCO` triplet. At the right of the tabs, the **Reviewed** chip sets or clears the [review mark](#mark-reviewed) of an invoice in error. A **fullscreen toggle** in the header switches between a windowed and a full-screen view.

**Previous / next arrows** (and the ← → keys) in the header move through the invoices of the list without closing the window — the same order and filters as the table on screen — with a position indicator (e.g. `3 / 50`). Past the last invoice, navigation loops back to the first.

  
    12345 / RI / 00070
    ⛶ ✕
  
  
    Summary
    Parties
    Lines (8)
    VAT
    Notes 3
    History (5)
    PDF
  
  Tab content — depends on the active tab

### Summary tab *(default)*

The Summary tab shows a coloured **status badge** at the top — with, under it, the status details and the **Rule set** the invoice was produced under (see [Rule sets](../ubl-tools/rule-sets.md)) — followed by **action buttons** (Edit UBL, Copy, Delete) on the right. **Delete** removes the invoice and every related record — log row (source XML, PA transaction reference, source file name), lifecycle, lines, VAT and validation — so a later run of the same document starts fresh and the [watched folders](../management/watched-folders.md) can pick its source file up again. Deletion follows the same protection as *Fix buyer*: the button is hidden once the PA has processed the invoice, except for a **213** rejection with an addressing reason. Right under the badge, when the platform returned them, the current **rejection reason**, **expected action** and **status note** are shown inline, and the full **status message** sits in a collapsed group — expand it for the platform's long error text. The same values feed the custom actions as `{message}`, `{reasonLabel}`, `{actionLabel}` and `{actionNote}` placeholders (see [Actions](../management/actions.md#custom-actions)), with no list-view column needed.

#### Fix buyer \{#fix-buyer\}

The most frequent PA rejections are about the **buyer's identifiers** — SIREN (BT-47), SIRET (BT-46), intra-community VAT (BT-48) and electronic address (BT-49). A **Fix buyer** button opens a compact form pre-filled from the stored UBL, with the [INSEE company search](./edirectory.md) and the PPF electronic-address picker, to correct just those fields without re-editing the whole invoice. Only the changed identifiers are replaced inside the stored UBL — the rest of the document stays untouched — then the invoice is **revalidated on the spot**, an audit event records the old and new values in the history, and an option **resends to the PA** when validation passes. The button appears only while the invoice is still correctable — before the PA has taken it over, or when it was **Rejected (213) for an addressing reason**: `ADR_ERR`, `REJ_ADR` (the platform's addressing control) or `DEST_INC` (recipient unknown in the directory). In those three cases the invoice never reached the customer, which makes the resend safe; every other PA-processed status stays locked. A repair whose validation raises no error also marks the invoice *Reviewed* in the list. The buyer electronic address (BT-49) keeps the scheme already on the document — `0225` when there is none. The correction is logged as a plain history entry (*Identifiants acheteur corrigés*), without triggering the notification rule of the current status again, and the outcome of the new validation (`9901` / `9902`) is added to the history whenever it differs from the latest event. The keys stored on the row when the document was first processed (alpha key, customer number, business unit, routing code) are kept; the same applies to a save from the edit window. Format safeguards (SIREN/SIRET length and coherence, VAT shape) and the PA-protection rule apply — the same checks as the `POST /api/invoices/{doc}/{dct}/{kco}/fix-buyer` endpoint in the [API reference](/nomaubl/api-reference).

Below the status, when the invoice is in a status that requires a follow-up action by the seller (e.g. `205`, `206`, `207`, `208`, `210`, `213`, `9904`, `9907`), a blue **Seller actions** banner appears with the recommended actions:

  Seller actions
  
    Mark payment received
    Issue credit note
    Cancel accounting
    Issue corrected invoice
  

Status-by-status mapping:

| Status | Suggested actions |
|---|---|
| **205** Paid | *Mark payment received* |
| **206** Partially approved / **207** Disputed | *Issue credit note*, *Issue corrected invoice* |
| **208** Suspended | *Send completed* |
| **210** Refused | *Cancel accounting* |
| **213** Rejected | *Cancel accounting*, *Issue new invoice* |
| **9904** Send error / **9907** PA rejected | *Resend to PA* |

Each action is bound to an *API connector endpoint* configured in *Configuration → API Connectors* — clicking the button executes the connector with the invoice's data. Greyed-out actions (faded) indicate the connector is not configured for this deployment.

A second group sits below the regulatory one — **Custom actions**. Always-visible buttons configured on the [Actions](../management/actions.md#custom-actions) page; each fires its own chain of connector calls and is independent of the invoice's current status. The result banner is anchored to the group whose button fired — a custom-action failure does not stomp on a regulatory-action banner shown at the same time, and stale banners are cleared automatically when the modal closes or switches invoice.

The rest of the Summary tab presents collapsible groups:

- **Document** — DOC / DCT / KCO, UBL number, invoice type, profile ID, contract / buyer / order / project references, accounting cost.
- **Dates & Currency** — issue date, due date, currency, period start / end.
- **Amounts** — total HT, total TTC, amount due.
- **Payment** — payment means code, IBAN, account name, BIC, payment ID, payment terms.
- **Document allowances / charges** — document-level discounts or charges with type, reason, amount, tax category.

### Parties tab

Three collapsible groups, populated from the UBL document:

- **Supplier** — name, SIREN, SIRET, VAT identifier, electronic endpoint, postal address, contact (name, phone, e-mail).
- **Customer** — name, company ID, electronic endpoint, VAT, address, contact.
- **Agent Party** *(optional)* — for the French extension — name, address, country.
- **Delivery** *(optional)* — date, party name, location ID, address.

A group with no data on the invoice is not displayed.

- Price-level allowance / charge (`BT-147`)
- Line-level allowances / charges (`BG-27` / `BG-28`)
- Additional item properties (`BG-32`)

When several lines share the same delivery group, document references (`BT-128`) or customer order number (`EXT-FR-FE-135`), a **delivery header**, a **document-reference header** or a **Customer Order Reference header** appears once at the top of that group rather than repeating on every line.
