### History tab

Three sections in this tab:

#### Action bar at the top

| Button | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Validate UBL** | Re-runs XSD + Schematron validation on the UBL stored in the database. The result is shown inline (valid / warning / error) with details when applicable. |
| **Set status** | Opens the *Set Status modal* — see below. |
| **Resend** | Submits the UBL to the Plateforme Agréée again. Confirms before running. |
| **Download UBL** | Saves the archived UBL of the invoice. |
| **Download CII** | Shown when the document has a [post-transform](../ubl-tools/post-transform.md): the archived UBL converted on demand, named after the post-transform (*Download converted file* when it has no name). |

#### Lifecycle group

The **lifecycle** is the audit trail of every status the invoice has been in. Each event shows:

- The status badge (code + colour-coded family).
- The status label and the message returned by the platform.
- Optional details for refusals: rejection reason code + label, expected action code + label, additional status note.

The lifecycle is append-only — events are added by the *Sync → Retrieve Statuses* sweep and never modified. Each event does carry a **delete** button (with confirmation): removing an event realigns the invoice status on the last remaining one — the clean manual fix when the platform delivered a stray status (a *Refusée* it later superseded, say). It is gated by a dedicated **Delete lifecycle event** action in the [roles](../configuration/security/roles.md).

The three refusal fields — **rejection reason**, **expected action** and **status note** — also live in the column catalog, so they can be pinned as list columns and filtered from the [List Views](../configuration/list-views.md) editor when a team needs to scan or sort by refusal reason without opening each invoice.

| Field | Description |

      📎
      FA-2026-001234.pdf · 142 KB · auto-attached from PDF tab
    
  
  
    Cancel
    Send
  

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **To** *(required)* | Recipient e-mail address. |
| **Cc** | Optional carbon copy. |
| **Subject** | Pre-filled with `Invoice <ublNumber>`; editable. |
| **Body** | Pre-filled with a French / English template depending on the user's language: greeting, main line referencing the invoice number and total amount, contact line, signature. Fully editable. |

The PDF currently shown in the PDF tab is automatically attached. If the PDF was not pre-loaded, the server fetches it from the database before sending.

While the e-mail is sending, an overlay covers the modal until the SMTP server confirms the send. A green banner indicates success; the modal closes automatically after ~2 s.

### Create / Edit invoice modal \{#create-invoice\}

Opens from **+ New Invoice** in the toolbar, or from the **Edit UBL** / **Copy** buttons in the Summary tab. Lets the user create a new invoice from scratch or adjust an existing one. The modal is laid out like a printable invoice — the user fills the form and NomaUBL produces the corresponding UBL document on **Save**.

Editing an existing invoice no longer flips its `cbc:CustomizationID` back to the EN16931 default. The form now carries the `customizationId` value from the source UBL and writes it back verbatim — new invoices still default to `urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017`.

  
    📝 New invoice
    ⛶✕
  

  
    
      
        
          N
          Nomana-IT SAS
        
        10 rue de Paris · 75001 Paris · FRSIREN 123 456 789 · VAT FR12123456789
      
      
        INVOICE
        N° FA-2026-001234
        Issue 2026-04-24 · Due 2026-05-24

        Nomana-IT SAS

        50 avenue des Champs69002 Lyon · FR
        🔎 PPF lookup

        Payment
        SEPA · IBAN FR76 3000 4000 0312 3456 7890 143
        BIC BNPAFRPP · Terms 30 days net EOM
      
      
        Subtotal HT4,500.00
        VAT 20%900.00
        
        Total TTC5,400.00 EUR
      
    
  

  
    📄 UBL will be generated and submitted to the Plateforme Agréée on save
    
      Cancel
      Save & generate UBL
    
  

The modal is split into vertical sections:

- **Document** — invoice number, type, profile ID, contract / buyer / order references.
- **Header** — issue / due dates, currency, period start / end, the **Despatch advice** (BT-16 — number and date), plus a **Preceding invoices** block (BG-3, 0..n): each row a reference number (BT-25) and an optional issue date (BT-26), added or removed with **＋ Add a preceding invoice (BG-3)**. On a credit note this is the reference to the corrected invoice.
- **Supplier** — pre-populates from the supplier directory (*UBL Defaults → Suppliers / Companies*); editable per invoice.
- **Customer** — filled end to end from the company search: results show the badge, name and identifier on one line with the address below; searching a bare SIREN or SIRET lists every establishment (the same second INSEE lookup as [E-Directory](./edirectory.md)), and an optional SIRET field completes the SIREN. The electronic address is **not guessed** from the SIREN/SIRET — a PPF electronic-address list (opened automatically after picking a company, or anytime via the button next to the identifier field) shows the addresses registered for the SIREN with their active/disabled state; picking one fills the identifier and its scheme, then the list closes. An **Other ids (BT-46)** block adds any number of extra buyer identifiers, each with its scheme from the EAS list — a routing code or a second SIRET carried on the document is now visible, editable and removable instead of travelling invisibly.
- **Delivery** — optional document-level delivery group (BG-13). It shows only the delivery set at document level; deliveries carried by the lines stay on the lines and are never copied up to the header.
- **Payment** — payment means code, IBAN, BIC, mandate, terms.
- **Allowances / charges** — document-level discounts / charges.
- **Notes** — free-text notes per `BT-22` prefix.
- **Lines** — invoice lines with item, quantity, unit, price, allowances, item properties. The unit-price input accepts fine precision (up to 6 decimals), to match prices that carry more than 2 decimals at source. A per-line **Price (BG-29)** block sets the gross unit price (**BT-148**) and the price discount (**BT-147**); the net price is derived and drives the line amount, and the line amount divides by the **price base quantity** (BT-149) so a price per 100 or 1,000 units is computed correctly. The line *References* block also holds per-line **Preceding invoice** references (EXT-FR-FE-136) — number, optional date and a **DocumentStatusCode** picked from `INFORMATION` / `DETAIL` / `GROUP`. Three quick-add buttons in the same block fill the **order references** of the line, all carried by `cac:OrderLineReference`: **Customer Order Reference** (the buyer's order number, EXT-FR-FE-135 — the key the PDF groups lines on), **Order number** (the seller's order number, EXT-FR-FE-144) and **Customer line no.** (the line number inside the buyer's order, BT-132). A fourth button, **Despatch advice**, adds the line's despatch advice reference and date (EXT-FR-FE-BG-07).
- **VAT summary** — auto-computed from the lines (read-only — line edits are reflected here).
- **Totals** — auto-computed (read-only).

The **Save** button at the bottom validates the input, writes to the database, generates the UBL document and submits it to the PA according to the e-invoicing template's settings. The modal closes after a successful save.

A **fullscreen toggle** in the header swaps between windowed and full-screen edit, useful for invoices with many lines.

### Resend confirmation

The **Resend** button (in the History tab, or via Seller actions when status is `9904`/`9907`) opens a confirmation dialog before re-submitting the UBL to the Plateforme Agréée — the document is transmitted immediately and its status moves to *Pending* (`9906`). After confirmation, the invoice is re-submitted; an inline banner reports success or the error returned by the PA. The lifecycle is updated to reflect the new submission.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Start with the period.** *Yesterday* is the typical morning view, a custom range covers month-end reconciliation; set the opening period once under [Default periods](../configuration/default-periods.md). Filters apply on top of the period.
- **The stages are the fastest filter.** *To correct* and *Decision needed* with a non-zero count are usually the right place to start when chasing exceptions; the caret narrows the stage to one status.
- **The lifecycle (History tab) is the source of truth.** It records every status the invoice has been in, with messages, rejection reasons and expected actions — the place to investigate disputes or PA-side decisions.
- **Use the Seller actions banner.** The actions surfaced for `205` / `206` / `207` / `208` / `210` / `213` / `9904` / `9907` are the platform's recommended next step. They reduce a multi-step workflow (finding the customer, drafting the credit note, etc.) to a single click when the connector is configured.
- **Set status only when needed.** Manual `Set status → DB` desynchronises the local record from the PA. Reserve it for clean-up after restoring backups or for statuses the lifecycle sweep cannot catch.
- **Edit UBL, then save** is the canonical correction path — it rewrites the database record with the new UBL and re-submits to the PA. Avoid editing the source XML directly through *UBL Tools → XML Viewer* unless the data on disk is the authoritative one.
- **Use Copy for recurring billing.** It pre-fills every party / line / VAT field; only the document number, dates, and any specific changes need to be edited.

## NomaUBL — E-Documents
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/edocuments/

Browse every document captured in the NomaUBL archive — not only those that became invoices — with the archived source spool and the generated UBL side by side, and query the same archive over REST.

The **E-Documents** page lists **every document captured in the archive** — not only the ones that became invoices. A spool that failed early, or a document type that never produces an invoice, is still here. It is the archive browser next to the [E-Invoicing](./invoices.md) list, which shows only invoices.

Each row is a document as it was received; open it to see the **archived source spool** and, when the document became an invoice, the **generated UBL** — both formatted and downloadable.

---

## At a glance

---

## What each row shows

The default columns are the archive fields: **document number**, **type**, **company**, **activity**, **sub-type**, a **send-to-PA** flag, **customer**, **amount**, **document date**, **archive date**, **source file** and the **PA UUID**. Filters cover **activity**, **customer**, **source file** and the usual **period range**.

Columns and filters are configurable from *Settings → List Views → E-Documents* — the same list-view mechanism used elsewhere, so you can pin the columns your team scans and hide the rest. The catalog also carries the refusal fields — **rejection reason**, **expected action** and **status note** — so an archive view can surface why a document was refused as a column, without opening each one.

---

## Opening a document

Clicking a row opens a viewer with two panes:

- **Archived source spool** — the document exactly as it was received, before any transform.
- **Generated UBL** — present when the document became an invoice; the UBL that was produced and sent.

Each pane is shown formatted and can be **downloaded**, named after the document. When the document has a [post-transform](../ubl-tools/post-transform.md), the UBL pane also offers **Download CII** (or *Download converted file*): the archived UBL converted on demand. A document that failed before producing UBL shows only the source spool — which is precisely what you need to see why.

When the document has a **template** and an **archived source**, the viewer also offers an **Extract & Process** button: it re-extracts the archived spool and re-runs it through the document's template — the same pipeline as the [Extract & Process](../processing/extract-and-process.md) page with the *Archive* source, with the parameters taken from the document itself. Replace mode is forced, so the rerun overwrites the previous result. Handy to regenerate a document's outputs after a template or configuration change.

---

## Query it over REST

The same archive is reachable from an external application through `GET /api/list-documents` (documented in the built-in API reference), with per-document endpoints for the source spool and the generated UBL. It is the integration point for a downstream system that needs to pull an archived document without going through the UI.

---

## Access

The page follows the same **company / role** access rules as the [E-Invoicing](./invoices.md) list — a user sees only the companies their role allows. Grant the page to a role from *Settings → Roles* (under *Navigation*); it is not visible until granted.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Start here when a spool "disappeared".** If a document never reached the invoice list, E-Documents shows whether it was archived at all and lets you read its source spool to find the reason.
- **Pin the columns you scan.** Configure the E-Documents list view once (*Settings → List Views*) so the archive opens on the fields that matter to your team.
- **Use the REST endpoint for downstream pulls.** `/api/list-documents` gives an external system the same archive without screen-scraping.

---

## NomaUBL — E-Reporting
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/ereporting/

E-reporting declarations to the Plateforme Agréée — generate French flux 10.1 (B2C invoice detail) and flux 10.3 (B2BINT aggregated) for a chosen company, type and period; track each report's lifecycle, resend on demand, download the submitted XML.

The **E-Reporting** screen is the operational entry point for the **e-reporting workflow** of NomaUBL — the declaration track of the French *Réforme de la Facturation Électronique* (RFE). Where *E-Invoicing* sends a structured invoice to the recipient's Plateforme Agréée, *E-Reporting* sends an **aggregated declaration** to the tax authority through the same PA — covering the transactions that fall *outside* the e-invoicing flow:

- **B2C transactions** — sales to private individuals.
- **Intra-EU B2B transactions** — sales to a buyer in another EU member state.
- **Export and other out-of-scope transactions** — sales to non-EU buyers, intra-group internal flows, etc.

For these transactions the buyer never receives a structured invoice via the PA; the seller still declares the turnover so the tax authority can compute the VAT obligation. NomaUBL groups the relevant transactions, builds the corresponding XML, submits it to the PA and tracks its lifecycle.

The page applies regardless of source system — JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP.

---

## Where e-reporting fits

E-reporting is the **declaration-only** track of the French reform — the e-invoicing flow handles the structured B2B invoice, while e-reporting covers everything that does not go through that flow but still needs to be reported for VAT.

The BAR routing rule defined in *UBL Defaults → Document Type / BAR Routing* drives the split — set it correctly upstream and the right transactions land in the right flux automatically.

---

## The envelope, two sub-blocks, four document types

Each report is a single `<TransactionsReport>` envelope per `(company, period, direction)` — at most two XML files per `(company, period)`: one **outbound** envelope that aggregates every issued invoice (Issuer `RoleCode=SE`), and one **inbound** envelope that aggregates every received supplier invoice when the operator subscribes to the inbound flow (Issuer `RoleCode=BY`). The direction the envelope speaks for is taken from the `UHDRIN` flag stored on each F564231 row.

Inside an envelope, the French e-reporting specification defines **two sub-blocks** (the *flux* 10.1 and 10.3) and **four document types** that describe whether the envelope is an initial submission or a correction.

| Sub-block | Scope | Content shape |
|---|---|---|
| **`10.1`** | **B2BINT** invoice detail | One `<Invoice>` element per international B2B invoice in the period — ID, issue date, type code, currency, Seller (declarer), Buyer (counterparty), monetary totals, and one `<TaxSubTotal>` per VAT rate. B2C invoices are *never* emitted here, in line with the routing rule of the specification. Credit notes are emitted as positive-signed rows with their own type code. |
| **`10.3`** | **B2C / OUTOFSCOPE** aggregated | One `<Transactions>` block per *(category code, currency)*, with nested `<TaxSubTotal>` entries per rate carrying the taxable base (in source currency) and the VAT amount (always in EUR). Credit notes — UNTDID 1001 codes `261`, `381`, `396`, `502`, `503` per G1.01 — **subtract** from the aggregate, in line with G1.14 which allows negative amounts on `TT-82`, `TT-83`, `TT-87`, `TT-88`. A period dominated by credits comes through with the correct net taxable base and VAT. |

| Code | Meaning | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| **`IN`** | **Initial** | First declaration for the period — the default. |
| **`RE`** | **Replacement** | Replaces a previously submitted report for the same period after a correction. |
| **`CO`** | **Cancellation** | Cancels a previously submitted report (e.g. submitted by mistake). |
| **`MO`** | **Modification** | Adjusts specific lines of a previous report without full replacement. |

Reports follow a configurable **frequency** — `MONTHLY` (calendar month, default), `DECADAL` (1-10, 11-20, 21-end of month) or `WEEKLY` (ISO Monday → Sunday) — defined in the *e-reporting* template of `config.json`.

### Transaction category codes (flux 10.3)

The `<Transactions>` block in flux 10.3 carries a `<CategoryCode>` (TT-81) that classifies the underlying operation against the four codes accepted by the specification:

| Code | Meaning | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| **`TLB1`** | Taxable goods deliveries | Standard sales of goods subject to French VAT. |
| **`TPS1`** | Taxable services | Service supplies subject to French VAT. |
| **`TNT1`** | Non-taxable | Operations outside the scope of French VAT — intra-EU distance sales, services covered by Article 259 B CGI, exports. |
| **`TMA1`** | Margin regime | Operations under the VAT-on-margin regime (Articles 266 e, 268, 297 A CGI). |

NomaUBL derives the category from the underlying invoice line. When a source line carries a value outside the accepted set, the platform falls back automatically to `TLB1` (positive rate) or `TNT1` (zero rate).

:::info[VAT amounts are always in EUR]
Every `<TaxAmount>` and `<TaxTotal>` element produced by NomaUBL is forced to euros, regardless of the source invoice's currency. The `<TaxableAmount>` keeps the source invoice's original currency so the underlying operation amount stays auditable.
:::

---

## Lifecycle statuses

E-reporting reports go through a **dedicated lifecycle** distinct from the invoice statuses. NomaUBL writes one of these eight codes on each transition between *generation* and *PA acknowledgement (or rejection)*:

  Happy path
  9950 Created
  →
  9952 Sent to PA
  →
  9953 Pending
  →
  9955 Deposited ✓
  
  Failure / variants
  9951 Submit skipped
  ·
  9954 Error sent
  ·
  9956 Failed import
  ·
  9957 Rejected ✗

| Code | Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **`9950`** | `EREPORT_CREATED` | Report XML built and persisted; no submission attempt yet. |
| **`9951`** | `EREPORT_SUBMIT_SKIPPED` | Report generated; submission to the PA disabled (`sendToPA=N` on the *e-reporting* template). The XML is available for download but never reaches the PA. |
| **`9952`** | `EREPORT_SENT_TO_PA` | Report submitted to the PA over HTTP; awaiting initial acknowledgement. |
| **`9953`** | `EREPORT_PENDING` | PA has acknowledged receipt and is processing the report. |
| **`9954`** | `EREPORT_ERROR_SENT` | Submission to the PA failed at the network or HTTP level — typically transient. **Resend** can recover. |
| **`9955`** | `EREPORT_DEPOSITED` | PA accepted and registered the report — terminal success. |
| **`9956`** | `EREPORT_FAILED_IMPORT` | PA could not import the report (post-acknowledgement processing error). |
| **`9957`** | `EREPORT_REJECTED` | PA rejected the report on a validation rule — terminal failure. The next attempt requires a corrected `RE`. |
| **`9958`** | `EREPORT_ERROR_VALIDATION` | Report failed the **pre-send validation** (PPF schema + Annexe 7 rules) — it is never sent to the PA, the detailed findings are recorded, and its invoices stay available. **Self-healing**: once the cause is fixed, the next run rebuilds the same period automatically. |
| **`9959`** | `EREPORT_CANCELLED` | Report cancelled by a **Regenerate** — kept for audit while its invoices are freed and a replacement report is built for the same period. |

Codes `9950` – `9954` are *transient* (the report is still moving). `9955` – `9957` are *terminal* (no further automatic transition); a `RE` (replacement) report is the only way to override a `9957` for the same period. `9958` is a recoverable pre-send failure — see [Validation before sending](#validation-before-sending) — and `9959` is an audit record left behind by [Regenerate](#regenerate-a-report).

### Validation before sending \{#validation-before-sending\}

Every generated report is checked **before** it is sent — against the official PPF schema and the Annexe 7 rules — exactly like a B2B invoice. A report that doesn't conform is written with status **`9958` — Validation failed**, carries the detailed findings, and is **never sent** to the PA. Its invoices stay available, so once the cause is fixed the next run rebuilds the same period on its own — nothing to unlock by hand.

### Regenerate a report \{#regenerate-a-report\}

A report that was **not accepted** — created, send failed, import failed, rejected or validation failed — can be rebuilt from its **detail view** with **Regenerate**. The current report is cancelled (status **`9959` — Cancelled, regenerated**, kept for audit), its invoices become selectable again, and a fresh report is built for the **same period** — including any late arrivals — then validated and submitted according to your settings. A cancelled report no longer offers **Resend** or **Download**. A report already at the PA (sent, pending or deposited) can't be regenerated.

The toolbar above the table combines three free-text filters with two quick actions.

### Advanced Filters

A collapsible **Advanced Filters** panel below the toolbar exposes one row per filterable column from the active [List Views](../configuration/list-views.md) spec (`view.ereporting`) — with per-column operator pickers (`contains`, `equals`, `≠`, `<`, `≤`, `>`, `≥`, `between`, `empty`, `not empty`). Edits stay in draft until **Run** commits them.

The page runs in **hybrid client-side mode** — one capped server slice per *Run* (`spec.maxRows`, the *Rows loaded* of [Settings › Navigation & lists](../configuration/default-periods.md#lists) unless the view sets its own — 100 000 by default), then TanStack handles filter / sort / paginate inside the slice. An `X / Y rows` notice next to *Run* signals when the cap is hit. The `status` refList column gets a **multi-select picker** that issues an `IN (?,?,?)` clause on the server so picking several status codes returns the union.

## Detail modal

Clicking a row opens a modal with three tabs along the top: **Header**, **Invoices**, **History**. The modal title shows the report's `Flux / Kco / Rgdoc` triplet.

### Header tab *(default)*

Field grid summarising the report identity and submission outcome.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **RGDOC** | Internal report identifier. |
| **FLUX** | `10.1` or `10.3`. |
| **KCO** | Company code. |
| **Type** | `IN` / `RE` / `CO` / `MO`. |
| **Period start / Period end** | ISO 8601 dates of the declaration window. |
| **Sender** | Transmitter matricule, list ID `0238` — typically the entity registered with the PA. |
| **Issuer** | Legal issuer's identifier, list ID `0002` (SIREN). |
| **PA UUID** | Identifier returned by the PA on acceptance. Empty until the report has been accepted. |
| **Status** | Current lifecycle status — code + label. |
| **Status message** | Last message received from the PA — typically the rejection reason for failed submissions. |
| **Invoices** | Number of source invoices included in the report. |
| **Created** | Generation timestamp. |

### Invoices tab

Tabular view of every source invoice included in the report. The columns map directly to the underlying e-invoicing record so the report and its sources can be cross-referenced.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| **Number** | Invoice number — UBL `BT-1` when set, otherwise `DOC/DCT/KCO`. |
| **Date** | Issue date (`BT-2`). |
| **BAR** | BAR routing code carried by the invoice (`B2C`, `B2BINT`, `OUTOFSCOPE`, …). |
| **Customer** | Buyer party name. |
| **HT** | Total amount excluding VAT. |
| **VAT** | Total VAT amount. |
| **TTC** | Total amount including VAT. |
| **CCY** | ISO 4217 currency code. |

The list reflects the rows persisted at generation time — re-running a report (`RE`) does not retroactively reshape the prior `IN` view.

### History tab

The **lifecycle** of the report — every status it has been in, append-only, in submission order.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| **#** | Sequence number — `1` is the initial state at generation, subsequent rows are events from the PA. |
| **Status** | Status code + label drawn from the e-reporting catalogue (e.g. `9950 Created`, `9952 Sent to PA`, `9953 Pending`, `9955 Deposited`, `9957 Rejected`). See *Lifecycle statuses* above. |
| **Message** | Free-text message returned by the PA — typically the rejection reason or acceptance note. |
| **Date** | Event timestamp. |

The lifecycle is read-only here; the only action is **Resend to PA** at the modal header, which appends a new event after a successful resubmission.

### Header actions

| Button | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Download XML** | Downloads the formatted XML of the report (filename pattern `ereporting-<flux>-<kco>-<rgdoc>.xml`). The XML is pretty-printed when possible, with a fallback to the raw stored content. |
| **Resend to PA** | Re-submits the existing report XML to the Plateforme Agréée. Useful after a transient PA error. Hidden on read-only sessions. The lifecycle is updated with the new submission outcome. |
| **Close** *(✕)* | Closes the modal without modification. |

## Generate dialog \{#generate-dialog\}

Opens from **Generate report** in the toolbar. Builds and submits one or several reports for a chosen company / direction / period combination.

{/* svg:ergen */}

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Company (kco)** | A picker of the companies (the `list-companies` [custom list](../configuration/custom-lists.md#ready-made-lists)). *All configured companies* applies to every company declared in the *e-reporting* template. |
| **Direction** | **Outbound (sales)** and / or **Inbound (purchases)**, both selected by default; at least one is required. One report is produced per company and direction, and each report carries both flows: 10.1 (B2B international, detail) and 10.3 (B2C, aggregated). |
| **Document type** | One of `IN` (initial), `RE` (replacement), `CO` (cancellation), `MO` (modification). The default is `IN`. |
| **Period start / end** | ISO 8601 dates that delimit the declaration window. |
| **Compute period** | Auto-fills *Period start* / *Period end* with the next due window, exactly as the scheduled run does: it follows the **company's setup** (frequency `MONTHLY` / `DECADAL` / `WEEKLY`) and the **last valid report** of that company for the direction. The dialog states the frequency applied and the report it follows (*after the last report ending …*, or *no previous report, current period*). A company must be entered to compute. |
| **Cancel** | Closes the dialog without generating. |
| **Generate** | Builds the XML for each company and direction, stores the report row and submits it to the PA. The run happens **in the background**: the dialog shows its log as it goes, then refreshes the list when done, so a large period does not end in a proxy error. |

When the generator builds a report, it derives the per-invoice **Sender**, **Issuer** and **Business Process** blocks (TT-7 / TT-12 / TT-28 / TT-29) from the *e-reporting* template — those defaults are configured once in *Settings → System → E-Reporting* (Sender / PA matricule + role `WK`, Issuer / SIREN scheme `0002` for French companies, Business Process emitted only on B2BINT invoices). When no transmission ID is provided manually, the report is identified as **`{siren}-{flux}-{start}-{end}`** so it stays stable across regenerations of the same period and lets the PA deduplicate identical retransmissions.

The **buyer** block carries the buyer's **legal identifier**, not its electronic address: a French address (scheme `0225`) or a SIRET (`0009`) yields the SIREN under scheme `0002`, with the VAT number derived from it; schemes `0002`, `0223`, `0227`, `0228` and `0229` pass through. A buyer with no usable identifier (blank, `0`, an e-mail scheme) is left out of the report and the invoice is named in the log, so the customer record can be completed — the validation then reports the missing buyer on that invoice rather than a scheme error (G2.19) on the whole report.

After a successful run, the new reports appear at the top of the list with a `9950` (Created) status that quickly progresses through `9952` (Sent to PA) and `9953` (Pending), then lands on `9955` (Deposited) once the PA acknowledges receipt. When the *Send to PA* flag is off (`sendToPA=N`), the report stays at `9951` (Submit skipped) and the XML can still be downloaded for offline review.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Set the BAR routing first.** The list of invoices that ends up in flux 10.1 / 10.3 is driven by *UBL Defaults → Document Type / BAR Routing*. `B2BINT` feeds flux 10.1 (per-invoice detail); `B2C` and `OUTOFSCOPE` feed flux 10.3 (aggregated). A misclassified invoice will be missed by *both* tracks — ensure every document type maps to one of `B2B`, `B2G`, `B2C`, `B2BINT`, `OUTOFSCOPE` before the first run.
- **Use *Compute period* rather than manual dates.** It honours the frequency configured in the *e-reporting* template, so the suggested window matches the regulatory deadline (previous full month for `MONTHLY`, previous decade for `DECADAL`, previous ISO week for `WEEKLY`).
- **`IN` first, then `RE` for corrections.** A late-arriving invoice or a corrected amount calls for a `RE` report covering the same period — never re-issue an `IN` for a period that has already been declared.
- **Reserve `CO` for full cancellation.** Use it when an entire period has been declared in error; the `RE` track handles partial corrections.
- **The PA UUID is the receipt.** It is empty between submission and acceptance (statuses `9952` and `9953`), and final once the PA acknowledges with `9955` (Deposited). Use it as the legal proof of the declaration when responding to an audit.
- **Resend after a transient PA error, not after a Schematron rejection.** A `9954` (Error sent) is a network or HTTP failure — *Resend* recovers. A `9957` (Rejected) carries a Schematron or business-rule reason in the *Status message* — fix the upstream BAR or invoice data and generate a fresh `RE`, do not blindly resend. A `9956` (Failed import) sits between the two: read the message before deciding to resend or rebuild.
- **The Invoices tab is a snapshot.** It records the source invoices as they were at generation time. Edits to those invoices afterwards do not retroactively alter the submitted report — they appear in the next `RE` if material.
- **VAT data is read from the UBL document first.** When generating a report, NomaUBL parses the document-level `cac:TaxTotal/cac:TaxSubtotal` of each invoice's stored UBL XML — line-level subtotals are skipped to avoid double-counting. The VAT-summary table is consulted only as a fallback. If a B2C report ships with empty `<Transactions>` blocks even though the invoices and their UBL documents are present, the VAT summary is most likely stale relative to the UBL — regenerating from the UBL closes the gap.
- **Configure the Sender / Issuer / Business Process defaults once.** Settings → System → E-Reporting groups the PA matricule (Sender, default role `WK`), the issuer SIREN (Issuer, default scheme `0002` for French companies; `0223` / `0227` / `0228` / `0229` for international cases) and the per-invoice business process (emitted only in B2BINT). Maintaining them at the template level keeps every generated report consistent and avoids per-report overrides.
- **Out-of-list category codes are auto-mapped.** A source line carrying a tax category outside `TLB1` / `TPS1` / `TNT1` / `TMA1` is silently coerced to `TLB1` (positive rate) or `TNT1` (zero rate) at generation time. Set the category explicitly on the source line whenever the default is wrong (e.g. a service that should land on `TPS1` rather than `TLB1`).

---

## NomaUBL — E-Directory
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/edirectory/

Look up a French company in the INSEE registry by name, SIREN or SIRET, then check whether each match is reachable on the PPF directory for e-invoice delivery.

The **E-Directory** screen is the user-facing search tool for finding a French company in the **INSEE registry** (`recherche-entreprises.api.gouv.fr`) and checking whether the matching SIREN / SIRET entries are **reachable on the PPF directory** for electronic invoice delivery.

Use this page when:

- you need to look up a customer's exact SIREN / SIRET before issuing an invoice;
- you want to confirm a buyer is registered on the Plateforme Publique de Facturation (PPF) and ready to receive an electronic invoice;
- you are debugging an addressing rejection (e.g. `REJ_ADR`) and need to verify the directory state for a specific identifier.

The page applies regardless of source system — JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP.

The two underlying lookups are independent and have different roles:

- **INSEE search** — verifies that the company exists and pulls its name, address, administrative state. Free public API, no credentials needed.
- **PPF directory check** — verifies that the SIREN / SIRET is registered as a recipient on the Plateforme Publique de Facturation. Uses the credentials configured in *Configuration → System → e-directory*.

See the [Configuration → System → e-directory](../configuration/system/edirectory.md) page for the broader context — credentials, search roles and the PPF / INSEE distinction.

---

## At a glance

---

## How a search runs

The two lookups happen in sequence: INSEE first to populate the companies, then **one PPF directory call per company** to list its registered identifiers. The user sees the results fill in two passes. Expanding a company card then runs the [Peppol lookup](#peppol-directory) for that company.

---

## Search section

A single input + button at the top of the page.

| Element | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Search field** | Free-text query: company name, partial name, SIREN, SIRET, or any combination. Press **Enter** or click **Search** to submit. |
| **Search** button | Triggers the INSEE lookup. Disabled while a search is in progress and when the field is empty. |

The query is sent to `recherche-entreprises.api.gouv.fr` server-side; the API returns matching companies with their full establishment data.

---

## Results

Results are grouped **by company**: one collapsed card per **SIREN**, showing the legal name, the head-office address, the INSEE administrative state and an **electronic-address summary** — how many electronic addresses the PPF holds for the company and how many are enabled. Expand a card to reveal two groups:

### Establishments (INSEE)

An inner collapsible list of the company's establishments — each **SIRET** with its address and administrative state, from the INSEE registry. Searching by SIREN or SIRET lists **all** establishments of the company (a second INSEE lookup by company name fills what the numeric search omits).

### Electronic addresses

Every identifier registered for the SIREN on the PPF, **whatever its form** — a SIREN, a SIREN + SIRET, a routing code or a suffix — each with its **enabled / disabled** state. Identifiers that carry a suffix, such as `422250845_FGX`, are listed here too — a form the previous per-row check could not surface.

✓Enabled— Registered and reachable on the PPF; an invoice addressed to it is delivered.
✕Disabled— Registered but not currently reachable; addressing it would return a routing error (REJ_ADR).

The listing goes through the connector's `directory-check-siren` endpoint, which returns the full lines with per-endpoint response mappings (ATGP, Yooz and Esker shapes are supported — including numeric reachability flags such as Esker’s `HasAssignedPlatform` 1/0 alongside true/false). When that endpoint isn't configured, the page **says so** rather than guessing — set it under [Configuration → System → e-directory](../configuration/system/edirectory.md). The processing-time directory check is unchanged; the older `directory-check-siret` endpoint is obsolete.

### Peppol directory \{#peppol-directory\}

Expanding a company card also queries the **public Peppol network** — no account needed. A *Peppol directory* group lists each registered **participant** of the company, with its name, its **registration date** and the **service provider that operates it** — the PA (e.g. Pennylane) with its Peppol seat id, resolved through the official **SML/SMP** discovery. The access-point and SMP URLs sit in the provider's tooltip.

Participants are found in two ways:

- **Business cards** of the [Peppol Directory](https://directory.peppol.eu) matching the SIREN.
- **Direct SML probes** of every identifier a French company can hold — publishing a business card is optional, and some providers do not. The probes cover the SIREN under schemes `0225` and `0002`, every address registered in the PPF directory (bare, suffixed, SIRET, routed) under `0225`, and the SIRET of each establishment under `0009`. A participant found this way shows **no business card** in place of its registration date.

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| **Participant** | The Peppol participant identifier (ICD + value, e.g. `0225:80320631700015`). |
| **Plateforme (PA)** | The service provider operating the participant, with its seat id. When the SMP certificate cannot be read, the SMP host followed by *SMP non joignable*, the reason in the tooltip; `non résolu` with the reason when the SML gave no SMP. With *Resolve platform via SMP* = `N`, the SMP host. |
| **Enregistré le** | The participant's Peppol registration date — *no business card* for a participant found through the SML only. |

The lookup runs once for every open company card — including a card left open from a previous search — and is also available as `POST /api/peppol-lookup` for integrations (see the [API reference](/nomaubl/api-reference)). A participant with no reachable provider still lists its registration and name. The server log lists each unresolved participant with its reason. An outage of the Peppol Directory no longer hides the participants found through the SML.

The whole page is also available as a single call: `GET /api/e-directory/search?q=…` (or `POST` with `{q, peppol}`) returns the INSEE companies matching a name, SIREN or SIRET with head office and establishments, the PPF directory lines of each company and, with `peppol=true`, its Peppol participants.

---

## Network flows (firewall) \{#network-flows\}

Every E-Directory external call is made **server-side** — from the NomaUBL server, not the user's browser — so the firewall rules apply to the server's outbound traffic. Besides the PA connector, the destinations are:

| Purpose | Destination | Port / Protocol |
|---|---|---|
| Company search (INSEE) | `recherche-entreprises.api.gouv.fr` | HTTPS 443 |
| Peppol directory (business cards) | `directory.peppol.eu` | HTTPS 443 |
| Peppol SML resolution — **primary zone** (OpenPeppol) | DNS NAPTR queries on `*.iso6523-actorid-upis.participant.sml.prod.tech.peppol.org` | DNS 53 via the server's resolver |
| Peppol SML resolution — **fallback zone** (former European Commission SML) | DNS NAPTR queries on `*.iso6523-actorid-upis.edelivery.tech.ec.europa.eu` | DNS 53 via the server's resolver |
| Public DNS resolvers — only with *Public DNS fallback* = `Y`, when the server's resolver answers nothing | `8.8.8.8`, `1.1.1.1` | DNS 53 (UDP and TCP) |
| Peppol SMP (provider resolution) — only with *Resolve platform via SMP* = `Y` | dynamic — the SMP host of each participant's platform (e.g. `smp.pennylane.com`) | HTTPS 443 |

What matters for the rules:

- **INSEE and `directory.peppol.eu` are fixed hostnames** — easy to whitelist. The INSEE entry also covers the invoice modal's client search and the [Fix buyer](./invoices.md#fix-buyer) search (same API).
- **The SML moved in 2026.** OpenPeppol took over the Service Metadata Locator and participant records now live in the `participant.sml.prod.tech.peppol.org` zone. NomaUBL queries it first and keeps the former `edelivery.tech.ec.europa.eu` zone as fallback. A DNS policy that only allowed the former zone must add the new one — otherwise most participants are no longer found.
- **The SML step is DNS only** — no HTTP. If the server already resolves public DNS through the corporate resolver, there is nothing to open. Some corporate resolvers drop or mangle NAPTR queries: let the corporate resolver forward NAPTR queries for both zones, or set **Public DNS fallback** to `Y` in the [e-directory settings](../configuration/system/edirectory.md#peppol-lookup) and allow outbound DNS (port 53, UDP and TCP) to `8.8.8.8` and `1.1.1.1`. The fallback is **off by default**. A *no such name* answer from the server's resolver is final — an unregistered identifier is not retried elsewhere — and a failing public resolver is dropped for the rest of the lookup.
- **The SMP host can't be whitelisted in advance** — it's whatever domain each buyer's platform uses (Pennylane, Esker, Yooz… one per participant), so provider resolution needs a broad *HTTPS 443 outbound* allowance to work generally. If that isn't acceptable, set **Resolve platform via SMP** to `N`: the lookup stops at the SML answer and the *Plateforme* column shows the SMP host (`smp.pennylane.com`), which already names the provider — only its official name and seat are missing.
- **Diagnosis.** When `directory.peppol.eu` is unreachable, the participants found by the SML probes are still listed. When nothing is found at all, the Peppol section shows *Peppol Directory unreachable (directory.peppol.eu) — check outbound HTTPS/firewall*.

---

## Result count

Above the results, a small label indicates the number of companies returned by INSEE for the query (e.g. `12 results`).

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Search by name first, then narrow down.** INSEE returns the legal entity (SIREN) and its establishments (SIRET) — picking the right SIRET avoids the common "right SIREN, wrong establishment" mistake when issuing invoices.
- **A disabled line is not always permanent.** A buyer may not yet be registered, or a specific identifier not yet enabled; ask them to register before re-trying. The directory state changes daily as more companies subscribe to the PPF.
- **Match the exact identifier, not just the SIREN.** The electronic-address lines show which form is actually reachable — a plain SIREN, a SIREN + SIRET, or a suffixed code. Address the invoice to an **enabled** line; a company can have several, only some enabled.
- **Cross-check the establishment state.** A ceased establishment cannot receive an invoice even if the company appears in the directory. Check the INSEE state on the establishment before trusting an electronic-address mapping.
- **If the lines don't appear, wire the endpoint.** An empty directory list with a "not configured" note means the connector has no `directory-check-siren` endpoint — set it under *Configuration → System → e-directory*, with the response mappings for your platform (ATGP, Yooz, Esker). The listing reads its array from the endpoint's **Response field** (`records` for Esker, `results`…).

---

## NomaUBL — VAT Declaration
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/vat-declaration/

Aggregate every invoice for a period on the standard French CA3 form rows — sales / purchases × domestic / intra-EU / outside-EU × VAT rate × invoice type — with drill-down to the individual invoices behind each figure, and one-click Excel and CA3-formatted PDF exports.

The **VAT Declaration** screen aggregates every invoice booked in a period on the lines of the French **CA3 form** — sales / purchases × France / intra-EU / outside-EU × VAT rate × invoice type. Each rate unfolds into its transaction types and the individual invoices that make it up, and the result exports to Excel for accounting or to a CA3-styled PDF you can hand to the accountant.

Use this page when:

- you're preparing the monthly or quarterly VAT return and want a CA3-aligned summary built directly from the invoices already in the platform;
- you need to reconcile a CA3 line with the underlying invoices — which buyers, which document numbers, which amounts;
- you want a printable synthesis of the period to attach to the accounting file.

The page applies regardless of source system — JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP. The period filter is read on the **invoice's issue date** — the date printed on the invoice itself — so the period stays stable even if the underlying data is rebuilt later.

The matrix is served from the persisted VAT detail rows (`F564234`), not by re-parsing every UBL on each load — so the page opens in **a couple of seconds whether the period has 2 000 invoices or 200 000**. To keep it that way, leave *Store VAT details* on under *Settings → Connectors → db-nomaubl → Tables* — see [Detail Storage](../configuration/database-connectors/nomaubl.md#detail-storage).

---

## At a glance

---

## Filter bar

One bar sets the period, the company and the two exclusions, as on the dashboards.

| Control | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Month / Quarter** | Monthly or quarterly declaration. The page opens on the **previous full month** — the one you file. |
| **Year** and **month** / **quarter** | The period: the current year and the five before it; a month name, or `Q1` to `Q4`. The tag below the bar shows the dates and the previous period used for the changes (*compared with …*). The period is read on the **invoice's issue date**, so it stays stable even if the data is rebuilt later. |
| **Company** | A picker of the companies (the `list-companies` [custom list](../configuration/custom-lists.md#ready-made-lists)); *All companies* by default. |
| **Exclude refused and rejected** | On by default. Refused (`210`) and rejected (`213`) invoices call for an internal credit note: on, all are left out; off, only those customer service marked reviewed — see [Invoices left out](#excluded-invoices). The explanation shows on hover. |
| **Exclude invoices not at the platform** | Off by default. Also leaves out the invoices flagged to be sent whose status is still internal: validation, send or import failure, or not yet sent. |
| **Excel** | Downloads the workbook described under [Excel export](#excel-export). |
| **PDF** | Downloads the CA3-styled synthesis described under [PDF export — CA3 form layout](#pdf-export--ca3-form-layout). |

---

## Headline figures

| Figure | Value | Sub-line |
|---|---|---|
| **VAT collected** | VAT of the sales. | Base excl. VAT and number of invoices. |
| **VAT deductible** | VAT of the purchases. | Base excl. VAT and number of invoices. |
| **VAT due** / **VAT credit** | Collected minus deductible; shown as *VAT credit*, in green, when it is negative. | *Collected − deductible*. |

Below each figure, the change from the previous month or quarter (`+4.2 %`) and the previous amount (`vs …`), computed with the same company and the same exclusions.

---

## Invoices left out \{#excluded-invoices\}

The declaration counts the invoices issued in the period, minus:

| Case | Left out when |
|---|---|
| Refused by the buyer (`210`) or rejected by the platform (`213`) | *Exclude all refused and rejected* is checked (default) — or, unchecked, once customer service has marked the invoice reviewed in its window, the internal credit note being done. |
| To be sent, never reached the platform | *Exclude to-send invoices not at the platform* is checked: the invoice is flagged to be sent and its status is still internal (`99xx` other than `9906`, pending at the platform, and `9911`, export validated). |

The two rules apply to the matrix, the unfolded invoices, the Excel export and the PDF, whose footer states the rules applied. Over the API, the same choices are the `excludeMode` (`all` or `reviewed`) and `excludeUnsent` parameters.

---

## The CA3 matrix

The table reads by **direction**, then by **country group**, then by **rate**:

| Row | Content |
|---|---|
| **Sales (VAT collected)** / **Purchases (VAT deductible)** | The direction with its totals — taxable base (*Base HT*), VAT and invoice count. Sales come first; a direction without invoices is not shown. |
| **France**, **Intra-EU**, **Outside EU** | Each country group once, with its subtotal. |
| **Rate** (`20 %`, `10 %`…, *No rate*) | One row per rate found in the group, highest first, collapsed. Its chevron opens one row per BAR routing (`B2B`, `B2C`, `B2BINT`, `B2G`…), whose chevron opens the invoices — document, type, company, base and VAT, up to **200 rows** (the Excel export holds the full list). |
| **VAT due** / **VAT credit** | The net VAT of the period, *Collected − deductible*. |

The amounts are not links to the [Invoices list](./invoices.md), which cannot filter by VAT rate nor apply the two exclusions: the invoices behind a figure are read by unfolding its rate and routing rows, or in the *Details* sheet of the Excel export. Amounts, rates and percentages follow the number format of the interface language.

### Country group rules

The classification reads from the **counterparty country** captured on each invoice at insert time (buyer country on sales, supplier country on purchases) and from the *Sales / Purchases* direction stored on the invoice (`UHDRIN`).

| Country group | Sales (issued) | Purchases (received) |
|---|---|---|
| **France** | Buyer country = `FR`, or unknown. | Supplier country = `FR`, or unknown. |
| **Intra-EU** | Buyer country in the 26 other EU member states. | Supplier country in the 26 other EU member states. |
| **Outside EU** | Any other country. | Any other country. |

VAT rates rolled up under *Intra-EU* sales and *Outside-EU* sales appear as exempt (`—`) — they do not contribute to the VAT column, only to the taxable base. *Intra-EU acquisitions* on the Purchases side carry self-assessed VAT and contribute to both the taxable base and the VAT amount.

---

## When the matrix is empty

If the database does not yet hold any VAT detail row (`F564234`) for the selected period — typically right after *Store VAT details* was turned on but before any historical data was rebuilt — the page no longer shows a misleading empty matrix. It surfaces the exact command line to run, with the dates of the selected period already filled in:

  ⚠ No VAT details for April 2026
  The database does not hold any VAT detail row for this period. Run the rebuild command once, then reopen the page:
  ./nomaubl.sh backfill-vat prod 2026-04-01 2026-04-30
  Safe to re-run on the same period without creating duplicates.

The command is documented under [Command Line → `backfill-vat`](../management/command-line.md#backfill-vat). Once the rebuild has run, reopen the VAT page and the matrix is populated as expected.

A server-side failure — a database error, for instance — is never shown as an empty period: the page displays the error message, and the error is written to the server log.

---

## Excel export

The **Excel** button downloads `vat-declaration-<from>-<to>.xlsx`, with two sheets:

| Sheet | Content |
|---|---|
| **Summary** | Mirrors the on-screen matrix — sales / purchases × country group × rate × type — with subtotals per country group and per direction. |
| **Details** | One row per invoice contributing to the period: document number, document type, company, counterparty name, counterparty country, BAR routing, taxable base, VAT amount, currency, issue date. |

Numeric cells are written as real numbers, not as text. Totals, pivot tables and downstream Excel formulas work without any clean-up.

---

## PDF export — CA3 form layout

The **PDF** button downloads a one-page synthesis styled like the official **Cerfa 3310-CA3** (`vat-declaration-<from>-<to>.pdf`), so it can be filed alongside the rest of the accounting paperwork without re-typing. The PDF is in French whatever the interface language, with French number formats: amounts `125 315,78`, rates `5,5 %`, period `01/09/2026 – 30/09/2026`. Its footer states the exclusion rules applied.

| Block | CA3 lines |
|---|---|
| **Section A — Operations realised** | Line **01** (sales subject to VAT), **03** (intra-EU acquisitions), **04** (exports outside EU), **06** (intra-EU deliveries), **7B** (purchases of goods and services outside the EU). |
| **Section B — VAT brute then déductible** | One row per applicable rate: **08** (20%), **9B** (10%), **09** (5.5%), **10** (2.1%) and **14** (other rates), with total **16**. Then **20** (déductible VAT on goods and services) and total **23**. |
| **Solde** | Either **28** (*VAT à payer*) when the period ends in debt, or **32** (*crédit*) when déductible VAT outweighs collected VAT. |

The PDF is meant as a printable synthesis — not a substitute for filing on the DGFiP portal.

---

## Note on existing data

Invoices created before this release have no counterparty country on file. They are classified as **Domestic** by default until the underlying invoice is re-processed (so the country is captured from the UBL document and persisted). Any new invoice from now on lands with the correct country.

If you spot an intra-EU or outside-EU invoice still showing under *Domestic*, re-running it from the [Invoices list](./invoices.md) (Edit → Save, or a fresh Process from [Sync → Fetch Input](../sync/fetch-input.md)) refreshes the country.

---

## NomaUBL — Reports
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/reports/overview/

Reporting for NomaUBL — four cards: SQL integrity checks against a source system, and the audit, implementation and technical reports generated as PDF or Markdown. Status statistics are on the Statistics dashboard, free analyses in the Explorer.

The **Reports** page is the analytical view of NomaUBL — it turns the invoice, archive, lifecycle and validation data into figures a team can read and export, without writing SQL. A row of four cards picks the report, each saying what it is for; the page opens on the first one, **Integrity** — SQL checks that list what is missing or wrong compared with a source system. The three others generate a document on demand: the [Audit report](./audit-report.md), the [Implementation report](./implementation-report.md) and the [Technical report](./technical-report.md). The status statistics are on the [Statistics](../statistics.md) dashboard; free analyses — any field, grouping, chart or dashboard — are built in the [Explorer](../explorer.md).

Open it from the sidebar — **Reports**. Access is granted per role (see [Access](#access) below).

---

## At a glance

---

## Integrity \{#integrity\}

The **Integrity** card lists on the left the SQL checks defined under [Configuration → System → Integrity reports](../../configuration/system/integrity-reports.md)— each with its description, mode (*missing in the target*, *differences* or *direct query*), connector and *can integrate* when it carries an action. Pick a check, a period (the [default period](../../configuration/default-periods.md) of the *Reports › Integrity* view) and **Run**. A banner gives the outcome — *No anomaly* or the count of anomalies, the source and target counts and the duration — and *Show SQL* unfolds the queries. Every row of the result is one anomaly, shown in the standard grid (search, filters, columns, export). A check that carries an action lets you tick rows and **Integrate the selection** — see [Integrity reports](../../configuration/system/integrity-reports.md#reports-integrity) for the full walkthrough.

---

## Audit, implementation and technical reports

These three cards generate a document, in PDF or Markdown, rather than a grid:

| Card | Document | Page |
|---|---|---|
| **Audit report** | The activity of a period — volumes, situation, backlog, lifecycle, errors, operations and consistency checks — for an internal review or an auditor. | [Audit report](./audit-report.md) |
| **Implementation report** | The documentation of the instance as it runs — architecture, built-in rules, documents and UBL mappings, platform settings, operations, security — for a hand-over file or an upgrade snapshot. | [Implementation report](./implementation-report.md) |
| **Technical report** | The developer documentation of the release — data model, flows, configuration reference, status model, API — identical on every instance. | [Technical report](./technical-report.md) |

All three are also available from the [command line](../../management/command-line.md#report), to schedule them or keep them with a release.

---

## Access

The Reports page is gated **per role**: grant the *Reports* page in the **Navigation** group on the [Roles](../../configuration/security/roles.md) page. Without it, the sidebar entry is hidden.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Run the integrity checks after each night batch.** A clean result means NomaUBL holds everything the source system invoiced; set *Reports › Integrity* to *Yesterday* under [Default periods](../../configuration/default-periods.md) to make it the opening period.
- **Read the status statistics on the [Statistics](../statistics.md) dashboard.** It holds the detail table by activity, status and reason, compared with the previous period.
- **Build the recurring extractions in the [Explorer](../explorer.md).** A saved analysis keeps its fields, filters and view, can go into a dashboard and be sent by daily digest.
- **Keep the reports with the release.** The implementation and technical reports describe the instance and the release as they are; generate them after an upgrade and file them with the hand-over documents.

## NomaUBL — Audit Report
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/reports/audit-report/

Audit the electronic invoicing of a period from the NomaUBL tables — executive summary compared with the previous period, volumes, situation by status, backlog, lifecycle and delays, errors and their handling, operations and consistency checks — as a PDF or Markdown file, in French or English.

The **Audit report** card of the [Reports](./overview.md) page measures how the electronic invoicing of a period went: how many invoices were processed, deposited, approved, rejected or refused, what is still waiting for an action, how long each step took, which errors occurred and how they were handled. The figures come **only from the NomaUBL tables** at the time of generation; the platform is not queried.

The report is short whatever the volume — it lists no individual invoice — so it can be sent as is to a finance manager, an auditor or a steering committee. It applies to every source system (JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP).

Open it from **Reports → Audit report**.

---

## At a glance

The page shows **Settings** on the left, the **Contents** on the right and the action bar below.

| Control | Description |
|---|---|
| **Period** | The shared [period picker](../../configuration/default-periods.md#period-picker), **Last month** by default. Compared with the previous period of the same kind: a month with the previous month, other dates with the same number of days just before. |
| **Date basis** | In the footer of the period picker: **Issue date (BT-2)** *(default)* — an invoice belongs to the period by its issue date — or **Last update**. Statuses and amounts are always those of the generation day. |
| **Direction** | **Both** *(default)*, **Issued** or **Received**. |
| **Companies** | A multi-select of the companies (the `list-companies` [custom list](../../configuration/custom-lists.md#ready-made-lists)); empty = every company the signed-in user can see. The role's company visibility always applies. |
| **Language** | **Français** or **English**; defaults to the interface language. |
| **Contents** | One tile per section with a line on what it holds, all ticked by default; the header gives the count (`8 of 8 sections`) and the **All** / **None** links. |
| **Also run the SQL integrity checks against JDE (slower)** | Inside the *Consistency checks* tile, shown while it is ticked. Runs the checks configured under [Integrity reports](../../configuration/system/integrity-reports.md) on the period and adds their discrepancy counts. Each check queries the source system. |
| **Download PDF** / **Markdown** | Starts the generation **in the background**. A progress bar names the current step; the file downloads at the end and a copy is kept in `<appHome>/<env>/reports/nomaubl-audit-<date>-<time>.pdf` or `.md`. The rest of the application stays usable meanwhile. |

---

## Sections

### Scope

Environment, period and comparison period, date basis, companies, direction, generation date and author, release, and the tables read: invoice header (status and amounts), archive, VAT breakdown, lifecycle, validation findings.

### Executive summary

The key figures of the period next to the previous period and the variation:

| Indicator | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Invoices processed** | Invoices of the period, whatever their status. |
| **Not sent to the platform** | Invoices whose transaction type is configured not to be sent (B2C, international… per [Document types](../../configuration/system/document-types.md)). |
| **Deposited on the platform** | Invoices whose current status comes from the platform (`200` and following). The **deposit rate** is taken over the invoices **to send**. |
| **Deposited but not transmitted** | `200` with reason `NON_TRANSMISE`: the recipient is registered with no platform; the invoice has to be delivered through another channel. |
| **Approved / completed / paid**, **Refused (`210`)**, **Rejected (`213`)** | Outcomes of the period. |
| **To fix and resend** | `213`, `9905`, `9907`. |
| **Answer to the buyer expected** | `207`, `208`, `210`. |
| **In error today**, **Waiting for the platform (`9906`)**, **Excluded by rule (`9914`)**, **Received invoices** | States at generation time. |
| **Net and gross amounts deposited** | Totals BT-109 and BT-112 of the deposited invoices. |
| **First-pass validation** | Share of invoices validated without a fatal finding at their first run, taken from the lifecycle. |
| **Share in a terminal status** | Among the invoices to send. |
| **Delays** | Creation → deposit and deposit → first buyer status, median and 90th percentile. |
| **Send attempts, resends, send failure rate** | Every send ends in a failure (`9904`) or an acknowledgement (`9906`); the failure rate measures the platform's availability (HTTP 429, 503…). Resends include the automatic retries. |

A breakdown follows where every level adds up: not to send, to send, deposited (not transmitted, waiting for the next status, in progress at the platform, approved, rejected or refused), not deposited (validation, send or import failure, not sent yet, other). Then the **findings** in plain words — invoices in error not yet reviewed, deposited but not transmitted, to fix and resend, awaiting an answer to the buyer, failed e-reporting envelopes, backlog over all periods, resends, reprocesses and buyer-identifier fixes of the period.

### Volumes

The evolution inside the period — per day up to one month, per week up to six months, per month beyond — with the invoices, those to send, deposited and in error per bucket, and a chart. Then per **activity** (count, share, previous period, variation, amounts; deposit and error rates in a second table), per **company**, per **document**, per **transaction type** (with its send flag) and per **VAT category and rate** (base and VAT).

### Situation at generation time

The current status of the invoices of the period: code, label, catalogue groups, count, share, gross amount; the same per **family** (terminal, in progress, technical error, business error, excluded, other) with a donut chart; and the points of attention (waiting for the platform for more than 2 days, deposited but not transmitted, in error and not reviewed).

### Backlog, all periods

What still waits for an action **whatever its date**: invoices in error or refused not reviewed by customer service, waiting for the platform, deposited without being transmitted. Per status with the count older than 30 days, the reviewed count and the net amount; per company; per age (30 days or less, 31–90, 91–180, over 180) with a chart. The **Min invoice date** of the [e-invoicing settings](../../configuration/system/einvoicing.md) bounds these figures: older invoices are left out.

:::info[What « reviewed » means]
An invoice is *reviewed* once customer service has marked it handled in the invoice window. It leaves the backlog even if its status did not change (credit note issued outside NomaUBL, abandoned invoice, duplicate…).
:::

### Lifecycle and delays

The invoices of the period reaching each milestone for the first time — created, validated, validation failed, sent, deposited (first platform status), received, approved, refused, rejected, paid — per bucket with a chart; the delays creation → first send, first send → deposit, creation → deposit, deposit → first buyer status (median and 90th percentile, calendar days); then the action counters: send attempts and failures, resends, reprocesses (`9912`), buyer-identifier fixes.

### Errors and their handling

- **Validation findings by rule**: source (CIUS-FR, EXT-CTC-FR, CPRO-B2G, XSD, NomaUBL rules…), rule, level, findings, invoices, sample message; a chart of the most frequent rules and a per-source table of fatal findings and warnings. The findings of a reprocessed invoice are those of its last run.
- **Platform and buyer rejections and refusals**: status, reason code and label, events, invoices.
- **Send and import failures**: the 30 most frequent messages with their counts.
- **Handling**: invoices with an error in the period, resolved (status left the error statuses), still in error but reviewed, open for 7 days or less, 8 to 30 days, over 30 days; events per status; resends, reprocesses and fixes.

### Operations over the period

What the server did, independently of the invoice date: **scheduled job runs** (runs, errors, average and maximum duration, last outcome), **files processed and invoices integrated** per document with the previous period, **portal notifications** per rule, **e-reporting envelopes** per status. A failed envelope is flagged: its operations are not declared until it is fixed and filed again.

### Consistency checks

Each check counts the invoices that break a rule, for the period and over all periods; `0` means compliant.

| Check | What it finds |
|---|---|
| Platform status without platform identifier | The identifier is missing when the status was set by hand or by a status poll without an import confirmation. Not blocking. |
| Sent invoice without archived UBL | A sent invoice whose UBL is not stored. |
| Waiting for the platform for more than 2 days | Stale `9906`. |
| Duplicate invoice number within a company | Two invoices with the same number. |
| VAT total (BT-110) ≠ sum of the breakdown (BT-117) | Header against the stored VAT breakdown. |
| Net total (BT-109) ≠ sum of the lines (BT-131) | Header against the stored lines. |
| VAT breakdown with an amount but no rate (BT-119) | The invoice is declared with VAT and no rate. |
| To fix and resend without follow-up | `213`, `9905`, `9907` neither followed up nor reviewed. |
| Answer to the buyer expected without follow-up | `207`, `208`, `210` neither followed up nor reviewed; an internal credit note is mandatory for a refused invoice. |

With the integrity option, the **SQL integrity checks against JDE** follow, with their discrepancy count; the detail is on the [Integrity](./overview.md#integrity) tab. The lifecycle ordering and the platform events missing locally are left to the daily [lifecycle check](../../sync/scheduled-jobs/lifecycle-checks.md).

---

## PDF layout

Same layout as the [implementation report](./implementation-report.md): cover with environment, period, date, author and version; clickable table of contents; running header and footer; shaded reading notes; charts drawn in the PDF (bars per bucket and per activity, status-family donut, milestones per bucket, most frequent rules).

## Command line

```bash
java -jar nomaubl.jar -audit <configFile> [--from <yyyy-MM-dd> --to <yyyy-MM-dd>] \
     [--basis issue|update] [--kco a,b] [--direction I|R] [--lang fr|en] \
     [--format md|pdf] [--out <file>] [--date <label>] [--sections a,b,...] [--integrity]
```

Defaults: the previous month, every section, Markdown, French. See [Command line](../../management/command-line.md#audit).

The API runs the same report in the background: `POST /api/reports/audit/start` returns a job id, `GET /api/jobs/{id}` gives the current step, `GET /api/reports/audit/result/{jobId}` returns the file once.

---

## Access

The tab belongs to the *Reports* page — grant **Reports** on the [Roles](../../configuration/security/roles.md) page. The figures follow the company visibility of the signed-in user.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Generate it on the first working day of the month** for the previous month: the default period is exactly that.
- **Read the backlog with the findings.** The summary covers the invoices of the period; the backlog shows what older periods still leave open.
- **Mark the invoices handled outside NomaUBL as reviewed.** A credit note issued directly in the ERP does not change the status of the original invoice; marking it reviewed keeps the backlog meaningful.
- **Set the Min invoice date after a go-live.** Test or migration invoices dated before the go-live then stay out of the all-periods figures.
- **Each step's duration is written to the server log.** On a large instance, the [Server log](../diagnostics/server-log.md) shows which section takes the time.

## NomaUBL — Implementation Report
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/reports/implementation-report/

Generate the technical and functional documentation of a NomaUBL instance from its configuration and database — context, architecture, built-in rules, documents, UBL transform and mappings, platform settings, operations, security and reference data — as a PDF or Markdown file, in French or English, with secrets masked.

The **Implementation report** card of the [Reports](./overview.md) page writes the documentation of the instance you are signed in to: what is configured, how each document is turned into UBL, which rules apply, who can do what. Everything is read from the configuration files and the database at the time of generation, so the report always describes the instance as it runs — whatever the source system (JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP).

Typical uses: the hand-over file of a project, the description an auditor or a tax adviser asks for, the snapshot taken before an upgrade, the reference a support team keeps next to the production instance.

Open it from **Reports → Implementation report**.

---

## At a glance

| Control | Description |
|---|---|
| **Language** | **Français** or **English**. Defaults to the language of the interface. Labels of settings, statuses and lists follow the language. |
| **Date label (cover)** | Free text printed on the cover (e.g. *Go-live V2*). Blank = today's date. |
| **Show technical keys next to setting labels** | Adds the configuration key after each label (`Allow reprocess · allowReprocess`). Useful for a technical reader; off by default. |
| **Contents** | One tile per section with a line on what it holds; the first nine are ticked by default, the two appendices are optional because of their length. The header gives the count and the **All** / **None** links. |
| **Download PDF** / **Markdown** | Generates the file and downloads it. A copy is kept in the environment's `reports` folder (`<appHome>/<env>/reports/nomaubl-implementation-<date>-<time>.pdf` or `.md`). |

---

## What the report contains

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Environment, release and standard version (XP Z12-014), generation date, application home, database type and schema, companies, number of documents, author, and whether the instance is a demo instance. |
| **Architecture** | The flows enabled on the instance and their trigger: sending to the PA, import poll, status poll, received invoices, e-reporting, directory check, scheduled batch jobs, watched folders, JDE print queue reports, connectors per type, authentication. A flow shown as *off* is configured without a trigger and can still be run on demand. Then the processing chain: sources, transform, validation, archive tables, directions. |
| **How it works and built-in rules** | The functional guide: what every page is for (in menu order — Billing overview, Operations, IT dashboard, Statistics, … Explorer, Schematrons), the invoice lifecycle, the protection of deposited invoices, the rules of edit / fix buyer / resend / validate / set status / e-mail with the permission each one requires, the two reprocess modes, the status poll with the integrity and ordering checks, the review flag and notifications, a quick reference of the platform statuses (AFNOR XP Z12-014) and of the internal `99xx` stages, then **Dashboards, lists and exports**: sales or purchases, the comparison period, the five stages, *Exclude reviewed errors*, *Yesterday*, exports with labels, list views, and the table of the instance's [default periods](../../configuration/default-periods.md) (every view and per view, with their key). |
| **Documents** | One table of every document (source, direction, processing type, PDF template), the path variables with their value on this instance, then one subsection per document: folders, XSL and RTF files, UBL sheet, reprocess options, links to its pre-transform and UBL sheet, index fields and other settings. Then the PDF templates: documents that use each one, layout, logo, colours, sections and their options. |
| **UBL transform and rules** | Shared defaults (currency, specification identifier, schemes, defaults per BT), issuing companies, mapping tables and rules (transaction type, VAT category, exemption, payment means, unit of measure…), validation packs with their version and rule counts, house rules, coverage per document, then one subsection per pre-transform (renames, custom rules, drops) and per UBL sheet: profile, redefined mappings, and the full **source field → BT → UBL path** mapping. |
| **Platform settings** | E-invoicing settings (default and per company), e-reporting, directory, document types with their send and validation flags. |
| **Operations** | Scheduled jobs with their trigger, watched folders, notification rules with the actions they trigger, invoice actions, integrity checks, connectors with their host and authentication type, then the [Explorer](../explorer.md) analyses and dashboards saved on the instance. |
| **Security** | Authentication mode and session timeout, roles (pages, actions, companies, features, users), users with role, state and pending password change. |
| **Reference data** | The status catalogue (labels, PA codes, groups), every reference and custom list with its entries, the configured table names. |
| **Appendix: configuration keys** | Every property of every system template, secrets masked. |
| **Appendix: API reference** | The API document of the instance, operation by operation. |

:::info[Secrets are never printed]
Passwords, tokens, client secrets, API keys, URLs of connectors and instance keys appear as `••••••`. The report can be handed to a third party without editing; check only that the business content (customer e-mails in notification rules, user names) may be shared.
:::

---

## PDF layout

The PDF follows the document conventions of the product: a cover with the environment, date, author and version; a clickable table of contents and a PDF outline; a running header and a page *x / y* footer; reading notes in shaded boxes; path variables (`APP_HOME`, `ENV`, `PROCESS_HOME`, `TEMPLATE`, `FILE_NAME`) shown as chips inside paths; *see § 5.10* links between a document and its UBL sheet. The Markdown file carries the same content for a wiki or a Git repository.

## Command line

The same report is available without the interface, for a scheduled snapshot or a pipeline:

```bash
java -jar nomaubl.jar -report <configFile> [--lang fr|en] [--format md|pdf] [--out <file>] \
     [--date <label>] [--keys] [--sections context,architecture,...]
```

Defaults: the first nine sections, Markdown, French. See [Command line](../../management/command-line.md#report).

---

## Access

The tab belongs to the *Reports* page: grant **Reports** in the Navigation group on the [Roles](../../configuration/security/roles.md) page. The API route is `GET /api/reports/implementation`.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Generate it after each go-live and each upgrade.** The copy kept in the `reports` folder becomes the dated history of the configuration, next to [File versions](../../management/file-versions.md).
- **Keep the technical keys off for a business reader.** Labels are enough for a project team; turn the keys on for the people who edit configuration files or read the API.
- **Add the appendices for an audit file only.** The configuration-keys and API appendices make the PDF several times longer.

## NomaUBL — Technical Report
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/reports/technical-report/

The NomaUBL technical report — the developer documentation of the release generated from the code scans bundled at build: architecture, data model, flows, configuration reference, status model, impact matrix, API reference, command line, build and packaging, as PDF or Markdown, in French or English.

The **Technical report** card of the [Reports](./overview.md) page writes the **developer documentation of the release**: how NomaUBL is built, what each table and configuration key is for, which flows touch them, what the API offers. It is generated from the code scans bundled in the application at build — the same sources as the [Developer reference](../../references/developer.md) — so it is **identical on every instance of a release**, whatever the source system (JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP).

It complements the two other documents of the page: the [implementation report](./implementation-report.md) describes how *this* instance is configured, the [audit report](./audit-report.md) what happened over a period.
