## `-fetch-single` — extract one document, then process it

Equivalent of the *Application → Extract and Process* page. Extracts a single document from a source channel, drops the resulting file into `dirInput` (XML template) or `<dirInput>/ubl/` (UBL template), then immediately runs the matching pipeline. The XML-vs-UBL choice is **inferred from the template's `source` property** — no separate `processType` argument anymore.

```text
-fetch-single <configFile> <template> <source> <sourceArgs…> [<type>] [flags…]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| **`configFile`** | Absolute path to `config.json`. |
| **`template`** | Document name. Its `source` property selects the pipeline (XML or UBL). |
| **`source`** | Extraction channel — see table below. |
| **`sourceArgs`** | Source-specific arguments. |
| **`type`** | Processing type for XML templates (`AUTO` \| `SINGLE` \| `BURST` \| `UBL`). Ignored on UBL templates. |

**Source channels**

| Source | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **`archive <doc> <dct> <kco>`** | Document number, document type, company code. | Pull the source from the JDE archive directory. |
| **`ftp <report> <version> <language> <job>`** | Report code, version, language, JDE job number. | Download via FTP / SFTP. |
| **`bip <jobNumber>`** | JDE BIP job number. | Read from the BIP Print Queue (`F95630` / `F95631`). |

**Optional flags**

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--verbose` `--replace` `--no-send` | Same as `-process`. |
| `--validate` `--send` | UBL templates only. |
| `--input` *(default)* `--output` `--both` | BIP extraction mode — input XML, output documents, or both. |

**Examples**

```bash
# XML template — pull from the archive, AUTO routing
java -jar nomaubl.jar -fetch-single /opt/nomaubl/demo/config/config.json \
                      invoices archive 12345 RI 00070 AUTO --verbose

# UBL template — single BIP job, validate-only
java -jar nomaubl.jar -fetch-single /opt/nomaubl/demo/config/config.json \
                      ubl-invoices bip 19 --validate
```

---

## `-fetch-all` — batch extract + process

Equivalent of the *Application → Fetch Input* page. Extract **every** matching document from a source, then process them all. The XML / UBL choice is again inferred from the template — no `processType` argument. Returns exit code `1` if at least one document failed.

```text
-fetch-all <configFile> <template> <source> [<type>] [flags…]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| **`source`** | `directory` — scan `dirInput` (XML template) or `dirInput/ubl` (UBL template) for ready-to-process files. `bip` — pull every new BIP job whose number is greater than `lastBipJobNumber` (persisted in the *global* template after each successful run). |

For each `bip` job the wrapper resolves the **per-job template** from the BIP report filters when one is defined; otherwise it falls back to the `template` CLI argument. After a successful run, `lastBipJobNumber` in `config.json` is updated to the highest job number processed, so the next sweep only picks up new jobs.

The `bip` sweep also honours the **BIP Lookback (days)** floor from *Settings → Global → Batch Processing*: with a non-zero value, only jobs updated in the last N days are eligible, on top of the `lastBipJobNumber` watermark — handy on a first install or after a long gap to avoid walking years of history.

**Examples**

```bash
# Process every XML waiting in the input directory
java -jar nomaubl.jar -fetch-all /opt/nomaubl/demo/config/config.json \
                      invoices directory AUTO --verbose

# Drain new BIP jobs against a UBL template (validate + send)
java -jar nomaubl.jar -fetch-all /opt/nomaubl/demo/config/config.json \
                      ubl-invoices bip --send
```

---

## `-extract` — JDE BIP raw extraction

Low-level extraction from the JD Edwards BIP Print Queue (`F9563110` header, `F95630` input XML, `F95631` output files). Same engine as `fetch-single … bip`, but **without** running the processing pipeline afterwards — useful to drop a job's payload into a directory for off-line inspection.

```text
-extract <configFile> <jobNumber> [--input|--output|--both] [--type <outputType>] [--lang <language>] [outputDir]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| **`jobNumber`** | JDE job number (`RJJOBNBR`). |
| **`--input`** *(default)* | Extract the input XML only. |
| **`--output`** | Extract the generated output files only. |
| **`--both`** | Extract input + output. |
| **`--type <val>`** | Filter output files by type — `XML`, `PDF`, `EXCEL`, `HTML`, `RTF`, `PPT`, `ETEXT`. |
| **`--lang <val>`** | Filter by language code (e.g. `FR`). |
| **`outputDir`** | Optional output directory — defaults to `global.dirInput`. |

**Example**

```bash
java -jar nomaubl.jar -extract /opt/nomaubl/demo/config/config.json 19 \
                      --both --type PDF --lang FR /tmp/jde-19/
```

---

## `-pdf2xml` — JD Edwards PDF → XML adapter \{#pdf2xml\}

 Converts a JD Edwards EnterpriseOne report **PDF** into the same XML shape JDE emits natively when XML output is enabled — so a site can keep JDE in PDF-output mode and still feed the existing XML → XSL → UBL pipeline unchanged. Unlike the other modes it takes no environment: it is a standalone file-to-file converter.

```text
-pdf2xml <input.pdf> <output.xml> [<manifest.xml>]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| **`input.pdf`** | The JDE report PDF to read. |
| **`output.xml`** | Where to write the extracted XML. |
| **`manifest.xml`** *(optional)* | A JDE-native XML sample of the same report (R-program) version. When supplied, the output is byte-identical to JDE's native XML; without it, the OWObject DD alias is used as the element prefix. |

:::info[JDE-specific]
The adapter reads the `OWObject` metadata embedded in the PDF, so the JDE INI flag that disables PDFlib stream compression (Oracle's *third-party tag readers* option) must be on — otherwise the metadata is compressed away. The universal `_ID<oi>` suffix on each element is the contract in both modes, so XSLs that key on the OI suffix work with or without a manifest.
:::

**Example**

```bash
nomaubl.sh pdf2xml ./input/R42565.pdf ./output/R42565.xml
# byte-identical to JDE's native XML, with a manifest:
nomaubl.sh pdf2xml ./input/R42565.pdf ./output/R42565.xml ./manifests/R42565_FBL0001.xml
```

### Text mode — any PDF → flat XML \{#pdf2xml-text\}

```text
-pdf2xml <input.pdf> <output.xml> --text [--config <file> --template <name>]
```

Converts **any text PDF** — not only JD Edwards — into the flat XML of a [PDF-source template](./documents.md#pdf-extraction): labelled values, one table, every printed row. It gives the sample to load in the document editor and the XSL editor. With `--config` / `--template`, the template's PDF extraction settings apply (table anchors, layout match, regex fields); otherwise the defaults. Scanned PDFs are refused.

---

## Flags reference

A consolidated view of every CLI flag — which modes accept it, what it does.

| Flag | Modes | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **`--verbose`** | `xml`, `ubl`, `fetch-single`, `fetch-all` | Print processing messages on stdout. |
| **`--replace`** | `xml`, `ubl`, `fetch-single`, `fetch-all` | Overwrite the existing record (delete-then-insert for `ubl`; respects `replaceDocument` semantics for `xml`). |
| **`--validate`** | `ubl`, `fetch-single`, `fetch-all` | Validate only — no DB insert, no PA send. Implies `--no-send`. |
| **`--send`** | `ubl`, `fetch-single`, `fetch-all` | Force PA submission, overriding the configured default. |
| **`--no-send`** | `xml`, `ubl`, `fetch-single`, `fetch-all` | Skip PA submission. |
| **`--no-db`** | `xml` | Skip the database write step. Implies `--no-send`. |
| **`--input`** *(default)* | `extract`, `fetch-single` (bip), `fetch-all` (bip) | BIP extraction — input XML only. |
| **`--output`** | `extract`, `fetch-single` (bip), `fetch-all` (bip) | BIP extraction — output documents only. |
| **`--both`** | `extract`, `fetch-single` (bip), `fetch-all` (bip) | BIP extraction — input + output. |
| **`--type <t>`** | `extract` | Filter output files by type — XML, PDF, EXCEL, HTML, RTF, PPT, ETEXT. |
| **`--lang <l>`** | `extract` | Filter by language code. |

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Schedule sweeps via the `-serve` background scheduler rather than cron.** Configuring `fetchImportInterval` and `fetchStatusInterval` in the *global* template gives a single point of truth and survives an environment restart; running the same sweeps via cron risks overlapping with the in-process scheduler.
- **`fetch-all` is idempotent on `directory` source, append-only on `bip`.** A `directory` rerun re-picks files that are still in `dirInput` — typically nothing once they have been processed and removed. A `bip` rerun only fetches jobs newer than `lastBipJobNumber`, so a successful previous run is never repeated.
- **Use `--validate` when promoting UBL files between environments.** It exercises XSD + Schematron without writing to the DB or contacting the PA — a safe smoke test before flipping the real run.
- **Place `fetchAllParams` in the *global* template once, not on every cron entry.** The scheduler builds its batch run from this single JSON object, mirroring the *Configuration → System → Fetch Invoices* page.
- **Reserve `-extract` for inspection or recovery.** `fetch-single` and `fetch-all` already extract internally; the standalone `-extract` mode is for dropping a BIP job's payload onto disk for off-line review or replay.
- **Run `-install` on a fresh directory and edit `config/config.json` afterwards.** The installer never overwrites an existing `config.json`, so a stale config from a previous attempt will silently win — start from an empty `targetDir` to be sure.

---

## NomaUBL — Settings Overview
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/settings-overview/

How the NomaUBL Settings page is organised — a navigation by intent (Platform, Security, E-invoicing, E-reporting, Jobs & inbound, Views & UI, API, SQL and FTP connectors, Reference data, Custom data), a search over every field label, hint and key, Advanced folds for rarely used settings, and the header actions.

The **Settings** page holds the configuration of the instance: platform, security, e-invoicing, e-reporting, jobs, connectors and reference data. Open it from **Settings**, at the bottom of the side menu; it is shown to users whose role grants the settings.

Documents, PDF templates, actions, notification rules and watched folders are not on this page: they have their own pages in the **Management** group of the menu (see [Documents](../management/documents.md) and [PDF templates](../management/pdf-templates.md)). The jobs themselves — polls, batch jobs, digest, auto-retry, lifecycle checks — are run and edited from [Scheduled jobs](../sync/scheduled-jobs/overview.md).

---

## At a glance

---

## Navigation by intent

The navigation on the left groups the entries by **what you want to set**, not by storage. Every area starts collapsed and shows its entry count; an area opens on click, and opens by itself when another page links to one of its entries.

| Area | Entries |
|---|---|
| **Platform** | The [global settings](./system/global.md) tabs — *Directories & environment*, *Processing*, *Server log*, *PDF rendering*, *Email*, *AI assistant*, *License* — then **Promotion targets** (the instances the [Promotion](../management/promotion.md#targets) page can promote to) and the databases: [NomaUBL database](./database-connectors/nomaubl.md), [JD Edwards database](./database-connectors/jdedwards.md) and any other database connector. |
| **Security** | *Authentication* (global tab), [Single sign-on (OIDC)](./system/oidc.md), [Users](./security/users.md) and [Roles](./security/roles.md). |
| **E-invoicing** | [E-invoicing](./system/einvoicing.md), [Document types](./system/document-types.md), [Status catalogue](./system/statuses.md), [Directory lookup](./system/edirectory.md). |
| **E-reporting** | [E-reporting](./system/ereporting.md) and the *E-reporting status catalogue*. |
| **Jobs & inbound** | *Job defaults* (global tab), [JDE print queue (BIP)](./system/fetch-invoices.md), [Integrity checks](./system/integrity-reports.md). |
| **Views & UI** | [List views](./list-views.md) and [Navigation & lists](./default-periods.md#default-periods) (global tab *Periods*: start page, navigation auto collapse, default periods, rows per page and rows loaded of the lists, dashboard cache). |
| **API connectors** | One entry per [API connector](./api-connectors.md), with the `api` badge. |
| **SQL connectors** | One entry per [SQL connector](./sql-connectors.md), with the `sql` badge. |
| **FTP connectors** | *JD Edwards file transfer* and the other [FTP connectors](./ftp-connectors.md), with the `ftp` badge. |
| **Reference data** | The [reference lists](./reference-lists.md) shipped with NomaUBL, with the `list` badge. |
| **Custom data** | The [custom lists](./custom-lists.md), with the `custom` badge. |

Each entry shows a label and a one-line description; the system templates keep their technical name, shown in small type next to the editor title (for example *Job defaults* · `global`). A global entry opens **only its tab** of the global editor.

---

## Search

The box above the navigation — *Search a setting, a field, a template…* — matches the labels and descriptions of the entries, the template names, and **every field label, hint and key** of the editors. Areas with a match open, and under each entry a line says which fields matched, with their group (up to three):

> ↳ Processing log (days) (Retention) · Step timings (days) (Retention) · Job runs (days) (Retention)

Searching `retention`, `smtp` or `maxThreads` therefore lands on the right tab without knowing which template holds the setting.

---

## Advanced folds

Settings rarely changed are folded under an **Advanced** line, closed by default — for example the Ghostscript command of the *Processing* tab, or the TLS and corporate-proxy settings of the *AI assistant* tab (*Advanced — TLS / corporate proxy*). Open the fold to edit them; their values are kept whether the fold is open or not.

---

## Header and editor actions

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Add API** · **Add SQL** · **Add List** | Create an API connector, a SQL connector or a custom list. |
| **Add OIDC** · **Add integrity reports** · **Add promotion targets** | Shown while the instance has no single sign-on, integrity-check or promotion-target template; creates it. |
| **Copy** | Duplicate the selected template under a new name. Not available on the system templates. |
| **Remove** | Delete the selected template. Not available on the system templates. |
| **Description (optional)** | Free description of the template, shown under its entry. |
| **Save** | Save the template being edited. The status bar at the bottom of the editor reports the result. |

Every save is recorded in [File versions](../management/file-versions.md), and the connectors, lists and settings templates — except the global settings and single sign-on — can be carried to another environment with [Promotion](../management/promotion.md).

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Search before browsing.** The field index finds a setting from any word of its label or hint.
- **Leave the Advanced folds closed** unless the default no longer fits — they hold settings that rarely need changing.
- **Name custom connectors and lists clearly.** Their name is the label of their entry in the navigation.

## NomaUBL — E-Directory
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/edirectory/

Configure the connection to the French PPF (Portail Public de Facturation) directory and the INSEE company search used to validate addressing codes and look up customer information before sending an e-invoice. Two-tab layout: Directory (Enable Check + INSEE Search) and Connector (api-connector picker + per-task endpoint overrides).

The **E-Directory** editor configures two complementary services NomaUBL uses to validate recipient information before producing an e-invoice:

- **PPF (Portail Public de Facturation) directory** — verifies that the **electronic addressing code** carried by the document exists and is **active** in the public e-invoicing directory.
- **INSEE company search** — looks up a company by **business name, SIREN or SIRET** to retrieve its official identification data (legal name, address, registration status…).

The two are typically chained: an INSEE search resolves the customer's identifiers, then the PPF directory check confirms that the addressing code on the document is valid for that customer.

The page applies regardless of source system — JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP — once the source is mapped to UBL.

The editor has **two tabs**:

1. **Directory** — Enable Check toggle and INSEE search settings.
2. **Connector** — pick the api-connector that holds the PPF transport, plus per-task endpoint name overrides.

---

## Opening the editor

- *Settings* → **e-directory** template (the system-level resource).

---

## At a glance

---

## Tab 1 — Directory

### Directory Check

| Field | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Enable Check** | `Y` / `N` | When enabled, NomaUBL queries the PPF directory **before sending each invoice** to verify that the **electronic addressing code** on the document exists and is active in the public directory. Disable to skip the verification (useful for testing). |
| **Recipient not found** | `Warn and send (default)` / `Block the send — invoice stops at validation failed` | What happens when the check does not find the recipient. **Warn**: the miss is recorded as a warning finding `DIRECTORY_CHECK` and the invoice is sent. **Block**: on an invoice meant for the platform, a definitive answer — not registered, or found but not reachable — or a missing electronic address (`EndpointID`) is a fatal finding; the invoice stops at validation failed (`9905`) and is not sent. A connector or network error only warns in both modes, and invoices configured not to be sent are never blocked. |

### INSEE Search

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Results per page** | `10` | Maximum number of results returned per INSEE search query. Increase to widen each result page; decrease to limit network payloads. |

### Peppol lookup \{#peppol-lookup\}

Settings for the [Peppol lookup](../../application/edirectory.md#peppol-directory) of the E-Directory page, for servers on restricted networks (see [Network flows](../../application/edirectory.md#network-flows)).

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Resolve platform via SMP** | `Y` | `Y` reads the provider's name and seat from its SMP certificate — HTTPS to each provider's SMP host. `N` stops at the SML answer: the *Plateforme* column shows the SMP host (e.g. `smp.pennylane.com`), with no call to wait for. Set `N` when the network does not allow HTTPS to the providers' SMP hosts. |
| **Public DNS fallback** | `N` | `N` uses the server's resolver only. `Y` retries the SML lookups through `8.8.8.8` / `1.1.1.1` when that resolver gives no answer. Keep `N` when the network forbids external resolvers. |

---

## Tab 2 — Connector

The PPF directory's HTTP transport — authentication flow, base URL, endpoints — lives in a reusable [api-connector](../api-connectors.md). This page **references it by name only** and never carries auth fields or HTTP endpoints inline. The bundled `ppf-directory` connector covers the standard flow; pick a custom connector when the directory exposes non-standard auth or routes through a tenant gateway.

### API connector

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Connector** | Dropdown listing every `api-connector` template. The selected connector holds the directory's `baseUrl`, `authType`, credentials, token endpoint and the catalogue of HTTP endpoints. Edit the connector itself under [API Connectors](../api-connectors.md). |

### Per-lookup endpoint overrides

When the api-connector exposes endpoint names different from the defaults, set an override below. Leave a field blank to use the default name shown.

| Field | Default | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| **Directory check** | `directory-check` | The generic directory check (when the document already carries the routing identifier). |
| **Directory check (SIREN)** | `directory-check-siren` | Lookup branch when only a SIREN is known. |
| **Directory check (SIRET)** | `directory-check-siret` | Lookup branch when a SIRET is known. |

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Keep Enable Check on in production.** Sending an invoice with an inactive or unknown addressing code leads to a downstream rejection by the receiving Plateforme Agréée.
- **Use INSEE search to bootstrap customer records.** A lookup by SIREN / SIRET avoids transcription mistakes and aligns NomaUBL's data with the official registry.
- **Edit timeouts and TLS settings on the api-connector itself.** The HTTP-level parameters live on the [API Connectors](../api-connectors.md) page, not here — same connector can serve several pages, so the timeout and SSL Verify flag are set once.
- **Never disable SSL Verify in production.** It opens you to man-in-the-middle interception of credentials and document metadata. Set it on the api-connector, not here.
- **The PPF connector is bundled.** A fresh installation already ships a `ppf-directory` connector pointing at the standard endpoints — pick it from the dropdown and you are done. Custom connectors are only needed for non-standard transports.

---

## NomaUBL — E-Invoicing
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/einvoicing/

Configure how NomaUBL talks to a Plateforme Agréée (PA) — through a reusable api-connector reference, an optional SFTP fallback for outbound submission, and a status-retrieval section. Four-tab layout: UBL Validation · PA Connection · FTP/SFTP · Status. The api-connector holds the auth flow and endpoints; this page only references it by name and overrides per-task endpoint names when needed.

The **E-Invoicing** editor tells NomaUBL **how to talk to a Plateforme Agréée (PA)** — the certified platform that receives, validates and dispatches e-invoices to the French e-invoicing public infrastructure. It also defines the local UBL transformation step (XSL directory) and the parameters of the lifecycle-status retrieval loop.

The page applies regardless of source system — JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP — once the source is mapped to UBL.

The editor has **four tabs**:

1. **UBL Validation** — directory of XSL transforms used to convert the source XML into UBL.
2. **PA Connection** — picks the api-connector that holds the PA's HTTP transport, plus per-task endpoint name overrides and connection-level parameters.
3. **FTP/SFTP** — Send Mode toggle and the SFTP server credentials used when the toggle is set to `FTP`.
4. **Status** — Status-retrieval cursor and hint that points to the polling intervals on `global`.

---

## Opening the editor

- *Settings* → **e-invoicing** template (the system-level resource).
- The default scope is the platform-wide `e-invoicing` template. Per-company overrides live on `e-invoicing-{kco}` templates and follow the same shape; the runtime resolver looks at the per-company template first and falls back to the platform-wide one.

---

## At a glance

---

## Tab 1 — UBL Validation

This tab configures the **directory of XSL files** used to **transform the source XML into UBL**. The local UBL conformity check runs through standard schematrons and is documented separately on the [Validate](../../ubl-tools/validate.md) page.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **XSLT Directory** | Directory containing the `.xsl` transform files used to convert the source XML into UBL. The placeholder `%APP_HOME%` expands to the NomaUBL install root. |

### Manual / template-less invoice defaults

Applied when an invoice has **no document** — one created in the manual editor, or an already-formed UBL processed without a doc-template. A document's own values always take precedence.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Activity (FEAA10)** | Mandatory activity code written to the `F564230` log row. Without it a manual invoice can't save. |
| **Type (typePiece)** | Document type stamped on the log row. |
| **LISIBLE** | `Y` renders a readable PDF from the UBL and embeds it as the LISIBLE copy. |
| **PDF template** | Which template renders the LISIBLE — *Built-in*, or any custom one from [PDF Templates](../../management/pdf-templates.md). |
| **Locale** | Locale for the rendered PDF (e.g. `fr_FR`, `en_US`). |

---

## Tab 2 — PA Connection

### API connector

The PA's HTTP transport — authentication flow, base URL, endpoints — lives in a reusable [api-connector](../api-connectors.md). This page **references it by name only** and never carries auth fields or HTTP endpoints inline. The bundled `pa-default` connector covers the standard flow; pick another one when the PA exposes a non-standard auth scheme or when several PAs need different connectors.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Connector** | Dropdown listing every `api-connector` template. The selected connector holds the PA's `baseUrl`, `authType`, credentials, token endpoint and the catalogue of HTTP endpoints. Edit the connector itself under [API Connectors](../api-connectors.md). |

### Per-task endpoint overrides

Each PA task in NomaUBL has a default endpoint name. When the api-connector exposes a different name for the same task, set an override below. Leave a field blank to use the default name shown.

| Field | Default | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| **Import** | `import` | Submitting an invoice to the PA. |
| **Import status** | `import-status` | Polling whether the PA has accepted an import. |
| **Invoice statuses** | `invoice-statuses` | The lifecycle-status retrieval loop. |
| **Resolve invoice** | `resolve-invoice` | Looking up a PA-assigned identifier from a NomaUBL document key. **Optional** — when it is left undefined, pushing a status back to the platform uses the platform UUID captured at submission instead of a lookup, so a connector without a search endpoint still works. Platforms that require the lookup keep using it. |
| **Post status** | `post-status` | Pushing seller statuses (regulatory actions) back to the PA. |
| **Report import** | `report-import` | E-Reporting submission when the [e-reporting](./ereporting.md) template falls back to the e-invoicing connector. |

### Connection

Connection-level parameters that apply to **every call routed through the picked api-connector**.

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Timeout (ms)** | `30000` | HTTP request timeout in milliseconds. Long-running calls are aborted past this. |
| **SSL Verify** | `true` | Whether to validate the PA's TLS certificate. Set to `false` only in non-production environments using self-signed certificates. |

---

## Tab 3 — FTP/SFTP

### Send Mode

| Field | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Send Mode** *(`paMode`)* | `API` *(default)* / `FTP` / *(empty)* | Transport used to **send invoices to the PA**. `API` routes the submission through the api-connector picked on the previous tab; `FTP` spools the UBL to a temp file and uploads it via SFTP using the server below; *(empty)* skips outbound submission entirely (useful while wiring up a new document type). Status retrieval, import polling and seller actions always go through the API regardless of this choice. |

### SFTP Server

The whole card is dimmed when *Send Mode* ≠ `FTP` — these fields only apply to the SFTP transport.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Host** | SFTP host (e.g. `ftp.plateformeagree.fr`). |
| **Port** | SFTP port. Default `22`. |
| **User** | SFTP user. |
| **Password** | SFTP password. |
| **Outbound Dir** | Remote directory where NomaUBL drops UBL files for the PA (e.g. `/out/invoices/`). |
| **Inbound Dir** | Remote directory where the PA writes status updates that NomaUBL pulls back (e.g. `/in/status/`). |

---

## Tab 4 — Status

The **Status Retrieval** section drives the lifecycle-status retrieval loop.

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Page size** | `100` | Number of statuses fetched per page when polling the PA. For an AFNOR flow search (a `limit`, no offset) it must match what the endpoint sends as `limit` through the `{{pageSize}}` placeholder: in *Last event* mode a full page is followed by a new search from its newest event until a page comes back short, so a burst larger than one page is never cut. |
| **Last retrieved at** | *(updated automatically)* | ISO datetime of the most recent successful retrieval (e.g. `2025-01-01T00:00:00Z`). Updated automatically after each retrieval run; manual edits act as a starting point — useful to re-replay a window. Kept **per status source**: a company override that polls through its own status connector or endpoint keeps its own date (on its first run it starts from the default's), while overrides sharing the default connector follow the default template's date. A failed page holds back only that source. |
| **Status connector** | *(blank = same as the PA connector)* | Connector used **only** for lifecycle status retrieval. Set it on a company override when the PA issues separate status credentials per company (Esker): sending keeps the shared PA connector, statuses go through this one. |
| **Watermark advance** | `Now` *(default)* | Search mode only. *Now* moves the cursor to the poll time. *Last event* moves it to the source `updatedAt` of the newest fetched item — for PAs that cap their search without paging (Yooz: 200 flows), so a burst is drained over successive polls instead of losing its tail. Needs the connector mapping `event.updatedAt` (e.g. `item.updatedAt`) and items returned oldest-first. |
| **Import status mode** | `per-invoice` *(default)* | `per-invoice` polls each pending invoice by its stored transaction id. `search` instead asks the platform for every flow updated since the last check (the date is kept between runs) and matches the results to the pending invoices — for platforms with no per-invoice status lookup, such as Yooz Rising. |
| **Import parallel** | *(default `4`, max `8`)* | How many pending invoices (status 9906) the import-status check polls **at the same time**. Raise it to clear a large pending backlog faster; set `1` for the previous one-at-a-time behaviour. |
| **Poll parallel** | *(default `4`)* | Same setting for the per-invoice lifecycle poll — how many invoices its status is fetched for concurrently. |
| **Min invoice date** | *(empty = no cutoff)* | An **ingestion cutoff**: an XML-pipeline invoice dated before this date is skipped at the door — no database write, no generation, no PA send. It guards re-runs of old BIP jobs and legacy archives (a document with an archive row but no header would otherwise look "never sent" and be resent). Empty or unparseable invoice dates are never blocked. |
| **Lifecycle endpoints** | *(blank = `invoice-statuses`)* | Connector endpoint name(s) to poll for lifecycle events, comma-separated. Add `invoice-statuses-selfbilled` next to `invoice-statuses` when the platform splits its sales and purchase (self-billing) lifecycle across separate endpoints, so both are collected. Unknown endpoints are skipped. |

:::info[Self-billed invoices route to their own endpoints]
A self-billed invoice (type 261, 389, 471, 473, 500, 501 or 502) is submitted through the platform's procurement channel: NomaUBL automatically uses the `-selfbilled` variant of an endpoint (`import-selfbilled`, `import-status-selfbilled`) when the connector defines it, and falls back to the standard endpoint otherwise. The platform connection — URL and credentials — is unchanged; only the endpoints differ.
:::

:::info[Polling intervals live on `global`]
The intervals that drive how often the background scheduler polls the PA — `fetchImportInterval`, `fetchStatusInterval`, e-reporting cadence — are global settings edited from each job of the [Scheduled jobs](../../sync/scheduled-jobs/overview.md) page; they apply across all companies.
:::

---

## Action bindings

Multi-call action bindings are edited on their own page under [Management → Action Bindings](../../management/actions.md). They are stored on this template (`action.N.id` / `.connector` / `.endpoint` / `.params`). That page handles the multi-call list, the per-call *Stop on failure* flag, and the response chaining via `{call.N.fieldName}` placeholders.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Pick the api-connector first.** Without a connector, the *Per-task endpoint overrides* fields stay hidden and the PA cannot be reached. The bundled `pa-default` connector is a reasonable starting point.
- **Leave the per-task overrides blank when the connector's endpoint names already match.** A `pa-default` connector with an endpoint literally named `import` does not need an override on the *Import* row. The page only stores values that differ from the default — typing the default name is harmless but adds noise.
- **Start with `paMode=` (empty)** when first wiring up a new document type. The UBL pipeline runs end-to-end without involving the PA, so source mappings and Schematron failures surface before the network is in the loop. Flip to `API` once the data side is clean.
- **Use SFTP only when the PA actually requires it.** REST is simpler to debug, and the api-connector test runner gives clear feedback. SFTP is appropriate when the PA mandates file drop or for high-volume batch submissions.
- **Edit polling intervals on the Scheduled jobs page, not here.** Open the *PA import poll* or *PA status retrieval* job; saving reloads the schedules at once.
- **Test against a Postman mock or a local stub** when offline: point the api-connector at the mock URL.
- **Per-company overrides go on `e-invoicing-{kco}`.** Copy the platform-wide `e-invoicing` template under the new name from *Settings* and edit only the fields that differ — typically `connector`, a couple of endpoint overrides, or the SFTP credentials when company `00070` uses a separate PA.

---

## NomaUBL — E-Reporting
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/ereporting/

Configure how NomaUBL produces and submits e-Reporting bundles — Sender / Issuer identity, schedule, the api-connector that holds the PA's HTTP transport, and the SFTP fallback for outbound submission. Four-tab layout: Identity · Reporting · PA Connection · FTP/SFTP. paMode = API / FTP / empty replaces the legacy sendToPA Y/N flag.

The **E-Reporting** editor configures how NomaUBL **produces and submits the periodic e-Reporting bundles** required by the French e-invoicing reform. Each company files a regulatory report covering its B2BINT, B2C and out-of-scope flows on a fixed cadence (monthly by default); this page controls the sender / issuer identity emitted in the bundle, the cadence, and the PA transport used to upload the bundle once generated.

The page applies regardless of source system — JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP — once the source is mapped to UBL.

The editor has **four tabs**:

1. **Identity** — Sender (PA) and Issuer (Declarant) identification fields emitted in the bundle.
2. **Reporting** — Business Process (B2BINT) plus Schedule.
3. **PA Connection** — picks the api-connector that holds the PA's HTTP transport, plus the per-task endpoint name override and connection-level parameters.
4. **FTP/SFTP** — Send Mode toggle and the SFTP server credentials used when the toggle is set to `FTP`.

---

## Opening the editor

- *Settings* → **e-reporting** template (the system-level resource).
- A **Scope** bar at the top picks the setup being edited: **Default (e-reporting)** or **Company *kco* (e-reporting-*kco*)**. Type a company code and click **Add override** to create a company setup seeded from the default; **Delete override** removes the selected one. Each company can thus carry its own issuer, frequency and PA connection.
- The runtime looks at the company setup first and falls back to the default. The companies to run are detected from the company setups; **Companies (kco) override**, on the default, only names the companies to run **with the default settings** — a company with its own setup uses that setup instead.

---

## At a glance

---

## Tab 1 — Identity

The Identity tab carries the actors emitted on every report bundle. Both blocks are rendered as XML elements inside the AFNOR XP Z12-014 envelope (`<Sender>` and `<Issuer>`).

### Sender (PA)

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Matricule** | — | PA matricule (4 chars), emitted as `<Sender><Id schemeId="0238">`. |
| **Name** | — | Optional. Emitted as `<Sender><Name>`. |
| **Role Code** | `WK` | Default `WK` (PA). Emitted as `<Sender><RoleCode>`. |

### Issuer (Declarant)

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Identifier (SIREN)** | — | Declarant identifier emitted as `<Issuer><Id schemeId="0002">`. |
| **Name** | — | Optional. Emitted as `<Issuer><Name>`. |
| **Scheme ID** | `0002` | ISO 6523 ICD scheme. Default `0002` (SIREN France). |
| **Role Code** | `SE` | `SE` for sales reporting (default), `BY` when reporting purchases. |
| **Companies (kco) override** | *(empty)* | Comma-separated list of companies to process. Leave blank to auto-detect from invoices and per-company override templates. |

---

## Tab 2 — Reporting

### Business Process (B2BINT only)

These fields are emitted on per-invoice `<BusinessProcess>` elements, **only for `B2BINT`** invoices.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Business Process ID** | Optional. TT-28 *cadre de facturation* (e.g. `B1`, `P1`). |
| **Business Process Type ID** | Optional. TT-29 specification identifier. |
| **Flow Name** | Optional. TT-2 emitted as `<ReportDocument><Name>`. |

### Schedule

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Frequency** | `MONTHLY` | Drives the period auto-computed by the scheduler and the *Generate* dialog default. |
| **Default Type Code** | `IN` | Default report type code. |

Each report carries both flows — 10.1 (B2B international, detail) and 10.3 (B2C, aggregated) — for one company and one direction; the direction is chosen in the *Generate* dialog of [E-Reporting](../../application/ereporting.md#generate-dialog).

---

## Tab 3 — PA Connection

### API connector

The PA's HTTP transport — authentication flow, base URL, endpoints — lives in a reusable [api-connector](../api-connectors.md). E-Reporting **picks its own connector** rather than sharing the one set on [E-Invoicing](./einvoicing.md), so reporting can target a different platform — or use different credentials on the same platform — than invoice import.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Connector** | Dropdown listing every `api-connector` template. Use a different connector than e-invoicing if the reporting flow goes to a separate platform or uses different credentials. Edit the connector itself under [API Connectors](../api-connectors.md). |

### Per-task endpoint override

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Report import** | `report-import` | Endpoint name on the picked connector for report submission. Leave blank to use the default. |

### Connection

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Timeout (ms)** | `30000` | HTTP request timeout in milliseconds. Long-running submissions are aborted past this. |
| **SSL Verify** | `true` | Whether to validate the PA's TLS certificate. Set to `false` only in non-production environments using self-signed certificates. |

---

## Tab 4 — FTP/SFTP

### Send Mode

| Field | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Send Mode** *(`paMode`)* | `API` *(default)* / `FTP` / *(empty)* | Transport used to **submit generated reports** to the PA. `API` routes the bundle through the api-connector picked on the previous tab; `FTP` spools the report XML to a temp file and uploads it via SFTP using the server below; *(empty)* lets NomaUBL **generate reports without submitting them** — useful while validating the identity before involving the PA. |

The `paMode` field works the same way as on the E-Invoicing page.

### SFTP Server

The whole card is dimmed when *Send Mode* ≠ `FTP` — these fields only apply to the SFTP transport.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Host** | SFTP host (e.g. `ftp.plateformeagree.fr`). |
| **Port** | SFTP port. Default `22`. |
| **User** | SFTP user. |
| **Password** | SFTP password. |
| **Outbound Dir** | Remote directory where NomaUBL drops report bundles for the PA (e.g. `/out/reports/`). |
| **Inbound Dir** | Remote directory where the PA writes acknowledgements (e.g. `/in/reports/`). |

---

## Configuration check

The configuration check on the [IT dashboard](../../application/tech-dashboard.md) validates the template against these rules:

- `paMode=API` without a `connector` is reported as an error (the API transport has nothing to call).
- `paMode=FTP` without `paFtpHost` is reported as an error (the SFTP transport has no server).
- `paMode=` (empty) with a `connector` is fine — reports generate locally and are not submitted.
- `issuerSiren` and the `connector` are checked whenever `paMode` is non-empty (i.e. the bundle will actually be submitted).

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Pick a separate api-connector when the reporting platform differs.** A multi-platform install often has e-invoicing on one PA and e-reporting on another — that's why each system template carries its own connector reference. Set both to the same connector name when they share a platform.
- **Start with `paMode=` (empty)** when first wiring the company up. NomaUBL generates the report locally so the identity can be validated against a sample without touching the PA. Flip to `API` once the bundle reads correctly.
- **Use SFTP only when the PA mandates file drop.** REST submission is simpler to debug and works with the api-connector test panel; SFTP is appropriate for high-volume submissions or when the PA does not expose a REST report-import endpoint.
- **Per-company overrides go on `e-reporting-{kco}`.** Copy the platform-wide `e-reporting` template under the new name from *Settings* and edit only the fields that differ — typically `issuerSiren`, the `connector` reference, or the SFTP credentials when company `00070` reports through a different platform.
- **Frequency drives the auto-computed period.** Setting it to `MONTHLY` makes the scheduler emit one bundle per month covering the previous month; `QUARTERLY` extends the window. The *Generate* dialog still lets the user override the period at run time.
- **Companies (kco) override is rarely needed.** NomaUBL auto-detects companies from the invoices it processes and from the existence of `e-reporting-{kco}` templates. Set the field manually only when reporting must be limited to a subset (e.g. one division during a phased rollout).

---

## NomaUBL — Fetch Invoices
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/fetch-invoices/

Configure which JD Edwards BI Publisher (BIP) jobs NomaUBL retrieves for batch processing, and which document to use for each.

The **Fetch Invoices** editor controls which **JD Edwards BI Publisher (BIP)** jobs NomaUBL pulls in for processing. It is used by the batch import and the background scheduler to decide *which BIP outputs are eligible* and *how each one should be parsed*.

A job is picked up once its BI Publisher output is done (`D`, `FD`). A job in **`FX`** — the UBE ran but the BI Publisher transformation failed — still stores its source XML, which is all the UBL flow needs: batch scans and single extracts in **input** (or both) mode accept it too. Output-only extracts keep `D` / `FD` and report an explicit error on an `FX` job.

:::info[JD Edwards–specific page]
This page is one of the **JDE-specific** parts of NomaUBL — it talks to a JD Edwards BIP server. The other configuration pages are source-agnostic.
:::

---

## At a glance

---

## BIP Report Filters

A list of the BIP reports NomaUBL is allowed to pick up. Each row is a filter: NomaUBL only enqueues BIP jobs whose **Report** name (and optionally **Version**) matches one of the rows. If the table is **empty**, NomaUBL fetches **all jobs** — handy for testing, almost never what you want in production.

### Per-row fields

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| **Report** | Name of the BIP report (e.g. `R42565`). |
| **Version** | Specific report version to allow (e.g. `FBL00001`). Disabled when **All Versions** is checked. |
| **All Versions** | When ticked, every version of the report is accepted and the **Version** field is cleared / disabled. |
| **Template** | The NomaUBL **document** used to **produce the PDF attachment** when generating the UBL from this BIP output. **Required** when the document type produces a UBL with a PDF attachment (the dropdown lists templates of type `document` defined in your environment — see *Configuration → Documents*). |

Use the **+ Add Report** button to append a row, and the **×** button on a row to remove it.

### How it's used

- **Batch processing** — when you run the import manually, only jobs whose Report (and Version, unless All Versions is set) match a row are queued.
- **Scheduler** — when serve mode is enabled, the same filter applies on each polling tick.
- **Template** — once a job matches, NomaUBL uses the configured **document** to produce the PDF that gets attached to the UBL during generation. The template provides the RTF / XSL chain defined in *Configuration → Documents*. It is **required** whenever the document type produces a UBL with a PDF attachment.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Always configure at least one filter in production.** Leaving the list empty pulls in every BIP job from the connected JDE environment, which is usually too broad.
- **Use All Versions sparingly.** It's useful when you have many ad-hoc versions of the same report; otherwise, prefer pinning a specific Version per row so you know exactly what's being processed.
- **One row per (Report, Version, Template) tuple.** If the same report needs different templates for different versions, add multiple rows.
- **Don't forget to assign a Template.** A row without a template can still match jobs, but the UBL generation will fail to produce a PDF attachment when one is expected.

---

## NomaUBL — Integrity Reports
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/integrity-reports/

Integrity reports are read-only SQL checks that list what is missing or wrong in NomaUBL compared with a source system — print jobs never integrated, amounts that differ — shown on Reports → Integrity, with an optional action on the selected rows.

The **Integrity reports** system template holds a list of **SQL checks** that compare NomaUBL with a source system and list what is **missing or wrong**: print jobs that were never integrated, accounting records whose amounts differ from the e-invoices… Each check runs read-only `SELECT` statements — a single query, or a source query and a target query on two different databases compared in memory — and **every row it returns is one anomaly**. The results are shown on the **Integrity** tab of the [Reports](../../application/reports/overview.md#integrity) page, where a check can also carry an **action** on the selected rows.

Open it under **Configuration → System → Integrity reports**. On an installation that does not have the template yet, an **Add integrity reports** button creates it without restarting the service. The template ships empty: nothing appears on the Reports page until a check is defined.

---

## At a glance

---

## Global settings

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Max rows** | `5000` | Row cap per run. A larger result is cut and flagged *result truncated at the row cap* on the Reports page. |
| **Timeout (s)** | `120` | Statement timeout, in seconds. |

---

## Modes \{#modes\}

The **Mode** field of a check decides how its rows are produced.

| Mode | Result |
|---|---|
| **Direct** *(default)* | One query; its rows are the anomalies. For two systems in the same database. |
| **Missing** | Source rows whose key is absent from the target. |
| **Extra** | Target rows whose key is absent from the source. |
| **Mismatch** | Keys present on both sides whose compared columns differ. |

The three comparison modes run a **source query** and a **target query**, each on its own connector — JD Edwards on SQL Server and NomaUBL on PostgreSQL, for instance — and match their rows **in memory** on the key columns. Keys are normalised before matching: trailing spaces, leading zeros, decimal scale and date formats no longer get in the way.

---

## Checks

Each check is a collapsible group — click its title to open it, **×** removes it, **+ Add check** appends one.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Name** | Identifier shown on the Reports page (e.g. `missing-pdf`). Keep it stable. |
| **Description** | One line explaining what the check finds (e.g. *PDF print jobs not integrated*). |
| **Start from** | Optional. Pre-fills the check from a known JD Edwards comparison — see [Query templates](#query-templates). |
| **Mode** | *Direct*, *Missing*, *Extra* or *Mismatch* — see [Modes](#modes). |
| **Connector** | The [database connector](../database-connectors/nomaubl.md) the `SELECT` runs against — the JD Edwards database, the NomaUBL database or any other connector declared on the platform. |
| **Key columns** | Optional. Comma-separated result columns that identify the record an action works on (e.g. `JCPID, JCVERS, JCJOBNBR`, or document number + type + company). |
| **SQL (SELECT only)** | The query. A single `SELECT` (or `WITH`) statement; anything else is refused before it reaches the database. The connection is opened read-only. |
| **Action** | What the Reports page can do with the selected rows: *none*, or **Integrate BIP jobs**. |

In the comparison modes, **Connector**, **Key columns** and **SQL** become **Source connector**, **Source key columns** and **Source SQL**, and further fields appear:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Target connector** | Database connector of the target query — it may differ from the source. |
| **Target key columns** | Columns of the target result matching the source key columns, in the same order. Empty = same names. |
| **Target SQL** | The target query (e.g. `SELECT TRIM(FEWDS1) AS JOBKEY FROM F564230 WHERE FEUPMJ >= {fromJde}`). The date placeholders apply to both queries. |
| **Compare columns** *(Mismatch)* | Comma-separated `SOURCE=TARGET` column pairs (e.g. `AMOUNT_HT=UHATXA, DOC_DATE=UHDIVJ`). A row is an anomaly when any pair differs. |
| **Tolerance** *(Mismatch)* | Numeric values differing by at most this amount are equal. Default `0.01`. |

In *Mismatch* mode, the result carries the source columns, then one `TARGET_<column>` column per compared pair with the target value, and a `DIFFERENCE` column naming the columns that differ.

### Date placeholders

The SQL can use the period picked on the Reports page. Placeholders are replaced before the run; without a period, the range is `1900-01-01` → today.

| Placeholder | Format | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `{from}` / `{to}` | `yyyy-MM-dd` | `2026-09-01` |
| `{fromJde}` / `{toJde}` | JDE Julian date (`CYYDDD`) | `126244` |
| `{fromDMY}` / `{toDMY}` | `dd-MM-yyyy` | `01-09-2026` |

The SQL field suggests the usual shape of a check — the source records of the period that never reached the NomaUBL log (`F564230`):

```sql
SELECT … FROM … WHERE JCSTDTIM > TO_DATE('{fromDMY}','dd-MM-yyyy')
  AND … NOT IN (SELECT TRIM(FEWDS1) FROM PRODDTA.F564230 WHERE FEUPMJ > {fromJde})
```

The **Insert placeholder** picker, under the label of each SQL field, lists every placeholder with its format and inserts it at the cursor.

### BIP placeholders \{#bip-placeholders\}

:::info[JDE-specific]
These placeholders read the report list of the [JDE print queue (BIP)](./fetch-invoices.md) settings.
:::

Three more placeholders follow the BIP setup, so a check never needs a hand-kept list of reports and versions:

| Placeholder | Replaced by |
|---|---|
| `{bipReports}` | The configured report names, quoted, for an `IN` list: `'R42565','R03B505'`. |
| `{bipFilter:REPORTCOL,VERSIONCOL}` | The predicate the BIP scan uses, on the named columns: `((TRIM(REPORTCOL)='R42565' AND TRIM(VERSIONCOL)='XJDE0001') OR TRIM(REPORTCOL)='R03B505')`. A row set to all versions matches on the report alone. |
| `{bipTemplate:REPORTCOL,VERSIONCOL}` | A `CASE` expression giving the document of each row, from the document set on each report row. |

With no report configured, the filter becomes `1=0` and the list `NULL`: the check returns nothing rather than every job.

### Query templates \{#query-templates\}

The **Start from** list pre-fills a check — mode, connectors, key columns, SQL and action — from a known comparison:

| Template | Check |
|---|---|
| **BIP jobs not integrated (F986114 vs F564230)** | The BIP print jobs of the configured reports that never reached NomaUBL, with the *Integrate BIP jobs* action. Uses `{bipFilter}` and `{bipTemplate}`. |
| **Accounting invoices not in NomaUBL (F03B11 vs F564231)** | Customer ledger invoices of the period absent from NomaUBL. |
| **Sales-order invoices not in NomaUBL (F4211/F42119 vs F564231)** | Invoices written by sales order update, open and history lines, absent from NomaUBL. |
| **Amounts JDE vs NomaUBL (F03B11 vs F564231, mismatch)** | Invoices present on both sides whose amounts differ. |

On a check that already has SQL, the editor asks for confirmation before replacing it (*Replace this check?*). The schema prefixes (`PRODDTA`, `SVM920`) and the status codes are the usual ones: adjust them to the JD Edwards environment, then save.

### Action *Integrate BIP jobs*

:::info[JDE-specific]
This action extracts JD Edwards BI Publisher jobs. Checks without an action work on any source system.
:::

When **Action** is set to **Integrate BIP jobs**, the selected rows are integrated exactly like the command `fetch-single <template> bip <job>` (see [Command line](../../management/command-line.md)), through the [Fetch Invoices](./fetch-invoices.md) batch. Five fields map the result columns:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Job column** | Result column holding the JDE job number (`RJJOBNBR`). Required. |
| **Template column** | Result column holding the document name. Leave empty to use the fixed template. |
| **Fixed template** | Document used when the template column is empty or missing. |
| **Host column** | Result column holding the JDE execution host — only on JD Edwards installations with several hosts. Optional. |
| **Processing type** | `AUTO` *(default)*, `SINGLE`, `BURST`, `UBL` or `BOTH`. |

---

## On the Reports page \{#reports-integrity\}

  
    Check
    missing-pdf ▾
    📅 Last 30 days
    ▶ Run
    Show SQL
  
  Connector: db-jde · Key columns: JCPID, JCVERS, JCJOBNBR · Action: fetch-single invoices bip {'{JCJOBNBR}'}
  
    3 anomaly(ies)
    
    Integrate selection (2)
  
  
    JCPIDJCVERSJCJOBNBRJCSTDTIM
    ☑R42565ZJDE000113533062026-10-08 06:12
    ☑R42565ZJDE000113534122026-10-09 06:10
    ☐R42565ZJDE000213535202026-10-10 06:11
  

1. **Pick a check** and a **period** (last 30 days by default), then **Run**. **Show SQL** displays the query of the check.
2. The header line recalls the connector, the key columns and the configured action. On a comparison check, a second line adds the mode, the target connector and, for *Mismatch*, the compared columns with the tolerance; **Show SQL** then displays both queries, and the count reads *N source / N target*. The result reads **No anomaly** or *N anomaly(ies)*, every row being one anomaly in the standard grid — search, filters, column chooser and export.
3. When the check carries an action, tick the rows and click **Integrate selection (N)**. A confirmation recalls that the jobs are extracted and processed like a normal run — validation, storage and sending follow the template settings.
4. After the action, the check runs again: integrated rows drop out of the result, and a summary banner shows *N integrated, N failed out of N*, with the name of every failed job.

---

## API

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/reports/integrity` | Lists the configured checks (name, description, connector, key columns, SQL). |
| `POST /api/reports/integrity/run` | Runs one check — body `{ "name", "dateFrom", "dateTo" }` — and returns the result columns and rows. |
| `POST /api/reports/integrity/action` | Runs the check's action on the selected rows — body `{ "name", "jobs": [...], "templates": [...], "hosts": [...] }` — and returns the per-job result and the summary. |

See the [API reference](/nomaubl/api-reference) for the full schemas.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **One question per check.** A check that answers a single question (*jobs not integrated*, *amounts that differ*) gives a result that can be acted on row by row.
- **Return the key columns.** Even without an action, key columns make each anomaly easy to trace back to its source record.
- **Bound the query with the period.** The date placeholders keep the query on the window the user picked and well under the timeout.
- **Point the action at the job number, not a label.** The job column must contain the JDE job number; rows without one are ignored by *Integrate selection*.

---

## NomaUBL — Global
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/global/

Application-wide NomaUBL settings in ten tabs: directories and environment, processing, server log, PDF rendering, email, AI assistant, job defaults (quiet window, bulk send, retention, BIP watermarks), license, authentication and default periods.

The **Global** settings hold what applies to the **whole NomaUBL application**: file system layout and environment, processing options, the server log, PDF rendering, the email server, the AI assistant, the defaults shared by the scheduled jobs, the license and the authentication. They apply whatever the source system — JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP; the few BIP-specific settings are flagged where they appear.

The editor has **ten tabs**: Directories, Processing, Logs, PDF, Email, AI, Job defaults, License, Authentication, Periods. In the [Settings navigation](../settings-overview.md) each tab is an entry of its own — *Directories & environment*, *Processing*, *Server log*, *PDF rendering*, *Email*, *AI assistant* and *License* in **Platform**, *Authentication* in **Security**, *Job defaults* in **Jobs & inbound**, *Navigation & lists* in **Views & UI** — and opens that part only, without the row of tabs. The search box of Settings finds any field of these tabs by its label, hint or key.

The jobs themselves — polls, batch document jobs, daily digests, auto-retries, lifecycle checks, retention purge — are not set here: they are on the [Scheduled jobs](../../sync/scheduled-jobs/overview.md) page.

---

## At a glance

---

## Tab 1 — Directories

### Home Directories

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Application Home** | Root install directory of NomaUBL (e.g. `/app/nomaubl`). Resolved by the `%APP_HOME%` placeholder used in document paths. |
| **Demo instance** | `N` (default) / `Y`. Marks the instance as a demonstration instance: only then can it be filled with fictitious invoices — see [Demo corpus](../../installation/demo-corpus.md). Never on a customer instance. |
| **Environment** | Short environment name (e.g. `demo`, `PD`). Resolves the `%ENV%` placeholder used in document paths (`rtf`, `xsl`, `ublXslt`) so the same template can target multiple environments. The name is also shown as a **badge right of the application title** and in the browser tab. |
| **Theme colour** | Colour picker, next to the environment. Replaces the accent blue of the whole interface — title, environment badge, primary buttons, links, focus rings — so each environment is told apart at a glance. Badge and colour are served by a public endpoint, so the login page already carries them. Blank keeps the default blue. |
| **Process Home** | Working directory used by NomaUBL during processing (e.g. `/app/nomaubl/process`). |

The path fields — *Process Home*, the directories below and the *Server log file* of the Logs tab — carry the **insert placeholder** button `{ }`: it lists `%APP_HOME%`, `%ENV%` and `%PROCESS_HOME%` and inserts the one picked at the cursor.

When *Demo instance* is `Y`, the tab also shows a **Demo corpus** block that fills or resets the demonstration data as a background job — see [Demo corpus](../../installation/demo-corpus.md#from-the-settings).

### File Paths

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Input Directory** | Where new documents to process are dropped (XML spools, attachments…). |
| **Process Directory** | Where in-flight files live during processing. |
| **Temp Directory** | Scratch space for temporary artefacts. |
| **Single Output Dir** | Output directory for documents processed in *single* mode. |
| **Bursting Directory** | Output directory for documents produced by *bursting* mode (one file per invoice). |
| **Errors Directory** | Where a file that fails processing is moved. During a directory run, moving the failed file aside stops a repeated scan from retrying the same file endlessly. Leave it blank to keep the file in place (the previous behaviour). |

---

## Tab 2 — Processing

### XSL Paths

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **XDO Config** | Path to the BI Publisher `xdo.cfg` configuration file used during PDF generation. |

### Options

| Field | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Update DB** | `Y` / `N` | When `Y`, processing runs persist their results to the database. Set to `N` only for dry runs / debugging. |
| **Max threads** | *(blank = all cores)* | Caps how many invoices are processed at once. An XML-spool template can process its whole input folder in a single **parallel** pass — much faster on a folder of thousands of single-invoice files, and used the same way by a scheduled scan, an on-demand run and the command-line batch. Each file stays its own unit (name, source archive and traceability kept) and one file's failure doesn't stop the others. Set a value to keep headroom for other services on a shared host; leave it blank to use every available core. UBL templates and per-job (BIP) processing are unaffected. It also bounds the bulk reprocess, which runs one batch per template. |
| **`debugProfile`** | `Y` / `N` | When `Y`, every processing run writes **per-step timing rows** to `F564237` covering each pipeline stage: header parsing, lines parsing, validation, UBL emit, PA send. The rows surface on the [IT dashboard](../../application/tech-dashboard.md) — the *Live process events* tail flags them with their step name, and the *Template processing time* widget breaks the average down by stage. Leave at `N` in production; flip to `Y` for the duration of a batch run when triaging a slow pipeline. Disable once the slow stage is identified — the extra rows inflate `F564237` quickly under load. |

:::info[Advanced]
The **Ghostscript** group is folded under *Advanced* at the bottom of the tab.
:::

### Ghostscript

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **GS Command** | Full Ghostscript command line used for PDF post-processing (e.g. `gs -dBATCH ...`). Multi-line values are accepted. |

---

## Tab 3 — Logs

### Server log

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Server log file** | *(blank = automatic)* | File read by the [Server log](../../application/diagnostics/server-log.md) view. Blank = the file the launcher redirects the server output to (`nomaubl-<env>.log`); set it when the server runs under another launcher. |
| **Log size cap (MB)** | `100` | Above this size the live log is copied to `.1` and truncated in place, the older copies being shifted. The launcher keeps writing to the same file. `0` = never rotate. |
| **Log files kept** | `5` | Rotated copies kept next to the log. |
| **Log repeat window (s)** | `600` | A WARN or ERROR line identical to one written within this window is counted, not written; one summary line follows with the count. `0` = off. |
| **Log levels** | *(blank = everything)* | Minimum level per module — `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN`, `ERROR` — as `MODULE=LEVEL` pairs separated by commas; `*` stands for all other modules (e.g. `STATUS=WARN, API=INFO, *=INFO`). |

The rotation, the repeat suppression and the levels apply in server mode only; a command-line run writes to its own output. For a PA code missing from the status catalogue or an invoice unknown to NomaUBL, the status poll writes no warning per event: the run ends with one line per code, with its count and a sample invoice, and the unmapped codes are listed by the configuration check of the [Tech dashboard](../../application/tech-dashboard.md).

---

## Tab 4 — PDF

### PDF

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Logo path** | Path to the company logo drawn at the top of the supplier block when a PDF template has *Show logo* on (see [PDF Templates](../../management/pdf-templates.md)). Accepts the path variables `%APP_HOME%`, `%ENV%`, `%PROCESS_HOME%`, `%KCO%`, `%DOC%`, `%DCT%` and any `{{token}}` from the invoice catalogue — e.g. `%APP_HOME%/logos/{{kco}}.png`, so each company resolves to its own logo. A `{ }` button opens a searchable token list. PNG, JPG and GIF are supported. |
| **Logo offset X (pt)** | Horizontal shift of the logo, in points, to absorb whitespace baked into the source image. Default `0`. |
| **Logo width (pt)** / **Logo height (pt)** | Box the logo is scaled to fit, in points: ratio kept, enlarged when the image is smaller; one dimension alone lets the other follow the image. Blank = the previous cap of 200 × 80 points, without enlarging. The visual builder preview uses the same size as the produced PDF. |

## Tab 5 — Email

Configures the outbound mail server NomaUBL uses to send notifications and document deliveries by email.

### SMTP Server

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Host** | SMTP host (e.g. `smtp.example.com`). |
| **Port** | SMTP port (typically `587` for STARTTLS, `465` for implicit SSL, `25` plain). |
| **TLS (STARTTLS)** | `Y` / `N` — upgrade the connection to TLS via `STARTTLS`. |
| **SSL** | `Y` / `N` — open the connection in implicit SSL mode (rare in modern SMTP, mutually exclusive with STARTTLS). |

### SMTP Credentials

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Username** | SMTP authentication user. |
| **Password** | SMTP authentication password. |

### Sender

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **From address** | Default `From:` address on outbound mail (e.g. `facturation@example.com`). |

## Tab 6 — AI

Settings of the in-app [AI assistant](../../application/ai-capabilities.md).

### Anthropic AI

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **API Key** | Anthropic API key. Without a valid key, the assistant panel is disabled. |
| **Model** | Model used unless the panel picks another one. Default *Sonnet 5.5*; Opus, Fable and Haiku are also offered. |
| **Max output tokens** | Length cap of one answer, from `1024` to `32000` (default `8192`). |

### Documentation

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Source** | `llms` *(default)*: the documentation file is downloaded and searched on this server. `sitemap`: the model fetches the pages itself (previous behaviour). |
| **llms-full.txt URL** | English pages (default `https://docs.nomana-it.fr/llms-full.txt`). Refreshed every 6 hours; a URL, a local path or a `file:` URL. If it cannot be reached at start, the copy bundled in the application is used. |
| **llms-full.fr.txt URL** | French pages, used when the interface is in French (default `https://docs.nomana-it.fr/llms-full.fr.txt`, also used when the field is blank). When the French file cannot be loaded, the assistant falls back to the English pages. |
| **Section** | Part of the file to index (its `# === … ===` header, e.g. `NomaUBL`). Blank = the whole file. |

### Playbooks

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Custom playbooks** | Diagnostic procedures the assistant loads on demand, one per `## name` heading. A built-in name — `refused-invoice`, `missing-invoice`, `ereporting-error`, `status-not-updated` — replaces the built-in procedure. |

### Assistant behaviour

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **System Prompt** | Optional prompt prepended to every chat. Empty = the built-in NomaUBL prompt. |
| **Allowed Doc Domains** / **Docs Sitemap URL** / **Docs Path Prefix** | *Sitemap* mode only: domains the model may fetch, sitemap address (cached 6 hours), prefix of the entries kept. |
| **Custom Tools** | Read-only tools on this instance's data offered to the model (invoices, errors, history, dashboards, server log, settings with secrets masked). |

The **TLS / corporate proxy** group (custom truststore path and password, *Disable TLS validation* for a short diagnosis only) is folded under *Advanced*.

---

## Tab 7 — Job defaults

Settings shared by the background jobs. The jobs themselves — intervals, daily times, batch document jobs, digests, auto-retries and lifecycle checks — are managed on **Synchronization → [Scheduled jobs](../../sync/scheduled-jobs/overview.md)**; saving there reloads the schedules at once.

### Quiet window

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Quiet window from / to (HH:mm)** | A daily window during which both PA pollers (import poll and status retrieval) skip their runs automatically — set it over a send campaign so per-invoice import polls don't pile up while the PA is integrating the batch. May cross midnight; leave both empty to disable. It applies without a restart and shows on the IT dashboard's *Scheduler* card, highlighted while active. |

### Bulk Send

Defaults for every bulk send to the PA — *Send all waiting* and *Resend all* on the [IT dashboard](../../application/tech-dashboard.md), the [invoice-list bulk resend](../../application/invoices.md#bulk-resend), and the `-send-waiting` CLI. Each nightly [Auto-Retry](../../sync/scheduled-jobs/auto-retry.md) routine can override them on its own row.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Parallel workers** | *(default `4`)* How many invoices are sent to the PA at the same time. Set `1` for sequential sending. |
| **Delay per worker (ms)** | *(default `100`)* Pause each worker waits between two calls, to stay inside the PA's rate budget. |

### Retention \{#retention\}

Database rows kept per store by the daily **Retention purge** job. Off by default: nothing is deleted until a number of days is set, except the notifications, which keep their 90 days, so an upgrade deletes nothing by itself. The server log file is bounded separately (Tab 3).

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Processing log (days)** | `0` | Per-file START / END / error rows of the runtime log (`F564237`). Empty or `0` = keep forever; suggested `180`. |
| **Step timings (days)** | `0` | Per-step timing rows written by `debugProfile` (`F564237`). Suggested `30`. |
| **Job runs (days)** | `0` | Run rows of the scheduled jobs (`F564237`). Suggested `90`. |
| **Validation errors of finished invoices (days)** | `0` | Errors (`F564236`) of invoices in a terminal status (completed, deposited, refused…). Suggested `365`. |
| **Notifications (days)** | `90` | Inbox notifications (`F564253`). Empty = 90 days; `0` = keep forever. |

Before setting a value, the **Count only** button of the Retention purge job (or `java -jar nomaubl.jar -purge <configFile> --dry-run`) reports what each store would lose with the saved values.

### BIP print queue

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **BIP job hosts** | One high-water mark **per JDE execution host** (`RJRPDEXHST`). The mark tracks each host by **job completion time**, not by job number — a job number is assigned at submission, so a long-running job that finishes after a shorter, higher-numbered one could otherwise fall below the mark and never be fetched. The completion date is shown next to the job number for each host, and is **editable**. Add each host with its starting number (the first batch after an upgrade fills the date automatically), or click *Retrieve last job # per host* to seed them all from the current maximum; from then on they advance after each job, so an interrupted batch resumes exactly where it stopped. **Only listed hosts are scanned.** *(BIP / JDE-specific.)* |
| **BIP Lookback (days)** | Date floor on the BIP scan. `0` = no floor — every job after the watermark is eligible. `N > 0` = only jobs updated in the last N days. Handy on a first install or after a long gap, to skip years of history rather than walking the whole queue. Applies to the manual scan, the scheduled batch and the `nomaubl -fetch-all` command. *(BIP / JDE-specific.)* |

|---|---|
| **License Key** | Full NomaUBL license key. **Without a valid key, the *Navigation*, *Synchronisation* and *UBL* menus are disabled** — only Configuration remains accessible. |

## Tab 9 — Authentication

### Authentication

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Enable Authentication** | `Y` / `N` — turn on password-based user login. When `N`, NomaUBL runs without a login wall (typically dev / on-prem behind a corporate VPN). |
| **Auth Mode** | `internal` / `oidc` / `both` — drives the login screen. `internal` *(default)* keeps the local username + password form. `oidc` switches to a single-sign-on button only. `both` shows the SSO button above the local form, so operators with a database account can still sign in if the IdP is unavailable. Pair with the [OIDC template](./oidc.md) to configure the SSO side. |
| **Session Timeout (minutes)** | How long an authenticated user session remains valid. Default `480` (8 hours). |

:::info[Self-service password reset]
With **Auth Mode = `internal`** (or `both`), the login screen exposes a *Forgot password?* link. The user is prompted for both username and email; if they match an active account, a one-shot link valid 60 minutes is sent to the email on file. The link lands on a dedicated page that lets the user choose a new password.

Requires **SMTP** configured under *Tab 5 — Email*. Tokens are persisted in `F564255` (see [Database tables](../../references/database-tables.md#f564255--password-reset-tokens)) and expire after a single use.
:::

## Tab 10 — Periods \{#periods\}

Shown in the Settings navigation as **Navigation & lists**: the **start page** after sign-in (`startPage`), the **auto collapse** of the navigation (`navAutoCollapse`), the **dashboard cache** in minutes (`dashboardCacheMinutes`, 60), and the period each page opens on: **Every view** (*This month* unless set) and one override **Per view** (*Same as every view* by default) for the Billing overview, Operations, Statistics, Invoices, E-Documents, Diagnostics, Integration errors, Processing log and Reports › Integrity. Stored as `defaultPeriod` and `defaultPeriod.<view>`. A **Lists** group sets the *Rows per page* (50) and *Rows loaded* (100 000) of every list without its own values (`defaultPageSize`, `defaultMaxRows`). See [Period picker, default periods and lists](../default-periods.md#default-periods).

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Set Environment and Theme colour.** The `%ENV%` placeholder lets one configuration roll forward from `demo` to `PD` without editing every path, and a distinct colour per environment avoids working on production by mistake.
- **Bound the server log before going live.** The defaults (100 MB, 5 copies) suit most servers; add `STATUS=WARN` to the levels when the status poll is verbose.
- **Turn the retention on once the volumes are known.** Start with the suggested values, run *Count only*, then enable the purge job.
- **License gates the runtime.** If the Navigation, Synchronization and UBL menus disappear, check the License Key first.
- **Point the assistant at the French pages** for French-speaking users: fill *llms-full.fr.txt URL*.
