## NomaUBL — Database Tables
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/database-tables/

NomaUBL database schema reference — every table that backs the application: invoice archive, UBL header / lines / VAT, lifecycle events, validation errors, processing log, e-reporting, notifications and authentication. Functional descriptions, primary keys and field references for Oracle and PostgreSQL.

NomaUBL persists every artefact of the e-invoicing pipeline — the original ERP source, the generated UBL document, the per-line and per-VAT-rate breakdown, the lifecycle events, the validation errors, the runtime processing log, the e-reporting submissions and the user / role / session triplet.

The schema is **identical on Oracle and PostgreSQL** — the DDL is dialect-aware (`BLOB` ↔ `BYTEA`, `NUMBER` ↔ `INTEGER`, `VARCHAR2` ↔ `VARCHAR`) but the column names, primary keys and semantics are the same. Every table name is configurable in the `db-nomaubl` system template and created by the **Initialize Database** action of the *Settings → Database Connectors* screen.

The schema applies regardless of source system — JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP. Tables follow the JDE `F564XXX` naming convention because the platform was built around JDE first; the conventions are functional, not source-specific.

---

## Naming conventions

| Convention | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Table identifier** | `F564XXX` — JDE-style file prefix. Configurable per environment. |
| **Column prefix** | Two-letter prefix tied to the table (`FE` for archive, `UH` for UBL header, `UL` for lines, `UV` for VAT / validation, `US` for status / users, `RG`/`RH`/`RI` for e-reporting…). |
| **Dates** | JDE Julian — integer in `CYYDDD` format where `C = 1` for 2000–2099, `YY` is the last two digits of the year, `DDD` is the day of the year. Example: `125108` → 2025-04-18. Converted on the fly for the UI. |
| **Times** | Integer in `HHMMSS` format. Example: `143052` → 14:30:52. |
| **Scaled numerics** | Some amounts and rates are stored as integers scaled by a fixed factor — divide on read: `ATXA × 100` (2 decimals), `QNTY × 10000` (4 decimals), `UPRC × 10000` (4 decimals), `TXR1 × 1000` (3 decimals). |
| **XML payloads** | Stored as `BLOB` (Oracle) / `BYTEA` (Postgres) for JDE source XML, generated UBL **and e-reporting XML**. UTF-8 bytes throughout. |
| **Auto-incremented sequences** | `SEQN` columns use `COALESCE(MAX(SEQN), 0) + 1` on insert — no Oracle sequence or Postgres serial required. |

---

## Schema overview

  solid arrow — hard FK relationship
  dashed arrow — soft / cross-domain link
  highlighted card — domain anchor

---

## Invoice domain

The seven tables that carry an invoice through its complete life — from the raw ERP payload to its definitive lifecycle status.

### F564230 — Source archive & PA submission log

Stores the **original ERP XML** alongside the routing flags and the PA transaction UUID returned after submission. One row per source document.

- **Primary key**: `FEDOC + FEDCT + FEKCO`
- **Notable**: `FETXFT` carries the source XML payload (UTF-8 bytes); `FEUKIDSZ` holds the UUID returned by the Plateforme Agréée after successful import; `FEEV10` is the *send to PA* flag (`1` = yes, `2` = no).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FEDOC` | Integer | Document number (PK). |
| `FEDCT` | Text(2) | Document type (PK). |
| `FEKCO` | Text(5) | Company code (PK). |
| `FEAA10` | Text(10) | Activity / routing code. |
| `FEAA20` | Text(25) | Document sub-type. |
| `FEALKY` | Text(25) | Customer alpha key. |
| `FEAEXP` | Decimal × 100 | Document amount (scaled). |
| `FEIVD` | Date (Julian) | Invoice date. |
| `FEARDU` | Date (Julian) | Due date. |
| `FEUPMJ` | Date (Julian) | Last update date. |
| `FEPID` | Text(10) | Program ID. |
| `FEVERS` | Text(5) | Version. |
| `FEUSER` | Text(10) | User who created the row. |
| `FEJOBN` | Text(10) | Job name. |
| `FEUPMT` | Time (HHMMSS) | Last update time. |
| `FEWDS1` | Text(80) | Source file name. |
| `FEEV01` | Text(25) | Routing code. |
| `FEAC04` | Text(5) | Business unit / office. |
| `FEEV10` | Integer | *Send to PA* flag — `1` = yes, `2` = no. |
| `FETXFT` | BLOB | Original ERP XML (UTF-8 bytes). |
| `FEUKIDSZ` | Text(100) | PA platform transaction UUID returned on import. |

### F564231 — UBL invoice header

The **EN 16931** view of the invoice plus the generated UBL 2.1 document. One row per invoice; same primary key as F564230.

- **Primary key**: `UHDOC + UHDCT + UHKCO`
- **Notable**: `UHTXFT` stores the generated UBL document (UTF-8 bytes); `UHK74RSCD` is the current lifecycle status code from the *statuses* reference list; `UHY56BAR` is the BAR routing code (`B2B` / `B2G` / `B2C` / `B2BINT` / `OUTOFSCOPE` / …).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `UHDOC` | Integer | Document number (PK · FK → F564230). |
| `UHDCT` | Text(2) | Document type (PK). |
| `UHKCO` | Text(5) | Company code (PK). |
| `UHODOC` / `UHODCT` / `UHOKCO` | Integer / Text(2) / Text(5) | Original (referenced) document — non-empty for credit notes pointing at a prior invoice. |
| `UHK74FLEN` | Text(25) | UBL invoice number — BT-1. |
| `UHK74XMLV` | Text(50) | Profile ID — BT-23. |
| `UHK74LDDJ` | Date (Julian) | Issue date — BT-2. |
| `UHDDJ` | Date (Julian) | Due date — BT-9. |
| `UHK74LEDT` | Text(3) | Invoice type code — BT-3. |
| `UHATXA` | Decimal × 100 | Tax-exclusive amount — BT-109. |
| `UHSTAM` | Decimal × 100 | Tax amount — BT-110. |
| `UHAG` | Decimal × 100 | Tax-inclusive amount — BT-112. |
| `UHAAP` | Decimal × 100 | Amount due — BT-115. |
| `UHCRCD` | Text(3) | Currency code — BT-5. |
| `UH55RSF` | Text(40) | Order reference — BT-13. |
| `UHY74CTID` | Integer | Contract reference — BT-12. |
| `UHAN8` | Integer | Customer AN8 (JDE address book). |
| `UHALKY` | Text(25) | Customer alpha key. |
| `UHALPH` | Text(40) | Customer name — BT-44. |
| `UHTXFT` | BLOB | Generated UBL 2.1 XML (UTF-8 bytes). |
| `UHK74RSCD` | Text(4) | Current lifecycle status code (see *Status Reference*). |
| `UHK74MSG1` | Text(500) | Status message. |
| `UHY56EPID` / `UHY56EPSC` | Text(100) / Text(25) | Customer endpoint ID + scheme — BT-49 / BT-49-1. |
| `UHY56PYIN` | Text(3) | Payment means code — BT-81. |
| `UHY56BAR` | Text(10) | BAR routing code (`B2B`, `B2G`, `B2C`, `B2BINT`, `OUTOFSCOPE`, …). |
| `UHY56RSRC` / `UHY56RSRCL` | Text(50) / Text(250) | Rejection reason code + label. |
| `UHY56ACTN` / `UHY56ACTNL` | Text(10) / Text(250) | Expected action code + label. |
| `UHY56ACTND` | Text(1000) | Status note (raw JSON returned by the PA). |
| `UHUSER` / `UHPID` / `UHJOBN` / `UHUPMJ` / `UHTDAY` | — | Audit columns — created by, program, job, last-update date and time. |

### F564233 — UBL invoice lines

One row per UBL line. Stored values for quantity, price and tax rate are **scaled** — divide on read.

- **Primary key**: `ULDOC + ULDCT + ULKCO + ULLNID`
- **Notable**: `ULLNID` is the JDE line ID × 1000 (BT-126). `ULY56QNTY` ÷ 10000, `ULUPRC` ÷ 10000, `ULATXA` ÷ 100, `ULTXR1` ÷ 1000.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ULDOC` / `ULDCT` / `ULKCO` | — | Document number / type / company (PK · FK → F564231). |
| `ULLNID` | Integer × 1000 | Line ID — BT-126. |
| `ULDSC1` | Text(40) | Item description — BT-153. |
| `ULLITM` | Text(35) | Seller item ID — BT-155. |
| `ULY56QNTY` | Decimal × 10000 | Invoiced quantity — BT-129. |
| `ULY56UM` | Text(3) | Unit of measure code — BT-130. |
| `ULUPRC` | Decimal × 10000 | Unit price — BT-146. |
| `ULATXA` | Decimal × 100 | Line extension amount — BT-131. |
| `ULREBL` | Decimal × 10000 | Allowance / charge — BT-136. |
| `ULCRCD` | Text(3) | Currency code. |
| `ULK74TVCC` | Text(2) | Tax category code — BT-151. |
| `ULTXR1` | Decimal × 1000 | Tax rate — BT-152. |
| `ULK74EXRC` | Text(100) | Tax exemption reason — BT-121. |
| `ULUSER` / `ULPID` / `ULJOBN` / `ULUPMJ` / `ULTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564234 — UBL VAT summary

One row per **(tax category, tax rate, currency)** breakdown carried by the invoice — the EN 16931 BG-23 group.

- **Primary key**: `UVDOC + UVDCT + UVKCO + UVSEQN`
- **Notable**: `UVSEQN` is auto-incremented via `COALESCE(MAX(UVSEQN), 0) + 1` on insert.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `UVDOC` / `UVDCT` / `UVKCO` | — | Document number / type / company (PK · FK → F564231). |
| `UVSEQN` | Integer | Sequence number (PK). |
| `UVK74TVCC` | Text(2) | Tax category code — BT-118. |
| `UVTXR1` | Decimal × 1000 | Tax rate — BT-119. |
| `UVATXA` | Decimal × 100 | Taxable amount — BT-116. |
| `UVSTAM` | Decimal × 100 | Tax amount — BT-117. |
| `UVCRCD` | Text(3) | Currency code. |
| `UVK74EXRC` | Text(500) | Tax exemption reason — BT-120. |
| `UVUSER` / `UVPID` / `UVJOBN` / `UVUPMJ` / `UVTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564235 — Lifecycle events

The **append-only history** of every status the invoice has been in. One row per event, in submission order. This is the source of the *History* tab in the invoice detail modal.

- **Primary key**: `USDOC + USDCT + USKCO + USSEQN`
- **Notable**: `USSEQN` is auto-incremented; events are written by `StatusTransition.apply()` together with the corresponding update of `F564231.UHK74RSCD`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `USDOC` / `USDCT` / `USKCO` | — | Document number / type / company (PK · FK → F564231). |
| `USSEQN` | Integer | Event sequence (PK). |
| `USK74RSCD` | Text(4) | Status code at this event. |
| `USK74MSG1` | Text(500) | Status message. |
| `USTRDJ` | Date (Julian) | Event date. |
| `USY56RSRC` / `USY56RSRCL` | Text(50) / Text(250) | Rejection reason code + label. |
| `USY56ACTN` / `USY56ACTNL` | Text(10) / Text(250) | Expected action code + label. |
| `USY56ACTND` | Text(1000) | Status note (raw JSON from the PA). |
| `USUSER` / `USPID` / `USJOBN` / `USUPMJ` / `USTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564236 — UBL validation errors

XSD and Schematron errors recorded for an invoice. One row per error / warning — feeds the *History → Validation errors* group of the invoice detail modal and the *Integration Errors* page when no matching `F564231` row is found.

- **Primary key**: `UVDOC + UVDCT + UVKCO + UVSEQN`
- **Notable**: `UVY56LEVEL` is `ERROR` / `WARNING` / `INFO`. `UVSRCL` flags the validator: `XSD`, `SCH` (Schematron) or `DB`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `UVDOC` / `UVDCT` / `UVKCO` | — | Document number / type / company (PK; can be orphan when no F564231 row). |
| `UVSEQN` | Integer | Error sequence (PK). |
| `UVY56LEVEL` | Text(10) | Severity — `ERROR`, `WARNING`, `INFO`. |
| `UVSRCL` | Text(25) | Source — `XSD` / `SCH` / `DB`. |
| `UVY56RULE` | Text(50) | Rule ID (e.g. `BR-01`, `PEPPOL-EN16931-R001`). |
| `UVK74MSG1` | Text(2000) | Error / warning message. |
| `UVUSER` / `UVPID` / `UVJOBN` / `UVUPMJ` / `UVTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564237 — Runtime processing log

Every event written by `RuntimeLogHandler` during XML / UBL / BIP / FTP processing — `START`, `END` and any intermediate method. Backs the *Processing Log* page (Management menu).

- **Primary key**: `FEUKID` (sequence computed via `COALESCE(MAX(FEUKID),0)+1` on insert — used as a tiebreaker for events sharing the same timestamp).
- **Notable**: `FERMK` is the processing type (`SINGLE`, `BURST`, `UBL`, `BOTH`, `UBL_VALIDATE`, `PROCESS`, `AUTO`); `FETMPL` is the template name (empty for UBL processing); `FERMK2` is `START` / `END` or the failing method name on errors.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FEUKID` | Integer (BIGINT) | Sequence id (PK · stable insert order). |
| `FEWDS1` | Text(60) | Source file name — links to `F564230.FEWDS1`. |
| `FEUPMJ` | Date (Julian) | Event date. |
| `FEUPMT` | Time (HHMMSS) | Event time. |
| `FERMK` | Text(30) | Processing type (renamed from `FEMODE`). |
| `FETMPL` | Text(40) | Template name. |
| `FERMK2` | Text(30) | Operation — `START` / `END` / failing method name (renamed from `FEMETHOD`). |
| `FEK74MSG1` | Text(1024) | Status message or error detail (renamed from `FEMESSAGE`). |

---

## E-Reporting domain

Three tables that record the *(period, flux, company)* declarations submitted to the Plateforme Agréée — flux **10.1** (B2BINT detail) and **10.3** (B2C / OUTOFSCOPE aggregated).

### F564260 — Report log

One row per generated report. Stores the `<ReportDocument>` XML and the latest known status.

- **Primary key**: `RGUKID` (globally unique sequence — no flux / company component).
- **Notable**: `RGY56BAR` is `10.1` or `10.3`; `RGDCT` is the document type (`IN` initial, `RE` replacement, `CO` cancellation, `MO` modification); `RGTXFT` carries the generated XML as **UTF-8 bytes** (BLOB / BYTEA).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RGUKID` | Integer (BIGINT) | Report sequence id (PK). |
| `RGY56BAR` | Text(10) | Flux code — `10.1` / `10.3`. |
| `RGKCO` | Text(5) | Issuing company code. |
| `RGDCT` | Text(2) | Document type — `IN` / `RE` / `CO` / `MO`. |
| `RGEFTJ` | Date (Julian) | Period start. |
| `RGEFDJ` | Date (Julian) | Period end. |
| `RGY56EPID` | Text(125) | Issuer SIREN (scheme `0002`). |
| `RGK74RSCD` | Text(10) | Current lifecycle status code. |
| `RGK74MSG1` | Text(1024) | Last status message. |
| `RGNINV` | Integer | Number of invoices included. |
| `RGTXFT` | BLOB | Generated `<ReportDocument>` XML (UTF-8 bytes). |
| `RGUSER` / `RGPID` / `RGJOBN` / `RGUPMJ` / `RGTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564261 — Report lifecycle events

The append-only history of statuses for a given report — same shape as F564235 for invoices.

- **Primary key**: `RHUKID + RHSEQN`
- **Notable**: `RHSEQN` is auto-incremented. `RHUKID` is the FK to the parent log (`F564260.RGUKID`).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RHUKID` | Integer (BIGINT) | Report sequence id (PK · FK → F564260.RGUKID). |
| `RHY56BAR` | Text(10) | Flux code (denormalised for query convenience). |
| `RHSEQN` | Integer | Event sequence (PK). |
| `RHK74RSCD` | Text(10) | Status code at this event. |
| `RHK74MSG1` | Text(1024) | Status message. |
| `RHUSER` / `RHPID` / `RHJOBN` / `RHUPMJ` / `RHTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564262 — Report / invoice mapping

Tracks **which invoices were included in which report** — composite PK avoids re-including invoices that were already declared on a prior run.

- **Primary key**: `RIUKID + RIDOC + RIDCT + RIKCO`
- **Notable**: A secondary index on `(RIDOC, RIDCT, RIKCO, RIY56BAR)` answers "in which report was this invoice declared?" efficiently.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RIUKID` | Integer (BIGINT) | Report sequence id (PK · FK → F564260.RGUKID). |
| `RIY56BAR` | Text(10) | Flux code. |
| `RIDOC` / `RIDCT` / `RIKCO` | — | Invoice triplet (PK · FK → F564231). |
| `RIUSER` / `RIPID` / `RIJOBN` / `RIUPMJ` / `RITDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

---

## Authentication + notifications domain

Five tables for built-in user / role / session / permissions management plus the notifications inbox. The auth block is active when `authEnabled = Y` in the *global* template.

### F564250 — Users

One row per user. Passwords are stored as **PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256** hashes — never in clear text.

- **Primary key**: `USUSER`
- **Notable**: `USLDAPPSWD` format is `iterations:base64(salt):base64(hash)` (bytes). `USSECF3 = 'Y'` forces a password change on the next login (default for new accounts).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `USUSER` | Text(10) | Username (PK). |
| `USLDAPPSWD` | BLOB | PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hash — `iterations:salt:hash` (renamed from `USPASSWD`). |
| `USROLE` | Text(36) | Role name (FK → F564251.RLROLE). |
| `USFULLNAME` | Text(50) | Display name. |
| `USEMAIL` | Text(75) | Email address. |
| `USENABL` | Text(1) | `Y` = active, `N` = disabled (renamed from `USACTIVE`). |
| `USSECF3` | Text(30) | `Y` = must change password on next login (renamed from `USFORCEPASSWD`). |
| `USUPMJ` | Date (Julian) | Account creation / last update date. |
| `USTDAY` | Time (HHMMSS) | Matching time. |

### F564251 — Roles (identity only)

One row per role. This table stores **role identity only** — the grants (pages, companies, read-only, settings access) live row-by-row in `F564254`.

- **Primary key**: `RLROLE`
- **Notable**: No schema change is needed to introduce a new permission dimension — just insert rows with a new `PMCRAPPID` in `F564254`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RLROLE` | Text(36) | Role identifier (PK). |
| `RLROLEDESC` | Text(255) | Human-readable description. |
| `RLUSER` / `RLPID` / `RLJOBN` / `RLUPMJ` / `RLTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564252 — Sessions

One row per active session. Sessions are validated on every API request; expired rows are pruned by the auth handler.

- **Primary key**: `SSLSID` (UUID, renamed from `SSTOKEN`)
- **Notable**: The token is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <SSLSID>` on every API call. Two indexes on `SSUSER` and `SSETDTIM` keep lookups and cleanup efficient.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SSLSID` | Text(100) | Session token / UUID (PK). |
| `SSUSER` | Text(10) | Username (FK → F564250.USUSER). |
| `SSSTDTIM` | Timestamp | Session creation timestamp (renamed from `SSCREATED`). |
| `SSETDTIM` | Timestamp | Session expiry timestamp (renamed from `SSEXPIRES`). |

### F564253 — Notifications

One row per delivered notification. Backs the portal **inbox** and the **bell** in the utilities bar (see [Notifications](../application/notifications.md)).

- **Primary key**: `NTUKID` (globally unique sequence).
- **Notable**: `(NTDOC, NTDCT, NTKCO)` is the FK back to `F564231` when the notification relates to an invoice (nullable for system alerts). `NTUSER` is the recipient username, or `*` for a broadcast (auth-disabled mode). `NTEV01` is the read flag (`Y` = read, `N` = unread) — drives the bell badge.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NTUKID` | Integer (BIGINT) | Sequence id (PK). |
| `NTUSER` | Text(10) | Recipient username (`*` = broadcast). |
| `NTY56RULE` | Text(20) | Name of the rule that fired the dispatch. |
| `NTMSGP` | Text(40) | Short subject / title. |
| `NTK74MSG2` | Text(1024) | Full message body. |
| `NTDOC` / `NTDCT` / `NTKCO` | mixed | Invoice triplet (FK → F564231 when populated). |
| `NTK74RSCD` | Text(10) | Status code that triggered the rule. |
| `NTK74MSG1` | Text(1024) | Status message. |
| `NTY56RSRC` / `NTY56RSRCL` | Text(50) / Text(250) | PA rejection reason code + label. |
| `NTY56ACTN` / `NTY56ACTNL` | Text(10) / Text(250) | Expected action code + label. |
| `NTEV01` | Text(1) | Read flag (`Y` / `N`). |
| `NTUPMJ` / `NTTDAY` | Date / Time | Creation timestamp. |

A daily sweep driven by `global.notificationsRetentionDays` (default 90, `0` = disabled) deletes rows older than the retention window.

### F564254 — Role permission grants (row-based RBAC)

Stores role grants as typed rows. One row per `(role, permission type, value)` triplet.

- **Primary key**: `(PMROLE, PMCRAPPID, PMCRAPPVAL)`
- **Notable**: An empty result set for a given `(role, type)` means *unrestricted* on that dimension. Adding a new permission dimension is an INSERT — not a DDL change. Drop + Init Database re-seeds the default grants without touching existing role rows.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PMROLE` | Text(36) | Role identifier (PK · FK → F564251.RLROLE). |
| `PMCRAPPID` | Text(30) | Permission type — `page` / `company` / `feature`. |
| `PMCRAPPVAL` | Text(175) | Value within the type — page id, company code, or feature name (`settings`, `readonly`, …). |
| `PMENABL` | Text(1) | `Y` = grant, `N` = explicit deny. |
| `PMUSER` / `PMPID` / `PMJOBN` / `PMUPMJ` / `PMTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

Currently used `PMCRAPPID` values:

| Type | `PMCRAPPVAL` | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `page` | page id (e.g. `dashboard`, `invoices`) | Page allowed for the role. |
| `company` | company code (`KCO`) | Company allowed for the role. |
| `feature` | `settings` | Role can access the *Configuration* menus. |
| `feature` | `readonly` | Role is restricted to read-only (no edit / delete / resend). |

### F564255 — Password reset tokens

Backs the *Forgot password* flow. One row per emailed link. The token is a UUID embedded in the `/reset?token=…` URL; it is single-use and expires after ~60 minutes.

- **Primary key**: `PRTOK`
- **Notable**: `PRUSED = 'Y'` marks a consumed token — the row stays briefly for audit before sweep. A purge deletes expired tokens and consumed tokens past their audit window.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PRTOK` | Text(100) | UUID token embedded in the `/reset?token=…` link (PK). |
| `PRUSER` | Text(10) | Target user (FK → F564250.USUSER). |
| `PRSTDTIM` | Timestamp | Token issued-at. |
| `PRETDTIM` | Timestamp | Token expires-at (~60 min after issue). |
| `PRUSED` | Text(1) | `Y` once the token has been consumed; prevents replay. |

---

## Recommended indexes

The DDL bundles a small set of indexes that every production deployment should keep — they back the most common queries from the UI:

| Index | Table | Columns | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `F564231_STATUS_IX` | F564231 | `UHK74RSCD` | Dashboard counters and *E-Invoicing* status filters. |
| `F564231_DATE_IX` | F564231 | `UHK74LDDJ` | Date-range queries on the invoice list. |
| `F564231_CUST_IX` | F564231 | `UHAN8` | Customer-scoped views. |
| `F564230_UUID_IX` | F564230 | `FEUKIDSZ` | PA UUID look-up after import. |
| `F564260_PERIOD_IX` | F564260 | `RGKCO`, `RGY56BAR`, `RGEFDJ` | E-Reporting list filters. |
| `F564262_INV_IX` | F564262 | `RIDOC`, `RIDCT`, `RIKCO`, `RIY56BAR` | "In which report is this invoice?" lookup. |
| `F564250_ROLE_IX` | F564250 | `USROLE` | User → role join. |
| `F564252_USER_IX` | F564252 | `SSUSER` | Sign-out / list-sessions per user. |
| `F564252_EXP_IX` | F564252 | `SSETDTIM` | Expired-session pruning. |
| `F564253_USR_IX` | F564253 | `NTUSER`, `NTEV01`, `NTUPMJ DESC` | Bell badge + inbox sort. |
| `F564254_ROLE_IX` | F564254 | `PMROLE`, `PMCRAPPID` | Fast per-role grant resolution. |
| `F564255_USR_IX` | F564255 | `PRUSER` | Active tokens per user (abuse protection, invalidation). |
| `F564255_EXP_IX` | F564255 | `PRETDTIM` | Expired-token sweep. |

The full DDL — including dialect-aware variants for Oracle and PostgreSQL — ships in the JAR under `sql/oracle/ddl.sql` and `sql/postgres/ddl.sql`, and is materialised on disk by **Initialize Database**.

## NomaUBL — Developer Reference
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/developer/

The NomaUBL Developer page — tables and columns, configuration keys, flows, impact analysis and the API of the instance — generated at build time from the database DDL, the configuration classes, the settings editors, the Java sources and the OpenAPI document.

The **Developer** page answers the questions of whoever maintains, extends or audits NomaUBL: *what is in this table, who writes this column, where is this setting edited and who reads it, which flows a status goes through, what this API returns*. Everything on the page is **generated when the application is built**, from the database DDL, the table and column configuration, the settings editors, the Java sources and the OpenAPI document — it always matches the release that runs.

Open it from **Documentation → Developer**.

---

## At a glance

---

## Tables

The data dictionary of the sixteen NomaUBL tables, grouped by flow — *Invoice lifecycle*, *E-reporting*, *Notifications*, *Security* — with a search over table names, columns, comments and BT codes.

- **The table card** gives the purpose and notes from the DDL, the primary key and indexes, the accessor and its configuration key, the name currently configured in the [NomaUBL database settings](../configuration/database-connectors/nomaubl.md) when the table is renamed (*Renamed to*), and the flows that write and read it. The invoice tables carry a clickable strip of the lifecycle across tables, from the archive to the processing log.
- **The columns grid** — column, override, type, description (inline and `COMMENT ON` of the DDL), BT code, accessor, configuration key, screens that show it, flows, write and read counts, nullable, default. A row opens the code references, writes first, grouped by flow: processing, import poll, status poll, received invoices, e-reporting, inbound, jobs, notifications, authentication, API, screens, database, command line. The grid is the shared data table; its view is listed in the [List views](../configuration/list-views.md) editor.

The complete reference of the tables is also published in [Database tables](./database-tables.md).

---

## Configuration

Every configuration key, with **where it is edited** and **who reads it**. The templates are listed on the left, grouped like the [Settings navigation](../configuration/settings-overview.md) — Global settings, Documents, PDF templates, API and SQL connectors, E-invoicing, E-reporting, Jobs & inbound… — with their key count and their gaps. The grid shows the keys of the selected template:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| **Key** | The configuration key. |
| **Label** | The field label in the settings editor. |
| **Edited in** | Template, tab and group of the editor field. |
| **Read by** | The flows whose code reads the key. |
| **Call sites** | Number of Java reads. A row opens the editor field and the code. |
| **State** | *editable, read* · *editable, never read* · *read, not editable*. |
| **Templates** | Templates that carry the key. |
| **Hint** | The help text of the field. |

Two check boxes isolate the gaps, one at a time: **Read but not editable** (a key the code reads that no screen offers) and **Editable but never read** (a field that has no effect). Keys built at run time — `fetchAll.N.*`, `folder.N.*`, `filter.*` — are not literal in the code and show as editable only.

---

## Flows

One short page per flow: **process a file**, **import poll**, **status poll**, **e-reporting**, **watched folders**, **reprocess**. Each gives the trigger, the command-line switch, the log module, the tables touched, the statuses written, the settings read and the steps in order. Pick a flow on the left to read it.

---

## Impact

What a change reaches. The picker goes in steps:

1. the **kind** — *Column*, *Configuration key* or *Status*;
2. the **table** or the **template**;
3. the **item**, in a wide list that shows the label first.

The result lists the **flows**, the **screens**, the **API endpoints** and the **command-line switches** the item reaches, the editor field that exposes it, then the code. Endpoints come from a scan of the server routes down to their handler class; status codes and labels come from the [status catalogue](../configuration/system/statuses.md) of the instance.

---

## API

The API of the instance, read the way the other views are read:

- **tag groups and tags** on the left with their operation counts — Invoices & documents, Processing, Platforms, Operations, Administration, Developer;
- **one row per operation** in the shared data table: method, path, summary, tag, group, access (*public*, *any signed-in user*, or the action a role must grant);
- **a window per operation** with the description, the parameters and request and response samples built from the schemas, references resolved.

**Getting started** opens the introduction of the document (session and token, rights, responses, invoice key, dates, paging, background runs). **Open the public reference (Redoc)** opens the same document in Redoc, which also serves readers outside the application — see the [API reference](/nomaubl/api-reference/) of this site.

---

## Access

Grant **Developer** in the Documentation group on the [Roles](../configuration/security/roles.md) page. The page reads the files generated at build time and, for the *Renamed to* field, the table names of the current settings; it runs no query on the invoice tables.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Check Impact before renaming a column or retiring a setting.** The flows and endpoints listed are what to retest.
- **Review the gaps of the Configuration view after an upgrade.** A key *editable, never read* is a field to clean up; a key *read, not editable* is a setting only reachable by editing the file.
- **Send the Flows pages to a new team member** before the code: they describe each chain in a page.

---

## 2026.10.25.1 — 2026-10-25 \{#v2026-10-25-1\}

### Improvements
- **Explorer PDF: readable pivots.** In a PDF, each row level of a pivot gets its own column, group rows and the total are in bold, and a single measure no longer repeats its name in every column header.
- **Explorer: build your own analyses.** A new Explorer page, next to Reports, replaces the Requêteur tab. On the left, the fields of seven entities around the invoice (invoices, archived documents, lifecycle events, validation findings, invoice lines, VAT breakdown, notifications); drag or click them onto the Rows, Measures and Filters shelves, pick a period on any date, then run the analysis as a table, a pivot with totals, or detail rows. Dates group by day, week, month, quarter or year; measures are count, distinct count, sum, average, min and max, in real units; a filter on events or lines selects the invoices that have such a row. A result row or pivot cell opens the rows behind it, and a detail row opens the invoice. Analyses are saved and shared, one file each, promotable; the saved reports of the former query tool are converted automatically. Granted per role with the new Explorer page. Works unchanged on every supported database.
- **Explorer: charts.** An analysis can now be drawn as bars (vertical or horizontal, grouped or stacked), a line or area, a pie or donut, or KPI cards. The second row field gives the series, with the ten largest and the rest grouped as Others; dates read in order, other categories by size. Hovering shows the values, clicking a bar, point or slice opens the rows behind it, and the chart downloads as PNG. Switching between table, pivot and charts does not run the query again; the chart options are saved with the analysis. The toolbar keeps the entity, the views, Top and Run on one fixed row, the options of the current view on a second row.
- **Explorer: dashboards.** The Explorer gains a Dashboards mode: saved analyses become tiles on a four-column grid, each with its width and height, its chart, table or pivot, and one period at the top applied to every tile. A tile drills like its analysis and opens it in the editor; dashboards are saved and shared like analyses. Analyses and dashboards can be promoted to another instance, a dashboard bringing its analyses, and the implementation report lists them. A daily digest can send a saved analysis: it runs over the digest's window and arrives as a spreadsheet.
- **Explorer: calculated fields, richer pivot, ready-made analyses.** An analysis can define calculated fields with a small expression language — arithmetic on amounts, the age of an invoice or the days between two dates, conditions and choices such as `age(dueDate) > 30 ? 'late' : 'on time'` — tested on a few rows before use and usable as rows, measures or filters; it runs the same on every supported database. The pivot nests its row fields with collapsible subtotals and shows each cell's share of its parent or of the total. Twelve analyses and three dashboards come ready for IT (Operations), accounting (Month end) and audit (Audit period); they are installed once and never overwritten, so they can be adapted. One of them reproduces the status statistics of the Reports page, whose tab stays as it is. Every analysis has an option to exclude reviewed errors. The cross table and a whole dashboard export to Excel, the dashboard one sheet per tile; the saved analyses and dashboards are listed by audience and name. Saving opens a window with the name in the interface's language, who can see it (everyone or only me), Save and Save as — Save as is how a provided analysis or dashboard is copied and adapted. A coded field shows the labels of the list chosen for that column in Settings › List views (Invoices, E-Documents, Integration errors), so a short list for the transaction types applies to the Explorer as well. An analysis or a dashboard exports to PDF in the audit report's layout — cover page with environment, period, date, author and version, contents for a dashboard, running headers — with each chart and all its data, filters noted. In a calculated field, the fields and the functions are picked from lists and inserted at the cursor. A daily digest can send a saved analysis or a whole dashboard, as Excel (one sheet per tile) or as a PDF in the same layout, built on the server over the digest's window; the lists show the names and audience groups of the Explorer. Picking a saved analysis runs it at once with its own period, as a dashboard tile does.
- **Settings: Custom data.** The custom lists leave Reference data for an area of their own, Custom data, right after it in the Settings navigation.
- **API connectors: platform endpoints folded.** The "Endpoints NomaUBL uses" block of an API connector is collapsed by default, with a count of the endpoints configured, since it only concerns platform connectors.
- **Invoice types: complete list, invoice or credit note.** The invoice types list now holds every UNTDID 1001 code accepted by EN 16931, each marked Invoice or Credit note in a new Type column. That type decides whether a document is produced as a CreditNote and whether it counts negatively in the e-reporting B2C totals. On upgrade, an existing list receives the missing codes and its codes get their type, labels unchanged.
- **Payment means: complete list.** The payment means list now holds every UNTDID 4461 code, with French and English labels; an existing list receives the missing codes on upgrade.
- **VAT categories: Canary Islands and Ceuta / Melilla.** The VAT categories list gains L (Canary Islands general indirect tax, IGIC) and M (IPSI, Ceuta and Melilla); an existing list receives them on upgrade.
- **Units of measure: more codes.** The units list gains 24 common UN/ECE Rec 20 codes — area, length, weight, volume, energy, time, hundred and thousand, lot and packaging (bag, bale, box, carton, drum, jerrican, pallet, package, roll); an existing list receives the missing ones on upgrade.
- **JDE SQL connector.** A ready-made `jde-sql` connector comes with prebuilt queries for the JDE database, `getUDC`, the values of a user-defined code (product code and code type) as code and labels, for example to fill a custom list, and `updateInvoiceStatus`, which puts an invoice's receivable lines on pay status H and stops their dunning letters unless already paid, for example from an invoice action, and `getCompanies`, the JDE companies with their names. Set its connection, schema and control schema once; queries write the schemas as `{{schema}}` and `{{ctlSchema}}`, so the same query runs on every JDE environment. Every SQL connector gains the control schema field and both placeholders.
- **Upgrade: new connector endpoints and queries.** On upgrade, a shipped API or SQL connector already present on the instance receives the endpoints or queries it lacks, matched by name; its connection settings and its existing endpoints and queries are kept. The upgrade report lists what was added.
- **List views: value lists by default.** On a new installation, the Invoices, E-Documents, Integration errors and E-Reporting lists show labels for document types, companies, activity codes, processing categories, review, invoice types, countries and reason codes, picked from lists in their filters, with the same column names across pages (Party Number, Party Name); E-Documents also gains the status, document type, reason, due date, UBL number and template columns, with their filters. An instance that has saved its list views keeps them.
- **Custom lists filled from NomaUBL's own tables.** A custom list's sync source can now be the NomaUBL database: Sync now adds the activity codes, sub-types, document types, companies, business units or send-to-PA flags found in the archived documents, or the levels found in the validation findings, and keeps the labels already entered. New lists come ready: sub-types (refreshed this way, like activity codes), send to PA, validation levels, validation sources and the e-reporting direction (inbound purchases, outbound sales), the E-Reporting list's former Flux column now named Direction; the company list syncs from the JDE SQL connector. Validation rules get a built-in list, kept in step with the Schematrons, that shows each rule with its description in the columns, filters and Explorer of Integration errors and Diagnostics › Failures. E-Documents, Integration errors and Failures use these lists, and the company filter of Failures becomes a list.
- **E-reporting: generate by direction and company.** The Generate dialog chooses the direction — outbound (sales), inbound (purchases) or both — instead of the 10.1 / 10.3 flux chips, which had no effect since each report carries both flows; the company is picked from the companies list, blank for all configured companies. The unused Flux setting of the e-reporting settings is removed.
- **Company pickers.** The VAT declaration, the audit report, the archive source of Extract and process and the integrity check of status retrieval choose their company, or companies for the audit report, from the companies list (code and name), like the list filters; with the list still empty, the text field remains.
- **Processing log: filter by status.** In the grouped view, the processing log filters the runs by status: OK, error, or partial (start or end missing).
- **Diagnostics: kinds and severities as lists.** Failures picks its kinds (with their counts) and the server log its severities from a multi-select list instead of a row of checkboxes; nothing selected means all.
- **Explorer: findings per day, validation or integration.** The ready-made analysis of the Operations dashboard now splits each day's findings into validation (the invoice data broke a Schematron or XSD rule, customer packs included) and integration (a technical step failed: platform, database, transformation, PDF, XML, UBL generation, validator, processing), instead of one colour per Schematron pack; a copy left untouched is updated on upgrade.
- **Billing overview (Synthèse).** A new page right after the Dashboard, for accounting, sales and the board, speaks in amounts and labels, never status codes, with a Sales / Purchases switch next to the period. It is the page NomaUBL opens on (the Operations dashboard under a restricted licence), first in the menu, on this month by default. Four headline figures, each compared with the matching earlier period — this month to date with the same days of last month, a whole month with the previous month, a quarter with the previous quarter, this year to date with the same dates last year: revenue excl. VAT, net of credit notes (invoices and credit notes shown under it), VAT, the number of invoices and credit notes, and the transmission rate — the share of the amount transmitted, with how many invoices were issued and how many not yet (acceptance rate for purchases). Below: twelve months of amount split into transmitted, in progress, to correct, and refused or disputed; "What needs a decision", all dates, in amounts incl. VAT — one line per business status (refused, disputed, suspended…), rejected by the platform, to correct before sending — each opening the invoices concerned; the split per company and per transaction type (national B2B, international B2B, B2C); and for sales, per company the last e-reporting declaration and the next period due. The period picker carries the date basis (document date by default), and "Exclude reviewed errors", on by default, also applies to what needs a decision. Visible with the Dashboard access.
- **Billing overview: PDF export.** A PDF button on the Billing overview downloads the page in the audit report's layout: cover page with the period and the direction, key figures with the previous period and the change, the twelve-month chart stacked and coloured as on screen with its table, what needs a decision, and the splits per company, per transaction type and, for sales, e-reporting. In every PDF chart, round axis steps; in PDF tables, amounts line up on the right in both languages.
- **Invoices: status by stage.** The row of status chips and its "+N more" menu give way to five stages, as on the dashboards: to correct, decision needed, processing, at the platform, completed, each with its count. A click on a stage shows all its statuses; its arrow lists them with their counts to tick one or several, across stages. The counts follow the period, the direction and Exclude reviewed errors, like the list.
- **Statistics dashboard.** A new Statistics page, the fourth dashboard after the Billing overview, Operations and IT, shows where the invoices of the period stand, sales or purchases, on this month by default. Four headline figures compared with the previous period: invoices and their amount, the share that reached the platform, the invoices to handle, those open for more than 7 days. A bar of the five stages (to correct, decision needed, processing, at the platform, completed) with their counts and change; the period day by day, week by week or month by month by stage; the open invoices by waiting time; every status with its share and change; the most frequent reasons; the split per transaction type and per activity code; and the detail by activity code, status and reason with one column per transaction type, in number of invoices or amount excl. VAT, each line compared with the previous period, with its own Excel export. Each stage, status or bar opens the invoices concerned. Excel export (one sheet per block, with the data) and PDF in the audit report's layout. Visible with the Dashboard access.
- **Status statistics move to the Statistics dashboard.** The Status statistics tab leaves Reports: its table by activity code, status and reason, per transaction type, is now on the Statistics dashboard, with the comparison to the previous period and Excel and PDF exports. Reports opens on Integrity.
- **Default periods.** Every page with a period now opens on this month, unless the user has picked another one there. Settings › Views & UI › Default periods sets the period for every view and, if needed, a different one per view (Billing overview, Operations, Statistics, Invoices, E-Documents, Diagnostics, Integration errors, Processing log, Reports). The Explorer's analyses and dashboards keep their own period.
- **List views settings grouped.** Settings › List views groups the lists by where they appear — e-invoicing, diagnostics, jobs, documentation and administration — sorted by name, and a list without an override is marked default. Opening it no longer highlights NomaUBL database in the settings menu.
- **Implementation and technical reports brought up to date.** The implementation report lists every page as it is today — Billing overview, Operations, IT dashboard, Statistics, Explorer, Schematrons — and gains a section on dashboards, lists and exports: sales or purchases, the comparison period, the five stages, Exclude reviewed errors, exports with labels, list views and the instance's default periods. The technical report describes the dashboard and analysis layer and the shared interface (lists, period picker, status stages).
- **Reports redesigned.** The Reports page opens on four cards — Integrity, Audit, Implementation, Technical — each saying what it is for. The audit, implementation and technical reports share one layout: settings on the left (the audit period with the shared period picker, last month by default, date basis inside it; direction, language and companies as switches), the contents on the right as tiles with a line on what each section holds, All / None, and a bar with PDF, Markdown, the progress and the result. Integrity lists its checks with their description, mode and connector, runs over a period and shows the outcome as a banner — no anomaly or the count, with source and target counts and duration — above the grid; the SQL folds away.
- **Diagnostics: views as cards.** The four views of Diagnostics — Integration errors, Processing log, Failures, Server log — are picked from a row of compact cards under the header, each saying what it shows, instead of the switch at the top right; only the views the role grants are shown.
- **Explorer: Analyses and Dashboards as tabs.** The switch at the top right gives way to two tabs on the first row of the Explorer, Analyses and Dashboards, each with the number saved; the picker of saved analyses or dashboards and Save sit on the same row, at the right.
- **VAT declaration redesigned.** Three headline figures open the page — VAT collected, VAT deductible and VAT due (or VAT credit), each with its base, its number of invoices and the change from the previous month or quarter. One filter bar as on the dashboards: Month / Quarter, year, month or quarter, company, the two exclusions as switches with their explanation on hover, Excel and PDF. The table reads by direction, then by country group, then by rate: Sales and Purchases carry their totals on their line, France, intra-EU and outside the EU appear once with their subtotal, each rate below them; amounts are in the normal colour and open the invoices on hover. The net VAT is no longer shown in red. The period labels are translated. In the CA3 PDF, amounts are written 125 315,78, rates 5,5 % and the period 01/09/2026 – 30/09/2026.
- **Synthèse and Statistics: permissions of their own.** The two business dashboards no longer follow the Operations dashboard permission: each has its own page in the roles (Synthèse, Statistics), also checked by the server and the AI assistant's tools. On upgrade, every role that had the Operations dashboard receives both, once, so nobody loses a page; removing them from a role afterwards is kept. A role without the Synthèse opens on the first page it grants.
- **Role row filters on document columns.** A role restricted on a column of the archived document — activity code, business unit, sub-type, source file, job, program, routing… — or on the direction saw empty dashboards, status counts and Synthèse, and could not open its own invoices from the list. These filters now apply everywhere as they do in the invoice list.
- **Role row filters across lists.** A row filter now applies to every list that has the field, under the name that list gives it (customer, activity code, job, UBL number, status…), and is ignored on a list that has no such field: a role restricted to FATAL severity keeps its invoices, documents and dashboards instead of seeing nothing. An E-Documents window opens under the same rules as its list.
- **Roles: row filters by table, dashboard cards removed.** The row-filter picker lists each field once, by scope: the keys doc, dct and kco, which secure every table that has them; the fields of the archived document (F564230), which secure every table linked to it; then the fields of each other table (invoice, validation findings, processing log, e-reporting), which secure that table. The per-card permissions of the Operations dashboard are gone: a role sees the dashboard or not; card grants already stored are ignored and dropped when the role is next saved. The "Contract" column of the integration errors is the customer's alpha key, as on the invoice list.
- **New invoice on E-Invoicing.** Creating an invoice moves to a New invoice button on the E-Invoicing list (with the invoice.create permission). The Quick actions block of the Operations dashboard is removed.
- **VAT declaration: no drill-down.** The amounts no longer open the invoice list, which could not reproduce the rate and the exclusions; each rate still unfolds into its transaction types and invoices. Amounts follow the interface language.
- **IT dashboard translated.** The title, the description and every card of the IT dashboard are translated.
- **Roles editor translated; wording aligned.** The roles editor — tabs, features, actions with their help, data scope, messages — is translated. The Explorer's switch reads "Exclude handled errors" in French like everywhere else, the English menu says IT dashboard, the VAT declaration's description no longer mentions opening the invoices, and the daily digest hides "Send even when the period has no errors" for the Synthèse and the Statistics, which are always sent.
- **Refresh on the business dashboards.** The Billing overview and the Statistics get a refresh button next to their filters, as on Operations.
- **Stylesheet errors explained.** When a UBL or post-transform stylesheet does not compile, the error recorded on the invoice now gives Saxon's reasons — file, line and message — instead of only "Errors were reported during stylesheet compilation".
- **Notifications fired again.** Since the Explorer's "Reviewed error" field, every status change logged "NOTIFY : maybeFire" and no notification rule fired; rules are evaluated again.
- **Upgrade: customised UBL defaults kept compiling.** When an instance's ubl-defaults.xsl holds its own version of a framework template (the seller party, for example), the upgrade now adds the parameters the new framework passes to it — with their shipped defaults, the template's body untouched — as it already did for the per-document stylesheets; the upgrade report still lists the template, whose customised body ignores the new values until it is updated from ubl-defaults.xsl.upstream. Until now such an instance stopped producing UBL after the upgrade ("Parameter … is not declared in the called template").
- **Daily digest: the business dashboards.** A digest can send the Synthèse or the Statistics, as PDF (the page's figures, charts and tables) or Excel, over last month, the month to date or the digest window, for sales or purchases. It can be built as a role sees it — its companies and row filters — so each recipient group receives only its scope. Any digest can be sent on one day of the month only (for example on the 1st, last month's overview); Send now ignores it.
- **Invoice types: enable or disable.** In Settings › Invoice types, each code has an Active box. An unticked code stays in the list — its labels still show on existing invoices and its invoice / credit note kind still applies — but it is no longer offered in the pickers (UBL defaults, invoice form, list and Explorer filters). A new installation offers the 16 codes of French e-invoicing (380, 381, 384, 386, 389, 393, 396, 261, 262, 471, 472, 473, 500 to 503); an upgrade leaves the existing list as it is.
- **Exclude reviewed errors: invoices without a review mark kept.** An invoice in error whose review mark was empty (an invoice written without it) disappeared from the error counts and lists as if reviewed; only an invoice marked reviewed is left out now.
- **API: form creation route removed.** POST /api/invoices answered success without creating anything; it is removed. Invoices are created with POST /api/invoices/create-ubl (a UBL document) or POST /api/process (a source file through a document's mapping).
- **Desktop app.** NomaUBL can be installed as a desktop application on Windows and macOS from Chrome or Edge (Install button in the address bar) or Safari (File › Add to Dock): its own window and icon, no browser bars, always the server's version. Each environment installs as its own app, named after it ("NomaUBL · TEST"). Requires the server to be reached over HTTPS. The application icon shows the full NomaUBL logo.
- **List views: Reset to defaults in one click.** The button now shows the shipped columns at once; saving keeps them. It used to show the customised columns again until a second click.
- **Invoices: mark errors as reviewed.** Customer service can mark invoices in error as reviewed: from the invoice list (select them, then Mark reviewed) or from the invoice window, where a "Reviewed" chip at the right of the tabs sets or clears it; each time after a confirmation. A reviewed invoice keeps its status and is left out of the error counts while "Exclude reviewed errors" is on. New permission "Mark reviewed", given on upgrade to the roles that can edit invoices or push a status in the database.
- **Invoices: Send to PA column.** The default invoice list shows whether each invoice is meant for the platform (for the platform, not for the platform, held for review before sending), with its labels and a filter on the list, instead of the status note. A list view already customised keeps its columns.
- **Navigation: auto collapse.** Settings › Navigation & lists can fold the navigation to its icons: the pages get the width, and hovering the icons opens the menu over the page; picking a page folds it back.
- **Promotion: a document's files on their own.** Each file a document uses (transform, XSL, RTF, UBL stylesheet, customer Schematron, PDF layout) is listed among the files, with the documents using it, and can be promoted alone — a stylesheet shared by several documents no longer requires promoting a document.
- **Processing log: processing and scheduled jobs apart.** A switch Processing / Scheduled jobs / All sits next to Grouped / Flat; the log opens on Processing, so the runs of the status and import polls (every few minutes) no longer bury the file processing. A job run opened from Failures lands on Scheduled jobs. Their retention is already separate: Settings › Job defaults › Retention, "Job runs (days)".
- **Start page.** Settings › Navigation & lists chooses the page shown after sign-in (Billing overview unless set): a dashboard, Invoices, E-Documents, E-reporting, VAT declaration, Diagnostics, Reports or the Explorer. A user whose role does not grant it opens the Billing overview, else the first page the role grants.
- **Dashboards: cached figures.** The Billing overview, Statistics and Operations dashboards keep the figures they loaded, so coming back to them or changing page no longer queries again; an open dashboard reloads on its own after the delay, and Refresh reloads at once. On the IT dashboard, only documents processed per day is kept, on the server for every user. Each shows when its figures were loaded. Delay in Settings › Navigation & lists (60 minutes unless set, 0 = always reload).
- **Reviewed errors left out by default.** The Operations dashboard and the invoice list open with "Exclude reviewed errors" on, like the Billing overview and Statistics; a link from a dashboard keeps its own choice.
- **Billing overview: transmission rate over the invoices to send.** The transmission rate, its issued / not issued split and the per-company share count only the invoices meant for the platform (sent, or held for review); invoices of document types not sent to the platform no longer lower it. The "Reached the platform" rate of the Statistics dashboard follows the same rule, and so does the daily digest.
- **Portal notifications without a recipient go to everyone.** With sign-in enabled, a rule on the portal channel with no user or role recorded nothing; it now writes one entry visible in every inbox, as without sign-in. The rule editor names this choice "Everyone".
- **Notifications from the status poll.** A scheduled status poll waits for the notifications it triggered before exiting (they were cut after two seconds), and a settings change on a running server lets the queued ones finish.
- **Lists: rows per page and rows loaded by default.** Settings › Navigation & lists sets, for every list, the rows per page (50 unless set) and the rows loaded per refresh (100 000 unless set, instead of 5 000); a list view of Settings › List views can still set its own. The E-reporting list is no longer limited to 200 declarations.
- **List filters: pick or type.** The filters on a coded column — advanced filters, column filters and the Explorer — still offer the list's values, and also accept codes typed in the search box (Enter, comma-separated for several), so a list that is incomplete or still empty (for example a custom list of document types or sub-types) still filters.
- **Mapping check: invoice type code.** A blank BT-3 mapping is no longer reported as missing: the code comes from the UBL defaults (invoice-type rules, then the default code), like the other fields filled by the defaults.
- **Diagnostics › Failures: fast with "Unresolved only".** Whether a failed file was processed successfully later is now worked out in one pass over the processing log instead of one pass per failure.
- **Statistics: fast on large archives.** The page no longer reads the whole document archive: the activity code is fetched for the invoices of the period only, so it loads quickly where the archive holds millions of documents.
- **PDF: wide tables.** Columns size to their content without crushing the text: a column never gets narrower than its header's longest word or its longest word, a number or a percentage never splits (a value with its share breaks only at the dot), and a table too wide for the page switches to a smaller font instead of breaking words.
- **PDF: euro sign in italic notes.** In the notes under a section title, the euro sign no longer runs into the following word.
- **AI assistant: new pages and two tools.** The assistant knows the Billing overview, Statistics, Explorer and the invoice stages, and reads the figures of the two business dashboards: billing_overview (revenue, VAT, credit notes, transmission rate, decisions, per company and per transaction type, compared with the previous period) and status_statistics (invoices by stage, statuses, reasons, waiting time, activity × status × reason with the previous period). Since it reads the implementation report, it also knows the default periods and the dashboard rules of the instance.
- **List exports carry the labels.** In every list, the CSV and Excel exports of a column backed by a value list (company, document type, activity code, reason…) now write the code with its label, as on screen, instead of the code alone.
- **Operations dashboard reorganised, IT dashboard reorganised.** The former Dashboard is now named Operations, opens on this month and is organised around what the team has to handle, with the same header as the other pages and the same Sales / Purchases switch as the Synthèse, which every widget follows. Under a one-line summary of the period, three work queues — in progress (followed automatically), to correct and send again (IT), a new invoice to issue (customer service) — each show their total and their breakdown by status, label first with the code as a small tag; every number opens the invoices concerned. Then one activity chart whose legend carries the period's counts (replacing the separate pipeline bar), grouped by week beyond two months and by month beyond a year; the invoices blocked the longest and the latest events side by side, in plain words; and a row with the most-failing rules, the platform delay and e-reporting. The per-company chart moves to the Synthèse. The IT dashboard is reorganised the same way: a health strip of six tiles (application, database, scheduler, disk, memory, configuration — green, orange or red, each opening its detail), the four action cards (send failures, held for review, to reprocess, to reprocess in full) in one row, their figures aligned, one card for the last 14 days with tabs — documents processed per day with those now in a technical error (a bar opens that day's invoices), errors, retries, time per document — what is running right now (processes, live events, scheduler, sessions), the recent errors, and the technical details (system, filesystem, JVM, configuration check, database tables, links) folded at the bottom; nothing is removed.
- **New period picker.** Every page's period is now one button showing the range itself ("1 – 30 Sep 2026"). It opens a panel with the presets as a list — today, yesterday, last 7 and 30 days, this month, last month, this quarter, this year, last 12 months, all — a two-month calendar to pick any range, and, where the page has one, the date it applies to (activity, document or archive date), which used to sit in separate buttons on the dashboard, invoices, e-documents and status statistics. Next to it, "Exclude reviewed errors" is the same on every page — a switch framed like the period button, lit when on — on the dashboard, invoices, status statistics and the Explorer. "Yesterday" still covers yesterday and today, so a night batch running across midnight shows whole, and "Last year" is named "Last 12 months", which is what it covers.
- **Lighter web interface.** Each page is now loaded when it is first opened instead of with the application, and the large libraries and the translations are separate files the browser keeps between releases: the first load is lighter and the build reports no warning.
- **Schematrons page.** A new Schematrons page, under Documentation after Business Rules, shows the rules of one Schematron at a time: those shipped with NomaUBL (EN 16931, CIUS-FR flux 2, extended CTC, Chorus Pro, NomaUBL, e-reporting flux 10) with their version, and the customer packs named by the document templates, with the templates using them. Each rule is a row — code, severity, description, context — that can be searched, filtered and exported, and opens on its test and message. Visible with the Business Rules access.
- **Integration errors: activity code.** The integration errors list shows and filters the activity code, with its labels.
- **Promotion: promote from the selection.** Promote to an instance moves under Export, next to the package download: pick the target and press Promote…; the selection is checked on the target and a window shows what would change there (new, changed, identical, each with its field diff), with the policy and the comment; Promote writes and the same window shows the result. The separate Promote tab is gone.
- **Shared checkboxes everywhere.** Notification rules, actions, users, enrichment, the PDF designer, file versions, status retrieval, integration errors, the buyer fix and the row selection of every table use the application's checkbox instead of the browser's.

### Fixes
- **Grouped tables: checkbox stays first.** When a table is grouped, the selection checkbox stays in the first column instead of moving after the grouped column, and a group's label and count are no longer cut by the column width.
- **Explorer: New clears the page.** Choosing New analysis or New dashboard while one is open now starts from an empty one instead of keeping the previous content.
- **Transaction types in English.** The document-types list carries only French labels; English screens, PDFs and spreadsheets showed its send flag (1, 0) instead. The French label now serves both languages.
- **E-reporting: consolidated credit notes.** A 262 credit note (consolidated credit note) now counts negatively in the B2C totals, like the other credit notes.
- **Line amount warning (BR-NOMAUBL-02) reworded.** The warning now opens with the rule itself — the line net amount must equal the unit price divided by the base quantity, times the quantity, less line allowances plus line charges — then gives the line, the declared and the computed amounts; its description in the integration errors and the Schematrons page is that rule instead of a raw piece of the Schematron.
- **Explorer charts: legend for a single series.** A chart split by a field (Series) now shows its legend even when the period holds only one value of that field, so a single bar still says what it counts.
- **Clicking outside a dropdown only closes it.** Closing the period picker or a dropdown by clicking elsewhere no longer also triggers what was clicked, such as opening the invoice of a table row.
- **Chart tooltips on one line.** A chart's tooltip keeps each label and value on one line and opens on the side of the pointer with room, instead of wrapping against the chart's edge.
- **Explorer pivot: aligned values with shares.** When a pivot shows each value with its share, the values now line up down the column whatever the width of the percentage ("6.2 %" or "100.0 %").
- **Custom lists: wider code column.** The code column of a custom list is wide enough for longer codes.
- **Dropdowns show "All".** A dropdown left on its "all" choice (All sources, All templates, All companies…) now shows it instead of an empty field.
