## 2026.10.24.1 — 2026-10-24 \{#v2026-10-24-1\}

### Improvements

- **Diagnostics: one page for errors and logs.** Integration Errors, Processing Log and Server Log leave the menu and become views of a single Diagnostics page, next to a new Failures view. The switcher reads Integration errors, Processing log, Failures, Server log; each view appears only when the role grants its former page, and the dashboard links that opened the old pages land on the right view with the same filters. Integration errors opens by rule by default, and every dated view starts on yesterday. The by-rule grid no longer flickers on scroll or hover with many rules: the cards dropped their background blur and off-screen cards are skipped by the browser; the cards also stay in place while a new period loads, and the first load no longer races the period filter.
- **Failures: every failure in one list.** The Failures view lists, with one shape, the validation findings, the PA rejections, the send and import failures, the processing failures per file and the failed job runs: when, kind, source (invoice number, file or job), template, company, current status, level, rule, message. Unresolved only by default, which hides failures the invoice, file or job has moved past (status left the error statuses, a later successful run). Filters on period, kinds with their counts, template and company; the message search runs on the server across every page. A row opens the invoice window, the processing log narrowed to the file, or the scheduled jobs. Export as on every grid.
- **Every job run is recorded.** Each run of a scheduled job, fired by the schedule or by Run now, writes a start row and an end or error row in the runtime processing log, with its duration and a one-line outcome; the same for the command-line job switches. The Scheduled jobs page shows the last runs of a job behind a History action, and keeps its last-run column across restarts. The run id appears in the server log lines of that run, so the two can be joined.
- **Retention purge.** A daily job can bound the stores that nothing bounded: processing rows, step timings and job runs of the runtime log, validation errors of invoices in a terminal status, notifications. Days per store are set in Settings → Job defaults → Retention or in the job's editor; the job is off by default except the notifications, which keep their 90 days, so an upgrade deletes nothing by itself. A "Count only" button in the job editor and `nomaubl.sh purge --dry-run` report what each store would lose before anything is deleted.
- **Developer reference: configuration, flows, impact.** The Data dictionary page becomes Developer, with four views. Tables is the dictionary. Configuration lists every configuration key with where it is edited (template, tab, group, label, hint), the flows that read it and its call sites, generated by a build-time join of the settings editors' fields with every property read in the Java code, helpers and constants included; two toggles isolate the keys read but not editable and the keys editable but never read, and a row opens the editor fields and the code. Flows gives one short page per flow — process a file, import poll, status poll, e-reporting, watched folders, reprocess — with trigger, command-line switch, log module, tables, statuses, settings and steps, bundled from the docs folder. Impact takes a column, a configuration key or a status and shows the flows, screens, API endpoints and command-line switches it reaches, the editor that exposes it, then the code; endpoints come from a scan of the server routes down to their handler class, status codes and labels from the catalogue of the instance. The build also renders the three parts as one Markdown file for the docs site, next to the API reference.
- **Developer: API view and guided impact picker.** A fifth view shows the API of the instance the way the other views are read: tag groups and tags with their counts on the left, one row per operation in the shared data table (method, path, summary, tag, access), and a window with the description, the parameters and request and response samples built from the schemas with their references resolved, as Redoc shows them. A Getting started button opens the introduction; the public Redoc page stays reachable from the view and for readers outside the application. The Impact picker is now in steps — the kind (column, configuration key, status), then the table or template, then the item in a wide list that reads the label first — instead of one mixed list.
- **Promotion: move items, not files.** A new Promotion page under Management, next to File Versions, promotes configuration items between instances with the ZIP as transport only. Export: tick document templates, PDF templates and reference or custom lists in a tree by kind; a template carries the files it references (pre-processing and indexation XSL, RTF, UBL XSLT and its PDF companion, custom Schematron) and the PDF template it names, shown under it and added automatically. The package holds a manifest (items, checksums, source instance and release, author, date), one fragment per item and the files with paths relative to the environment root, so the path placeholders stay valid on the target. Passwords, secrets, tokens, API keys, the license, the environment name and colour and the watermarks never travel. Import: a preview first, one row per item and per file — new, changed, identical, skipped — with the field diff of a changed template, target against package; then apply with a policy, replace or keep the target for changed ones, and a comment. Each template is upserted by name into its own configuration file, the other templates of that file untouched; each file is written after a version snapshot; instance keys already present keep their values; the import is one entry of the versioning log with its author. The package mode of File Versions stays for raw files. Other kinds (notification rules, digests, retries, checks, integrity checks, connectors, settings) come next.
- **Developer: Configuration view reorganised.** The templates are listed on the left with their key counts and gaps, grouped like the Settings navigation; the grid shows the keys of the selected template with their label, where they are edited, who reads them and their state. The build-time scan only keeps real configuration keys, so stray words from the code no longer appear.
- **Promotion: every kind.** The Promotion page now covers notification rules, daily digests, auto-retries, lifecycle checks, connectors (API, SQL, database, FTP), the settings templates (e-invoicing, e-reporting, e-directory, watched folders, integrity checks, reports, JDE print queue) and the shared UBL defaults file, next to the document templates, PDF templates and lists. Instance keys never travel and, when already present on the target, keep their values: passwords, secrets, tokens, API keys, the license, URLs, hosts, users, the database schema, the environment name and colour, the watermarks. Promoting the e-invoicing settings from test to production thus carries the behaviour, the document types and the actions, not the platform account. Global and single sign-on never travel.
- **Roles: grants that read like the menu.** The page grants of a role are shown as cards, one per sidebar group, in the menu's order and names, with a count and an all / none link; each page is a toggle chip, its id and description in the tooltip. Diagnostics appears once with its four view grants under it, each still granted on its own, so existing roles keep working. Dashboard cards and action groups use the same cards. The server's admin page list, which seeds the admin role on a fresh install, gains VAT declaration, Reports and Upgrade history, and the sidebar shows Diagnostics to a role that holds any of its view grants.
- **Implementation report.** Reports gains an Implementation report tab that generates the technical and functional documentation of the instance from its configuration files and database, in French or English, as Markdown or PDF; a copy is kept under the environment's reports folder, and the command line has the same with `report <env>`. Sections: context, architecture (the flows enabled, polls, batches, connectors), a functional guide (what every page is for, the invoice lifecycle, the protection of deposited invoices, edit / fix / resend rules with their permissions, reprocess, status poll with the integrity and ordering checks, review and notifications, a light reference of the platform statuses and of the internal stages), the documents with their files, index fields, pre-transform and UBL sheet references and the PDF templates, the UBL transform (shared defaults, issuing companies, mapping tables and rules, validation packs with their rule counts, coverage per document, one subsection per pre-transform and per UBL sheet with the source field to BT mapping and the overrides), platform settings and document types, operations (scheduled jobs, watched folders, notification rules and invoice actions in detail, integrity checks, connectors), security (roles and users), reference data (status catalogue and every list), and optional appendices (configuration keys, API reference). Secrets and instance keys are masked; technical keys are an option. The PDF has a cover, a clickable table of contents and outline, running header and footer, placeholder chips in paths, and section links.
- **Wording.** Document templates are now called documents throughout, and the French interface and notes say « modèle » rather than « gabarit ».
- **Audit report.** Reports gains an Audit report tab: the electronic invoicing of a period, from the NomaUBL tables only, as Markdown or PDF with the same cover, contents and layout as the implementation report; the command line has `audit <env>`. Period (previous month by default), date basis (issue date or last update), companies, direction and sections are chosen on the tab; the signed-in user's company visibility applies. Sections: scope; executive summary with the previous period of the same length and the variation (processed, deposited, approved, refused, rejected, in error, pending, excluded, received, deposited amounts, first-pass validation rate, terminal share, delays from creation to deposit and from deposit to the first buyer status) followed by the findings in words; volumes per month, company, document, transaction type and VAT category; the situation at generation time by status and family with the stale pending and unreviewed errors; the errors and their handling (findings per rule and source, rejections and refusals per reason, send and import failures, resolved / reviewed / open by age, resends and reprocesses). No invoice lists, so the report stays short whatever the volume. The report runs as a background job with a progress bar naming the current step; each step's duration is written to the server log.
- **Implementation report wording.** The French text says « règles spécifiques » for the NomaUBL rule pack.
- **Audit report: lifecycle and consistency checks.** Two sections join the audit report. Lifecycle and delays: the invoices reaching each milestone per month (created, validated, failed, sent, deposited, received, approved, refused, rejected, paid) and the delays from creation to first send, first send to deposit, creation to deposit and deposit to first buyer status, as median and 90th percentile. Consistency checks: invoices in a platform status without a platform identifier, sent invoices without an archived UBL, stale pending, duplicate invoice numbers within a company, VAT total against the stored breakdown, net total against the stored lines, refusals and rejections without follow-up; an option adds the configured SQL integrity checks against JDE with their discrepancy counts. The executive summary and the status section count the invoices deposited but not transmitted (200 with reason NON_TRANSMISE) and explain that the recipient is not registered with any platform. The status table is sorted by code.
- **Audit report: operations, activity, evolution and charts.** An Operations section lists the scheduled job runs with errors and durations, the files processed per mode and document, the portal notifications per rule and the e-reporting envelopes per status. Volumes open with the evolution inside the period, per day, week or month according to its length, with the invoices deposited and in error per bucket; a table per activity gives invoices, deposits, errors and amounts per line of business; the company, document and transaction-type tables carry the previous period and the variation. The PDF draws charts: invoices per period bucket, per activity, the status family donut, the milestones per bucket and the most frequent rules. A whole calendar month, quarter or year compares to the preceding months instead of the same number of days; the tab offers a calendar-month picker next to custom dates. Rejections, refusals and error events are sorted by code; e-reporting envelopes covering a period that ends in the audit period are included.
- **Audit report: consistent, readable and complete.** The executive summary gains a breakdown of the processed invoices where every level adds up: not to send to the platform (transaction types configured not to be sent, such as B2C or international), to send, deposited, in progress, approved, rejected, not deposited and why. Deposit rates are taken over the invoices to send, in the summary, per day and per activity. Send attempts, resends (automatic retries included) and the send failure rate measure the platform's availability. Buyer-identifier fixes are reported as actions. The follow-up check covers every status awaiting an action, in two families: to fix and resend (rejected, validation failed, import failed) and answer to the buyer expected (disputed, suspended, refused). The backlog section lists the unreviewed invoices older than 30 days per status and shows net amounts; the Min invoice date setting bounds its all-periods figures. New checks: VAT lines with an amount but no rate; failed e-reporting envelopes are flagged. Per-activity tables are split in two, chart legends wrap, the per-mode table and the command-line hints are gone.
- **AI assistant: the instance, the period, offline documentation.** Two new tools: the implementation report of the instance, read by section or searched, so the assistant answers from the actual configuration (documents sent to the platform, rule packs, notification rules, roles and users, which action a status allows); and the period figures, the audit report's summary and backlog in seconds, for a monthly summary, rates, amounts or what awaits an action, within the user's company visibility. The playbooks follow the two action families (fix and resend; answer to the buyer, credit note mandatory only for a refusal) and a backlog playbook is added. The documentation index is per language: the French pages ground French answers (new URL setting, empty = English pages). The NomaUBL section of the documentation is bundled in the jar and used when the site is unreachable, with a note in the answer; the URL also accepts a local file. The starter questions become a domain picker (period, backlog, invoices, statuses and errors, configuration, documentation, technical, this invoice) with four questions each, the page choosing the starting domain; the domains stay available after an answer next to its follow-ups.
- **Technical report.** Reports gains a Technical report tab, with the API route and the command line, that generates the developer documentation of the release as Markdown or PDF from the scans bundled at build: scope, architecture, data model (every table with its columns, configuration keys, flows and call sites, and the name resolved in this instance when it differs), the flow documents each completed with the tables, statuses and keys their code touches, the configuration reference (every key with its settings field, where it is edited, flows, call sites and state, with a gaps summary), the status model (invoice and e-reporting tags with codes, labels, groups and setting flows), the impact matrix per flow with the most referenced columns and keys, the API reference with access per operation, the command line from the built-in help, the build steps with the generated artefacts and the jar layout, and an appendix of code references. Two options: detail every API operation, include the code snippets. Identical on every instance of a release.
- **Placeholder picker everywhere a token is resolved.** The insert-placeholder button now sits beside every field the server substitutes: the path constants on the Global directories and server log file, the document's UBL XSLT and custom Schematron, the E-invoicing XSLT directory, the watch-folder directory and manifest, and the image source of a PDF template block; the processing directories and the document XSLT also offer the run-time tokens of the document name and the input file name. API connector endpoints offer, per endpoint, the built-in credentials and token, the endpoint's own declared parameters and the values the callers pass; the authentication body and headers offer the authentication names; connector sources offer the single-brace tokens; SQL connector queries offer their declared parameters as :name tokens. The panel opens to whichever side has room and is no longer clipped by its row.
- **VAT declaration: refused, rejected and unsent invoices.** The declaration counted every invoice issued in the period whatever its status. Invoices refused by the buyer (210) or rejected by the platform (213) call for an internal credit note: a checkbox, on by default, leaves them all out; unchecked, only those customer service marked reviewed are left out. A second checkbox, off by default, also leaves out the invoices flagged to be sent that never reached the platform (validation, send or import failure, not yet sent). Both apply to the matrix, the drill-down, the Excel export and the PDF, whose footer states the rules applied; the API takes excludeMode and excludeUnsent.
- **Directory check: warn or block.** The E-directory settings gain a "Recipient not found" mode. Warn and send, the default, keeps today's behaviour: the miss is recorded as a warning and the invoice is sent. Block: on an invoice meant for the platform, a definitive answer from the directory (not registered, found but not reachable) or a missing EndpointID is a fatal finding; the invoice stops at validation failed and is not sent. A connector or network error only warns in both modes, and invoices configured not to be sent are never blocked. The UBL-file pipeline now records the lookup result like the JDE pipeline.
- **Demo instance: a sample corpus in one command.** A Global setting marks an instance as a demo instance; on such an instance only, the `-demo` command line fills the database with fictitious invoices: five issuing companies and thirty buyers with valid identifiers, invoices and credit notes of every type, every VAT category, document and line allowances and charges, prepayments, payees, tax representatives, deliveries, every payment means, attachments and references, spread over the last six months. Every invoice passes the French rule packs, a few are deliberately invalid, and all go through the real processing pipeline; the invoices meant for the platform are then driven through realistic paths, sent, pending, deposited, refused, rejected, disputed, suspended, approved, paid, with send and import failures, dated over the period. The same seed gives the same corpus; a reset switch removes everything the command created. The corpus also comes as JDE-like XML spools and as text PDFs, through two more demo documents that use the real XML pipeline: the spool mapping, generated from the framework template, shows nested paths, a constant, a summed VAT total, a field reached anywhere in the block and a line break in the payment terms; the PDF document shows the PDF-to-XML conversion with two address blocks, labelled rows, one table and regex fields for the document key. One run produces the three sources (60 % UBL files, 30 % spool invoices, 10 % PDF invoices); `--sources` narrows it. The demo requires the global Update DB switch at Y and writes its processing-log rows like the Process page. It also covers the platform side: supplier invoices received as UBL through a fourth demo document and driven through the buyer path (made available, under processing, approved and paid, disputed, refused); e-reporting envelopes generated by the real handler for every completed month, blank issuer and sender filled from the first demo company, then driven to deposited, import failed or rejected; a portal-only notification rule for refusals, rejections and failures, with the dispatcher started only when no rule of the instance sends e-mail. When the Demo instance flag is Y, Settings › Global shows a Demo corpus block that fills or resets the corpus as a background job with the usual progress window. The reset removes everything the demo created.
- **Promotion: promote to another instance, and a history.** Target instances are defined once in Settings › Promotion targets (name, URL, account; the password is stored encoded and used on the server for the call only, never in a package). On the Promotion page, a Promote view sends the Export selection to the chosen target: a dry run first shows the target's own preview, new, changed, identical, skipped with the field diffs, then Promote applies it with the usual policy and comment. The ZIP export stays for sites that cannot reach each other. A History view lists every package exported, import applied and promotion applied on the instance, with who, when, the counterpart, the policy, the comment and the full plan; a source keeps its promotions, a target its imports.
- **Mapping tab: rule sets.** The Variable Mapping tab of the XSL editor now reads a rule set: EN 16931 basic, EN 16931, or France extended, preselected on the one the template produces today and switchable to preview another. Every tag shows whether the set requires it, requires it under a condition (with the note and the rule ids), leaves it optional, does not know it, or gets it from the UBL defaults. Filters narrow to the required and conditional tags or to the required ones still missing; tags outside the set are hidden unless asked for, so the French extension tags appear only under the extended set. A completeness line per group counts the required fields with a source, a constant or a default. "Check mapping" lists the required fields without a source, then transforms the loaded sample with the mapping as edited and validates it; the report groups the findings by field and the tags concerned are highlighted. The rule sets are generated from the UBL reference data at build and can be overridden per environment. A document template can now name its rule set on its UBL tab: the validator then runs the packs the set lists, in every pipeline and in the invoice window's validation; blank keeps today's choice from the customization id, and the two default sets list exactly today's chain. The invoice window names the set an invoice was produced under, and the UBL reference and Business rules pages take the same set filter, with the status of each field.
- **Mapping: more tag syntaxes.** Tag values in a document mapping accept three more forms: `sum(a, b, …)` adds the amounts found at several paths, `//Field` finds a field anywhere in the spool, and `"\n"` in a concatenation inserts a line break. Existing mappings produce the same output as before. The mapping panel lists the path syntaxes above the root fields.
- **UBL defaults: VAT rate by source code.** The VAT tab gains a grid mapping the line's VAT category source (a tax zone, a tax type or a composite code built in the mapping) to a rate, with a switch: keep the source rate and let the grid fill blank rates, the default, or let a matching entry win over the printed rate. The same rate applies to the VAT breakdown rows, and a document can override the grid like the rest of the VAT family. On the category and rate grids a source ending in `*` covers every code starting with it; exact codes are tried first. An exemption reason is never emitted on the taxed and zero-rated categories, whatever the source says. Nothing changes in the produced invoices until the grid is filled; the upgrade adds the grid to each existing defaults file.
- **Post-transform: the validated UBL in another syntax.** A document's UBL tab gains a Post-transform stylesheet and an output suffix. After a validation with no blocking finding, the UBL is run through the stylesheet and the result is written next to it; a failure is recorded as a warning and the UBL keeps its course. UBL remains the pivot everywhere. The invoice and document windows gain a download of the derived file, named after the post-transform's name set on the document, computed on demand from the archived UBL. The platform connector body can send the converted file instead of the UBL with two new placeholders, derived content and derived file path, on the initial send and on resend alike; the UBL keeps the routing. Shipped stylesheet: UBL to Cross Industry Invoice (CII D16B, EN 16931 core), checked on the demo corpus against the official EN 16931 CII rules; the demo UBL document is configured with it.
- **API connectors: platform endpoints folded.** The list of endpoints NomaUBL calls on a platform is collapsed by default in the connector editor, with the configured count on its header; expand it to add one.

### Fixes

- **E-reporting envelope: credit notes and EU buyers.** The detailed block of a credit note or a corrective invoice carried no reference to the preceding invoice, which the platform's rule G1.32 requires; the preceding invoices are now read from the archived UBL's billing references and written with their date. The buyer's legal identifier was omitted when the buyer's electronic address was a national VAT number under its national scheme (German, Dutch, Italian, Spanish…), which failed rule G6.28; those schemes are now folded to the VAT identifier the envelope expects.
- **Job progress window.** It drew its own backdrop, so the page showed through it; it now uses the shared modal shell, like the resend from the IT dashboard.
- **Audit report on a large instance.** The report ran the lifecycle ordering check over the whole lifecycle table and sorted every lifecycle row in the database; both froze the generation on a large instance. The ordering check is left to the daily lifecycle check, the rows are folded in memory, the previous period computes only its summary counts, the findings query no longer sorts every message, and the error analysis reuses the rows already read. The report runs as a background job with a progress bar naming the current step, and each step's duration is written to the server log. Two checks were wrong: the platform identifier test missed blank-padded values on Oracle, and the integrity discrepancies were counted as zero.
- **Developer → API crashed.** Three request examples added with the promotion endpoints were plain text inside the OpenAPI document, which made it invalid JSON for the API view and for Redoc. They are proper JSON objects now, and the view shows a message instead of failing when the document cannot be read.
- **"Contains" filters with an underscore.** The shared filter builder treated the underscore as an explicit wildcard, so a value such as a file name fragment was sent without surrounding wildcards and had to match the whole value. Only the percent sign is a wildcard now; this fixes the file filter of the processing log and every text filter on the other grids.
- **XSD card of the by-rule view.** The card without a rule id drilled into the events with an empty filter and showed everything. It now drills on "no rule id" plus its source; the source column of the integration errors view became a server filter.
- **Audit report figures.** The first-pass validation rate counted the platform send failures as validation findings and missed the invoices fixed since; it is now taken from the lifecycle. The deposited milestone, the delays and the summary used three definitions of a deposit; all use the first platform status. Buyer-identifier fix events were counted as import failures. The status family table did not add up to the total. The approved row included plain deposits. The failures table did not say it was capped.
- **Audit report on PostgreSQL.** The send-intent filter compared the flag column to a number; the column is a string on PostgreSQL, which rejected the query. It is now compared as text on both databases.

## 2026.10.23.1 — 2026-10-23 \{#v2026-10-23-1\}

### Improvements

- **Invert sign on a document template.** A new "Invert sign" setting in the Processing tab (UBL group) flips the sign of the amounts read from the source: line net amounts, document totals, prepaid and rounding amounts, total VAT and every VAT breakdown row. The unit price is always emitted as a positive value, allowance and charge amounts are read as absolute values, and the quantity takes the sign of its line amount. Three choices: No (default), Credit notes only (documents resolved as 381, 396, 261, 262, 502, 503) and All documents. A spool that prints a credit note with negative amounts thus yields the positive CreditNote the standard expects, with no change to the customer XSL. The value is passed to the transform at run time; a customer document XSL picks the behaviour up once the upgrade merge has refreshed its framework body.
- **Watched folders: own page, every template, new options.** The watched folders are now a page of the Synchronization group, with Save and Refresh in the header, and no longer appear in the Settings list. Each folder is a collapsible card with its fields in three groups: folder, scan and batch. New per-folder options: the scan window ("since last scan", the previous behaviour, or "all files", every matching file whatever its date, with no watermark) and the batch options of a scheduled Directory job (replace mode, send to PA, processing mode); replace mode takes a file already processed again. Every file-based template is supported: XML and PDF templates keep the single-JVM batch, a UBL template gets the per-file loop with failures moved to the errors folder. A folder that is the template's own input folder is a plain batch trigger, no copy, no date, no dedup, which is the watched-folder form of a scheduled Directory job. The run order is unchanged: all conversions first, then one batch per template. Folders feeding the same template must carry the same batch options; the first row wins and a mismatch is logged. Existing rows and scheduled jobs keep their behaviour, and the Directory and BIP scheduler sources remain available.
- **Environment badge and theme colour.** The global settings gain a "Theme colour" next to the environment name. The environment is shown as a badge right of the title and in the browser tab, and the colour replaces the accent blue of the whole interface: title, badge, primary buttons, links, focus rings. Both are served by a public endpoint, so the login page already carries them. Blank colour keeps the default blue.
- **Integrity checks: BIP placeholders, query templates, placeholder picker.** Three placeholders resolved from the fetch-invoices report list at each run, so a version added there is covered without editing the SQL: `{bipFilter:REPORTCOL,VERSIONCOL}` (the report/version predicate on the named columns), `{bipReports}` (quoted names for an IN list) and `{bipTemplate:REPORTCOL,VERSIONCOL}` (CASE giving each row's document template). A "Start from" selector pre-fills a check from four JDE comparisons: BIP jobs not integrated, customer ledger invoices absent from NomaUBL, sales-order invoices absent from NomaUBL, and an amount comparison between the customer ledger and NomaUBL headers (mismatch mode, HT, tax and TTC, tolerance 0.01). Both SQL fields carry the insert-placeholder button. The checks list opens collapsed and the hint is one line.
- **Scheduled batch failures named in the log.** After "Processed N/M document(s), K failed" the scheduler now lists each failed file with its first error message, so the cause is readable without opening the processing log. The single-JVM batch prints its failed file names at its end.
- **AI assistant rebuilt.** Answers are grounded on the documentation indexed from the site's `llms-full.txt`, downloaded and searched on the server (search, page reading, table of contents) instead of live page fetches by the model; the legacy sitemap mode stays selectable. The panel sends what you look at — current page and filter, open invoice — so "why is this invoice refused?" needs no reference typed, with a context chip you can dismiss and suggested questions per page. New read-only tools: one-call invoice dossier (header, lines, VAT, errors, lifecycle), dashboard counters, IT dashboard, server log tail, integrity checks (list or run), template settings with secrets masked and gated by the settings right, e-directory lookup, reason codes, and invoice search by number. Four built-in diagnostic playbooks the model loads on demand (refused invoice, missing invoice, e-reporting error, status not updated), extendable in the global settings. Default model Sonnet 5.5, selectable in settings and in the panel (Sonnet, Opus, Fable, Haiku), longer answers, more tool rounds, prompt caching on the fixed prompt. Each answer ends with clickable follow-ups; the conversation survives a reload; a New chat button; the panel stays usable while an invoice window is open. Strings in EN and FR.
- **File versions record who changed a file.** Each version and each action now carries the signed-in user when authentication is on, or "system" for an upgrade or a command-line run. The File Versions history shows a "By" column; versions recorded before this release show a dash. The versions database gains the column by itself on first use.
- **Assistant: a new invoice starts a new conversation.** Opening a different invoice drops the previous thread, which was about another document; closing the window keeps the current one.
- **Server log kept readable and bounded.** The status poll no longer prints one warning per event for a PA code missing from the statuses catalogue or for an invoice unknown to NomaUBL; the run ends with one line per code with its count and a sample invoice. Unmapped PA codes are listed by the IT dashboard configuration check with the number of events skipped, since the fix is a catalogue entry. A log policy, active in server mode only, caps the live log file (default 100 MB, 5 copies kept, copy-then-truncate so the launcher is untouched), collapses a WARN or ERROR line repeated within ten minutes into one summary line, and applies an optional minimum level per module. Four settings under Global → Processing: size cap, files kept, repeat window, levels. The Server log page is now the shared data table with its filters, sorting, paging and export, its view is listed in the List views editor, and the page uses the shared controls.
- **API reference reorganised.** A getting-started section opens the document: session and token, public routes, rights, the response envelope and HTTP codes, the invoice key, dates, paging, the background-run and polling pattern, the assistant's event stream, proxy behaviour. The menu is grouped by audience (Invoices & documents, Processing, Platforms, Operations, Administration, Developer) and the tags are described in user terms. Every operation now states its access, in the text and as `x-permission`: the action a role must grant, the settings feature, the template flags for a reprocess, "any signed-in user", or public. Descriptions render as paragraphs: the document's line breaks were never escaped, so Redoc folded every description into one block since the first release. Shared schemas describe the recurring shapes (error, invoice key, log entry, run start and progress). The build runs a documentation lint over the 158 operations (summary, usable description, response example, access marker; currently zero findings, report-only) and renders the same document to Markdown for the docs site.
- **Settings organised by intent.** The left list of the Settings page is no longer one entry per template file. It is grouped by what you want to do: Platform (directories and environment, processing, server log, PDF rendering, email, AI assistant, license, the two databases), Security (authentication, single sign-on, users, roles), E-invoicing (settings, document types, status catalogue, directory lookup), E-reporting, Jobs & inbound (JDE print queue, scheduled jobs, integrity checks), Views & UI (list views), API, SQL and FTP connectors, Reference data. Entries carry a human label and a one-line description, the technical template name stays visible in the editor header. Opening an entry such as "Server log" shows only that part of the global settings, without the row of tabs; the list views are edited on their own. The search box matches entry names and every field label, hint and key, and says under the entry which field matched. Rarely used groups (Ghostscript, the assistant's TLS proxy) are folded under Advanced. All areas start collapsed. Storage, template names, saving and file versioning are unchanged.
- **Scheduled jobs: one page for everything the server runs on a schedule.** A new page of the Synchronization group lists every background job in the shared data table: the PA import poll and status retrieval, the e-reporting cycle, the received-invoices fetch, the batch document jobs (BIP, directory, watched folders), the daily digests, the auto-retries, the lifecycle checks and the notifications purge. Each row shows its kind, trigger ("every 5 min", "daily 04:00"), state (On, Off, Paused, Running), last run, duration, result, next run. Disabled jobs are listed too, as Off, so they can be enabled from the page. Three actions per row: Run now (outside the schedule, ignoring the pause and the quiet window; a running job is not started twice), Pause / Resume for every job (the pause keeps the schedule and skips the fires until resumed or the server restarts; Run now ignores it), and the job name, which opens the editor. The editor is the same form as before for each kind, in a window: interval and quiet window for the polls, label, trigger and parameters for a batch job, the full digest, auto-retry and lifecycle check forms with Send test and Delete. New job creates a batch job, a digest, an auto-retry or a lifecycle check and opens it. Saving or deleting reloads the schedules at once, where a changed hour or interval used to wait for the next server restart; the pauses survive the reload. Filter by kind, auto-refresh, export. The IT dashboard scheduler card links to the page.
- **Navigation and settings follow.** The Daily Digest, Auto-Retry and Lifecycle checks pages are removed from Management, their forms now live in the Scheduled jobs editor; existing role grants for those pages are simply ignored. Watched folders returns to Management, next to File versions: it configures folders, its schedule is a batch job on the Scheduled jobs page. In Settings, the Scheduling tab becomes "Job defaults" and keeps only real settings: quiet window, bulk send throttle (parallel workers, delay per worker), BIP watermarks and lookback. The poll intervals, the notifications retention and the batch jobs list left Settings for the page. Three intervals that had no field (e-reporting cycle, received invoices, notifications retention) are now editable from their job. Storage, template names, the command line and the scheduler's behaviour are unchanged; the status endpoint gains the next run, a running flag, the pause flag and the batch source per job, and two operator endpoints (run now, reload) join the existing pause endpoint, which now accepts any job.
- **Data dictionary replaces the Cross-Reference page.** Same place in the Documentation menu, same page grant. The page is generated at build time from three sources that existed apart: the database DDL (table purpose and notes, primary key, indexes, column type, nullability, default, inline and COMMENT ON descriptions), the configurable names (table and column accessors with their configuration keys) and every Java call site of each accessor, classified as a write or a read and attributed to a flow (processing, import poll, status poll, received invoices, e-reporting, inbound, jobs, notifications, authentication, API, screens, database, CLI). The left list shows the sixteen tables by flow group with a search over names, columns, comments and BT codes. The table card gives the purpose, key, accessor, the current rename from the NomaUBL database settings, indexes, notes and the flows that write and read it; the invoice tables carry a clickable lifecycle strip from the archive to the processing log. The columns grid is the shared data table (listed in the List views editor): column, override, type, description, BT code, accessor, screens that show it, flows, write and read counts; a row opens the code references, writes first, by flow. Served by a new endpoint next to the cross-reference one, which remains. A side effect of the join: the Columns editor of the NomaUBL database settings still offered the e-reporting bar code column dropped in May 2026 and lacked the direction column that replaced it; fixed.

## 2026.10.22.1 — 2026-10-22 \{#v2026-10-22-1\}

### Improvements

- **Full reprocess of validation failures.** A new "Allow full reprocess" setting on the document template lets an invoice in *Validation failed* (9905) be reprocessed in full from its archived source once the data was corrected at the source: the enrichment is queried again, the UBL regenerated, validated and sent to the PA when the template and document type say so. The status history is kept and a reprocess marker opens a new cycle, so the statuses that follow are recorded as new. Available from the invoice window ("Reprocess" button on a 9905), from the invoice list selection, from a new "To reprocess in full" card on the IT dashboard, on the API (`kind: "full"`) and on the command line (`-reprocess --full`). The existing reprint of deposited-not-transmitted invoices is unchanged and keeps its own "Allow reprocess" setting. Both apply to XML and PDF sources.
- **Replay-safe pre-processing and enrichment.** A reprocess replays the archived source, which already went through the template's pre-processing XSL and enrichment. The enrichment now replaces the rows of a previous run instead of adding to them (single-row rules already overwrote their fields), and the pre-processing field of the document editor states the rule for customer transforms: every element the XSL adds must be guarded with `not(...)` so a second pass adds nothing. The IT dashboard shows the four counter cards on one row.
- **Bulk reprocess as a single batch.** "Reprocess all" and a selection of several invoices now stage the sources in a working folder and run one processing batch per template, in the background with its live log, instead of one JVM per invoice: the "Max threads" setting of the global settings bounds the parallelism and an invoice is never processed twice. A single invoice still runs on its own. The command line gains `--input-dir <folder>` on `-process` to run a batch on a folder other than the template's input.
- **Running processes on the IT dashboard.** A new card lists the processing JVMs alive on the host: those started by this server, with the last line each printed, and the detached ones left by a previous instance, a cron or a manual run. Each row shows the mode, the arguments, the elapsed time and a Stop button, which terminates that JVM and its own child processes only; it requires the integration-run grant. Nothing is stopped when the server restarts, so a batch can run through an upgrade; the launcher script is unchanged.
- **Server log page.** Under Management, after File versions: the end of the server log file, newest lines first, with the amount read (128 KB to 8 MB), severity checkboxes, a module list built from the lines seen, a text search and an auto-refresh. Stack traces stay attached to the line that threw them. The file is found on its own (the launcher's `nomaubl-<env>.log`, or the server's redirected output on Linux); a "Server log file" setting in the global settings covers another launcher.

### Fixes

- **Spurious "PDF creation" error on templates without an RTF.** Forcing the readable PDF ("Keep PDF" on a document type, or a reprint) on a template that has no RTF template, PDF-source templates among them, logged a PDF creation error. The forced render is now skipped when there is nothing to render with.

## 2026.10.21.1 — 2026-10-21 \{#v2026-10-21-1\}

### Improvements

- **E-reporting: per-company setups.** The e-reporting settings gain the same scope bar as e-invoicing: pick the default or a company setup, create a company setup (`e-reporting-{kco}`) seeded from the default, delete it. Each company can thus carry its own issuer, frequency and PA connection. The companies to run are detected from these setups; the "Companies" list on the default only names companies to run with the default settings.
- **E-reporting: generation runs in the background.** Generate returns at once and the dialog shows the run's log as it goes, then refreshes the list when done. A large period no longer ends in a proxy error while the run continues unseen on the server.
- **PDF: logo size.** Two new settings next to the logo path and offset, "Logo width" and "Logo height" in points: the logo is scaled to fit that box, ratio kept, enlarged when the image is smaller; one dimension alone lets the other follow the image. Left blank, the previous cap of 200 × 80 points applies without enlarging. The visual builder preview uses the same size as the produced PDF.
- **Ordering check runs in the background.** Check and Clean return at once, the page shows the run's log as it goes and then the findings. The status-drift scan reads the history once, in a single pass, and logs its progress every 50 000 rows, the result by "current → expected" pair, and a closing summary. A large base no longer ends in a proxy error.
- **Users: password change at first login is a choice, and SSO-only accounts.** Creating a user, or resetting a password, now shows a "Require a new password at the first local login" checkbox, ticked by default. With SSO enabled the password at creation is optional: left empty, the account signs in through the identity provider only, has no local password and is never asked to change one. A session opened through SSO is no longer sent to the change-password screen, which asked for an old password the user never had.
- **Watched folders: one batch at a time, scan in the background.** The processing batch of a template now takes a lock on its input folder for its duration, so a second batch cannot start on the same files: a manual or scheduled scan that finds the folder locked converts the new files but leaves the batch to the running one and says so in its log. The "Scan and process" button of the settings runs in the background with the live log, instead of a request that outlived the proxy timeout and invited a relaunch.

### Fixes

- **Invoice status realigned on a reprocess artefact.** Until 11 October a reprocess regenerated the document through the normal pipeline, leaving a "validation successful" event just before its reprocess marker. The header realignment then landed on that event, and Monday's Clean set 1 967 invoices to 9901 or 9902 instead of their deposited status. A generation event sitting directly under a reprocess marker is now ignored like the marker, as is a history row without a code, everywhere the status is realigned. The drift scan also no longer skips reprocessed invoices whose order is correct, which hid these from the list.
- **SSO: token exchange refused with invalid_client.** The client secret was passed through a Base64 decode on load although it is stored as typed. A secret made of letters and digits decodes without error into random bytes, which were sent to the identity provider; whether a secret survived depended on its length and characters. The decode is now kept only when it yields printable text, and with debug logging the token request prints a length and SHA-256 fingerprint of the secret actually sent, to compare with the provider's.
- **Batch processing: one failing file killed the whole batch.** A fatal error on a file, a missing input or a failed transformation, stopped the batch JVM with every other file in flight, which appeared as started-but-never-ended rows in the processing log and left their inputs to be processed again. The file is now marked failed and moved to the errors folder while the others finish. Two batches on the same folder, which this and a relaunch produced, were also the cause of "no such file" errors on inputs deleted by the other batch and of documents processed twice. Batch mode also no longer deletes the attachment PDFs of files still in flight after a successful file.
- **E-reporting: buyer identifier refused (G2.19).** The buyer block carried the buyer's electronic address (scheme 0225, the PPF routing address) instead of its legal identifier. A French address or a SIRET now yields the SIREN under scheme 0002 with the VAT number derived from it; 0002, 0223, 0227, 0228 and 0229 pass through. A buyer with no usable identifier (blank, "0", an email scheme) is left out of the report and the invoice is named in the log, so the customer record can be completed; the validation then reports the missing buyer on that invoice rather than a scheme error on the whole report.
- **E-reporting: "Compute period" ignored the settings and the previous reports.** The dialog always assumed a monthly frequency, and the lookup of the last report never matched, so the current month was proposed every time and then submitted as the period. The computation now follows the company's setup (monthly, decadal, weekly) and the last valid report of the company for the direction, exactly as the scheduled run does, and the dialog states which frequency it applied and which report it follows. A company must be entered to compute.

## 2026.10.20.1 — 2026-10-20 \{#v2026-10-20-1\}

### Improvements

- **PDF source: labelled segments inside a value.** A value printed as segments separated by " / " where some carry their own label, such as `VIREMENT / IBAN : FR76 … / BIC : CCBPFRPPBDX / Titulaire : ACME SA`, now keeps the unlabelled part in its element and yields one sibling element per labelled segment (`Paiement`, `Paiement_IBAN`, `Paiement_BIC`, `Paiement_Titulaire`), each mappable on its own. Grouping spaces inside the IBAN are removed as for other identifiers.
- **Peppol lookup on restricted networks.** Two new settings on the e-directory template. "Resolve platform via SMP" (default Y): set to N when the network does not allow HTTPS to the providers' SMP hosts; the lookup then stops at the DNS answer and the platform column shows the SMP host (`smp.pennylane.com`) instead of the provider name and seat read from its certificate, with no call to wait for. "Public DNS fallback" (default N): the lookup uses the server's resolver only; Y allows a retry through 8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1 when that resolver gives no answer. When the SMP cannot be read, the page now shows the host and the reason instead of a bare "unresolved", and the server log lists each unresolved participant with its reason.

### Fixes

- **Peppol lookup very slow when external resolvers are blocked.** An identifier not registered in Peppol was retried through the public resolvers on both DNS zones, which on a server without access to them cost over a minute per identifier. A "no such name" answer from the server's resolver is now final, and a failing public resolver is dropped for the rest of the lookup.
- **PPF directory lines not listed with an Esker connector.** The SIREN listing read the response array under a property name the connector editor does not write, so only a response whose array happened to be named `results` worked. The "Response field" of the endpoint is now honoured, `records` included.

## 2026.10.19.1 — 2026-10-19 \{#v2026-10-19-1\}

### Improvements

- **Integrity check: progress and logs on the page.** The run reports its progress as it goes: pages fetched from the platform, events compared every thousand with the running counts, and a final summary. From the Import Status page these lines now appear live under the Integrity check section while the run works, instead of being readable only in the server log. Events outside the requested window are dropped with a logged count (a connector bounding only the start date returns everything up to now), duplicates delivered twice are collapsed, and the invoice lookups are done once per invoice instead of once per event. The command line gains `--until <ISO>` and `--company <kco>` on `-status-integrity`.
- **Ordering check: invoice status drift.** The check now also reports an invoice whose status differs from the latest real state of its history, shown as "current → expected", and realigns it on apply. Until now a header carrying a stale value was fixed only when a row of the same invoice had to be removed or re-sequenced. The scheduled run and the command line pick the new finding up with no change.
- **E-Directory as an API.** `GET /api/e-directory/search?q=…` (or POST with `{q, peppol}`) returns in one call what the E-Directory page assembles: the INSEE companies matching a name, SIREN or SIRET with head office and establishments, the PPF directory lines of each company, and with `peppol=true` its Peppol participants. Documented in the API reference.
- **Peppol lookup without business card.** Publishing a business card in the Peppol Directory is optional, and some providers do not. The lookup now also probes the SML directly for the identifiers a French company can hold: the SIREN under schemes 0225 and 0002, every address registered in the PPF directory (bare, suffixed, SIRET, routed) under 0225, and the SIRETs of the establishments under 0009. A company registered on an SMP without a business card now lists all its addresses with the resolved platform, marked "no business card" in place of the registration date.

### Fixes

- **Peppol lookup failing intermittently.** OpenPeppol took over the Service Metadata Locator in 2026 and participant records moved to its DNS zone. The lookup still queried the former European Commission zone, so it only worked for participants not yet removed from it. It now queries the Peppol zone first, with the former zone as fallback, retries DNS and falls back to public resolvers when the system resolver answers nothing. A Peppol Directory outage no longer hides the DNS results.
- **E-Directory: Peppol not checked after a second search.** A company left open from a previous search came back open but its Peppol lookup never ran. It now runs for every open company whose lookup has not started.

- **Statuses of a resent invoice not recorded.** After a rejection and a resend, the statuses of the second cycle (deposited, received, transmitted…) were ignored by the status retrieval and by the integrity check, because the duplicate guard considered every code the invoice had ever carried as already recorded. The guard now works per submission cycle: a code counts as recorded only since the last send, pending or reprocess event, while the exact same platform event (same code and timestamp) is still recognised across cycles.
- **Integrity check limited to 500 missing events.** The result listed at most 500 rows, so the Apply button could only backfill the first 500 and the check had to be rerun. Missing and applied rows are no longer limited; only the informational not-found and unmapped rows stop being listed past two thousand, with a log line saying so. The scheduled run was not affected.
- **Invoice status overwritten by the reprocess or mail-sent marker.** When the history of an invoice ended with the reprocess marker (9912) or the mail-sent marker (9908), the ordering check, the integrity backfill, the status retrieval and the deletion of a history event copied that marker into the invoice status. All header realignments now take the latest real state of the history, looking past both markers in whatever order they appear, so a deposited 200 NON_TRANSMISE stays as such. The mail-sent marker is also treated as an application event: the status retrieval no longer drops it and the ordering check no longer reports it as misordered.

## 2026.10.18.1 — 2026-10-18 \{#v2026-10-18-1\}

### Improvements

- **PDF as a document source.** A document template can now take a text PDF from any system (not only JDE) as its source. The PDF is converted into a flat XML that the XSL editor maps like a spool: one element per labelled value on the page (amounts, percents and dates normalised, spaced identifiers such as VAT numbers compacted, a rate printed in a label like "TVA 20,00%" split into its own element, a period into its start and end), one table (columns named after its header, or inferred from the first row when the header is a single cell, wrapped labels merged, closed by a ruled line), the party boxes as address blocks (name, street lines, postal code, city, country, plus the labelled lines printed against them such as supplier code, SIRET, VAT, phone, e-mail), every printed row kept for anything else, and the path of the PDF so the original can be embedded as an attachment. Settings on the template: table start and end anchors, a layout match, a page match (a print holding a statement and the invoice keeps the invoice pages only), and regex fields with an optional rewrite (`Type_JDE|^FACTURE=>F9`). The Process document page, watched folders and the command line process PDF-source templates like XML ones; `-pdf2xml <in.pdf> <out.xml> --text` converts a file on its own; the document editor and the XSL editor load a sample straight from a PDF. Scanned PDFs are refused with an explicit error.
- **Force send from the Process document page.** The send option of XML and PDF sources now offers "Force send" next to "Use settings" and "Skip": every document of the run is sent to the PA as if its document type said F. Available on the command line as `--send`.
- **XSL mapping: constants and flat recaps.** A mapping variable can hold a constant between backticks (`TAG_COMPANY_CODE` = `` `00009` ``), so a single-company source still gets its company in the UBL number and the seller block. A repeating-group variable can point at the document itself with `.`, for a source whose single VAT recap is printed on the document rather than in a group.

### Fixes

- **UBL defaults: per-template payment default not saved.** With the payment override enabled on a document template, the default payment code was written to the global defaults and lost on save. The override now carries its own default.
- **UBL defaults: suppliers override no longer compiles.** A suppliers override saved recently produced a seller template missing the additional-identifiers parameter the framework now passes, and the transform failed with XTSE0680. Fixed for new saves; a template whose suppliers override was saved before this version needs one re-save from the UBL defaults page.

## 2026.10.16.1 — 2026-10-16 \{#v2026-10-16-1\}

### Improvements

- **Repair option on the Process document page.** A new "Repair" setting rebuilds the invoice tables of a document whose header, lines, VAT summary and validation rows were lost while its archived source and its status history survived (a case produced by an earlier replace that failed midway). The document is regenerated from its source with the chosen template, exactly as a normal run, but the archive row is kept untouched (PA transaction id, send flag, source), the status history is neither purged nor appended, the rebuilt header takes the status, reason and action of the latest history event that is a real state (the reprocess marker 9912 is looked past, so a reprinted 200 NON_TRANSMISE comes back as such), and nothing is sent to the PA. No notification rule fires during a repair, since the invoice does not change state. Also available on the command line as `-process … --repair`. A document with no history at all is processed normally.

### Fixes

- **Credit notes: project reference rejected by the schema.** UBL 2.1 has no project reference element on a credit note, so every RM document carrying one failed the XSD check (cvc-complex-type.2.4.a on ProjectReference). The XSL framework now emits the project reference (BT-11) of a credit note as an additional document reference of type 50, as the EN 16931 binding prescribes; invoices are unchanged. The invoice window builds and reads both forms, and the PDF prints the project reference from either. Operator templates pick the change up at their next upgrade.
- **API documentation page blank.** The embedded API documentation loaded the Redoc viewer from the CDN without a version. Redoc 3.0 was published on 14 October with a different entry point, and the page stopped rendering on every installation that day. The viewer is now pinned to the 2.x line.

## 2026.10.14.1 — 2026-10-14 \{#v2026-10-14-1\}

### Improvements

- **PDF labels per template.** Every text the PDF generator prints (46 labels: document header, parties, lines table, line details, VAT summary, totals, payment) can now be overridden per PDF template and per language, from a new "Labels" panel in the visual builder: the default wording shows as placeholder, a blank field keeps it, a search box and an "overridden only" filter help find them, each row can be reset, and the labels of another PDF template can be copied in. The live preview reflects the overrides. A customer asking for "N° de facture" instead of "N° facture UBL" gets it on their template only; other customers and existing templates are unchanged.
- **Processing rules per document template.** A new "Processing rules" group on the document template (Document tab) routes documents of the XML pipeline before anything is generated. Each rule combines conditions on the document (JDE document type, resolved document type, raw processing type, invoice amount, company, activity, type piece, customer number, document number, or any XPath / spool tag, with in-list, equality, zero, comparison, emptiness and regex operators) with one of two outcomes: "treat as document type X", which continues the document with that type's send / validate / mode / keep settings (for example a zero-amount gratuity routed to ARCHIVEONLY), or "exclude", which records the document only. An excluded document keeps its archived source and header, carries the new status "Excluded by rule" (9914, message = rule name) with a lifecycle event, is visible in the list and counted by the integrity checks, but is never validated, output nor sent. Rules are ordered, the first match wins, and apply to every XML ingestion path (scheduler, watched folders, process, fetch-single, Fetch Input). UBL documents are deliberately left out: their transaction type is already written in the document.
- **Sequence key mode for UBL documents.** A UBL-source document template can now number its documents itself instead of deriving the key from the invoice number: key mode "Sequence" on the Document tab, with a fixed document type (II, incoming invoice, by default), a fixed company and a sequence start. The next number is one above the highest stored for that type and company. Meant for received invoices, whose number follows each supplier's own format, and usable for emitted UBL when the format is not known. The invoice number itself stays stored as the UBL number (BT-1). A document processed twice gets two numbers. The regex pattern and the connector lookup modes are unchanged.
- **Release notes page: collapsible version list.** The version chips show the twelve most recent releases, with a "Show all" chip for the full list and "Show less" to fold it back; the choice is remembered per browser.
- **Despatch advice references.** The XSL framework, the XSL editor, the invoice window and the PDF now handle the despatch advice at document level (BT-16: reference and date) and at line level (EXT-FR-FE-BG-07: reference EXT-FR-FE-140, date EXT-FR-FE-201, optional despatch line number). New mapping slots TAG_DESPATCH_REF / TAG_DESPATCH_DATE and TAG_LINE_DESPATCH_REF / TAG_LINE_DESPATCH_DATE / TAG_LINE_DESPATCH_LINE_ID; the invoice window offers the fields in the header and per line; the PDF prints them in the invoice block and as a line detail, with their own toggles and an overridable label.

### Fixes

- **Invoice line identifiers unique per invoice.** With lines grouped by delivery, the line number (BT-126) restarted at 1 on every delivery, giving duplicated identifiers inside one invoice and, on the database side, line rows lost on the key collision. Numbering is now continuous across the delivery groups; the fallback line numbers of the order and despatch line references follow it.
- **Invoice window: line reference buttons.** The "Customer Order Reference", "Order number", "Customer line no." and "Despatch advice" buttons on a line did not open their field.

## 2026.10.12.1 — 2026-10-12 \{#v2026-10-12-1\}

### Improvements

- **Integrity reports.** A new "Integrity" tab on the Reports page runs SQL checks that list what is missing or wrong in NomaUBL compared with a source system: JDE print jobs never integrated, accounting records whose amounts differ, … The checks are defined in the new "Integrity reports" settings template: name, description, database connector, SQL (SELECT only, read-only, row cap and timeout), key columns, and date placeholders filled from the page's period (\{from\}/\{to\}, \{fromJde\}/\{toJde\}, \{fromDMY\}/\{toDMY\}). Results show in the standard grid (search, filters, columns, export), every row being one anomaly. A check can carry an action: "Integrate BIP jobs" maps the job, template and host columns of the result and, on the selected rows, runs the same extraction and processing as `fetch-single <template> bip <job>` through the fetch-invoices batch, with confirmation; the check is re-run afterwards and the summary lists any failed job. Other action types (API or SQL connector calls) will follow.
- **Integrity reports across two databases.** A check can now compare a source query and a target query running on different connectors (JDE on MSSQL, NomaUBL on Postgres…), matched in memory on key columns: "Missing" lists source rows absent from the target, "Extra" the reverse, "Mismatch" the keys present on both sides whose compared columns differ (amounts within a tolerance, 0.01 by default), with the target value and the differing columns added to the result. Keys are normalised before matching (trailing spaces, leading zeros, decimal scale, dates). The single-query "Direct" mode is unchanged.
- **Confirmation before resending to the PA from the invoice window.** The "Resend to PA" button now asks for confirmation, since the document is transmitted immediately and its status moves to Pending (9906). The resend from the invoice list already had one.

### Fixes

- **VAT declaration on Oracle.** The declaration queries placed the table alias in front of the TRIM call, which Oracle rejects (ORA-00904 "UH"."TRIM"); the page then showed "No invoices in this period" instead of the error. Both are fixed: the queries are valid on every dialect, and a server-side failure is now displayed on the page and logged.

## 2026.10.11.1 — 2026-10-11 \{#v2026-10-11-1\}

### Improvements

- **SSO (OIDC): token endpoint authentication mode and debug logging.** A new "Token endpoint authentication" setting on the oidc template selects how the authorization code is exchanged: PKCE with the secret in the request body (default, unchanged) or HTTP Basic (Authorization header, no PKCE), for identity providers that accept only the latter. A "Debug logging" switch writes the discovery result, the authorize URL, the token exchange and the ID-token claims to the server log, with tokens and secrets redacted. Sign-ins and refusals (IdP error, expired state, token exchange failure, domain refusal, unknown account) are now always logged.
- **Status statistics by amount.** The status statistics report gets a "Measure" switch: invoice count (as before) or net amount (sum of the tax-exclusive amount, BT-109). Cells, subtotals and percentages follow the selected measure, since a few invoices can weigh most of the money. The Excel export follows the view and its data sheet carries both figures. The API returns an `amount` per grouped row.
- **Reprocess is a reprint.** Reprocessing a non-transmitted invoice regenerates the readable PDF/XML and the UBL file from the archived source into the output and burst folders, without any database change and without re-validating: the stored e-invoice (including a later Fix buyer correction) and its validation results stay as they are, no error status is written. A `--no-validate` option is available on the process command.

### Fixes

- **Integrity check: disputed and suspended statuses.** Disputed (207) and suspended (208) are interim statuses that may be followed by a lower code such as approved (205) or refused (210). The ordering check sorted them by code and pushed them after the final status, which then became the header status. They now keep their chronological position among the other statuses of their cycle, and never count as an inversion. Histories already mangled this way are repaired by the next run.

## 2026.10.06.1 — 2026-10-06 \{#v2026-10-06-1\}

### Improvements

- **Invoice deletion follows the PA protection and removes the document entirely.** Deleting an invoice (invoice window button or API) is now refused once the PA has processed it (any standard lifecycle status, 9911, 9913), with the same exception as Fix buyer: a 213 rejection for an addressing reason can still be deleted. The deletion also removes the F564230 log row (source XML, PA transaction reference, source file name), so a later run of the same document starts fresh and the watched folders can pick its source file up again. The button is hidden on protected statuses and the confirmation lists the log among the removed records.

### Fixes

- **Business unit and routing code kept on edit / Fix buyer.** Saving an invoice from the invoice window or correcting the buyer blanked F564230.FEAC04 (business unit) and FEROUT (routing code), since the UBL path carries neither. Both now keep the values set when the document was first processed, as the alpha key already did.

## 2026.10.05.1 — 2026-10-05 \{#v2026-10-05-1\}

### Improvements

- **BI Publisher jobs in FX status are picked up when the source XML is extracted.** A job whose UBE ran but whose BI Publisher transformation failed (RJRPDJBSTS = FX) still stores its source XML, which is all the UBL flow needs. Batch scans and single extracts in input (or both) mode now accept FX jobs alongside D / FD. Output-only extracts keep D / FD and report an explicit error on an FX job instead of waiting for it.
- **Generated PDF: information lines.** A line whose billing reference carries the INFORMATION status (the sub-type marker of a zero-amount line) is shown as "Information line" instead of a preceding invoice reference. Real preceding references are unchanged.

### Fixes

- **Integrity check: lifecycle ordering on re-emitted invoices.** Invoices sent again after a correction (Fix buyer, edit window, reprocess keep the history) carry several PA cycles. The ordering check treated the whole history as one cycle: it merged the second run's statuses into the first, pushed the rejections to the end, and reported the second cycle's "Import validated" event as misordered. Each cycle, opened by a sent / pending / reprocess event, is now ordered on its own, membership being decided on event time. Histories already mangled by the previous rule are detected and put back in order by the next run; correctly ordered re-emitted invoices are no longer reported.

## 2026.10.02.1 — 2026-10-02 \{#v2026-10-02-1\}

### Improvements

- **"Exclude reviewed errors" on the Dashboard, the Reports and the invoice list.** A new toggle hides the invoices already reviewed by customer service (F564231.UHALRTPSD = Y) that still sit in an error status (the errorTech / errorBusiness groups of the statuses template), so the error KPIs show what is left to handle. Reviewed invoices in any other status stay counted, and the totals remain the true number of invoices. Available on the Dashboard filter bar (kept across navigation), on the Reports status statistics tab and on the invoice list; a dashboard tile click carries the toggle to the list so both agree. The APIs take `excludeReviewed=true` (invoice stats, dashboard overview, status statistics) and `excludeReviewedErrors=true` (invoice list), default off.
- **Line order references: customer order, order number and customer line number.** The invoice line carries three distinct references in the same UBL group (`cac:OrderLineReference`): the customer line number (BT-132, `cbc:LineID`), the customer order number (EXT-FR-FE-135, `cac:OrderReference/cbc:ID`) and the seller's order number (EXT-FR-FE-144, `cbc:SalesOrderID`). The XSL framework gets one mapping slot for each (TAG_LINE_ORDER_LINE_REF, TAG_LINE_ORDER_REF, TAG_LINE_SALES_ORDER_REF); when only the order number is mapped, the mandatory order id falls back to the header purchase order (BT-13). The invoice window offers the three fields per line. The generated PDF groups lines on the order band "Customer Order Reference: … Order number: …" and prints the customer line number under each line; with grouping off, the three references appear as detail rows under each line. Previously the customer line number was treated as the customer order, which printed a band before nearly every line.

### Fixes

- **Fix buyer / edit window: successful re-validation now recorded in the history.** When an invoice in "Echec de validation" (9905) was repaired and validated successfully, the status row was updated to 9901 but no lifecycle event was written, so the history still ended on 9905. The validation outcome (9901 / 9902) is now appended whenever it differs from the latest event; an identical re-save stays silent.
- **Fix buyer: no more spurious notification, electronic address scheme kept.** The audit line "Identifiants acheteur corrigés" is now a plain history entry; it no longer re-fires the notification rule of the current status (e.g. 9905) on every correction. The buyer electronic address (BT-49) keeps the scheme already on the document, or 0225 when none, instead of being inferred from the digit count (a 9-digit identifier used to get 0002).
- **Invoice window: removed elements no longer come back on save.** Deleting a line VAT exemption, a note, a delivery block, an order reference or an item detail in the invoice window is now kept after saving. Previously the save merged the original document back in and restored any element the form no longer emitted. Elements the window does not manage are still preserved unchanged.

## 2026.10.01.1 — 2026-10-01 \{#v2026-10-01-1\}

### Improvements

- **Hand-corrected invoices are marked reviewed.** Saving an invoice from the invoice window or repairing it with Fix buyer now sets the customer-service review flag (F564231.UHALRTPSD = Y), provided the validation that follows raises no error. The Review column of the invoice list shows "Reviewed" on every flagged row, whatever its status; the dash stays for untouched happy-path rows and "Pending" for error rows awaiting a look. The API keeps today's behaviour: the new `alertProcessed` field of the create-ubl and fix-buyer endpoints defaults to N.
- **Scheduler status lists the daily lifecycle checks** next to the digests and auto-retries, with their time and last run.
- **Cleaner build**: no compiler warning left with every lint category on, unused imports and code removed.

- **Watched folders: JDE PDF / XML pickup, conversion and batch inside the application.** New *Watched folders* system template: rows of directory, file-name pattern, document template, optional pdf2xml manifest, overlap window and a "must be a mounted share" guard. A run lists each folder for files matching the pattern and newer than the last scan minus the overlap, drops the ones already processed (source file name in F564230) or already waiting as XML in the template's input folder, converts the PDFs in parallel into that folder (XML files are copied as is), then runs one batch per template — the batch keeps its own parallelism. The last-scan date advances on every run, so a failed file is retried while it stays inside the overlap window and reported by name instead of blocking the others; an unmounted share is reported instead of read as empty. The page offers a dry run and a run with an optional backfill date. Available as the batch job source *Watched folders* under global → Scheduling, as `nomaubl.sh watch-folders <env> [--folder N] [--since d] [--dry-run] [--no-process]`, and as `POST /api/watch-folders/run`. The upgrade creates the template empty; nothing runs until a folder and a job are configured.
- **Batch jobs can fire once a day.** Each batch job under global → Scheduling gains a *Daily at (HH:mm)* field: when set, the job runs at that local time instead of its interval, like the auto-retry and the lifecycle checks. The job list, the technical dashboard and the scheduler health card show "daily at 06:30". When the source is Watched folders, the job picks a folder from a dropdown listing the configured directories, or all of them.

### Fixes

- **E-Documents detail shows the template again.** The archived-document modal took the template, type and UBL number from the list row, which only carried the columns of the current view layout; with those columns hidden the Summary showed dashes and Reprocess stayed disabled with "No template recorded". The list now sends them on every row whatever the layout.
- **Invoice window no longer invents a header delivery.** Opening an invoice whose deliveries are on the lines filled the header delivery form with the first line's delivery, and saving wrote it back as a document-level delivery (BG-13), which then showed a Delivery box on the PDF. The window now reads only the document-level delivery; line deliveries stay on the lines.
- **Fix buyer and the edit window no longer overwrite the customer keys.** Saving a corrected invoice replaced the alpha key (F564230.FEALKY) with the buyer SIREN read from the UBL and reset the customer number (F564231.UHAN8) to zero, because the replace rewrote both from the document instead of the stored row. The stored alpha key is now kept whenever it exists — the SIREN remains the fallback for invoices created directly from UBL — and the customer number is carried over when the caller has none. Applies to Fix buyer, the edit window and any replace-mode reprocess, with or without resend; batch processing from a JDE spool is unchanged.
